payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a recorded verify gate when it is inspected then it names the verify mode the checks that ran and the resolved version of each tool, and given two machines running the same mode then the fingerprints are comparable well enough to tell an environment difference from a code difference
payload.description:
## Context

D9 requires dispatch inputs to be reproducible and recorded, but says nothing about the deterministic side. A recorded verify gate currently means passed on some machine with some tool versions: the gate result carries pass or fail and a provider, not the verify mode, the check set that ran, or the versions of the tools that ran them. A teammate therefore cannot tell whether a green gate is comparable to their own, and on a machine with different tool versions the same green means something different.

Record the mode, the check names, and the resolved tool versions alongside the gate result, as the deterministic counterpart to the dispatch-input recording in basicly-kjc5.28. Evidence rather than state - nothing branches on it, so a missing fingerprint degrades the audit trail without blocking a track.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a recorded verify gate when it is inspected then it names the verify mode the checks that ran and the resolved version of each tool, and given two machines running the same mode then the fingerprints are comparable well enough to tell an environment difference from a code difference

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
payload.title: Fingerprint the environment behind a gate result so it is portable evidence

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a dispatch whose resolved spec is a handoff runner while the result reports execution when the dispatch is recorded then no exception escapes and the record is written with an empty command
payload.close_reason: Fixed in d8f51db: command derivation guarded so a handoff spec paired with an executed result degrades to an empty command instead of raising; verified green on all three CI runners
payload.description:
## Context

Regression from basicly-kjc5.28, caught by CI on all three runners 2026-07-25. runner.record_dispatch derives the redacted command with format_command whenever the result does not report a handoff, and format_command raises ValueError for a handoff-only spec that has no command. The call sits outside every exception guard, so a telemetry helper can abort a dispatch.

It passed locally because select_runner with default auto resolves to a headless CLI on a developer machine; CI has no agent CLI installed, so it resolves the manual handoff runner and the mismatch appears. The same crash is reachable from the loop and supervisor dispatch paths, not only from the rubric judge, so this is a robustness defect rather than a test artifact - telemetry must never fail a landing, which is the stance the surrounding suppress calls already take.

Guard the command derivation so a mismatch degrades to an empty command, and cover it with a test that passes a handoff spec together with an executed result.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Resolve the manual runner spec and build a RunResult with executed true and handoff false.
2. Call runner.record_dispatch with that spec and result.
3. It raises ValueError saying the runner is handoff not headless and has no command.

Expected: the record is written with an empty command and nothing is raised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatch whose resolved spec is a handoff runner while the result reports execution when the dispatch is recorded then no exception escapes and the record is written with an empty command

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
payload.title: Telemetry recording must never raise on a spec and result mismatch

payload.close_reason: Fixed at the source: the hard-kill signal now has a portable module fallback and the tests assert against it; reproduced the exact CI error before fixing and verified with pyright resolving as Windows plus the kill-tree tests under a complete POSIX-name simulation
payload.description:
## Context

quality-gates has been red on main since 2225cfe (basicly-kjc5.15, 2026-07-24) - before the 2026-07-25 session, which did not cause it. Three tests fail on windows-latest with AttributeError: module os has no attribute getpgid, because monkeypatch.setattr requires the attribute to exist and os.getpgid is POSIX-only. pyright fails on the same reference.

The tests exercise the process-tree kill introduced by kjc5.15, which is deliberately platform-conditional. The fix is to make the POSIX branch's tests skip or patch tolerantly on Windows while keeping the coverage on POSIX, rather than weakening the kill path itself.

Note for whoever picks this up: main is red for this reason independently of any other work, so a green local verify does not mean a green CI. The repo's own os-matrix decision is why this is caught at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the suite on Windows, or inspect the quality-gates run for any commit at or after 2225cfe.
2. tests/test_runner.py fails three kill-tree tests with AttributeError on os.getpgid, and pyright reports the same missing attribute.

Expected: the suite and pyright pass on all three runners while the POSIX kill path stays covered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the Windows CI runner when the suite runs then no test monkeypatches a POSIX-only os attribute that is absent there and pyright reports no error for it, with the process-group kill path still covered on POSIX

## Scope

- `tests/test_runner.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Owner correction 2026-07-25: a fix or a check that lives outside the repo is not replicable or transferable, and must not be how correctness is established.

Two real defects this session were caught only by ad-hoc local shell incantations that nobody else will know to run. basicly-kjc5.53 - telemetry raising on a handoff spec paired with an executed result, reachable from the loop and supervisor dispatch paths - was invisible locally because a developer machine has an agent CLI on PATH and CI does not, so select_runner resolves differently there; it was found by re-running the suite with a stripped PATH. basicly-kjc5.54 - POSIX-only names in the kill-tree tests - was verified with pyright --pythonplatform Windows and by deleting os.getpgid and os.killpg in a throwaway interpreter, and that simulation is what revealed a second patch site the first attempt missed.

Both checks belong in the repo. Add them to the verify gate or as marked test configurations so they run for everyone: type resolution for every supported platform rather than only the host, and a dispatch path exercised with no agent CLI resolvable. The pattern to avoid is the one this bead exists to correct - proving something with a command only one machine ever ran.

Related: basicly-kjc5.41, where the same principle applies to the loop ceremony, since the previous session hand-rolled a shell wrapper outside the repo instead of the engine providing the command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the verify gate when it runs on any platform then it resolves types for every supported platform and exercises the dispatch path with no agent CLI resolvable, so a defect that only appears on another runner is caught before the push rather than by CI

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/`

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a landing whose verify gate fails with a known dependency-defect signature when the landing is scored then the gate is reported unreliable and no rework attempt is charged without needing the failure to fail to reproduce and the signature register is narrow enough that a failure the work under test could have caused is still scored as a merit failure with tests covering both directions
payload.description:
## Problem

basicly-55yh shipped the right idea and it does not cover the defect it was built for. When a landing gate fails, `verify.rerun_failures` re-runs exactly the failed checks in the same tree; if they pass the landing returns verify-unreliable and charges no rework (`loop.py:590` wires this into the single-track path, `merge.py` into the queue).

That detects a flake only if it fails to reproduce within seconds. The `br` clock defect is not a per-run coin flip: when the host clock has stepped backwards it stays stepped for a window, so the re-run reproduces and the failure is scored as a merit failure.

Measured on basicly-m4zv.9's landing 2026-07-27:

    unreliable events on m4zv.9 gate='merge':  0
    unreliable events on m4zv.9 gate='verify': 0
    rework verify: 1

Zero unreliable events with rework charged means the re-run reproduced. Contrast the kjc5.22 dogfood, where re-running gave 1 fail then 2 passes and the mitigation would have worked. So coverage is probabilistic against precisely the defect that motivated it.

The signature is unmistakable and cannot be produced by the work under test:

    Error: Validation failed: updated_at: cannot be before created_at

It can only come from `br`'s own validation, which rejects a write whose `updated_at` precedes its `created_at` when the machine's clock steps backwards. Root cause on this host: two time authorities correcting one clock - Hyper-V TimeSync IC 4.0 plus an active systemd-timesyncd.

Deliberately NOT fixed by stabilising the developer's clock. That is not committable, does not port to CI or the other platforms, hides the defect from consumers, and would remove the only reliable way to reproduce the condition while testing this fix.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a landing advance whose verify gate fails on the clock signature while the host clock is still stepped.
2. Observe the landing returns verify-failed and charges a rework attempt.
3. Observe `policy.unreliable_gate_events` records nothing, because `rerun_failures` reproduced the failure.

Observed: a dependency defect consumes the bounded rework budget.
Expected: the signature is recognised on the first failure and the gate is scored unreliable with no re-run needed.

## Notes

Complements basicly-vkh0.6 rather than duplicating it: vkh0.6 carries the clock error forward as a requirement with a regression test so the replacement cannot reintroduce it; this stops the harness paying for it in the months before cutover. Also independent of the clock specifically - the signature list is the mechanism, and a second entry can be added when another dependency defect is proved.

Keep the register narrow and evidenced. A signature earns its place only when it can be shown to be impossible for the work under test to cause, otherwise this becomes a way to launder real failures.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
payload.title: Score a known dependency defect as an unreliable gate without waiting for a re-run

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a landing whose merged diff touches the modules that score a landing when the verdict is reported then the report states the verdict came from the pre-merge code and that a re-run applies the merged logic so no rework attempt is spent rediscovering it with a test covering a diff that touches those modules and one that does not
payload.description:
## Problem

`basicly loop run` executes from the base checkout. Python imports `merge`/`verify`/`loop` from base's files at process start, then the landing merges the harness branch into base *during that same process*. Modules are never reloaded, so the landing is scored by the code as it was **before** the merge it just performed.

For most work this is invisible. For a change to the landing logic itself it is actively misleading: the fix looks broken on its own landing, and the run spends rework attempts proving it.

Observed on basicly-kjc5.56, which added signature-based unreliable-gate scoring. Commit timestamps on main:

    23:29:53  fix v1 merged  (singular-only signature register)
    23:30:14  merge commit
    23:34:20  attempt 2 process starts - imports base modules from disk
    23:34:26  fix v2 merged  (adds the plural br message shape)
    23:34:47  merge commit

Attempt 2 therefore ran v1's matcher against a message only v2 recognises, did not match, and escalated at rework 2/2. Base's code forgives that exact message when called afterwards, so the fix was correct the whole time. The bead spent its entire rework budget on the defect it fixes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Change the scoring logic in `merge._verify_for_landing` or `verify`.
2. Commit it on the harness branch and run `basicly loop run <id>`.
3. Observe the landing merges the change and then scores itself with the pre-merge code.

Observed: the new behaviour does not apply, and a failure it would have forgiven charges rework.
Expected: either the landing scores itself with the code it merged, or it says plainly that it did not.

## Notes

Not obviously worth making the engine re-exec itself - that is a real complexity cost for a narrow case, and re-exec mid-landing has its own failure modes. The cheap and honest option is to name it: when the merged diff touches the landing-scoring modules, print that the verdict was produced by the pre-merge code and that a re-run will use the new logic. Then nobody spends a rework budget rediscovering it.

Related: basicly-55yh (the re-run mitigation), basicly-kjc5.56 (the signature register), basicly-4tjt (clearing a rework counter after an escalation).

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
payload.title: A change to the landing logic cannot take effect on the landing that merges it

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a catalog source that declares a raw model id or alias when catalog lint runs then it fails naming the source and the tier field to use instead, and given a source that declares a tier when agents-build runs then the projected agent file carries no model line for any family, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Re-scoped 2026-07-29 after the owner picked the tier-table-as-catalog-data design. Supersedes
the earlier "declare a model per configured agent" framing, which put provider model ids in
config; the defect is that a model id is never portable across agent families.

Measured: `providers/github-copilot/models/claude-haiku-4.5.toml` on models.dev spells the
same model `claude-haiku-4.5` where Anthropic spells it `claude-haiku-4-5`. Hyphens on
Anthropic, dots on Copilot, and they coincide only on the `-5` generation. A one-character
divergence per entry, which is why a model id must never appear in a family-agnostic
catalog source.

This is already leaking: `.basicly/core/agents/test-runner/agent.yaml` declares
`model: haiku`, an Anthropic-only alias, and it lands verbatim in
`.claude/agents/test-runner.md` frontmatter while the copilot projection has no model field
to receive it at all.

The roster design already owns the portable vocabulary - four tiers low, medium, high,
maximum, with "the concrete model behind each tier is config (R2)". Reuse it; do not invent
a second vocabulary.

Scope: `.basicly/core/schemas/agent.schema.json`, `src/basicly/agents.py`,
`src/basicly/catalog_lint.py`, `.basicly/core/agents/test-runner/agent.yaml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a catalog source that declares a raw model id or alias when catalog lint runs then it
  fails naming the source and the tier field to use instead, and given a source that declares
  a tier when agents-build runs then the projected agent file carries no model line for any
  family, with tests
payload.title: Declare a capability tier on a catalog entry instead of a model id

payload.text: [harness-info] Design input from the 2026-07-30 oh-my-openagent analysis (reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-openagent.md). Their model-core is a working implementation of exactly this bead: a work item declares a named tier, never a model id, and a pure injected resolver walks an ordered (providers, model, variant) fallback chain against what is reachable, returning the chosen model plus a provenance enum of override, category-default, provider-fallback or system-default (model-resolution-pipeline.ts:88-274; tiers at category-model-requirements.ts:3-162). About 400 lines of pure logic that ports to stdlib Python unchanged. Pair with model-settings-compatibility.ts:107-206, which never refuses an unsupported knob but clamps it down a fixed ladder and records each downgrade as a field/from/to/reason record - the graceful-degradation contract to copy. DECISIVE for this bead's design: their HEAD commit fix/task-reject-category-with-model makes tier and raw model id MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with a typed error, because a call-site model override would silently bypass the routing. If a catalog entry may declare both, the tier is decoration - so the schema must reject the pair rather than define a precedence between them.

[harness-policy] CORRECTION 2026-07-30 (references.md 2.2, basicly-imnu.12). The earlier comment on this bead described oh-my-openagent's tier logic as 'about 400 lines of pure logic that ports to stdlib Python unchanged'. WITHDRAW THAT. Their LICENSE.md is the Sustainable Use License 1.0, which is not open source: 'You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or personal use. You may distribute the software or provide it to others only if you do so free of charge for non-commercial purposes.' The three files cited live in packages/model-core, which carries no licence of its own and is therefore governed by that root licence - only pi-goal, pi-webfetch and lsp-tools-mcp have their own MIT, and omo-senpi/plugin/LICENSE is a scoped MIT covering six named portions only. basicly is distributed, so a port would be distribution of a derivative work outside the permitted purposes. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the substance: the design is an idea and freely usable - a work item declares a named tier rather than a model id, the resolver returns a provenance enum for which rule chose the model, and an unsupported setting is clamped down a ladder with the downgrade recorded as field/from/to/reason rather than refused. payload.description:
## Context

Re-scoped 2026-07-29 for the tier design. basicly-kjc5.58 gives catalog entries a tier;
basicly-kjc5.61 gives the engine a committed tier-to-model map. This is the resolution seam
that consumes both at spawn time - the mechanism that sets the model per coding agent
without any model id living in a projected agent file.

Resolution order, most specific first: an explicit `model` pin on `[[runner.agents]]`, then
a configured tier on that agent, then the tier the role or catalog entry declares, then the
family default tier, then refuse. Refusal names the agent and the config key rather than
dispatching an unpinned runner - the same stance `_apply_model` already takes when a model
placeholder has no model.

`model` is a declared field on all 122 run records in `.basicly/usage/run-records.json` and
null on all 122, because no built-in RunnerSpec pins one and `basicly.toml` declares no
`[[runner.agents]]` at all. The plumbing from spec to run record already exists
(`runner.py` writes `model=spec.model`); what is missing is a resolved value to put in it.
That null is why basicly-jr0l.21 has no key to calibrate a per-model forecast against.

Claude subagents need no per-file model: `agents.DEFAULT_MODEL` is `inherit` and the
frontmatter omits it, so a session model set here is inherited. Where a role's tier differs
from the session tier and the family has no per-agent model slot - copilot has none - fall
back to the session model and record that the tier was not honoured rather than implying it
was.

Scope: `src/basicly/runner.py`, `src/basicly/run_record.py`, `src/basicly/config.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a configured agent whose tier resolves to no model when a dispatch is attempted then
  the engine refuses with a message naming the agent and the config key and no agent process
  starts, and given a resolvable tier then the concrete model id and the tier it came from are
  both written to the run record, and given a role tier a family cannot express then the
  fallback to the session model is recorded rather than reported as honoured, with tests
payload.title: Refuse to dispatch an unresolved model and record the resolved value

payload.text: [harness-info] Observed-model clause added 2026-07-29. Verified that the adapters report the model they actually ran, so the record can carry both the pin and the observation: claude stream-json puts it on assistant message.model (probed: claude-opus-5) in the same dict _claude_last_turn_usage already parses, and copilot puts it on assistant.message.data.model and model.call_start.data.model and keys session.shutdown.data.modelMetrics by it (probed: claude-sonnet-5). Recording both is strictly better than either: a pin alone cannot detect the CLI ignoring it, which is the drift D9 exists to catch.

verified 2026-07-31 by probing the installed CLIs, because the AC's observed-model clause had no evidence behind it. Per-family observed-model channel: claude 2.1.220 (-p --output-format stream-json --verbose) carries it three ways - the system init event's model, every assistant event's message.model, and the result event's modelUsage keyed by model id; the keys are the DATED id (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) while each block also carries canonicalModel (claude-haiku-4-5), which is the map's anthropic-surface spelling, so equality against a pinned haiku or claude-haiku-4-5 would report a FALSE mismatch on every claude dispatch - join on canonicalModel. copilot 1.0.77 reports it as the session.shutdown modelMetrics KEYS (measured on 28 real local stores: claude-opus-5 x13, claude-sonnet-5 x15, claude-haiku-4.5 x1); 29 keys over 28 stores means a single dispatch can report TWO models, so observed is a set and mismatch means the pin is absent from it. codex 0.146.0 --json carries NO model field anywhere - full stream is thread.started/turn.started/item.completed/turn.completed only - so observed must stay null and be recorded as unobserved, never fabricated. All three CLIs accept --model (copilot does too), so only the manual handoff runner genuinely cannot express a tier.

payload.description:
## Context

Filed 2026-07-29 as the generation half of the tier design. basicly-kjc5.58 makes catalog
sources declare a tier; this resolves a tier to the concrete per-family model id, from data
rather than by hand.

models.dev publishes a documented unauthenticated API (`https://models.dev/api.json`, plus
`models.json` and `catalog.json`) whose per-provider serving records carry `cost`
(input/output/cache) and `limit`, and - decisively - a `base_model` field linking a
provider's serving id to the underlying model. So four hand-authored anchors, one per tier,
resolve to every family's own spelling automatically.

Per-family serving data is not cosmetic: copilot serves `claude-haiku-4.5` at a 136000-token
input limit where Anthropic's `claude-haiku-4-5` is 200000, which the working-set band needs.

The confirmed anchors are low `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, medium
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, high `anthropic/claude-opus-5` (the workhorse), maximum
`anthropic/claude-fable-5`.

Two hard constraints. The fetch runs at authoring and check time only, never in the dispatch
path, so no runtime network dependency is added and determinism holds. And because the
upstream is community-contributed, the generated map is committed and reviewed as a diff
while the drift check reports rather than auto-applies, so a bad upstream edit surfaces as a
failing check instead of silently changing dispatch behaviour.

Note medium reverts from 2 dollars/10 dollars to 3 dollars/15 dollars per MTok on
2026-09-01 when Sonnet 5 introductory pricing ends; the drift check is what catches it.

Scope: `.basicly/core/models/`, `.scripts/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the four tier anchors when the generator runs then it resolves each family serving id
  via base_model and writes a committed map carrying the model id input and output cost and
  input limit per family and tier, stamped with the upstream commit sha and the fetch date,
  and given a pinned id that no longer resolves upstream or whose cost moved when the drift
  check runs then it fails naming the id and the change without mutating the committed map,
  with tests
payload.title: Generate the family model map from models dev with pinned provenance

payload.text: SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (owner-driven, verified against live authoritative docs, not recall). This bead currently assumes models.dev alone can resolve a tier to a per-family model id. That is insufficient: the value you write to select a model differs by SURFACE, not just by family, and there are at least three spellings for one model. For claude-haiku-4.5 the three observed forms are: (1) Anthropic / Claude Code agent frontmatter - claude-haiku-4-5, hyphenated, or the short alias haiku; (2) GitHub Copilot and VS Code custom-agent frontmatter - the DISPLAY NAME with spaces dots and capitals, e.g. Claude Haiku 4.5; (3) models.dev provider serving id - claude-haiku-4.5. So the committed map must carry a per-surface spelling column, and models.dev covers only (3) plus the cost and limit data. Sources: VS Code custom agents doc states model accepts a single model name string or a prioritized list array, with the literal example model: ['Claude Opus 4.5', 'GPT-5.2'] - so copilot also supports an ORDERED FALLBACK LIST, which our schema has no way to express today and which is a genuinely useful reliability primitive for a tier. GitHub's supported-models reference page lists 29 models across 6 vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Moonshot AI, xAI) but publishes DISPLAY NAMES ONLY and gives no canonical config identifier list and no machine-readable endpoint, so the copilot spelling cannot be generated the way models.dev data can and needs a reviewed hand-maintained anchor set per tier with the drift check pinning it. Docs: docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models and docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration and code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/custom-agents

EMPIRICAL VALIDATION 2026-07-31, owner-suggested method, run live against copilot CLI 1.0.75. Method: write .github/agents/<name>.agent.md files declaring different model values, then ask the CLI to list agents (the command is /agent, singular - /agents is not it). Probed three values in one dispatch, deliberately including a known-bad one so a clean result could not be vacuous. Results: 'Claude Haiku 4.5' -> VALID, and the CLI named the canonical id as claude-haiku-4.5 WITH A DOT; 'claude-haiku-4-5' (the Anthropic hyphenated spelling) -> NOT a known id, flagged explicitly as needing a dot; 'Claude Haiku 9.9 Nonexistent' -> no such model. So copilot accepts BOTH the display name and the dotted id, and REJECTS the hyphenated Anthropic form. This is direct empirical confirmation of basicly-kjc5.58's founding premise and it agrees with models.dev, which also spells the copilot serving id claude-haiku-4.5. Consequence for this bead: the per-surface spelling column is required, and for copilot the dotted models.dev serving id is usable directly, so the copilot column CAN be generated from models.dev after all rather than hand-maintained - the display name is a second accepted alias, not the only accepted form. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the verdict above was produced by the model after it read the files with shell commands, not by a deterministic CLI validator, so under this repo's own rule (deterministic checks block, judged checks advise) this method ADVISES and must never be the sole gate. A deterministic equivalent still needs either a real validator flag or a machine-readable model list, and GitHub's supported-models page publishes display names only with no such endpoint. Cost of the probe: 24.3 AI credits, 80.6k input (49.9k cached, 28.2k cache-write) and 1.1k output including 404 reasoning tokens.

PREMISE CORRECTION 2026-07-31 - measured against the live endpoint before implementing, and the bead's stated mechanism does not exist. This description says models.dev carries 'decisively - a base_model field linking a provider serving id to the underlying model'. It does not. Fetched https://models.dev/api.json (HTTP 200, 3331578 bytes, 176 providers, 5911 model records) and base_model is present on ZERO of 5911 records; it is not in the record schema at all. The actual per-record fields are attachment cost description family id knowledge last_updated limit modalities name open_weights reasoning reasoning_options release_date structured_output temperature tool_call. Either the field was removed since 2026-07-29 or it was never there. WHAT TO JOIN ON INSTEAD: 'name' is identical across providers for all four anchors, corroborated by 'family'. Measured: low anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 vs copilot claude-haiku-4.5 - ids DIFFER, family claude-haiku on both, name 'Claude Haiku 4.5 (latest)' on both; medium claude-sonnet-5 both; high claude-opus-5 both; maximum claude-fable-5 both. So join on exact 'name' (handling the '(latest)' suffix) with 'family' plus cost plus limit as corroboration, not on base_model. SECOND MEASURED FINDING that shrinks the work: only the LOW anchor's id actually diverges between anthropic and github-copilot - the other three are byte-identical, because only haiku carries a minor version and copilot spells a minor version with a dot where anthropic uses a hyphen. That is exactly basicly-kjc5.58's 'they coincide only on the -5 generation' claim, now measured. The map is therefore small today, but the mechanism is still required: the next model with a minor version diverges again. THIRD: the per-family serving limit the description predicted is real and only on the copilot side - github-copilot records carry limit.input (haiku-4.5 136000, opus-4.5 168000, opus-5 936000) which anthropic records do not, and note copilot claude-sonnet-5 has NO limit.input, so the generator must treat it as optional rather than assuming every copilot record has one.

payload.description:
## Problem

A session with no grant has **no spend ceiling of any kind**, and now that the supervisor can seed
its own lanes it will happily dispatch metered agents under exactly that condition.

Both halves of D3's ceiling are keyed on the grant. `policy.spend_status` returns
`halted=False` outright when `grant is None or grant.token_budget is None`, and
`SpendStatus.remaining_tokens` returns `None` for the same case, which makes
`policy.check_pass_spend` return `None` — admitted. So an ungranted `basicly loop supervise <root>`
passes both the retrospective and the forward gate unconditionally and dispatches up to
`[worktree] concurrency` headless agents with no bound.

This was latent while `loop supervise` could not start work on a cold root: an operator had to
provision lanes by hand, which meant they were already deciding to spend. basicly-t73d removed that
step, so the hazard is now one command deep — and `[runner] default` is no longer `manual`
(basicly-euyt), so that command dispatches real agents. Observed while exercising t73d: with
basicly-jr0l's grant revoked, a supervise pass provisioned three worktrees and would have dispatched
into them; nothing was spent only because the run was interrupted.

The authorization argument matters as much as the arithmetic. A grant is the one human confirm that
authorizes delegated spend. Dispatching a metered runner with no grant spends money that nobody
approved and that no ceiling bounds.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run basicly policy grant <root> --revoke
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import policy
s = policy.spend_status(Path('.'), '<root>')
print('grant', s.grant, 'halted', s.halted, 'remaining', s.remaining_tokens)
print('forward verdict:', policy.check_pass_spend(10**9, s))
"
```

Observed - `grant None halted False remaining None`, and the forward verdict is `None` for a
forecast of a billion tokens, i.e. admitted. A supervise pass on that root then provisions and
dispatches.

Expected - a **metered** dispatch requires a covering grant with a token budget; without one the
pass refuses and says so, and the refusal is surfaced the way the other spend refusals are. A
handoff runner is unaffected, because it spends nothing.

## Scope

- src/basicly/supervise.py
- src/basicly/policy.py
- tests/test_supervise.py
- tests/test_policy.py

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a session whose root carries no grant with a token budget when a supervised pass would
  dispatch a metered headless runner then it dispatches nothing and reports that a covering grant is
  required, while a handoff runner still proceeds because it spends nothing
payload.title: A session with no grant has no spend ceiling yet still dispatches metered agents

payload.description:
## Context

Root cause of the only CI red this session (run 30168113819, macos-latest, three tests): the StallWatchdog tests asserted a timing outcome after a fixed time.sleep, so passing depended on how fast the host scheduled a background thread. Green on ubuntu and windows, red on macos. The failure did not reproduce locally even under twelve CPU spinners, so the constant could not have been tuned with any confidence - the shape of the test was wrong, not the number in it.

The test-discipline skill already carries two sections paid for by earlier sessions (Set up the condition the code actually reads, and A seam is not duplication). It has nothing about timing.

Proposed section, authored as a general rule with no Python or basicly specifics: 'Wait for the condition, not for a duration.' A test that sleeps then asserts encodes an assumption about host speed, and the assumption is invisible until the slowest runner in the matrix disagrees. Poll the condition with a generous timeout instead, so the test asserts what it means (the thing happened) rather than when it happened. Pair it with the prohibition's alternative: if the assertion really is about elapsed time, measure it with a monotonic clock and assert a bound, never a sleep-then-check. Include the corollary that a fixed sleep long enough for the slowest CI runner is far too slow for a laptop suite, so tuning the constant trades one failure mode for another.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the test-discipline skill when it is projected then it carries a section teaching wait-for-the-condition over fixed sleeps with the monotonic-bound alternative, authored as a general rule with no language-specific or repo-specific detail, and the catalog lint and skills-check gates pass
payload.title: Teach the wait-for-the-condition rule in the test-discipline skill

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a source that fails load-time validation when the error is rendered on a user-facing surface then the path is shown relative to the repo root and matches the style catalog_lint already emits for the same finding, and given a source outside the repo root then an absolute path is still shown rather than a misleading relative one, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 by the basicly-axqe lane and measured 2026-08-01 before filing.

`schema.ValidationError.__str__` renders `f"{self.path}: {self.message}"`, and every call site
passes an absolute path. So a load-time validation failure prints a machine-specific absolute path
on a user-facing surface, while `catalog_lint`'s own violations print a repo-relative one.

## Measured

Both lines below come from ONE `basicly catalog lint` run over a scratch consumer repo, with the
same bad value (`technologies: [notatechnology]`) placed in an overlay source and in a core source.
The first line is the load-time `ValidationError`, the second is `_check_technology_vocabulary`:

    <abs>/consumer-probe-1/.basicly/core/agents/test-runner/agent.yaml: unknown technologies: ...
    .basicly/core/agents/test-runner/agent.yaml: unknown technologies: ...

Same finding, same run, two path styles - so the inconsistency is visible to a single reader, and
the absolute form is the one that leaks a home directory or a username into anything pasted into an
issue or a CI log. The repo rule is that no user- or machine-specific path is ever emitted, and
there is a `tracker-path-scan` hook enforcing the same principle for the tracker export; nothing
enforces it for lint output.

## Not in scope

The same probe measured the OTHER asymmetry the axqe lane reported - that
`_check_technology_vocabulary` is core-only for agent sources. That is NOT a defect: an overlay
source with a bad technology value is already rejected (rc=1) by `schema.validate_technologies` at
load time. The core-only walk is redundant on that axis, which is exactly why the core case reports
the finding twice and the overlay case once. No bead is owed for it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/schema.py`
- `tests/test_schema.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Session retro (basicly-kjc5.9). A commit run from a loop worktree with `git -c core.hooksPath=.git/hooks commit` passed with no hook output: a linked worktree has `.git` as a *file*, so the relative path resolves to a directory that does not exist and git skips every hook silently - pre-commit, commit-msg, and the beads gate all bypassed without a word. The next amend without the override caught a subject the gate rejects, proving the first commit had been ungated.

Root cause: nothing in the harness prose says the shared hooks dir is already wired by provisioning and must not be overridden. The worktree-isolation skill documents hook provisioning but not this failure mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the worktree-isolation skill when an agent commits from a loop worktree then the skill states that hooks are already wired to the shared dir and that overriding core.hooksPath there silently disables every gate with the projection gates green

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/worktree-isolation/**`

payload.description:
## Context

Raised by the owner 2026-07-31: they read that `AGENTS.md` is larger because everything must be
inlined for codex, and challenged it, citing OpenAI's official documentation for the view that codex
does not support commands / rules / instructions as separate files.

Verified against the live OpenAI docs (`learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*`) on 2026-07-31. **The projection's
behaviour is correct and needs no change. The docs describing why are wrong in two places, and the
owner was reading those.**

### What is actually true

Codex has **no glob- or pattern-based instruction scoping** — no `applyTo`, no `paths:` frontmatter,
no `globs` field, in `AGENTS.md` discovery, the config reference, `SKILL.md` frontmatter, or the
customization overview. Directory placement is the only scoping axis. Codex *does* support separate
instruction files (nested `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `project_doc_fallback_filenames`),
repo-checked-in skills at `.agents/skills/`, project subagents at `.codex/agents/*.toml`, and project
sandbox rules at `.codex/rules/`. So the mechanism our inlining rests on is the **glob-vs-directory
type mismatch**, exactly as §7.4 says — not any absence of separate files.

### The defects to fix

1. **Two surviving lines assert the rationale that `2d04834` (basicly-joj, 2026-07-15) retired**, and
   they contradict `docs/architecture/architecture.md:653-666` in the same file:
   - `docs/architecture/architecture.md:496` — "inlines scoped fragments (codex can't path-scope)"
   - `docs/architecture/architecture.md:507` — "scoped fragments inlined because it has no
     path-scoping mechanism"
2. **A stronger justification is unrecorded.** Nested `AGENTS.md` is loaded only along the path from
   project root **down to the cwd** — "Codex stops searching once it reaches your current directory".
   A file at `src/foo/AGENTS.md` is therefore **not loaded at all** when codex runs from the repo
   root. Per-directory offload would not merely lose glob fidelity; in the normal case it would not
   load. This strengthens the `[Deferred]` §11.3 offload decision and should be recorded next to it.
   (Exception worth noting: codex code review on GitHub does walk changed files, so that surface
   behaves differently from the CLI.)
3. **Stale cap figure.** `architecture.md:625` says a "shared soft cap of 8,000 chars" and
   `.basicly/core/targets/codex.yaml:4` says "Higher than claude/copilot (8000)", but both YAMLs set
   **9000** (raised in `e70e4db`, basicly-c5to). Also stale in `docs/archive/foundry-spike.md:307,343`.
4. **Stale doc URLs.** `developers.openai.com/codex/*` now 308-redirects to `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*`
   and page paths moved (`/codex/guides/agents-md` -> `/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md`). Any
   citation of the old path still resolves but is stale. `project_doc_max_bytes` is still 32 KiB and
   is configurable.
5. **Corrected measurements** (the cap counts characters via `len(content)` at `cli.py:311-317`; the
   figures previously carried were bytes):

   | Surface | chars | cap | headroom |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `AGENTS.md` | 10775 | 12000 | 1225 |
   | `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | 7894 | 9000 | 1106 |
   | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | 8026 | 9000 | 974 |

   A scoped fragment costs **~1500 chars (measured 1462 and 1614)**, to `AGENTS.md` only — not the
   "~1600" carried before. So: **copilot is tightest by absolute headroom**; `AGENTS.md` is the
   binding constraint **for the path-scoped tier specifically**, and the **next** scoped fragment
   already overflows its cap (1225 < ~1500) rather than "two more" as previously recorded. Correct
   this wherever it appears, including `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md:143`.
6. **Record the naming collision.** Codex's own "Rules" feature is a sandbox command-execution policy
   (`.codex/rules/`, Starlark `prefix_rule(pattern=...)`), unrelated to per-file instructions. Reading
   that page and concluding codex has no instruction rules is the exact trap the owner hit, so the
   distinction is worth one line wherever we describe the codex surface.
7. **Note that file-based custom prompts are deprecated** in favour of skills and are user-scope only
   (`~/.codex/prompts`), so they cannot ship in a repo — relevant if a codex command tier is ever
   proposed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `docs/architecture/architecture.md:496` and `:507`.
2. Read `:653-666` of the same file.
3. Observed: `:496`/`:507` say codex has no path-scoping mechanism, while `:653-666` documents that it
   does (root->leaf concat, nearest wins, `AGENTS.override.md`). The authoritative doc contradicts
   itself, and a reader acting on §4.4 reaches a conclusion the repo retired on 2026-07-15. Expected:
   one consistent rationale — the glob-vs-directory mismatch, plus the root->cwd loading limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the architecture doc and the catalog when the codex steering surface is described then the rationale is the glob-vs-directory mismatch plus the root-to-cwd loading limit with no surviving claim that codex cannot path-scope, the cap figure reads 9000 everywhere, the surface table gives characters not bytes with copilot as the tightest always-on surface, and the per-scoped-fragment cost reads about 1500 with the next fragment overflowing AGENTS.md
payload.title: Correct the superseded codex path-scoping rationale and the stale surface figures

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a dispatch whose recorded spend reaches the session grant ceiling mid-run when the next usage event arrives then the dispatch is stopped on the spend bound rather than running to the wall clock and given a dispatch emitting no events for the configured quiet bound then it is stopped as a runaway and given a lane that is emitting events and inside its budget then it runs past the former 1800s wall clock without being killed and the wall clock remains only as a backstop at a value it does not reach in normal operation with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Split out of `basicly-yvx9` on 2026-08-06 because that bead's acceptance criterion bundled an
independent, cheap fix with this one, which is blocked. `yvx9` keeps the half that needs nothing
new - preserving a killed lane's work - and can ship immediately. This is the structural half.

`yvx9` establishes the defect: terminal authority sits on the one signal that carries no
information about whether work is happening.

| | measures | knows if work is happening | power |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `runner_timeout` = 1800s | wall clock since spawn | **no** | **hard kill** |
| `StallWatchdog`, `stall_after` = 900s | commits + dirty tree | yes, partially | flag only |

Measured consequence: the longest *successful* lane ran 1712s, **95.1%** of the cap, and 10 of 68
successes finished past 80% of it. The ceiling sits inside the upper tail of legitimate work.

## Blocked on basicly-rupz, and rupz changes the answer

The obvious fix - make the idle bound terminal - cannot be done with today's probe.
`lane_activity` (supervise.py:2136) hashes `git rev-parse HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain`, so a
lane running a long test suite, or thinking, writes nothing and reads as **idle**. Making that
terminal at 900s would kill a lane running this repo's own gate set. It would trade one wrong kill
for another.

`basicly-rupz` removes that blocker: every metered adapter already emits a per-turn JSONL event
stream that the harness requests, pays for and discards. An event is proof of life whether or not a
file changed.

**And rupz changes what the right bound is, so do not simply implement the idle kill this bead was
first framed as.** Per-turn usage means the D3 spend ceiling can bind *during* a dispatch instead of
only at pass boundaries. Tokens accrue monotonically and are the resource that actually matters,
so a spend bound is strictly better than any clock. The cost of not having it is on the record: a
20,000,000-token grant on `basicly-vhft` overshot to 22,164,783 on 2026-08-06, because
`spend_status` is consulted before a pass and recorded after, with nothing in between.

## What the wall clock becomes

Not removed - **demoted**. A runaway agent looping edit -> test -> edit -> test on one file is
maximally active by every liveness measure; streaming makes it visible without bounding it. So a
terminal bound must remain, and after this bead it is spend plus no-events, with the wall clock
left as a last-resort backstop for the pathological case: a process that hangs holding the pipe, or
a stream that stops while the process does not exit. Set it where it never fires in normal
operation - the 3600s default it was lowered from, or higher.

Do **not** raise `runner_timeout` alone and call this done. That moves the cliff one tail-length out
and weakens the only runaway bound in the process, which is the trap `basicly-vz78`'s missing
forward forecast left behind.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run python -c "
import json, statistics
d=json.load(open('.basicly/usage/run-records.json'))
ok=[r['duration_s'] for rs in d.values() for r in rs
    if r.get('agent')=='claude' and r.get('outcome')=='executed' and r.get('duration_s')]
print('n', len(ok), 'max', round(max(ok)), 'pct of 1800:', round(max(ok)/1800*100,1))
print('above 80% of cap:', sum(1 for x in ok if x>1440))"
```

Reports the successful-lane tail sitting at 95% of the terminal bound.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
payload.title: Retire the wall clock as a lane's working bound once the event stream can replace it

payload.description:
From basicly-u0zg.2 (closed infeasible). GitHub Copilot CLI has NO config-file deny mechanism (deny is --deny-tool CLI-flag-only, session-scoped, never persisted; permissions-config.json stores allows only; github/copilot-cli#2398 unshipped). So the baseline deny-list cannot be projected as managed catalog output for copilot. The only enforcement is invocation-time: extend the copilot runner command template to inject --deny-tool flags derived from permissions.yaml. Belongs at the runner seam (overlaps basicly-45ld). Render-testable via runner dry-run.

Verified 2026-07-18 against copilot CLI v1.0.70: --deny-tool[=tools...] takes copilot-native tool specs and matches shell commands by PREFIX, e.g. --deny-tool='shell(git push --force)' (does not block plain 'git push'); tool names like 'write'. No infix wildcards, so the fine-grained claude glob deny-list maps only PARTIALLY - a documented best-effort projection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- permissions.yaml deny rules gain an optional copilot field of copilot-native --deny-tool specs, authored only for rules copilot can meaningfully express (destructive-rm, force-push, bypass-gates, destructive-git); rules with no faithful copilot form (env-read/env-edit) are omitted with a comment.
- permissions.py exposes the flat de-duplicated copilot deny specs (mirroring claude_deny_patterns).
- The copilot runner command injects one --deny-tool=<spec> per spec, placed after the binary and before -p, populated from the repo permissions.yaml at runner-config load.
- runner dry-run --runner copilot renders the exact argv including the --deny-tool flags; a non-copilot runner is unchanged.
- The prefix-match limitation (variants/flag-reordering not all caught; env rules omitted) is documented where the mapping is authored.
- Deterministic tests cover the spec loader, format_command injection, and the dry-run surface.
payload.title: Guardrails: inject --deny-tool flags on the copilot runner (invocation-time deny)

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a multi lane pass whose lanes each regenerate a shared generated artifact when a landing rebase conflicts only on paths the config declares generated then the merge queue regenerates and continues without spending rework and given a conflict touching any undeclared path then it still bounces to the lane
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-06, landing three lanes from the `basicly-u6jq.1` proof run.
`basicly-l7zo`, `basicly-5xcj` and `basicly-sco6` each edit a different catalog
source - the worktree-isolation skill, the fragments, the python skill - so their
declared scopes are disjoint. Each edit regenerates `.basicly/generated-manifest.json`.

Observed - the first two landed; the third could not:

```
[escalated] build -> build: merge failed: rebase of harness/basicly-sco6 onto main
            hit conflicts in: .basicly/generated-manifest.json (rework 2/2)
```

Expected - a pass whose lanes edit different catalog sources does not serialise on the
artifact those edits generate.

## Cause: o8p0's defect class, second variety

`basicly-o8p0` fixed the **append-only** case: `CHANGELOG.md` is written by every lane,
declared by none, and now carried in `[worktree] append_only_paths` so the grouping
contends on it and `preflight` warns. `.basicly/generated-manifest.json` collides the
same way and for the same reason - every lane touches it, no bead declares it - but it
is a **generated artifact**, so the two remedies o8p0 offers are both wrong for it:

- **Serialising** the lanes is unnecessary. The conflict is not semantic; the file is a
  pure function of the tree.
- **Giving one lane the entry** is meaningless. Every lane's edit legitimately changes it.
- **Union merge** would corrupt it outright - it is JSON, not a line-oriented log.

The correct resolution is **regenerate after merge**, which is what unblocked this lane:
`skills-build --all-default-roots` then `build`, so the artifact matches the merged tree
rather than either parent. Picking a side would have left a manifest describing neither.

## Fix shape

- A `[worktree] generated_paths` list (sibling to `append_only_paths`, same authoring
  home) naming artifacts the engine can rebuild. On a rebase conflict confined to those
  paths, the merge queue **regenerates and continues** instead of bouncing to the lane.
  Bounded deliberately: it applies only when every conflicting path is in the list, so a
  genuine source conflict still bounces.
- `preflight` reports it beside the `contend:` line, since the operator can otherwise
  only discover it at the merge queue.

The regeneration command already exists and is already gated - `projection-check` and the
four `projection-*` checks fail when a projected artifact is stale - so a wrong
regeneration cannot pass silently.

## Why this is not just o8p0 again

o8p0's `append_only_paths` is a *contention* declaration: those paths make lanes
serialise. This class wants the opposite treatment - the lanes need not serialise at all,
the artifact simply needs rebuilding once. Folding generated files into
`append_only_paths` would impose a serial chain on every catalog pass for no reason, which
is a throughput cost with no correctness gain.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`
payload.title: A generated shared artifact conflicts every multi lane pass and no bead declares it

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a shell command that wraps the real tool behind a wrapper token and its flags when the tool-usage hook records it then the credited head is the invoked tool rather than a flag value or the wrapper subcommand, and given a shell keyword or a function defined in the same command then it is not counted as a tool, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Found by the 2026-07-31 session retro while reading `basicly usage report`. The report's Terminal
tools table counts things that are not tools, which undermines its own stated purpose - the skill
uses it to name never-used catalog skills as culling candidates, so noise there can drive a real
culling decision.

**Not a heredoc bug.** `.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py` already tracks heredoc bodies and quote
state (basicly-zcvo). The heredoc-shaped entries (`def` 90, `assert` 83, `PYEOF` 33, `EOF` 28,
`return` 31) all carry `last used` dates of 2026-07-16/17 - they are pre-fix residue, and because
the counter file accumulates by design and is never reset, that residue never ages out.

The live defect is wrapper resolution. Measured on entries last used 2026-07-31 that are not on PATH:

- **Worktree names, 49 counts across 7 entries**: `basicly-kjc5-61` 36, `basicly-jr0l-37` 8,
  `basicly-sy8c` 3, `basicly-2rn9` 1, `basicly-qvd2` 1, `basicly-jr0l-38` 1, `basicly-jr0l-50` 1.
  These come from `uv run --directory <abs-path> <cmd>`: `uv` is in `WRAPPER_TOKENS`, so it unwraps,
  but the flag and its value are not skipped, so the path lands as the head instead of `<cmd>`.
- **`run` 64** - the `uv` subcommand itself surviving as a head rather than resolving to the command
  after it.
- **Shell keywords and functions**: `continue` 9, `break` 6, `write_src` 3 (a function defined and
  called in the same script).

So a session that runs its work through `uv run --directory <worktree>` - which is exactly what this
repo's own multi-lane pattern does - pollutes the table with one entry per worktree, and the real
tool it invoked is never credited.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run `uv run --directory /path/to/some-dir pytest -q` and then `basicly usage report`.
- Observed: the directory basename is counted as a terminal tool and `pytest` is not credited.
  Expected: `pytest` is credited and the path is not counted.
- Also run a script that defines and calls a shell function, and one containing `continue` or
  `break` inside a loop; observe each counted as a tool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a shell command that wraps the real tool behind a wrapper token and its flags when the
  tool-usage hook records it then the credited head is the invoked tool rather than a flag value or
  the wrapper subcommand, and given a shell keyword or a function defined in the same command then it
  is not counted as a tool, with tests
payload.title: Resolve a wrapped command past its flags so usage counts the real tool

payload.description:
## Context

Split out of basicly-m4zv.13 by owner decision 2026-07-31. That bead delivers the *mechanism*: a phase
may declare a required evidence artifact, and the advance is refused unless the declared path exists and
is non-empty (presence only — the engine never parses it).

It deliberately does not supply a producer, and today there is none. `verify.py` streams each check's
output straight to the terminal uncaptured (that is intentional, so a consumer sees tool output live),
and `rerun_failures(..., capture=True)` captures only on the failure re-run path. So on a **passing**
run nothing is written anywhere, and declaring an evidence artifact for the verify phase would refuse
every advance.

This bead gives verify something to point at, which is what lets this repo dogfood the gate by
declaring it in its own `basicly.toml`.

Design constraints inherited from m4zv.13:

- The engine gates on **presence only**; the producer owns the content. Do not add parsing.
- Live terminal output must not regress — a consumer watching a run still sees each tool's own output.
- Deterministic: no model involvement, no judged content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a passing verify run when it completes then a non-empty run artifact exists at a stable declared path and the live terminal output of each check is unchanged, so the evidence gate from basicly-m4zv.13 can be declared for the verify phase in this repo and passes

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
payload.title: Have verify produce a run artifact the evidence gate can point at

payload.description:
## Context

Cuts the first release since v0.5.1 (2026-07-20). 535 commits are unreleased - 42 feat and 39
fix - including the whole parallel factory: the supervisor, concurrent lanes, the merge queue,
the decision queue, L0-L3 autonomy grants with a spend ceiling, `basicly commit`,
`basicly release`, the invocation axis, the path-scoped rules tier, the recall eval and the
tracker usage ledger.

Version is 0.6.0: the owner ruled in basicly-m4zv.9 that requiring `invocation` on every skill
source is breaking, and a breaking change at 0.x is a minor bump. The tier work adds a second
breaking catalog-schema change by removing `model` from the agent schema.

Driven through the harness as a consumer would - `basicly loop` for the work,
`basicly release 0.6.0 --issue <this bead>` for the cut - so the release doubles as a dogfood
run. Awkwardness in the harness is a finding to file, never something to route around.

Two release-quality obligations that no gate covers:

- **The breaking-change audit.** Zero commits in the 535 carry a `!` marker or a
  BREAKING CHANGE footer, yet at least two breaking changes exist. The marker discipline did
  not hold, so grep cannot answer the question; the audit means reading the 42 feat and 39 fix
  subjects against the consumer-facing surfaces - catalog schema, projected output paths, CLI
  flags and their semantics, hook contracts, and `basicly.toml` keys.
- **Changelog curation.** `## [Unreleased]` holds exactly one entry against 81 feat and fix
  commits.

Also verify after tagging that the README roadmap's `✓ shipped` rows are true again - it
defines shipped as "running code in the current release", and about seven rows currently
describe code that exists only on main.

## Success Criteria

- Every blocking bead closed, the breaking-change audit written up with each break named or
  the audit recorded as finding none, `CHANGELOG.md` curated for v0.6.0, the annotated tag
  created by `basicly release`, both pushes done with explicit owner approval, and the GitHub
  release verified as published

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the blocking beads are closed and the changelog is curated when `basicly release
  0.6.0 --issue` this bead runs then it bumps the single-sourced version regenerates the
  version-stamped projections rewrites the pinned references creates the annotated tag and
  pushes nothing, and given the pushes are then approved and run then the GitHub release is
  published and `basicly status` on a fresh consumer clone reports the new version
payload.title: Release v0-6-0

payload.text: [harness-policy] grant level=L3 budget=25000000

[harness-policy] RELEASE SCOPE NARROWED 2026-07-30 by owner decision: cut the release first, do only what is most critical for it. Seventeen blocking edges were removed so this epic can advance; every one of those beads stays OPEN and is deferred past the release rather than dropped.

KEPT AS BLOCKERS (2):
- basicly-jr0l.38 - the codex adapter pins approval=on-failure, which is not in codex-cli's enum (untrusted, on-request, never), so every codex dispatch fails at argument parsing. Together with the closed jr0l.36 stdin hang this means the codex adapter has NEVER completed a dispatch. Release-critical because agent-agnostic dispatch across claude, codex and copilot is an advertised capability that a consumer will exercise immediately.
- basicly-jr0l.39 - the ship phase name reads as release and invites approving the wrong checkpoint. Cheap to fix and safety-relevant: the recorded incident is approving ship before the landing printed merged, which wedges an unmerged node with no un-approve. The owner misread the name; a consumer has strictly less context.

PLUS the two obligations already in this epic's description, which are the substance of the release and are not separate beads: the breaking-change audit of the 535 unreleased commits (zero carry a ! marker or a BREAKING CHANGE footer, so grep cannot answer it - it means reading the feat and fix subjects against the consumer-facing surfaces: catalog schema, projected output paths, CLI flags and semantics, hook contracts, basicly.toml keys), and curating CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

DEFERRED PAST THE RELEASE (17): jr0l.35, jr0l.40, 2rn9, kjc5.60, u6jq.1, l7zo, z25w, imnu.2, imnu.3, jr0l.32, jr0l.33, kvx5, sco6, g7os, jr0l.30, jr0l.31, kjc5.37. Rationale by group - internal telemetry and forecast work no consumer sees (2rn9, kjc5.60, jr0l.35, jr0l.40); u6jq.1 is blocked on the forecast chain and its last proof run cost 34 dollars for 46M tokens, so it is neither cheap nor available; the rest are catalog content, skill wording and the docs tutorial layer, which improve guidance but leave no consumer broken.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a user-invoked catalog entry when it is projected for an agent family whose loader requires a description then the emitted file loads without error on that family, and given the family cannot represent a user-invoked entry at all then no file is emitted for it rather than an unloadable one, and a check fails when a projected skill would not load, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-29 by running a freshly installed codex CLI against this repo's own projected
skills. Codex refuses to load three of them:

    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md: missing field `description`
    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-fzf/SKILL.md: missing field `description`
    failed to load skill .agents/skills/tool-git-delta/SKILL.md: missing field `description`

This is a regression inside the unreleased set, not a pre-existing wart. At v0.5.1
`tool-bat/SKILL.md` carried a description; on main it does not, because basicly-m4zv.1 makes
a user-invoked entry project no `description` line. Claude tolerates the omission - that
tolerance is what basicly-m4zv.7 had to fix when the generated marker leaked into the
description slot - but codex treats description as required and hard-errors, so the skill
simply does not exist for a codex consumer.

The design tension is real rather than a coding slip. The invocation axis says a user-invoked
entry carries no description because nothing can route to it, so a description is context
load bought for no reach. Codex's loader makes "user-invoked" unrepresentable: an entry either
carries a description or fails to load. This is the same shape as the model-id problem - a
portable catalog concept one family cannot express - and it wants the same kind of answer, a
per-family projection rule rather than a change to the portable concept.

Two candidate stances, to be decided in the work: project a description for user-invoked
entries on families whose loader requires one, or omit the entry entirely for those families
rather than emitting a file that cannot load. Silently shipping an unloadable file is the one
option to rule out.

Blocks the release: v0.6.0 would otherwise ship a change that removes three skills from every
codex consumer without saying so.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run any codex command in this repo, e.g. `codex exec --json -s read-only "reply with
  exactly: ok" < /dev/null`, and read stderr.
- Observed: three `failed to load skill ... missing field description` errors for the
  user-invoked skills tool-bat, tool-fzf and tool-git-delta.
- Compare `git show v0.5.1:.agents/skills/tool-bat/SKILL.md` (has a description) against the
  file on main (has none).
- Expected: every projected skill loads on every agent family the projection targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user-invoked catalog entry when it is projected for an agent family whose loader
  requires a description then the emitted file loads without error on that family, and given
  the family cannot represent a user-invoked entry at all then no file is emitted for it
  rather than an unloadable one, and a check fails when a projected skill would not load,
  with tests
payload.title: User-invoked skills fail to load on codex because they carry no description

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-30 while verifying a competitive claim from the `oh-my-agent` analysis
(`reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md`), and it turns out to be a hole in our own gate.

The repo's positioning - now in `README.md`, `site/index.html` and the GitHub About - claims
enforcement at **commit time** as the thing that distinguishes us from a projector whose drift
check is CI-only. On the specific axis of *projection staleness* that claim is currently false.

What actually runs locally:

- `protect-generated-commit` compares each **staged generated blob** against the hash in
  `generated-manifest.json`. Its docstring is precise about the case it covers: a hand-edit that
  skips the rebuild. It cannot see a stale projection, because a fragment edit does not stage the
  generated file at all - the output on disk still matches the manifest.
- `pre-commit-script` runs `[[verify.checks]]` mode `fast`: ruff, ruff-format, pyright, bandit,
  lint-imports.
- `pre-push-script` runs mode `full`: the above plus pytest.

`basicly check` appears in **none** of them. Nor do `skills-check`, `agents-check` or
`hooks-check`. They run in one CI job. `tests/test_docs_drift.py` is docs-to-code drift, not
projection drift, so pytest at pre-push does not cover it either.

So: edit a fragment, never rebuild, commit, push. Nothing local objects. The projection is stale
in the tree and on the remote until CI says so - which is exactly the posture we describe as the
competitor's weakness.

The fix is to add the four projection gates to the locally-run verify modes. They are the gates
`CLAUDE.md` already names as the projection gates, so this is wiring an existing check into the
stage that was supposed to run it, not new enforcement.

Open question this bead must settle rather than assume: whether they belong in `fast` (every
commit) or only `full` (pre-push). `fast` is the stronger guarantee and matches the published
claim; the cost is four extra subprocesses on every commit, and `skills-check
--all-default-roots` is the slowest of them. Measure before choosing, and if the answer is `full`,
then the published wording must say pre-push rather than commit time - correcting the claim is an
acceptable outcome of this bead, silently leaving it overstated is not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Edit any fragment body under `.basicly/core/fragments/`.
2. Do not run `basicly build`.
3. `git add` the fragment and commit, then push.
4. Observed: every hook passes; the generated instruction files are stale in the tree and on the
   remote, and only CI reports it. Expected: a local gate refuses the commit or the push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a fragment edited without a rebuild when the local git hooks run then a projection gate fails before the change can reach the remote, and the positioning wording in README site and repo About names the stage that actually enforces it
payload.title: No local gate catches a stale projection so the commit-time claim is overstated

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a catalog whose target output path is absolute or escapes the repo root or a fragment id containing a path separator or traversal sequence when the projection is planned then the build refuses with a diagnostic naming the field and the offending value and every planned output path is asserted to resolve inside the repo root
payload.description:
## Context

Surfaced by the 2026-07-30 `oh-my-agent` analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/oh-my-agent.md`) and
confirmed against our source and against pathlib's actual behaviour.

`planner.py` builds every projection output path by joining catalog-supplied strings onto the repo
root, with no containment check:

- `output_path=repo_root / output.path` (`src/basicly/planner.py:31`)
- `output_path = repo_root / output.path_template.format(fragment_id=fragment.id)`
  (`src/basicly/planner.py:39`)

Neither input is constrained. A schema audit found `pattern` on exactly two fields in the whole
catalog - `block.schema.json` `.properties.id` and `agent.schema.json` `.properties.name` - so a
fragment `id` and a target `path`/`path_template` are free-form strings.

Two distinct escapes, and the first is the nastier because it is silent:

1. **An absolute `path` replaces the root outright.** `Path('<redacted:posix-home-path>') / '/etc/passwd'` is
   `/etc/passwd` - pathlib discards the left operand. There is no traversal sequence to spot in a
   review; the string just looks like a path.
2. **A traversal sequence escapes upward.** `repo_root / '../../etc/passwd'` resolves outside the
   repo, and a `fragment_id` containing `../` reaches the same place through the `path_template`
   branch.

## Severity, stated honestly

**Not remote code execution and not a high-severity issue.** The inputs come from the catalog: our
own `.basicly/core/targets/` and the consumer's `.basicly-local/` overlay. Writing them is already
writing to the repo. So the realistic threat is a **third-party or copied overlay** a consumer
installs without auditing, and the realistic damage is `basicly build` writing a generated file
outside the repo - which is exactly the class of uninvited write `tracker_usage.is_enabled` was
already hardened against for a different reason.

It is worth fixing anyway on the repo's own rule - validate external input at trust boundaries -
and because the fix is small and the failure mode is silent. An overlay is a trust boundary the
moment it can come from somewhere else.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In `.basicly-local/`, declare a target output whose `path` is an absolute path outside the repo
   (or a `path_template` plus a fragment whose `id` contains `../`).
2. Run `basicly build`.
3. Observed: the projection writes outside the repo root, and the manifest records it. Expected:
   the build refuses the declaration and names the offending field.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a catalog whose target output path is absolute or escapes the repo root, or a fragment id containing a path separator or traversal sequence, when the projection is planned then the build refuses with a diagnostic naming the field and the offending value, and every planned output path is asserted to resolve inside the repo root
payload.title: Refuse a catalog path that escapes the repo root when planning the projection

payload.text: [harness-info] Review evidence 2026-07-30 at 2a0ba60: the escape is worse than filed - the write happens before any check would notice it. cli.py:304 write_if_changed(item.output_path) runs before the relative_to(repo_root) at cli.py:307 that would raise, so a hostile catalog gets one arbitrary file write per output before the crash. The refusal therefore belongs at plan time in planner.py (both join sites, planner.py:31 and :39), not in the render loop.

payload.description:
## Context

From the Archon analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/archon.md`). Its `evidence_policy.required`
plus typed node artifacts refuses terminal success unless a declared evidence file exists on disk -
the engine gating on **presence only**, the workflow producing the content. Their formulation is the
clearest statement of our own split: *"code computes, YAML coordinates"* (`schemas/workflow.ts:105`).

This plugs a hole we have. A lane can reach ship having recorded a passing verify gate with nothing
to point at: the gate records a status, not an artifact. When a landing is later questioned - a
forecast miss, a coupling dispute, a rework argument - the evidence is whatever happened to be
committed, which is exactly the situation the `[harness-*]` marker families were introduced to fix
for cost and decisions but never for verification output.

Presence-only is the important constraint and the reason this is cheap: the engine must not parse or
judge the artifact, only assert it exists and is non-empty, so it adds no nondeterminism and needs no
schema per artifact type. That keeps it on the deterministic side of the rubric contract.

Note the accompanying reject, worth recording next to it: Archon's own completion gate is
`completionDetected = signalDetected || bashComplete` (`dag-executor.ts:4602`), which lets a model's
self-emitted `<promise>DONE</promise>` short-circuit the deterministic check entirely. Adopt the
evidence requirement; reject the disjunction.

Open question this bead must settle: which phases owe an artifact, and whether a missing one blocks
or is recorded. Blocking every phase is likely too strict at first; verify is the phase where the
argument is strongest, because a verify gate with no output is the case that has actually caused
disputes here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a phase that declares a required evidence artifact when the loop attempts to advance past it then the advance is refused unless the declared path exists and is non-empty, the engine never parses or judges the content, and the artifact path is recorded on the bead
payload.title: Require a declared evidence artifact before a phase can report success

payload.text:
Owner decision 2026-07-31 — the open question is settled: **opt-in declaration, blocking where declared.**

- A phase may *declare* a required evidence artifact path. When one is declared, the advance past that
  phase is refused unless the path exists and is non-empty. Presence only — the engine never parses or
  judges the content, so it stays on the deterministic side of the rubric contract.
- Nothing is declared by default, so there is zero behaviour change for existing consumers and the
  change is reversible. Blocking every phase was rejected as too strict; record-only was rejected as
  toothless (it reduces to a log line and would not have prevented the disputes this bead was filed
  about).
- The artifact path is recorded on the bead.

Scope boundary found while deciding: `verify.py` streams check output straight to the terminal and
captures nothing on a passing run, so **no artifact file exists for verify today**. Declaring one
therefore needs a producer. That is deliberately NOT in this bead — it is filed separately, so this
bead delivers the mechanism only and cannot destabilise the landing path before the u6jq.1 proof run.

Archon's own completion gate (`completionDetected = signalDetected || bashComplete`) stays rejected:
adopt the evidence requirement, never the disjunction that lets a self-emitted signal short-circuit it.
