payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a supervisor pass that ranks the ready set when a lane is dispatched then its run marker records the scheduler score and rank and the fallback policy version so the pass ordering is reconstructible from the tracker alone
payload.description:
## Context

D9 requires dispatch inputs to be reproducible and recorded, and dispatch order is one of them. loop_state.ready_ranked passes br scheduler's rank through untouched as the primary ordering key, and nothing records it - so a pass's ordering cannot be reconstructed afterwards.

Research 2026-07-25 corrected an earlier characterisation: the ranking is not opaque. br scheduler emits schema br.scheduler.v1 with a per-item score, a fallback_rank, and an explicit fallback policy of priority ASC then created_at ASC then id ASC, noting that tied or incomplete evidence preserves the fallback rank. It is versioned and explainable, so the cheap fix is to record it rather than to replace it.

Record the score, the rank and the policy schema version into the dispatch marker (basicly-kjc5.28). Note for when we own the tracker: our own ranking must drop created_at, because age-based ordering makes dispatch order clock-dependent for an unchanged graph, which D9 forbids for anything outliving the pass - ordering becomes unblocked-only, then priority, then descending dependent count, then id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a supervisor pass that ranks the ready set when a lane is dispatched then its run marker records the scheduler score and rank and the fallback policy version so the pass ordering is reconstructible from the tracker alone

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
payload.title: Record the scheduler score and rank behind each dispatch

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a repo that discovers work belonging to another repo when it announces an offer in the development exchange then no write reaches the target repo's tracker, and given the target repo polls and pulls the offer then it creates its own bead recording the offer id and appends a claimed event to the exchange so a double pull is detectable
payload.description:
## Context

Settled by the owner 2026-07-25. Several repos are worked at once and work is routinely discovered in the wrong repo - a basicly bug surfaces while working in terminal. The resolution is Kanban pull semantics: announce, never push.

Each repo's ledger has exactly one writer, that repo. The development workspace hosts an exchange - an append-only log of offers rather than assignments. A repo that finds foreign work announces an event naming the target repo; it does not create a bead there. Design work brainstormed in development is decomposed in development and its children announced the same way, so the exchange is the single place work becomes available. Consumers poll at their own cadence, pull by creating a bead in their own tracker recording the offer id as provenance, and append the claim back to the exchange rather than to another tracker.

Event kinds are append-only and total - announced, claimed, declined, superseded - so an offer's state is a fold over its events and history is the audit trail. The design consequence worth preserving: an announcement carries no authority, which is the engine-disposes agents-propose stance applied across repo boundaries, and it is what keeps concurrency trivial since no component ever writes across a repo boundary.

This bead covers the design and the schema in docs/work-tracker.md section 8 plus the exchange format; the commands that announce, poll and pull follow once the format is settled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a repo that discovers work belonging to another repo when it announces an offer in the development exchange then no write reaches the target repo's tracker, and given the target repo polls and pulls the offer then it creates its own bead recording the offer id and appends a claimed event to the exchange so a double pull is detectable

## Scope

- `docs/work-tracker.md`
payload.title: Design the cross-repo work exchange as an append-only offer log

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the committed tracker export when it is scanned then no record carries a machine-specific absolute path or username, and the harness either strips the field on write or fails the secret-scan style gate that catches it
payload.description:
## Context

Found during the work-tracker review 2026-07-25. The committed .beads/issues.jsonl carries source_repo_path on 328 of its 332 records, and the values expose two different users' home directories - /home/<user-a>/development/basicly and /home/<user-b>/Development/basicly - plus a transient worktree path under .claude/worktrees. The file is committed and this repo is distributed to consumers, so the leak is published.

This violates the repo's own hard constraint that no machine or user specific absolute path, username or hostname may ever be committed. It is also a portability defect in its own right: a path that means something on one machine is noise or a wrong answer on another, and a consumer's clone inherits our directory layout as data.

The field is written by br rather than by the harness, so the fix is either to strip it on export, to configure br not to emit it if that is possible, or to add a gate that catches an absolute path in the tracker export the way secret-scan catches a credential. Whichever route, the requirement for our own tracker is recorded in docs/work-tracker.md: a record is path-free, and provenance is the repo identity rather than a filesystem location.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `grep -c "/home/" .beads/issues.jsonl` in a clean checkout.
2. It reports hundreds of matches.
3. Inspect one record with `head -1 .beads/issues.jsonl | jq .source_repo_path` and observe an absolute path containing a username.

Expected: no absolute path or username appears anywhere in the committed export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the committed tracker export when it is scanned then no record carries a machine-specific absolute path or username, and the harness either strips the field on write or fails the secret-scan style gate that catches it

## Scope

- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/`
payload.title: Stop the tracker export from committing machine-specific absolute paths

payload.title: Carry the br defects we already paid for as replacement requirements with a regression test each

payload.text:
[harness-info] Two requirements confirmed by shipping basicly-vkh0.5, 2026-07-26.

1. A record must be path-free. br stamps source_repo_path with the absolute canonical path of the producing workspace, and there is no config knob to suppress it (br config list carries nothing for it). Our replacement records provenance as the repo identity, never a filesystem location. Regression test: tests/test_tracker_path_scan.py.

2. Text already recorded must have a redaction path. This is the new one and it is worse than the field. br comments offers only add and list - no edit, no delete - so a machine path (or anything else) recorded in a comment cannot be removed through the documented CLI at all. Two usernames on closed beads were only fixable by redacting at export time, which means the committed artifact deliberately diverges from the local database. Our replacement needs a first-class redaction event: append-only history is right, but an append-only log with no redaction event cannot honour a deletion requirement.

Both are already enforced for the current tracker by the tracker-path-scan pre-commit gate plus br.scrub_export, so the replacement inherits a committed proof rather than a description.

[harness-info] Requirements input recorded 2026-07-29: the br clock defect (Validation failed: updated_at cannot be before created_at) blocked a lane twice consecutively with a different victim test each run. Tracked for our own resilience as basicly-jr0l.41; the replacement must never branch on a wall-clock comparison, which is the D3 rule the event log already states - a timestamp is evidence and nothing branches on it.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner decision 2026-07-29: raise basicly-vkh0 and target owning the work tracker as the release
after v0.6.0 unless it is blocked, because br is flaky and costs time and money through its own
errors. Twelve distinct br defects we have already paid for are listed on basicly-vkh0.

docs/plan/implementation-plan.md still encodes the old sequencing and now contradicts the
decision in several specific places, so it misleads any session that reads it as the roadmap:

- Section 5 states "Phase 6 is the largest effort but is **not** on this path" and describes it
  as a strategic dependency-removal that can proceed in parallel.
- Section 6 lists Phase 6 under "Defer deliberately, and say so", gated on vkh0.2 having a
  measured surface.
- Section 4's Phase 6 heading carries "Priority: P2, highest effort", which no longer matches
  the epic's P0.
- Section 9's appendix table lists the phase epics without the resequencing.

Also record what changed underneath the deferral: vkh0.1 has landed, so the usage ledger exists
and vkh0.2 (report the surface, then freeze it) is no longer waiting on anything - it has been
moved from deferred to open at P1.

The plan is the durable copy of order and reasons, which is the whole argument for it being a
file rather than living in the tracker, so leaving it stale defeats its purpose. This is a docs
edit only; no engine behaviour changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the implementation plan when it is read after this change then Phase 6 is sequenced as
  the next release after v0.6.0 with the owner's cost rationale stated, no section still
  describes it as deferred or off the critical path, its stated priority matches the epic, and
  the superseded wording is corrected rather than left alongside the new ordering

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given an engine tracker call made with a linked worktree as its repo root when the record is spooled then it lands in the base checkout's spool so teardown cannot discard it and the surface report counts it
payload.description:
## Context

Found immediately after basicly-vkh0.2 landed, by checking a claim that bead's own report
made: the surface report lists `where` as never used, yet `worktree._probe_redirect` calls
`br where --json` on every single worktree provisioning. Three provisionings later the
committed ledger still had zero `where` records.

The cause is that the usage spool does not follow `.beads/redirect` the way every other
tracker path does. `br.run_br` records with the `repo_root` it was handed, which for a lane
is the worktree; `tracker_usage.is_enabled` then sees the worktree's own checked-out
`.basicly/ledger/` directory and returns True, so the record is spooled to
`<worktree>/.basicly/usage/tracker-usage.jsonl`. The loop deletes the worktree at teardown,
taking the spool with it.

So every engine tracker call made from a worktree is silently discarded. That is not a
uniform sampling loss - it is exactly the traffic the harness generates while doing lane
work, and it makes one surface (`where`) read as never-used when the engine depends on it.

This matters because the ledger is the input to the Phase 6 surface freeze. A false
never-used entry is the worst error that artifact can contain: it would omit a surface the
engine calls on every provisioning.

`br.beads_dir` is the precedent to copy - it follows the redirect file to the base
checkout's `.beads`, whose parent is the base checkout.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Provision a loop worktree, which runs `br where --json` against the worktree path.
2. Run `basicly usage tracker --promote` in the base checkout.
3. Observed: no `where` record, and the report names `where` among the never-used surfaces.
   Expected: `where` recorded as an engine surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an engine tracker call made with a linked worktree as its repo root when the record is spooled then it lands in the base checkout's spool so teardown cannot discard it and the surface report counts it
payload.title: Stop a worktree teardown from discarding the tracker usage it recorded

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the work-tracker design when it is read after this change then the event schema carries a running aggregate with the tail-read query and the fold-as-authority both stated truncation records originalLength as the growth bound section 9.5 cites the measured millisecond-collision rate and the rejected sentinel approach is recorded with its reason
payload.description:
## Context

From the hankweave analysis (`reference-repos/_analysis/hankweave.md`), the only append-only journal
in the reviewed set running in production, measured against its own committed 6,467-event fixture.
Two mechanisms it has and `docs/design/work-tracker.md` does not, plus one measurement that turns a
section 9.5 assertion into evidence.

**1. The denormalized running aggregate.** Every event carries the totals that hold *after* it
(`state.transition.data.resultingState`, `event-schemas.ts:429-434`), so the overwhelmingly common
query - what is the current cost or count - is answered by reading the tail rather than folding the
whole log, while the fold stays available as the checkable authority. Section 4 of our design admits
the cost it does not solve ("a fold is O(events) and a naive reader re-folds per query") and section
10 defers the index by measurement. This is the mechanism that makes deferring the index defensible
rather than a hand-wave, and it costs one field.

**2. Honest truncation.** A large payload is stored truncated with `truncated: true` plus
`originalLength` (`event-schemas.ts:259-268`). Section 9.1 declines lossy compaction on the grounds
that it discards evidence git already packs - which stands - but that leaves growth bounded by
nothing. Truncation with a recorded original length bounds it while *saying* that evidence was
dropped and how much, which is a different and better thing than summarising it away.

**3. Evidence for section 9.5, not a change to it.** Their journal has **no sequence numbers** and
mints ids as `Date.now()` plus `Math.random()` (`utils.ts:26-28`). The analysis measured **44.5% of
events in their production fixture sharing a millisecond**, so total order exists only as an
unrecorded side effect of file append order. Our rule that a timestamp is evidence and nothing
branches on it was asserted; it can now cite a number.

Also record the rejection and why: their sentinels are injected LLM calls with a per-million-token
cost model (`sentinels/sentinel.ts:108`, `:502`), so their monitoring is a paid external API -
inadmissible under `basicly-ctdz`, and `StallWatchdog` already covers the condition that matters.

Net finding worth stating plainly in the design: our unbuilt design is more rigorous than their
shipped one, so this is an absorption of three narrow mechanisms, not a redesign.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the work-tracker design when it is read after this change then the event schema carries a running aggregate with the tail-read query and the fold-as-authority both stated, truncation records originalLength as the growth bound, section 9.5 cites the measured millisecond-collision rate, and the rejected sentinel approach is recorded with its reason
payload.title: Absorb the measured journal mechanisms into the work-tracker design

payload.text: [harness-policy] NARROWED 2026-07-30 on a licence finding (references.md 2.3, basicly-imnu.12). hankweave-runtime is stock Apache-2.0 but its NOTICE.md incorporates Southbridge's Terms of Service, whose key provisions include 'Competition restrictions on using Hanks to build competing products' and 'Managed services restrictions require prior written consent'. basicly is a coding-agent harness and hankweave an agent-orchestration runtime, so the restriction plausibly reaches us, and whether a NOTICE can add terms to Apache-2.0 at all is a legal question we are not qualified to answer. WHAT STAYS IN SCOPE: the measurements, because they are properties of published data rather than derived from code - specifically that 44.5 percent of events in their own committed 6467-event fixture share a millisecond while the journal has no sequence numbers, which turns work-tracker 9.5 from an assertion into evidence, and is the single most valuable thing this bead carries. WHAT IS HELD: adopting the running-aggregate and honest-truncation mechanisms with their source as the reference. Those are good ideas and may well be reachable as ideas, but do not implement from their files pending review by someone qualified. If the mechanisms are built, build them from a written description and record the clean-room posture, exactly as 2.1 requires for beads_rust.

[harness-policy] Owner decision 2026-07-30 on the hankweave licence question (references.md 2.3): do NOT pursue a legal review. If their mechanisms are ever wanted, obtain them clean-room from a written description - but the owner's reading, which matches the analysis, is that we already have what we wanted. The measurements are the value and they are already recorded here and in the review: 44.5 percent of events in their own committed 6467-event fixture share a millisecond while the journal carries no sequence numbers, which turns work-tracker 9.5 from an assertion into evidence. Treat hankweave source as permanently off-limits as an implementation reference. This bead's remaining scope is therefore the two mechanisms as CONCEPTS - a running aggregate carried on each event so the tail answers the common query while the fold stays the authority, and truncation that records originalLength rather than summarising - to be designed from first principles here, plus folding the measurement into 9.5.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given one or more lanes are dispatched and still running when the operator watches the supervisor output then each live lane reports its elapsed time and tokens spent so far while it runs rather than only after it finishes and the output stays readable when stdout is a pipe
payload.description:
## Context

A supervised run emits nothing at all between adopting a lane and that lane finishing, so an
operator watching the terminal cannot distinguish healthy work from a wedge. basicly-8veb fixed
the case where the supervisor's own header was swallowed by a pipe; it did not give a running lane
any progress output, because `_print_dispatch` is only reached after `dispatch_lanes` returns.

Measured on the 2026-08-01 single-lane run of basicly-jr0l.40. The log stopped at seven lines,
ending on the `adopted:` line, and stayed there for the whole run. The next line appeared 519.6
seconds later, when the lane had already finished. For 8.7 minutes the only way to tell the run
was alive was `pgrep -af claude` and `git -C <worktree> status`. At the intended multi-lane shape
this is worse, not better: several lanes run concurrently and none of them reports anything.

What a client already has to work with, and why the gap is narrow rather than deep. The dispatch
command is `claude -p <prompt> --output-format stream-json --verbose`, so the adapter is already
consuming an incremental event stream carrying usage as it goes -- it currently reads it for the
final totals only. The run record proves per-lane spend and duration are both available
(`tokens` 4079243, `cost` 3.657368, `duration_s` 519.5625, `occupancy` 106478). The
`harness-client` skill and `loop status` exist for attach-style observation, but neither surfaces
in-flight token spend or elapsed time for a running lane.

Desired shape, per the owner: non-intrusive and cheap, comparable to how a host CLI shows its own
subagents -- one compact line per live lane, updated as it runs, carrying at least elapsed time
and tokens spent so far. It must stay readable when stdout is a pipe or a log file, which is the
constraint that makes a naive cursor-redraw approach wrong (basicly-8veb is the precedent).

Explicitly not a progress bar over an unknown total: with basicly-vz78 open there is no reliable
forecast to divide by, so elapsed-and-spent-so-far is the honest form.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given one or more lanes are dispatched and still running when the operator watches the
  supervisor output then each live lane reports its elapsed time and tokens spent so far while it
  runs rather than only after it finishes, and the output stays readable when stdout is a pipe
payload.title: Show elapsed time and tokens spent for each live lane while it runs

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a ready lane whose description declares no ## Scope when a supervised pass admits it then the pass either refuses it or bounds it without the estimate and the operator is told which lanes carry no forecast before any runner is dispatched
payload.description:
## Problem

Both dispatch cost gates key on `decompose.dispatch_sizing`, which returns `None` for any
bead whose description carries no `## Scope` section. Only decompose-created children record
`## Scope`, so a hand-filed bead is unsizeable — and for such a lane the working-set band gate
(basicly-jr0l.16) and the forward spend-forecast gate (basicly-jr0l.22) both silently admit.

That leaves a supervised pass of hand-filed lanes with no forward cost bound at all. The only
remaining protection is the retrospective grant ceiling, and `dispatch_lanes` reads it once per
pass before starting anything, so N concurrent unsized lanes can overrun the grant's remaining
budget without limit inside a single pass. This is the exact failure mode of the 2026-07-26
proof attempt: 46026602 tokens and 34.16 dollars against a 5M ceiling.

The admitted-with-no-coverage path is also silent. `PassSpendAdmission.detail` returns an empty
string when `violation is None`, and no CLI caller prints `pass_spend` or `unforecast` at all,
so the operator is never told the pass carries zero forecast coverage. The refusal path is
surfaced as a queue item; the fail-open path is not surfaced anywhere.

## Steps to Reproduce

Measured on main at 7c1a4d3 against the five lanes `loop supervise basicly-jr0l` would
provision at `[worktree] concurrency = 5`:

```sh
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import supervise, policy
from basicly.config import load_sizing_config
p=Path('.'); sz=load_sizing_config(p)
adm=policy.spend_status(p,'basicly-jr0l')
lanes=['basicly-jr0l.40','basicly-jr0l.35','basicly-jr0l.24','basicly-jr0l.45','basicly-jr0l.44']
ws=tuple(supervise.admit_working_set(p,l,sz) for l in lanes)
for w in ws: print(w)
print(supervise.admit_pass_spend(p, ws, adm, sz))
"
```

Observed - four of the five return `sizing=None, violation=None, refused=False`, and the pass
admission is `PassSpendAdmission(forecast_tokens=None, remaining_tokens=4000000, counted=(),
unforecast=('basicly-jr0l.40','basicly-jr0l.35','basicly-jr0l.45','basicly-jr0l.44'),
violation=None)`. `refused` is `violation is not None`, so the pass dispatches. Only
basicly-jr0l.24 sizes at all, because it is the one candidate whose description has a `## Scope`
section; it estimates 111611 tokens and is correctly refused against `working_set_max` 64000.

Corroborating - `uv run basicly usage forecast` reports no pairable dispatch at all: 5 forecast
with no actual, 12 actual with no forecast, 162 with neither. `decompose.bead_class_and_scope`
returns `None` for each of the four unsized beads and a `('bug', (4 paths))` tuple for
basicly-jr0l.24.

Expected - a lane that cannot be sized is either refused, or admitted only under a bound that
does not depend on the estimate, and in both cases the missing forecast coverage is reported to
the operator before any runner starts.

## Scope

- src/basicly/supervise.py
- src/basicly/decompose.py
- src/basicly/cli.py
- tests/test_supervise.py

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a ready lane whose description declares no `## Scope` when a supervised pass admits it
  then the pass either refuses it or bounds it without the estimate, and the operator is told
  which lanes carry no forecast before any runner is dispatched
payload.title: An unsizeable lane defeats both dispatch cost gates and the pass reports no forecast coverage

payload.text:
[harness-info] CONFIRMED WITH REAL SPEND, 2026-08-01. This is no longer an inferred risk; a
single supervised lane overran its grant ceiling and the ceiling could not stop it.

Run: `basicly loop supervise basicly-jr0l --autonomy L1`, one lane (`[worktree] concurrency = 1`),
grant L1 with token_budget 3000000, runner default `auto` resolving to claude.

Measured from the lane's run record (basicly-jr0l.40):

- tokens 4079243 against a 3000000 ceiling - a 36 percent overrun
- cost 3.657368 USD, duration 519.6s, returncode 0, outcome executed
- forecast_tokens null, scope_tokens null, task_class null - the lane was unsizeable, exactly
  as this bead describes, so neither dispatch gate had anything to act on
- observed_models claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-opus-5
- blended rate 0.897 USD per million tokens (the figure in circulation was 0.74)

After the run `policy.spend_status` reports halted True, remaining 0, detail "L1 grant
token_budget spent (4079243/3000000 tokens under this grant)". The retrospective half works; it
simply cannot fire in time, because `dispatch_lanes` reads admission once per pass before
starting any runner and no runner is interrupted afterwards. A single unsized lane can therefore
exceed the whole grant, and N concurrent unsized lanes exceed it N-fold.

Consequence for sizing any future run: at this measured per-lane cost, five concurrent lanes
would be about 20.4M tokens and 18.29 USD. The plan recorded on basicly-u6jq.1 estimated
7 to 8 USD for that shape at a 10M ceiling. The estimate is low by about 2.4x AND the ceiling
would not have bounded it, for the reason above.

Second measured consequence: this run produced no forecast/actual pair. `basicly usage forecast`
went from "12 actual with no forecast" to 13, still reporting no computable forecast error. An
unsized lane cannot produce a pair, because there is no forecast half to pair with - so the
telemetry value attributed to a supervised run (basicly-vkh0.2's input, and the stated other
half of basicly-u6jq.1's value) is not obtainable at all until this bead lands.

[harness-info] Amplifier worth knowing before scheduling this: the missing `## Scope` does not only
disable the two dispatch gates, it also **starves the calibration that would fix the forecast**.

`decompose.calibrated_build_factors` counts a calibration sample only for "a bead whose task class
and declared scope are readable from the tracker", and `SizingConfig.calibration_min_samples` is 10
(window 50). So while this bead is open:

- an unsized lane produces no sample, so `build_factors` can never move off
  `DEFAULT_BUILD_FACTOR_SEEDS` (task 3.0, bug 2.0, chore 1.5)
- the forecast therefore cannot improve with use, which is the mechanism the whole
  forecast chain (jr0l.21, jr0l.22, jr0l.34, jr0l.35) was built to rely on

Consequence for sequencing: fixing this bead is a prerequisite for the engine ever learning its own
costs, not merely for bounding one run. And the learning itself has a price - at the measured
3.657368 USD per lane, the 10 samples needed to displace the seeds cost roughly **37 USD** of real
supervised runs. That is a reason to make sure the first sized runs are ones whose work is wanted
anyway, rather than probe runs.

payload.description:
The quality-gates Windows job failed on the four `basicly status` tests with `[WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified`. First Windows CI run to include the status command (3yv..kd8 landed locally, then pushed together).

Two root causes:
1. Product: hooks._git_hooks_dir runs `git rev-parse` but did not handle git being absent; status is documented to always exit 0 but crashed. Fixed: catch OSError and fall back to <repo>/.git/hooks.
2. Test realism: tests/test_cli.py run_basicly/run_basicly_consumer/cp1252 helpers replaced the process env with only PYTHONPATH, stripping PATH. POSIX has a default-path fallback for execvp so git still resolved; Windows has none, so git was not found. Fixed: base env on os.environ.

## Acceptance Criteria

- basicly status exits 0 when git is not on PATH (regression test); the CLI test helpers inherit PATH; full gate suite passes; Windows CI green.
payload.title: Fix Windows CI: basicly status crashes when git subprocess env lacks PATH

The second release tag shipped package metadata still reading 0.1.0: uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@v0.1.1 basicly --version prints basicly 0.1.0, and consumers' .basicly/state/install.json gets stamped with the stale basicly_version, breaking version-based upgrade/drift detection. Root cause: the version is duplicated in pyproject.toml and src/basicly/__init__.py, neither was bumped when the tag was cut, and nothing gates a tag against the package version.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Cut a tag without bumping pyproject.toml/src/basicly/__init__.py.
2. uvx --from git+https://github.com/niksavis/basicly@<tag> basicly --version → prints the old version.
3. basicly install in a consumer → install.json basicly_version records the old version.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Package version is single-sourced (hatchling dynamic version from the module) so pyproject and module cannot drift.
- Version bumped so the next tag ships matching metadata; v0.1.1 is NOT moved or re-tagged.
- Release workflow fails when the tag name and the package version disagree.
- Verified end to end: uvx at the new tag prints the matching version.
payload.title: release tags can ship stale package metadata

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a repository with the committed tier map and the kit installed but no basicly on PATH when a subagent whose definition declares no model is spawned in claude code then it runs on the model its tier resolves to and the transcript evidences that model, and given a consumer authored agent outside basicly catalog then its tier resolves the same way, and given a host that cannot intercept then the call is left untouched for the host default rather than silently substituted, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Owner requirement 2026-07-31, stated after the injection mechanism was proven experimentally.

**Stated best practice, and the design default this bead establishes:** a model value should NOT be
written statically into an agent definition file. It should be controlled at spawn time by the loop or
conductor that spawns the subagent. Static emission (basicly-a3yi) becomes the FALLBACK for hosts that
cannot intercept, not the preferred path.

Two further requirements that make this its own deliverable rather than part of a3yi:

1. It must work **with no basicly harness present**. A consumer should be able to take the concept and
   the data into another harness. So the unit of delivery is a kit - the committed tier-to-model map
   (basicly-kjc5.61) plus a small hook script plus setup guidance - consumable with zero basicly
   imports and no `basicly` on PATH.
2. It must work for a **custom local agent the consumer wrote themselves**, outside the set basicly
   ships. So resolution must key off something present on any agent definition (a declared tier, or a
   default tier for an undeclared agent) rather than off basicly's own catalog.

A skill (or equivalent invocable entry point) should be able to trigger the injection setup, so a
consumer without the harness can opt in deliberately.

## Verified feasibility - do not re-derive, see basicly-a3yi comments for the full evidence

- **Claude Code: PROVEN WORKING.** A `PreToolUse` hook matching the `Agent` tool, returning
  `updatedInput` containing the whole original `tool_input` PLUS `model`, overrides the definition's
  frontmatter. Demonstrated: frontmatter declared `opus`, hook injected `haiku`, the subagent's own
  transcript recorded 22 messages on `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` and no transcript in the run contained
  `opus`. Two traps: `updatedInput` REPLACES rather than merges on this tool (contradicting the docs), so
  the hook must echo the full input dict; and `model` is ABSENT from `tool_input` unless the caller set
  it, so it must be added rather than rewritten.
- **Copilot CLI: DOES NOT WORK TODAY.** `preToolUse` with `modifiedArgs` is documented, but a repo-level
  `.github/hooks/*.json` hook never fired across three probes (agent delegation; a shell tool with
  `--allow-all-tools`; the same without it). Possibly an SDK-only capability. Copilot's working path is
  static frontmatter, plus session-level `copilot --model` for harness-launched sessions.

So a first version is necessarily **hybrid**: dynamic on claude, static on copilot. Scope this bead to
claude plus copilot only. **Gemini, Cursor and other hosts are explicitly deferred to after v1.0.0** per
owner decision - do not design their adapters now, but do not hard-code a two-host assumption into the
kit's shape either.

## Constraints inherited from the harness

- The hook runs in the spawn path, so it must be deterministic, dependency-free and fast: read a
  committed JSON map, emit JSON, never call the network, never call an LLM.
- Fail closed on an indeterminate answer. If a tier cannot be resolved for the host, the hook must leave
  the call untouched (so the host's own default applies) or refuse - never silently substitute a
  different tier's model, which is the silent-demotion failure basicly-izda exists to prevent.
- Do not let the hook become a way to smuggle authority: it sets a model, nothing else.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a repository with the committed tier map and the kit installed but no basicly on PATH when a
  subagent whose definition declares no model is spawned in claude code then it runs on the model its
  tier resolves to and the transcript evidences that model, and given a consumer authored agent outside
  basicly's catalog then its tier resolves the same way, and given a host that cannot intercept then the
  call is left untouched for the host default rather than silently substituted, with tests
payload.title: Ship a portable tier injection kit that works without the basicly harness

payload.text: HARD CONSTRAINT found 2026-07-31 by exercising the landed wbsz.1 resolver from a consumer copy, before this child was dispatched. The resolver's map discovery walks up from cwd and THEN falls back to the map sitting beside the kit itself. Measured: run from a directory with no map anywhere in its tree, with the kit addressed by absolute path, it returned {model: claude-haiku-4-5, source: argument} and exit 0 - it did NOT no-op. That is documented, deliberate behaviour in wbsz.1 and is fine for a library, but it is a trap for THIS child. This child's AC requires: given a working directory with no committed map then the hook emits no rewrite so the host default applies. And the parent basicly-wbsz records the reason it matters: the copilot hook can only be installed at USER level (repo-level .github/hooks never fires, measured across three probes), so a user-level hook applies to EVERY repo on this machine. If the hook calls the resolver's discover() and takes whatever it returns, it will inject a model into unrelated repos that have nothing to do with basicly. So the hook must scope discovery to the spawn's own working directory and treat kit-adjacent fallback as NOT FOUND - pass the map path explicitly, or check the cwd-derived map exists before resolving. Do not fix this by changing wbsz.1's resolver default: other consumers may legitimately want the fallback, and the parent's requirement is about the hook's behaviour. Add a test that the hook emits no rewrite when the cwd has no map, with the kit reachable by absolute path - that is the exact shape that fooled this probe.

MEASURED 2026-08-01 before implementing, against live docs and the installed CLI binary. Two facts that change this child's design; read them before writing the hook.

1. THE INJECTABLE VALUE IS AN ALIAS NOT A MODEL ID. The AC says the hook returns updatedInput carrying the resolved model. The resolved model from wbsz.1 is a full id (claude-opus-5). The Agent tool will not accept one. Extracted verbatim from the parameter schema in claude 2.1.220:

    subagent_type: v.string().optional().describe(...),
    model: v.enum(["sonnet","opus","haiku","fable"]).optional().describe(`Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter...`)

So updatedInput.model is a four-value enum. Injecting claude-opus-5 fails tool-input validation. This is NOT the same surface as the definition frontmatter, which the subagents doc says does accept a full id: 'model: Model to use: sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full model ID (for example, claude-opus-5), or inherit'. Two different surfaces, two different vocabularies, and this child targets the strict one.

The probe was controlled first, per the zero-result rule: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (9 hits), subagent_type (50), hookSpecificOutput (40) and updatedInput (80) all matched, so the binary's strings are readable and a miss would have meant absent rather than compressed. This is the opposite of the copilot bundle case.

The design fork this opens is an owner call. For the claude host the tier to alias mapping needs no reverse lookup and no price parity: it is already committed as the kjc5.58 migration table, haiku=low sonnet=medium opus=high fable=maximum, 1:1 with the four tiers. So the hook can inject an alias directly from the declared tier. The question is where that table lives - a claude-specific alias surface on the kit, or in the hook - and whether the kit should expose alias output per host at all. Do not silently pick one.

2. AN ENV VAR OUTRANKS THE HOOK. The subagents doc gives the resolution order as: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, then the per-invocation model parameter, then the definition frontmatter, then the main conversation model. The hook writes the per-invocation parameter, which is rank 2 - so a machine with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL set makes every injection inert. Worth a no-op path and a test rather than a silent failure, since this hook installs at user level and applies to every repo on the machine.

3. Output shape confirmed for the implementation: {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "updatedInput": {...}}}, and updatedInput REPLACES the arguments, which is why the AC requires the whole original input to be carried through rather than just the added key.

Sources: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, fetched 2026-08-01; binary <redacted:posix-home-path>

OWNER DECISION 2026-08-01 resolving the design fork raised in the previous comment. The claude tier to alias table lives ON THE KIT, as an explicit per-host table beside HOST_SURFACES in tier_resolver.py, cross-checked by a test against the map's own family field for that tier so the copy cannot drift.

Chosen over (a) putting the dict in the hook and (b) deriving the alias at runtime by stripping the vendor prefix off family.

Reasons recorded so this is not re-litigated. The kit already owns exactly this class of knowledge in HOST_SURFACES - which map surface spelling a host's model field accepts - and an alias enum is the same knowledge one notch narrower: claude's tool-input model field takes a four value enum while its definition frontmatter takes a full id. Putting the table on the kit keeps one place where tier to host vocabulary lives, so wbsz.3's installer and any later host hook reuse it instead of re-owning it. The cross-check test is the repo's existing checked-mirror convention, the same shape as the HOST_SURFACES to FAMILY_MODEL_SURFACES assertion and the tracker-path-scan mirror of MACHINE_PATH_RULES.

Grounding measured this session on base 8d0e216: the map already carries family per tier on the anthropic vendor as claude-haiku, claude-sonnet, claude-opus and claude-fable, which is the enum with the vendor prefix stripped and is 1:1 with the four tiers. models.same_model already treats a bare alias as a legal pin, so injecting an alias does not break the mismatch detection contract that reports whether an injected tier actually took.

The runtime derivation option was declined because a rename of an upstream family would silently change an injected alias with no gate to catch it. The table is committed data and the test is the gate.

payload.text:
OWED LIVE PROOF, inherited from wbsz.2 which landed 2026-08-01. Do not close this child without it.

wbsz.2 shipped claude_tier_hook.py and everything about it was exercised for real EXCEPT the last link. What was measured: a basicly install into a fresh scratch repo materialized both kit files; that installed hook, driven under env -i with python -S -I and no PATH, emitted the exact PreToolUse envelope with model opus for a consumer authored agent declaring tier high, emitted nothing for a shipped agent that declares no tier, and emitted nothing from a directory with no map while the kit stayed reachable by absolute path. Thirteen mutations were each caught by exactly the right test and no other, in both directions.

What was NOT measured: that claude code accepts the emitted updatedInput and the spawned subagent actually runs on that model. That needs the hook wired into settings.json and a real subagent spawn, which is precisely what this child does, and the session that built wbsz.2 was operating under rules that forbade dispatching a subagent. So the AC clause "and the spawned subagent runs on that model" is carried forward here rather than claimed there.

The proof to run once the installer wires it up: install the hook, restart the host so it loads, spawn a subagent whose definition declares a tier, and confirm from the run record or the transcript that the model it used is the aliased one and not the session default. Use a tier that differs from the session model so the observation discriminates - spawning a high tier agent from an opus session proves nothing.

One trap already measured on wbsz.2 that will make this look broken: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL outranks the per invocation parameter the hook writes, so on a machine where it is set every injection is inert and the hook deliberately stays silent. Check the environment before concluding the injection failed.

CORRECTION to the comment above, written minutes later after reading the parent bead rather than trusting my own summary. The gap I described is narrower than I stated, and overstating it would have sent this child hunting for a proof that already exists.

The parent basicly-wbsz records under "Verified feasibility - do not re-derive" that the mechanism is already PROVEN WORKING live on basicly-a3yi: a PreToolUse hook returning updatedInput overrode the definition frontmatter, the frontmatter declared opus, the hook injected haiku, and the subagent's own transcript recorded 22 messages on claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 with no transcript in the run containing opus. Note what that experiment injected - haiku, a bare alias, not a full model id. That independently corroborates the alias finding wbsz.2 measured out of the 2.1.220 binary, from a completely different direction.

So what is actually owed here is narrower: not "can a PreToolUse hook change the spawn model" (answered, live, on a3yi) but "does the specific shipped claude_tier_hook.py do it end to end once the installer wires it up". Its emitted envelope was verified byte for byte against the shape the a3yi experiment proved, from a real basicly install, so the residual risk is in the wiring and the install scope rather than in the mechanism.

Everything else in the comment above stands, including the CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL trap and the advice to pick a tier that differs from the session model so the observation discriminates.

OWNER DECISION 2026-08-01 on install scope, plus a correction to an inherited claim that changes what this child builds.

DECISION. The claude installer writes the repository's own .claude/settings.json by default, and a --user flag writes the user level settings.json instead. Chosen over installing at user level on both hosts and over refusing user level entirely. Reasons: smallest blast radius, it matches a repo scoped harness, it is reversible per repo, and the hook is already written to be safe at user level for the consumer who opts in - wbsz.2 turned the resolver's kit adjacent map fallback off precisely so a machine wide install cannot inject into unrelated repositories. The entry point is therefore asymmetric by host and must say which host it configured and what it wrote.

CORRECTION, and this one narrows the build. The claim that the copilot hook can only be installed at USER level appears in wbsz.2's first comment and I repeated it when framing the decision. It is an inference, not a measurement. What was actually measured, and what the parent basicly-wbsz records, is only this: a REPO level .github/hooks/*.json hook never fired across three probes, so copilot does not work today and the capability may be SDK only. Nobody has measured whether a USER level copilot hook fires. Do not build the copilot half on the assumption that it does.

This matters because it lines up with a clause of this child's own acceptance criteria that would otherwise look unused: given a host that cannot intercept a spawn then it installs nothing for that host and says so rather than reporting success. On today's evidence copilot IS that host. So the expected shape is claude installs, copilot declines and names the measured reason, and the entry point reports both outcomes honestly rather than reporting success for a hook that will never fire. If a cheap probe shows a user level copilot hook does fire, that is a measurement worth recording here and it changes the answer - but it has to be a probe with a positive control, not an inference.

MEASURED 2026-08-01 on copilot CLI 1.0.77, answering the question the correction above left open: does a USER level copilot hook exist at all. On today's build there is no evidence it does, and this settles the copilot half of this child.

What was checked, all free and with no AI call:
- copilot --help across the whole option list mentions no hook of any kind. The help output is long and readable, and other option families such as MCP config and agents are all present in it, so a miss here is absence rather than an unreadable surface.
- ~/.copilot exists and is populated (config.json, settings.json, session-store.db, installed-plugins, logs, ide). There is NO hooks directory in it.
- ~/.copilot/settings.json parses and its key paths are footer.*, model, experimental and effortLevel. No hook key.

One probe was ATTEMPTED AND IS INVALID, recorded so nobody repeats it: strings over the 176M copilot ELF returned zero hits for preToolUse, modifiedArgs AND subagent_type. subagent_type is a positive control that must be present, so the zero is a property of the probe and not of the binary - the bundle is compressed and strings cannot read it. This is the opposite of the claude 2.1.220 case on wbsz.2, where the same technique had four working controls and a miss did mean absent. Do not cite a strings zero on the copilot binary as evidence of anything.

Consequence for this child. Copilot is the host that cannot intercept a spawn, so the installer installs nothing for it and says so, naming the reason, rather than reporting success - which is literally the third clause of this child's acceptance criteria. Copilot's working path stays what the parent records: static frontmatter plus session level copilot --model. Note also that copilot self-updates, so this finding is pinned to 1.0.77 and is worth re-checking rather than trusting when a hooks surface eventually appears.

LIVE PROOF, part 1 of 2 — measured 2026-08-01 11:28 CEST, opus session, hook installed at USER scope.

Preconditions confirmed before measuring, not assumed:
- CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL is unset, so the injection is live rather than inert by design.
- ~/.claude/settings.json carries the PreToolUse/Agent matcher pointing at this repo's
  .basicly/core/kit/claude_tier_hook.py.
- ~/.claude/agents/tier-probe.md declares tier low; the host session is opus, so the low/opus gap is
  the discriminator.

PROVEN: the shipped hook, as actually installed, resolves and emits correctly. Driving the installed
command with real PreToolUse payloads gave seven outcomes, each discriminating, both directions:

  tier low declared              -> updatedInput model=haiku
  definition with no tier key    -> silent
  unknown subagent name          -> silent
  caller already pinned a model  -> silent
  tool_name is not Agent         -> silent
  CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL set -> silent
  cwd outside any map            -> silent

Every case exited 0 with nothing on stderr. The positive case found the definition at user scope and
mapped low to the haiku alias, not to a model id, matching the enum finding from wbsz.2.

STILL OWED: that the host accepts the emitted updatedInput and the spawn actually runs on haiku.
Blocked on a host process restart, see below.

CORRECTION TO A CARRIED-FORWARD DIAGNOSIS. wbsz.2 recorded that agent definitions load "at session
start". Measured more precisely here: they load at HOST PROCESS start. A /clear starts a fresh
conversation but does not reload the agent registry. In this conversation both tier-probe.md, written
by the previous conversation at 11:15, and a brand new probe-control.md written minutes ago were
rejected with "Agent type not found", while the three project agents predating the process start
loaded normally. The control is what separates the two explanations: had the tier key been the
problem, the control without it would have loaded.

Consequence for the kit's consumers, and it belongs in the wbsz.4 docs: after installing the hook a
user must restart the host process, not merely clear the conversation. The installer currently says
nothing about this.

HALF 2 PROVEN, 2026-08-01 11:37. The host accepts the emitted updatedInput and the spawn really runs
on the injected model. The AC clause carried forward from wbsz.2 is now discharged, and this bead
owes nothing further.

Setup, all confirmed before the spawn rather than assumed:

  CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL   unset, so the injection was not inert by design
  hook                         installed at user scope, one PreToolUse Agent matcher group
  host default this session    claude-opus-5
  probe definitions            both loaded, present in the agent registry

That last line is itself the positive half of the process-start correction recorded above. The same
two definitions that a /clear had rejected as "Agent type not found" were registered normally after
the host process was quit and relaunched, with nothing about the files changed. The finding now has
evidence in both directions.

The measurement, two probes, the second one a negative control:

  tier-probe    declares tier low    ran on claude-haiku-4-5-20251001    replied probed
  probe-control no tier key          ran on claude-opus-5                replied control

The discriminator is the gap. The host default was opus, the tier-declaring probe came back on haiku
two tiers below it, and the byte-identical definition with only the tier key deleted came back on the
default untouched. A one sided proof would have passed by pinning everything; this one cannot, because
the control was not pinned.

Both models were read off the subagent transcripts, not off either agent's own claim about which model
it was. Every assistant message in each transcript carries the same model, so there was no mid run
switch.

TRANSCRIPT LOCATION HAS MOVED, worth knowing for the next probe. a3yi read the sidechain entries out of
the parent session jsonl. An async agent no longer writes there. Its transcript is a separate file at

  ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<agent-id>.jsonl

and the parent session jsonl contains no isSidechain records at all. Querying the parent the old way
returns empty, which reads as a failed probe rather than as a moved file.

UNINSTALLED, all three pieces, so no machine wide residue survives this session:

  removed ~/.claude/agents/tier-probe.md and ~/.claude/agents/probe-control.md, agents dir now empty
  removed the one PreToolUse matcher group naming claude_tier_hook.py from ~/.claude/settings.json

The settings restore was diffed against a backup taken first. The only change is the deletion of that
block. Because the file carried no hooks key before the install, and that group was the only hook in
it, the hooks key was dropped entirely rather than left as an empty object. The remaining five keys are
byte identical.

Left installed, this hook would have run on every Agent spawn in every repo on this machine, and would
have broken noisily the moment this repo moved, because the command it writes is an absolute path. That
absolute path at project scope is the separate defect already filed as basicly-dukb.

payload.text:
DOCS REQUIREMENT discovered 2026-08-01 while proving wbsz.3 live, and it belongs in this bead's AC
clause about the claude hook traps.

A third trap, and it is the one a consumer hits first: installing the hook has NO EFFECT until the
claude host PROCESS is restarted. Clearing the conversation does not reload hooks or subagent
definitions. Measured with a control - a definition written by an earlier conversation and a brand
new one written seconds earlier were both rejected as "Agent type not found" in a conversation begun
by /clear, while project agents predating the process start loaded normally.

So the failure mode for a consumer who follows the installer today is: the entry point reports
success, they clear their conversation, they spawn a tiered agent, nothing is injected, and every
diagnostic they can reach says the hook is correctly installed. The installer prints what it wrote
but says nothing about restarting.

Two things to write:
- the kit readme must tell the consumer to quit and relaunch the host after installing, in the
  install steps themselves rather than in a troubleshooting note;
- worth considering as a change to install_hook.py rather than only docs, since a one line
  "restart the host for this to take effect" in the installer's own success output is where the
  reader actually is. That would be a separate bead against the installer, not this docs bead.

Note the second trap already recorded elsewhere still applies and is independent:
CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL outranks the injected parameter, so on a machine where it is set the
hook is inert by design and stays deliberately silent.

PARTLY COVERED ALREADY, 2026-08-01, while fixing basicly-dukb. Read this before writing, so the same
text is not written twice and so the readme does not contradict what now ships.

The `tier-injection` skill was edited in the dukb landing (commit 4f8b06a) because dukb changed what
the installer writes and the skill documented the old shape. Two things in this bead's AC are already
satisfied there, for the SKILL surface only - the readme and the design note in this bead's scope
still do not exist:

- The restart trap is written, in the install steps rather than as a troubleshooting note, and it
  names the mechanism: quit and relaunch the host, the whole CLI process, because hooks and agent
  definitions are read when the process starts and clearing the conversation reloads nothing. The
  earlier wording said "settings load at session start", which is the exact ambiguity that cost an
  earlier session a turn.
- The two scope renderings and `--interpreter` are documented, with the project-scope command shown
  verbatim.

Still owed by this bead, unchanged: `.basicly/core/kit/README.md` and
`docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md` do not exist at all; the two claude hook traps the rewrite depends
on are recorded only on basicly-a3yi and in code comments; and nothing yet shows a consumer how to
drive the map from another harness with no basicly present.

A THIRD TRAP for the traps list, measured 2026-08-01 on wbsz.3 and worth writing beside the other two:
`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` outranks the per-invocation model the hook writes. Where it is set every
injection is inert and the hook stays deliberately silent, so a consumer debugging "the hook does
nothing" should check that variable before anything else.

Also confirmed live the same day, so the readme can state it as fact rather than as intent: the
shipped hook injects end to end. A probe declaring `tier: low` spawned on claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
from an opus host, and a byte-identical probe with only the tier key removed spawned on the host
default. Evidence on wbsz.3.

The installer-prints-a-restart-line idea in the comment above is still NOT done and is still a
separate bead against the installer rather than part of this docs work.

payload.close_reason: Delivered by basicly-rupz: the runner now reads its stdout on reader threads and the supervisor heartbeat carries tokens-so-far beside elapsed, verified by test at tests/test_supervise.py and by execution on two concurrent real lanes. A format with no incremental stream still reports elapsed alone rather than a fabricated zero. The 1.55x over-report of the printed figure is filed separately as basicly-jr0l.67.
payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-vu6u` delivered the elapsed-time half of live lane progress: the supervisor now reports
each in-flight lane and how long it has been running, on the heartbeat that already ticks during
dispatch. The owner also asked for **tokens spent so far** per lane, and that half is not done.

It is blocked on how the dispatch reads its child. `runner.run` uses
`proc.communicate(input=..., timeout=...)`, which returns only when the process is down, so there
is no incremental stdout to sample — `supervise.lane_activity`'s docstring already records this
("the runner drains its pipes only after the process is down"), which is why lane progress is
measured from commits and the dirty tree instead.

The data is there to be read. The claude dispatch already runs
`--output-format stream-json --verbose`, so usage events arrive incrementally on stdout and are
currently parsed only once, at the end, by `runner.extract_usage`.

## Why this was split rather than done

Restructuring `runner.run` touches the most safety-critical path in the engine: the `timeout` that
hard-kills a stalled lane, `_kill_tree`'s process-group kill, the Windows branch that has no
signalling equivalent, and the stdin-closing fix for `codex exec` (basicly-jr0l.36). A reader thread
per dispatch changes the shutdown ordering of all four. The repo has also watched added I/O on the
dispatch path break timing tests before. That is a deliberate piece of work with its own tests, not
a rider on a reporting change.

## Shape to consider

- Drain stdout/stderr in reader threads instead of `communicate`, preserving the timeout kill, the
  tree kill and the `KeyboardInterrupt` path exactly; the drained buffers still feed
  `extract_usage` unchanged so no adapter parsing moves.
- Expose a cheap "usage so far" read per format, keyed off the same incremental stream, and let
  `supervise._inflight_note` add it beside the elapsed figure.
- Formats that cannot report incrementally (`copilot-session-store`, and codex, which reports no
  model at all) must report elapsed only rather than a fabricated zero.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run basicly loop supervise <root>   # with a real headless runner and lanes in flight
```

Observed - `running:  <issue> 42s` per heartbeat, with no token figure. Expected - the same line
also carries tokens spent so far for a format that can report them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a lane is in flight under an adapter whose usage format reports incrementally when the
  supervisor emits its progress line then that line carries tokens spent so far beside the elapsed
  time, and a format that cannot report incrementally still reports elapsed alone rather than a
  fabricated figure
payload.title: Report tokens spent so far for an in flight lane not only its elapsed time

payload.text:
Delivered by basicly-rupz, which shipped 2026-08-06 and removed this bead's stated blocker -
runner.run no longer collects with one communicate after the process is down; it reads its pipes
on reader threads and hands each stdout line to a sink.

Both halves of the acceptance criterion are met and were verified twice.

By test: tests/test_supervise.py, test_inflight_note_reports_the_tokens_a_running_lane_has_reported
asserts "epic.1 12s 84000 tok" for a lane whose stream reported, and asserts the second lane shows
elapsed alone - so a format that cannot report incrementally is not given a fabricated zero.

By execution on real work, which is the half a test cannot show. First single lane:

  running:  basicly-lpsf 14s 174899 tok

Then two concurrent lanes, proving the per-lane attribution the AC implies:

  running:  basicly-vkh0.12 1090s 8875372 tok, basicly-vkh0.9 1090s 7211645 tok

Closing as delivered rather than as duplicate: the work landed under rupz because consuming the
stream was the blocking half. One caveat worth carrying forward - the figure this line prints is
1.55x the recorded run-record total, filed as basicly-jr0l.67. The AC asked for tokens spent so
far beside the elapsed time and that is what ships; the denomination defect is separate and does
not reopen this.

payload.close_reason: hooks-build now preserves unmanaged pre-commit comments and placement on rewrite via a ruamel.yaml round-trip that rebuilds only the managed block; added a regression test; verified end-to-end and via full suite (691 pass); landed via base checkout
payload.description:
Found while shipping basicly-yw28 (2026-07-18). `basicly hooks-build` rewrites `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and normalizes content OUTSIDE its managed hook block: it hoisted the hand-maintained `markdownlint` entry to the top of the file and dropped its explanatory comment ("Repo-wide run through .markdownlint-cli2.yaml ... so explicit paths can't bypass the config's ignore list"). `basicly hooks-check` only validates managed-hook PRESENCE, so the drop passes the gate silently — a single-hook add via the canonical `hooks-build` therefore clobbers unmanaged hooks' placement and comments as collateral. Workaround used in yw28: revert the full regen and surgically insert only the new managed entry, preserving markdownlint.

Two candidate directions: (a) hooks-build preserves out-of-block entries verbatim (placement + comments), only touching its own managed block; or (b) `.pre-commit-config.yaml` becomes fully managed (markdownlint moves into hooks.yaml as a managed git hook, so nothing is hand-maintained). Decide which; (b) is cleaner long-term but changes the consumer story for repos with their own hooks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running `basicly hooks-build` after adding/removing a managed hook leaves any unmanaged pre-commit entry (e.g. a consumer's own markdownlint) byte-for-byte unchanged, including its comments and position — OR markdownlint is folded into the managed set and the file is documented as fully generated.
- A regression test proves an unmanaged hook entry with a comment survives a hooks-build round-trip (or that no unmanaged entries are expected).
- Decision recorded (preserve-out-of-block vs fully-managed) in the bead or architecture.md.
payload.title: Tooling: hooks-build should preserve out-of-block content in the pre-commit config

payload.text: Decision: preserve-out-of-block via ruamel.yaml (user-approved new dependency). render_precommit_config now round-trips an existing config with ruamel (comment/order preserving) and rebuilds only basicly's managed local block in place; unmanaged repos/hooks keep their comments and relative order byte-for-byte. Fresh files still render via yaml.safe_dump (unchanged output for new installs). Chose this over (b) fold-markdownlint-into-managed, which would only remove basicly's own unmanaged hook and would NOT fix the clobber for consumer repos that bring their own hooks. Note: managed hooks stay consolidated in one appended block (existing invariant), so a previously-interleaved unmanaged hook lands before the managed block after the first rewrite; its comment and content are never dropped. Verified end-to-end: a sync_hooks rewrite from the dogfood markdownlint block kept all 3 comment lines + the files key and check stayed clean; basicly hooks-build is still a no-op on the real config.

payload.description:
On a fresh consumer repo, basicly install cannot auto-activate the git hooks. When pre-commit is not on PATH, install_hooks falls back to `uv run pre-commit` (hooks.py), which only resolves if the consumer repo declares pre-commit as a project dependency — a fresh consumer never does — so uv reports "Failed to spawn: pre-commit (program not found)" and the gates are left inert with a confusing message. Separately, a target folder without a .git directory cannot have hooks activated at all (pre-commit install needs a git repo), and today that surfaces as an opaque error rather than clear guidance.

Verified locally: `uv run pre-commit --version` in a fresh dir fails to spawn pre-commit, while `uv tool run pre-commit --version` (uvx) auto-provisions it and works. The consumer reliably has uv (basicly is installed via uvx), so uvx is the correct runner.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a fresh folder that has no .git and no pyproject declaring pre-commit.
2. Ensure pre-commit is not on PATH (only uv is available).
3. Run basicly install in that folder.
4. Observe: "Could not auto-activate git hooks: pre-commit install failed (error: Failed to spawn: pre-commit ... program not found); run manually: pre-commit install ...". The manual command also fails because pre-commit is not installed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- install_hooks and uninstall_hooks fall back to `uv tool run pre-commit` (uvx) instead of `uv run pre-commit` when pre-commit is not on PATH, so a consumer with only uv gets pre-commit auto-provisioned and activation succeeds.
- The "run manually" guidance points at a command that actually works without pre-commit pre-installed (uvx pre-commit install --install-hooks ...).
- When the target repo has no .git directory, activation is skipped with a clear actionable message (not a git repository; run git init then basicly hooks-build), and basicly install still exits 0 with projections written.
- Regression tests cover: the uvx fallback command is chosen when pre-commit is absent but uv is present; the no-.git path returns the clear guidance without spawning pre-commit.
- pytest, ruff, and the projection checks stay green.

## Scope

Fix the runner fallback and the no-.git precheck in hooks.py plus the caller message in cli.py. No change to the happy path (pre-commit on PATH). No new dependency. Does not change what hooks are projected, only how activation is invoked and guarded.
payload.title: Install cannot auto-activate git hooks on a fresh consumer repo

payload.description:
## Context

Two claims about GitHub Copilot were stated to the owner as fact and both were wrong,
2026-08-06. Copilot was said to report no token counts: GitHub moved every plan to
token-based billing on 2026-06-01, the CLI exposes a per-model breakdown, and this
repo's own `runner.py` has been extracting it from copilot's session store all along.

The failure was not a missing tool - WebSearch was available throughout. It was
**trusting a summary line in our own docs about a third party**:
`docs/design/factory-design.md` carried 'copilot has no counts' in a components table
while section 7.5 four hundred lines below documented the exact extraction mechanism.

## What the skill encodes

An order of evidence that puts **our own code that already touches the interface**
first, vendor docs second, and marketing nowhere; the rule to read the section a
summary cites; version-and-date pinning, which this repo already does well where it
does it at all; the distinction between a capability existing and our dispatch being
able to reach it; stating a claim at the precision the evidence supports, so a
correct-but-vague note does not invite a future reader to 'fix' it; and correcting the
document that carried the stale version rather than adding the new claim beside it.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given an agent in a repo with basicly installed and no prior context when it is asked to drive a supervised multi-lane run then a skill carries the procedure and the judgment end to end and defers to basicly loop preflight for the current facts rather than restating any of them
payload.description:
## Context

Tier 2 of basicly-ze8z: semi-deterministic, so a script for the facts plus a skill for the judgment.

The runbook for driving a supervised run does not exist in the catalog. Measured: `loop supervise` appears only in `docs/design/factory-design.md` and `docs/architecture/architecture.md`, which describe the system rather than how to drive it, and in the `harness-client` skill, which is about attaching as a second observer. The `harness-loop` skill is 271 lines and barely mentions supervise, grants or budget.

So everything about starting a run lived in an operator handover: mint a grant and why L1 rather than L3, size the budget from the measured per-lane cost, know that a dirty base refuses the landing after the lanes have already run, know which runner meters spend, know that concurrency is the lane-count dial.

`basicly loop preflight <root>` (filed under basicly-ze8z, landed) now answers the *facts*. This bead carries the *judgment* around them and points at that command instead of restating it:

- when a supervised run is the right tool versus single-track driving
- choosing the autonomy level, and what each one leaves to a human
- sizing a budget from `preflight`'s forecast, and what to do when it refuses
- reading the `spend:` coverage line, and why an assumed bound is not a measurement
- what to do with each routed outcome, and which ones are by design rather than defects

Either a new `harness-supervise` skill or a section of `harness-loop`. A skill costs nothing until invoked, which is why this is a skill and not a fragment - the always-on baseline is already near its cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an agent in a repo with basicly installed and no prior context when it is asked to drive a supervised multi-lane run then a skill carries the procedure and the judgment end to end and defers to basicly loop preflight for the current facts rather than restating any of them
payload.title: Carry the supervised run runbook in a skill instead of an operator handover

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given concurrent bytecode cache writes under the catalog hooks directory when the hook sync and hook check paths run then no bytecode cache file is copied compared or reported as drift and the affected test passes deterministically under parallel pytest, with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-07-31 during the `basicly-5ltn` lane, incidental to that change and not caused by it.
`tests/test_hooks.py::test_sync_hooks_prunes_hook_excluded_by_selection` failed once under
`pytest -q -n 4`, then passed on re-run and in the final full run.

Reported cause: a `shutil.copytree` over the catalog hooks directory raced a **vanishing**
`__pycache__/*.pyc.<tmp>` file. CPython writes a bytecode cache as a uniquely named temp file and then
renames it, so a concurrent tree walk can stat a name that no longer exists by the time it is opened.
With `-n 4` several workers import the same hook scripts at once, so the window is real rather than
theoretical.

This is the same family as `basicly-m4zv.14` (a machine-global beads write lock making gates flaky) -
a flake in a gate costs more than its own runtime, because it burns the loop's bounded rework budget
and trains an operator to re-run rather than read. It is P3 because it is rare and self-clearing, not
because it is harmless.

Two candidate fixes worth weighing rather than assuming:

- Copy with an ignore predicate that skips `__pycache__` entirely (`shutil.ignore_patterns`), which is
  also strictly correct - a bytecode cache is never catalog content and should not be projected or
  compared.
- Run the affected tests with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, which removes the writer rather than
  tolerating it. Note the `basicly-kjc5.61` lane independently hit a *different* `__pycache__` defect
  the same day - a mutation and its restore had identical size and same-second mtime, so a stale `.pyc`
  was reused and silently polluted the next mutation result - and fixed it exactly this way. So the
  same environment variable resolves two separate incidents, which argues for it.

Prefer the fix that also makes `check_hooks` and `sync_hooks` ignore `__pycache__` on principle: the
directory is machine-local build output, so including it in a catalog comparison can only ever produce
false drift.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Run `uv run pytest -q -n 4` repeatedly on a tree whose `.basicly/core/hooks/__pycache__` is being
  written by concurrent imports.
- Observed, intermittently: `test_sync_hooks_prunes_hook_excluded_by_selection` fails inside
  `shutil.copytree` on a `.pyc.<tmp>` path that no longer exists. Expected: the test is independent of
  bytecode cache files and cannot see them at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given concurrent bytecode cache writes under the catalog hooks directory when the hook sync and
  hook check paths run then no bytecode cache file is copied compared or reported as drift and the
  affected test passes deterministically under parallel pytest, with tests
payload.title: Stop a pycache race making the hook sync test flake under parallel pytest

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the non-interactive-shell fragment is projected to all three always-on surfaces when an agent follows its non-interactive-flag bullet to remove a directory then the command it forms is allowed by the projected permissions deny-list rather than denied, and given the fragment is edited then basicly check and the measured always-on byte counts still pass their soft caps
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

`.basicly/core/fragments/tools/non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml:15` is an always-on bullet on
every surface and reads:

> Use non-interactive flags (`cp -f`, `mv -f`, `rm -f`, package-manager `-y`, ...) for ops that
> can hang on a prompt

For the common case - removing a scratch **directory** - following that literally produces
`rm -rf <dir>`, and `.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml` denies every spelling of it
(`rm -rf*`, `rm -fr*`, `rm -r -f*`, `rm -f -r*`). The agent is steered by the always-on guidance
straight into a hard-denied command.

Observed 2026-07-31 during the v0.6.0 session: a scratch-dir reset was denied mid-task and cost a
turn to rewrite. It is a repeat - the same collision is already recorded in the operator's own
notes from an earlier session, so the guidance has now mis-steered at least twice.

Expected: the fragment names the recursive case and the allowed spelling, so the always-on text
and the deny-list agree.

Proposed fix (do not self-apply - this is a retro finding): extend the bullet to say that a
recursive delete uses `rm -r` and that the force variants are denied, e.g. "... for ops that can
hang on a prompt - but a recursive delete is `rm -r`, never `rm -rf`, which the deny-list blocks
outright; prefer a uniquely named fresh directory over clearing an old one." Cost is a few dozen
chars on all three surfaces; headroom at the time of filing was CLAUDE.md ~1060,
copilot-instructions ~926, AGENTS.md ~1167, so it fits - confirm before landing.

payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 dimension 3. basicly drift means config drift only. Derive a per-repo/per-agent health signal from the run-record log and flag behavioral regressions against a rolling baseline.

Design note (found while scoping): br gate results have no history — they overwrite in br (policy.py), so gate pass/fail over time is not queryable. The durable historical signal is the run-record log (.basicly/usage/run-records.json): append-only, keyed by bead, carrying agent + outcome (executed/failed/handoff) + timestamp. A failed dispatch is a failed run and a rework re-dispatch appends another record for the same bead, so run-record outcomes are a durable proxy for the gate-fail + rework signal without coupling to br's non-historical gate state. Signal source decided with the user: run-records only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New src/basicly/health.py (sibling to fleet.py, imports run_record only) with pure functions: agent_health(records_by_bead) and agent_drift(records_by_bead, window) plus health_report(repo_root, window). No new br calls and no new persisted state.
- Per-agent health covers: runs, counts by outcome, failure_rate (failed / dispatched runs, handoffs excluded), a rework signal (count of beads that agent re-dispatched), and a documented bounded health_score in [0,1] computed from named weight constants at module top.
- Rolling-baseline drift: an agent's most-recent window runs (recent window) are compared against all older runs (baseline window), sorted by the record timestamp. A behavioral regression is flagged when the recent failure_rate exceeds the baseline failure_rate by a documented regression delta AND both windows meet a documented minimum sample size, so a couple of runs cannot trip it.
- basicly health [--json] [--window N] prints a per-agent summary plus any flagged regressions for the current repo; --fleet [--root PATH] rolls up per-repo health via fleet.discover_repos. Read-only, always exits 0; a repo or agent with no run-records degrades to an empty report, not an error.
- Schema-versioned JSON payload like status/fleet; no wall-clock value in the payload so output is deterministic.
- Regression tests mirror tests/test_fleet.py and the run-record fixtures: the health math, drift regression / no-regression / insufficient-sample, empty and corrupt log resilience, CLI dispatch, and a docs-drift entry for the new command.
- docs/architecture.md dimension-3 (observability) updated to describe the health/drift signal and why gate-history is not a source; pytest, ruff, and the projection checks stay green.

## Scope

Signal is run-records only (decided with the user): no live br gate/rework querying, so it works on the durable log alone and stays deterministic. No token/cost health (those run-record fields are still null, reserved). No time-series storage or charting — drift is computed from the existing log's timestamps, not a new persisted baseline file. health_score weights and drift thresholds are documented module constants, advisory only (nothing gates on them). The --fleet roll-up reuses fleet.discover_repos; it does not replace the existing status --fleet run-record summary.
payload.title: Observability: health scoring and drift-over-time
