payload.description:
## Context

`.basicly/core/hooks/tool-usage.py` records a skill only when the Claude `Skill` tool is
invoked (`_skill_from_payload` requires `tool.lower() == "skill"`). Skills attached through
an agent definition's `skills:` frontmatter passthrough are *preloaded*, not invoked, so they
fire no `Skill` call and are invisible to the counter.

Consequence: `basicly usage report` lists them under "Never-used catalog skills (culling
candidates)". On 2026-08-13 that list named `decompose-plan`, `repair-in-place`,
`validate-as-consumer` and `root-cause` - which are exactly the four skills declared in the
engine's own agent frontmatter (`.claude/agents/decomposer.md`, `implementer.md`,
`validator.md`, `researcher.md`, `retrospector.md`).

The report invites culling on this list, so the instrument actively recommends deleting the
skills the engine depends on. Only the never-used side of a usage audit can be manufactured
by a measurement bug, which is why this one is worth fixing rather than annotating.

Unresolved and worth settling in the same unit: whether the host honours the `skills:`
passthrough at all. `agents.py:372` calls it deliberately untyped, "its shape is the host's
to define", and nothing in the repo asserts it is honoured. If it is not, the four agents
are running without the skills they declare and nobody would see it.

## Proposed check

Either count a preloaded skill at dispatch time from the agent definition, or exclude
frontmatter-declared skills from the never-used list and say why in the report. Whichever is
chosen, a test must show a preloaded skill does not appear as a culling candidate.
payload.title: Record a preloaded skill so the usage audit stops inventing never used

payload.text: Resolved by basicly-ey58 (shipped 2026-08-13, beb7f01). The open half of this bead was whether skills: has a defined shape; it does - a documented, typed list of skill names - and the defect was the spawn mode, not the schema. agents.py's 'deliberately untyped (its shape is the host's to define)' is refuted. The engine now reads the declared bodies and carries them in the dispatch prompt for every family, so the field has a runtime effect and catalog_lint's skill/role pairing enforces something real.

## Context

Found by the lane-A and lane-E surveys independently, 2026-08-14. Verified by hand.

```text
dispatch_brief.py:31   VALIDATE_GATE = "validate-as-consumer"    zero consumers
validate_gate.py:31    VALIDATE_GATE = "validate-as-consumer"    every consumer uses this one
integrity.py:182       the string spelled a third time
```

Vulture cannot see the dead copy. `validate_gate`'s uses of its own constant mask `dispatch_brief`'s by bare name. That is the same masking mechanism `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py:166-170` already records for `CreatedChild.depends_on`.

## Why the third spelling matters most

`integrity.py:182` decides whether a unit requires validation at L3. If a rename reaches `validate_gate` and not `integrity`, then `requires_validation` silently stops requiring validation. That is a fail-open on the gate this repository added one day ago.

## The second half

`policy.GATE_TYPE_BY_GATE` (policy.py:93-108) is introduced as every gate the engine names, and its pinning test at `tests/test_policy.py:3184` enumerates a set that omits `validate-as-consumer`. The gate is engine-named, engine-recorded (validate_gate.py:125-146) and required at L3. It falls to the REVISION default, which happens to match the behaviour at loop.py:437. So this is a false completeness claim rather than a behaviour defect, and the claim is what the map exists for.

## Why the fix is legal today

`validate_gate.py:24` already imports `VERDICT_PREFIX` from `dispatch_brief`, its direct junior in `.importlinter:30-31`.

## Acceptance

- When the string `validate-as-consumer` is searched under `src/basicly/`, then exactly one definition site remains.
- When `policy.gate_type` is asked for that gate, then an explicit entry in `GATE_TYPE_BY_GATE` answers it, and the pinning test includes it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/validate_gate.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/integrity.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_validate_gate.py`

## Warning

`policy.py` has 10 tokens of size headroom. The dictionary entry must ride with a deletion or a comment trim in the same diff.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_policy.py tests/test_validate_gate.py -q` and `uv run basicly check`.

payload.description:
## Context

Curating the v0.9.0 cut found **19 of the 54 beads closed since v0.8.0 carry no changelog.d fragment**, including basicly-4kdm - the seven specialist agents and five loop skills, which are vendored to every consumer by basicly install and are the single largest thing in the release.

The release body is a consumer surface. .github/workflows/release.yml extracts CHANGELOG.md from the **tagged** commit, so a missing fragment is unrecoverable after the tag: the note can never reach the published release. That is the same one-shot property basicly-m3od.1 already paid for from the other direction.

## Why nothing caught it

changelog.d refuses a fragment that is empty or misnamed, so the gate binds on **fragments that exist**. Nothing binds on a **closed bead that produced none**, and absence is exactly the shape a presence check cannot see. The eight fragments written by hand during the cut are the mopping, not the fix.

## What the check would be

A closed bead whose commits touched anything outside docs, tests and the tracker, with no matching changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md, is either a release note that was forgotten or a change that is genuinely invisible to a consumer - and the second case is a declaration, not a default. Ratchet it the way noqa-debt is ratcheted: freeze today's unaccounted set, fail on growth, so the backlog is not a blocker but a new omission is.

Note the discriminator problem this shares with basicly-r343 and the wired-or-deleted gate: bind the check on a marker the producer writes, because absence alone cannot tell a defect from a bead that predates the rule.

## Measured

- 54 beads closed since the v0.8.0 tag, 35 with a fragment, 19 without.
- Consumer-visible among the 19: 4kdm, u2hl.4, u2hl.11, u2hl.12, u2hl.13, u2hl.32, m4zv.6, a3ab.1, a3ab.12.
- Eight fragments were written by hand at cut time to close the gap for this release.

payload.description:
## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
The defect is real and shipping: `runner.py:151` still ships `claude: 200_000` and a consumer
with no `[runner] context_windows` inherits it. **Two things below are now wrong.**

**The remedy changed.** `implementation-plan.md:223` records the premise corrected 2026-08-09:
the binary reports its own window on the stream as `modelUsage.<id>.contextWindow`, so the fix
is to *read* it, not to ship a second hand-maintained constant. Nothing in `src/` reads that
field today - `runner.py:1794` reads `modelUsage` for model names only. **Acceptance criterion
1 below is therefore the wrong shape**: "assert the resolved window is not 200_000" pins a
second hand-written constant, which `factory-loop.md` section 15.6 forbids in the same breath
as deleting the ceiling.

**Its blocking consumer is being deleted.** Section 15.6 and D23 remove the context ceiling
outright: "a gate that has never once fired correctly - first at a fifth of its intended
point, then never - is removed rather than given a third constant." That is `basicly-u2hl.30`,
still open. Sequence this after it, at which point this bead narrows to the window declaration
and its provenance alone - which the bead's own text already concedes.

**The evidence needs replacing, and the replacement is stronger.** The "0 of 106 fire" figure
is unrefreshed. Measured over 346 records on 2026-08-13: `context_window_source` is
`{null: 220, "[runner] context_windows": 124, "conservative fallback": 2}` - the
**`adapter default` label appears zero times**, against a positive control where two other
labels do populate. So the shipped constant is unexercised *here*, which is precisely why it
reaches consumers unnoticed. Provenance recording is already built (`runner.py:158-161`,
`run_record.py:200-209`).

**Prerequisite:** `basicly-i4gg` (closed 2026-08-13) landed the envelope parse this remedy
reads from.

---

## Context

`basicly-23ep` fixed the claude context window after a stale `200_000` constant put the
finalize trigger at `120_000` and truncated healthy lanes for months — **18 follow-up beads
carrying `(context-ceiling overrun)`** are the recorded cost, and 51 of 79 lanes crossed
the wrong threshold.

**The fix reached this repo's config and nothing else** [M, 2026-08-08]:

```text
basicly.toml:568-569        [runner.context_windows]
                            claude = 1_000_000        <- this repo only
src/basicly/runner.py:142   _CONTEXT_WINDOWS = {"claude": 200_000, "codex": 400_000,
                                                "copilot": 128_000}   <- what SHIPS
```

`basicly` installs its harness into other repositories. A consumer that installs it and
does not hand-write a `[runner.context_windows]` override inherits `200_000`, so their
ceiling sits at `120_000` and truncates their lanes exactly as ours were truncated — the
defect `23ep` closed, still live for everyone but us.

## Why this is the sharpest form of a rule already in the plan

`implementation-plan.md` section 10: *"A constant describing an external capability must be
falsifiable against our own ledger. It is the one class of value that is correct when
written and rots silently as the vendor ships."* `23ep` added
`runner.window_violations` to make the **declaration** falsifiable — but it is falsifiable
against *this* repo's ledger, and the shipped default is the thing no ledger checks.

So this is not "update a number". Pasting `1_000_000` into `runner.py` is the same
unchecked declaration one generation on, and `23ep`'s own bead says so: *"Do not re-fix by
writing a bigger constant."* The adapter default needs either provenance and a staleness
check of its own, or it needs to stop being a silent default at all — e.g. refuse to meter
a ceiling when no window is declared for an agent, rather than assuming one.

## The second half: the ceiling is now inert here

Measured the same day: `ceiling_tokens(claude) = 600_000` against a maximum observed
occupancy of `403_051` over 106 metered dispatches, so **0 of 106 fire**. The gate has gone
from firing at one fifth of its intended point to being unreachable, and **neither state has
ever been correct**. `basicly-u2hl.30` deletes the ceiling on exactly that ground. If it
lands first, this bead narrows to the window declaration alone; if it does not, a consumer
still carries the mis-firing version.

## Steps to Reproduce

```text
$ grep -n '_CONTEXT_WINDOWS' src/basicly/runner.py
142:_CONTEXT_WINDOWS = {"claude": 200_000, "codex": 400_000, "copilot": 128_000}

$ grep -n -A1 'runner.context_windows' basicly.toml
568:[runner.context_windows]
569-claude = 1_000_000
```

Observed: a fresh consumer repo with no override meters claude at a 200,000 window.
Expected: a consumer inherits a window that is either correct or explicitly undeclared,
never a stale value presented as a default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a consumer repo with no `[runner.context_windows]` override, when a claude
  dispatch is metered, then it does not use a window smaller than the model's real one
  - check: a test loads config from a fixture repo carrying no override and asserts the
  resolved claude window is not `200_000`.
- Given any agent whose window is not declared with provenance, when the ceiling would be
  metered, then the engine records that it could not meter rather than assuming a default
  - check: a test asserts the unmetered case is recorded and named, not silently defaulted.
- Given the shipped defaults, when they drift from the vendor's published windows, then
  something fails - check: a test or gate that reads the declaration's recorded provenance
  and fails when it is absent or older than the declared staleness bound.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly usage --json` in a fresh consumer repo with no override reports the claude
window it will meter against, and that value is not `200_000`.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none

payload.description:
## Context

Surfaced by `basicly usage tuning` at session close, 2026-08-14, over 359 recorded dispatches.
Every per-class build factor in force is a **declared seed** and every one is far below what the
ledger measured:

```text
class   in force        advised (measured)   samples
bug     2   x scope     10.66                n=37
chore   1.5 x scope     11.93                n=10
task    3   x scope     17.25                n=27
```

Three classes, 74 samples, all `measured` rather than `seeded`, so each is past
`[policy.sizing] calibration_min_samples`. The smallest gap is 5.3x and the largest is 8.0x.

## Why this matters more than a mis-tuned constant

`architecture.md` §12.8.2 records that **nothing measures a working-set factor** - the calibration
that appeared to was measuring whole-lane spend, a different quantity, and was removed
(`basicly-z2wi`). So every forecast in the engine today is a declared constant times a scope
read-cost, and the record says so via `forecast_source`.

This is the first time the ledger has been able to answer what those constants should be, and the
answer is that they are systematically low by most of an order of magnitude. A forecast that low
feeds `supervise.admit_pass_spend`, the band, and every budget minted from a preflight.

## What this bead is NOT

It is **not** "apply the recommendation". `basicly usage tuning` is advisory by design and
changes no config, and `basicly.toml` is on the confirmation list. The tuner also warns that its
sample includes beads that never landed.

What is owed first is the classification the number needs: whether the 5-8x gap is the seeds being
wrong, or the scope read-cost the factor multiplies being wrong, or both. Those call for different
fixes and the ratio alone cannot separate them.

## Evidence

`uv run basicly usage tuning`, rows `policy.sizing.build_factor.{bug,chore,task}`.

payload.description:
## Context

`docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` §3.0 reasons about which `br` surfaces are used from the
committed ledger `.basicly/ledger/tracker-usage.jsonl`. That file was last written 2026-07-30
(`dc094ad`) and holds **1,568 invocations**. The unpromoted spool
`.basicly/usage/tracker-usage.jsonl` holds **91,891** - the committed evidence is 58x
under-sampled.

The consequence is the exact failure §3.0 lines 167-171 warns about, recurring: "a never-used
entry is the only finding in this report that a measurement error can fabricate". **Fifteen
surfaces the committed ledger records as never used are in fact in use**: `where` (171), `init`
(28), `dep tree` (14), `dep cycles` (10), `stats` (9), `schema` (4), `dep` (5), `gate` (3),
`label list` (2), `version` (2), `delete` (1), `capabilities` (1), `robot-docs guide` (1),
`comments` (4), `label` (1).

Distinct real surfaces: **17 of 87 committed, 31 of 87 in the spool.** The read:write ratio the
doc cites as 3.4:1 is **24.3:1** in the spool, and the top surface is `show` at 50,714 calls
(55%), not `comments list`.

`basicly-vkh0.8` was supposed to have closed this class by stopping a worktree teardown
discarding recorded usage. It did - but the **promotion** step never ran again, so the
committed artifact silently aged into being wrong while the gate that would notice does not
exist.

Related and worth checking in the same unit: `show` at 55% of 91,891 calls is far above the
read amplification `basicly-tcmy.15` describes, so the spool may be recording a diagnostic
loop rather than real load. Attribute it before citing it.

## Proposed check

Promotion runs on a schedule the repo enforces rather than by hand, and a gate fails when the
committed ledger's newest entry is older than the spool's by more than a declared window. A
test asserts the gate fires on a stale committed ledger against a fresh spool.

## Context

Found by the lane-A survey 2026-08-14. `basicly-tcmy.21` says remove or wire. Applied uniformly, that instruction deletes load-bearing fields. This bead is its loop-core slice with a verdict per symbol, each carrying its probe.

## Delete, no production caller

```text
policy.should_escalate           policy.py:598     rule spelled inline at 5 live sites
session.clear_overrides          session.py:49     docstring claims a caller that does not exist
loop.CeremonyResult.approvals    loop.py:2519      cli.py:3187 iterates events instead
loop_state.PHASES                loop_state.py:38  duplicates config.LOOP_PHASES plus "done"
loop_state.NodeState.agent_context  loop_state.py:126, 233   written, never read
loop_state.Ranking.fallback_sort loop_state.py:281, 312      constructed, read by nothing
```

The inline sites for `should_escalate` are `loop.py:2114`, `merge.py:1149`, `merge.py:1176`, `policy.py:2217` and `cli.py:2451`. They reuse a count already in hand to avoid a second tracker read. Do not substitute a re-reading form.

`agent_context` shows the masking hazard a second time. `decider_contract.py:72` reads the same bare name off a raw tracker record, and the gate matches bare names. `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py:166-170` already records the first instance.

```text
policy.Grant.unmetered_at_issue     read in module at policy.py:2063
policy.SpendMeter.estimated_tokens  read in module at policy.py:2074
policy.WaitEvent.waited_s           read by _wall_clock_seconds

```

The record-field rule counts cross-module reads only, so the gate's advice here would delete working fields.

## Also correct two comments

`roles.py:58-62` says VALIDATE and REPAIR have a role and no phase yet. `loop._run_agent` dispatches both today, at `loop.py:465` and `loop.py:1611`. `roles.py:62` calls `loop_state.PHASES` the one that is behind, which is no longer true.

- When the dead-symbol gate and the vulture check run after the change, then no stale suppression is reported and no new finding appears.
- When a symbol is deleted, then its suppression entry is removed in the same diff.
- When the six load-bearing entries are read, then each carries a note that it is read within its own module.

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/roles.py`

payload.text:
A checkable predicate for this audit, 2026-08-08, from a five-source review of CLAUDE.md authoring guidance. The bead asked 'does this line change behaviour versus the default?' and had no way to answer it. Two thirds of that is now mechanical:

1. Already enforced by a hook, linter, formatter or CI gate? -> DELETE, point at the gate. Mechanically checkable: grep the rule's subject against .pre-commit-config.yaml, .ruff.toml, basicly.toml [[verify.checks]]. The repo's own quality-gate fragment already says 'Point at gates, don't restate them' - this applies that rule to the always-on file itself.
2. Derivable from a config the agent can read (pyproject.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .ruff.toml)? -> DELETE. Mechanically checkable.
3. Restates default model behaviour? -> DELETE. NOT mechanically checkable, and no source in the review supplied a method beyond 'run some tasks and observe whether the rule is followed'. This is still the open half.

Evidence quality of the review, stated because it bounds how much weight to give the above: FIVE sources, ZERO measurements. No A/B, no adherence rate, no n, no method anywhere. Three sources gave three incompatible size ranges (40-80 lines, 50-300 lines) against the vendor's 'under 200', none with a method. One source's whole token-cost argument rests on 'CLAUDE.md is prepended to every Claude turn', which contradicts the vendor mechanism (delivered once as a user message after the system prompt) - so its sizing advice is unfounded. Two of the five sell a product whose premise is their own recommendation.

Also settled while reviewing, and it removes a risk rather than adding work: one source claimed Claude Code auto-loads AGENTS.md, which would mean every consumer of  double-loads ~22k chars since we project BOTH .claude/CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Measured against a live session's own context: the repo has AGENTS.md at root, the context lists two CLAUDE.md files by path, and AGENTS.md is absent from that list. A differential, not an empty probe - the announcing mechanism demonstrably works. No double-load on the installed version. /context is the authoritative check and needs a human to run it.

Unused new idea, recorded not adopted: counting IMPERATIVES rather than characters or lines as the size unit. Cited as '150-200 instructions before compliance drops' with no citation, no study, no link. Do not gate on it; at most report it beside the existing counters.

SHARPENED PREDICATE, 2026-08-08: 'enforced for one family is not enforced'.

Predicate 1 says 'already enforced by a gate -> delete, point at the gate'. That is true ONLY PER AGENT FAMILY, and this repo projects to three. Worked example on require-explicit-confirmation, measured against .claude/settings.json permissions.deny (25 rules):

    HARD-DENIED on claude   rm -rf (4 variants); git push --force/-f/--force-with-lease;
                            push|commit --no-verify/--no-gpg-sign; git reset --hard;
                            git clean -f; filter-branch/filter-repo; .env read+edit
    PROSE ONLY              git checkout -- <path>; git restore; git stash; rebase

4 of 7 items are strictly weaker as prose than the deny-list already enforcing them, so predicate 1 would delete the section. It must not:

1. The 3 commands with NO deny rule (checkout --, restore, stash) are exactly the ones the fragment's second bullet enumerates, because nothing blocks them and each discards uncommitted work irreversibly.
2. Copilot and Codex have no config-level deny at all. Copilot gets --deny-tool only when OUR runner dispatches (basicly-lqz5); a human typing copilot gets nothing. For those families the prose is the whole control.

RULE: before deleting a line under predicate 1, name the enforcing mechanism FOR EACH projected family. Delete only when all are covered; otherwise keep it and make it say which families it is load-bearing for.

Deliberately NOT adding a per-item table of what claude denies: permissions.yaml changes and a table rots, while the fragment's generic sentence ('covers only some of these and varies by agent') stays true and was verified accurate.

AUDIT RUN 2026-08-09. The headline is that this bead's premise is wrong: the always-on layer is not
what puts AGENTS.md over its cap, and evicting from it would damage three families to fix one
family's problem while leaving the cause untouched.

## Measured

  .claude/CLAUDE.md                8628 / 9000    372 UNDER
  .github/copilot-instructions.md  8727 / 9000    273 UNDER
  AGENTS.md (codex)               13550 / 12000  1550 OVER

  always-on body, 20 fragments     8462 chars   -> all three families
  scoped body, 3 fragments         5091 chars   -> AGENTS.md ONLY

Confirmed by differential rather than by inference: `Platform-Hermetic`, `PureWindowsPath` and the
external-review text each appear once in AGENTS.md and zero times in the other two.

## Cause

claude.yaml and copilot.yaml set `exclude_scoped: true` and receive the scoped tier as separate
`.claude/rules/*.md` files carrying `paths:`. codex.yaml does not set it, because codex has no
glob-based instruction scoping and never loads a nested AGENTS.md below the cwd. So codex must
inline the whole scoped tier into its always-on file. 8462 + 5091 = 13553, which is AGENTS.md.

The overage is therefore structural to codex, not a symptom of an accreted baseline.

## Predicates 1 and 2, run anyway because they have value independent of the overage

Predicate 1, a gate already enforces it: 8 of 20 fragments name a subject found in
.pre-commit-config.yaml, .ruff.toml, basicly.toml or pyproject.toml - require-explicit-confirmation,
quality-gate, commands, core-rules, secure-coding, git-discipline, catalog-authoring,
project-defaults. Those 8 total 4057 chars.

**None of them is deletable on that basis**, and the sharpened predicate already recorded on this
bead is why: every one of those gates is a git hook or a lint run, which fires at COMMIT time, after
the tokens that produced the violation are already spent. That is the same argument factory-loop
section 11 item 8 now makes. require-explicit-confirmation is the worked example the earlier comment
already settled - 4 of its 7 items have no deny rule on any family, and copilot and codex have no
config-level deny at all.

Predicate 2, a glob could scope it: 5 of 20 name a path token (commands, project-overview,
copilot-defaults, claude-defaults, project-defaults). Scoping any of them helps claude and copilot,
which are already under cap, and moves the text INTO codex's inlined tier - making AGENTS.md worse,
not better. Predicate 2 is actively counterproductive here and that is a property of the projection,
not of the lines.

Predicate 3, the no-op test, remains the open half. No source in the 2026-08-08 five-source review
supplied a method beyond running tasks and observing, and basicly-agzx.1 is the bead that would
measure it.

## What this bead should become

Not an eviction. The decision is how codex carries a tier it cannot scope, and the options are
recorded for the owner: raise codex's cap toward its real budget (project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB
default - 12000 was our conservative pick, not the vendor's limit); or set exclude_scoped on codex
and accept that codex gets no test-discipline, external-review or tier-routing guidance at all; or
build a per-fragment opt-out so only some scoped fragments inline.

payload.description:
D36, decided 2026-08-09. Supersedes basicly-a3ab.9's D35 half, which assumed paths was a front
matter line it is not.

## Why a fence rather than a top-level key

schemas/skill.schema.json carries exactly the Agent Skills portable subset - name, description,
license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools - with additionalProperties false. That is
deliberate: a projected SKILL.md is meant to be portable to any host. `paths:` is outside the subset
and is claude-only. A top-level key makes every shipped skill unportable to buy one behaviour.

## Scope

- `claude:` (or per-target) object in skill.schema.json holding host-specific keys.
- skills.py `_optional_frontmatter` emits fenced keys only into the roots that understand them:
  .agents/skills gets the portable six, .claude/skills gets six plus fenced.
- `paths: ["**/*.py"]` on python-guidelines under the fence.
- agent.schema.json already establishes this shape - follow it rather than inventing a second one.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` green; .claude/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md
carries the paths key and .agents/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md does not; touching a .py file in
a fresh session loads the skill without it being named.

## Constraint

D25 - catalog guidance, human approves the diff.

payload.description:
Measured 2026-08-09 by the gate basicly-u2hl.45 shipped, and it fires today:

  skill listing is 2081 tokens against a 2000-token budget
  (1% of claude's 200000 adapter-default window), from 31 model-invoked entries

## Why this is a consumer defect and not a local one

basicly.toml raises this repo's claude window to 1000000, so locally the listing sits at ~21% of
budget and looks fine. A fresh `basicly install` inherits the 200000 adapter default and is over.
The overrun is therefore invisible to anyone measuring here, which is how it went unnoticed.

## Why it compounds

The host drops descriptions starting with the LEAST-INVOKED skills. 8 of 34 were ever exercised when
that was last measured. So the entries this overrun silences are the ones already hardest to reach,
and silencing them makes them harder still.

## The remedy is authoring, not code

Options, in the order that costs least:
- Move a skill to `invocation: user`. A user-invoked entry carries no description and contributes
  only its name - that is the saving the invocation axis exists to buy, and it is now asserted by a
  test.
- Retire a skill nothing invokes. The usage telemetry (`basicly usage`) is the input.
- Shorten the longest descriptions. harness-loop 509, python-guidelines 458, wsl 408, python 392.

81 tokens is the overrun. One user-invoked move is likely enough.

## Constraint

D25 - catalog content, so the diff goes to a human. Do not retire a skill on a zero-usage reading
alone without checking whether it was ever reachable: an entry whose description was already being
truncated is not evidence of a skill nobody wants.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly catalog lint` emits no listing-budget warning.

payload.close_reason: Researched and decided: strong form rejected on four independent grounds, divergence rule adopted as D34 in factory-loop section 2 with section 9.2 item 3 amended and item 10 added. Implementation filed as basicly-a3ab.9; the branch not taken filed as OQ-17.
payload.description:
## Context

Owner, 2026-08-09: "the code always has authority, not comments; comments that describe the
code must not exist, outside of best practices. If you need to read the comments to understand
the code, then the code is not of adequate quality, too complex, and potentially hard to
maintain." Proposed as an always-on rule.

**It conflicts with this repository's current practice**, which is the reason it needs research
rather than adoption. src/ and .basicly/core/ are deliberately and heavily commented, and most
comments explain *why* a thing is the way it is rather than what it does. factory-loop section
9.2 already carries the weaker form - "a docstring restating the signature passes and is
worthless" - and the proposed rule is stronger than that.

So the research question is not "are explanatory comments bad" in the abstract. It is: **which
comments does the evidence actually condemn, and does this repo's population fall inside or
outside that set.**

## What must be established

- What PEP 8, PEP 257 and the CPython developer guide actually prescribe, quoted, not
  paraphrased. Distinguish what they mandate from what they suggest.
- Whether the "self-documenting code needs no comments" position has empirical support or is
  a repeated assertion. Look for measurement, not for essays citing essays.
- The distinction the literature draws between what-comments, why-comments, contract comments
  and provenance comments, since the owner's rule targets the first and this repo's population
  is mostly the second and fourth.
- What the ruff, pyright and pydocstyle rule sets already enforce here, so a new rule does not
  restate a gate we already run.
- Ask why until the answer stops changing, and record the branch not taken. The repo already
  holds a sourced caution on iterated-why (Card, BMJ Quality and Safety 2017) so the method
  has to answer its own literature.

## Deliverable

A verdict with sources, and one of: the exact fragment text to add, an amendment to the
existing section 9.2 line, or a recorded decision not to add a rule with the reason. Per D25
an agent never lands catalog guidance without a human.

## Method

Dispatch the `researcher` agent authored in this session. It is projected to both agent
families but does not load until the host process restarts.
payload.title: Verify the comments-versus-code rule against authoritative sources before making it always-on

payload.text:
RESEARCHED AND DECIDED 2026-08-09. Verdict: reject the strong form, adopt the divergence rule.
Landed as D34 in docs/requirements/factory-loop.md section 2, with section 9.2 item 3 amended and
item 10 added. Implementation is basicly-a3ab.9.

Four independent grounds, any one sufficient:

1. It targets an empty set here. 120-block hand sample over src/basicly and .basicly/core:
   41% contract, 40% why, 16% navigation, 3% directive, 0% NARRATION. Two whole-population probes,
   each validated against synthetic narration first: narration-opener regex 0 of 1389 while catching
   5 of 5 synthetics; code-echo >= 0.50 gives 9 of 1139, every one a cross-reference.
2. The strong form contradicts PEP 8, which MANDATES a describe-what comment for non-public methods.
   Google's "never describe the code" - which .ruff.toml already pins via convention = "google" -
   is stated immediately after a REQUIREMENT to comment complicated operations.
3. It arms a live gaming path. Stripping standalone comments returns 36.3% of config.py's section
   9.3 ratchet tokens, 17.0% of merge.py's (frozen at exactly its current count) and 11.6% of
   loop.py's. python-guidelines/skill.yaml:72 already names comment deletion as the way to game that
   gate.
4. No budget. AGENTS.md is 13135 chars against codex.yaml's 12000 cap, and the parent epic exists to
   RELIEVE the always-on layer. Filed as basicly-a3ab.10.

Not agent-actionable either: "outside of best practices" is an undefined exemption and "if you need
to read the comments" is a counterfactual about a reader the agent cannot query. Neither is
falsifiable. Divergence is - did this diff change a line whose comment still describes the old
behaviour.

The literature does not settle it. "Comments are always failures" traces to Clean Code ch.4, a trade
book with no cited study. Measured work is mixed: Nielebock et al. 2018 (n=277) "the real effect of
comments on software development remains uncertain"; a 2026 eye-tracking study (n=20) spans a 30%
decrease to a 34% increase.

CORRECTS THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE: the body claims this repo's comments are mostly why and provenance
comments. Measured, the largest class is CONTRACT at 41%, why at 40%, and provenance is not a class
at all but a modifier present on 31.7% of blocks across classes. The conclusion survives; the stated
proportions do not, and 0% narration is a stronger claim than the one asserted.

BRANCH NOT TAKEN (Card 2017): that the owner is right and density is a symptom - that config.py
being 36% comments argues for decomposition, not annotation. Partial support exists (over-cap median
9.9 per 100 code lines vs 7.6 under-cap) but it is confounded by age and size. Filed as OQ-17.

Three measurements independently re-derived by the session before landing.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` is green, the projected
.claude/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md carries the paths front matter, and touching any .py file
in a fresh session loads the skill without it being named.
payload.title: Implement D34 and D35 in the python-guidelines skill

payload.text:
SPLIT 2026-08-09. D34 is done; D35 is blocked on a design decision this bead assumed away.

D34 LANDED in a684dd4: the "Comments - the divergence rule" section is in
.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml and projected to both roots. Full suite 3580
passed, all six projection gates green.

D35 IS NOT DONE, and the bead's assumption that it is a front matter line is wrong.

.basicly/core/schemas/skill.schema.json carries exactly ten properties with
`additionalProperties: false`, and the six spec-portable ones are deliberately the Agent Skills
portable subset - name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools - which the
2026-08-09 research confirmed against the vendor documentation. `paths:` is NOT in that subset. It
is claude-only, copilot honours it, and codex has no glob scoping at all.

src/basicly/schema.py has a `scope_paths` field, but it belongs to FRAGMENTS, not skills.
skills.py `_optional_frontmatter` emits only the four optional spec fields.

So adding `paths:` needs a vendor-fence mechanism for skill front matter that does not exist today,
and inventing one inline would put an unportable key into the artifact whose portability is the
reason the schema is shaped this way.

## The decision this now needs

Either add a `claude:` (or per-target) fence to the skill schema and teach the renderer to emit
fenced keys only into the roots that understand them, or decide that skill front matter stays
strictly portable and path scoping is expressed some other way.

Both are catalog-architecture calls, so they belong to a human under D25 rather than being picked
here. Whichever wins, D35's stated benefit is unchanged: zero always-on characters, and no
dependency on basicly-a3ab.1's eviction.

payload.description: Anthropic's 95-page volume 'How the two-thirds argument was found' documents a 54-hour, 58-agent research campaign. An adversarial review of a distillation of it found that roughly half of what looked new is already implemented here (researcher recall contract, killed-run salvage, docs-claims check, de-facto-blind reviewers). What survives is a small set of verification-economics practices this repo's own measurement-failure history independently argues for. This epic carries only the surviving items. It is explicitly NOT sold as a success recipe: the volume prints only the two winning runs out of 58, so no agent-side practice in it is evidence-separated from the 30 no-gos.
payload.title: Adopt the verification practices the RH campaign volume evidences

payload.description: The campaign's one agent-side practice with no equivalent here: attempt to break a claim with a concrete counterexample search before defending it, and autopsy each kill for the precondition that carried the weight. Five candidate inequalities died that way before the sixth held (orig.txt:4090-4212). Distinct from test-discipline (test structure), root-cause (post-hoc why) and reviewer (diff adversary). Wire into decomposer and decider claude.skills: 26 of 34 skills sit unused because nothing loads them.
payload.title: Add a falsify-first skill and wire it into the proposer roles

payload.description: The source run ranked its own failure modes in decreasing order of worry and named which single one could kill the result: none of 2-4 can move the constant, only 1 can. The shared evidence-discipline block now carries what-this-is-not and credence-reported-separately, but not the ranking or the discriminator. Needs a home - the change summary an implementer returns, or the release record the curator binds.
payload.title: Carry a ranked kill list and its discriminator on a change summary

payload.description: review_prompt now tells a reviewer not to start at line 1 and to go first at the weakest acceptance check, the inconvenient input and the path no test names. The campaign handed each referee a worked plan of attack against a specific joint. Ours is generic because no field records a plan's named risks; blocked on the shape a4q3.10 settles.
payload.title: Hand each reviewer the named risks instead of a generic attack plan

payload.description: The campaign brief carried a DISCIPLINE block: all substantive reasoning into files via Write/Edit, every assistant message under a cap, a report checkpointed within the first ten tool calls. Its payoff was not readability - a run died of an infrastructure error four minutes after writing its lemma to disk, and the coordinator read the dead directory, checked the proof by hand and resumed the same agent. Our worktree conventions cover part of this; the dispatch prompt says none of it.
payload.title: Tell a dispatched agent to keep its reasoning in files and checkpoint early

payload.description: The coordinator printed all 106 inherited survivor claims, sorted each into four deflating classes, reached the previous session's verdict independently, and then used the ledger only as a do-not-repeat list handed to sub-agents. Our handover is inherited claims with no such pass, and closed beads are not surfaced to a lane at all.
payload.title: Hand a lane the closed-bead ledger as a do-not-repeat list

payload.description: The record's decisive moves each followed a long silence: 32 minutes before the first substantive action, 22 before the pivot that produced the result, 91 in the follow-up run. The claude output style asks for a status report after every third tool call, which rewards tool-call throughput and prices the long think. Not obviously wrong - a human watching a session wants signal - but the tension is real and undecided.
payload.title: Resolve the status cadence against the long silent think

payload.description: A number that enters a claim gets computed a second, independent way and the two are asserted to agree. This is the practice that caught the only real numerical error in the campaign (a prime-side and zero-side Gram matrix agreeing to 1e-6 while their signatures disagreed by 33, traced to cond(M)=7.6e9). It is also the rule this repo's own memory argues for three times over: a band figure read as a spend figure, a delegated measurement in the wrong unit, a stale capability constant refuted by our own ledger. The always-on layer has 4 characters of headroom on copilot, so this is a rewording of the existing fragment, not an addition.
payload.title: Carry a second-channel clause in the external-facts fragment

payload.description: Four small edits that share one idea: a surprise is only detectable against a prediction, and a claim is only readable next to what it is not. (1) decomposer emits an expected outcome per child, not just a forecast diff size. (2) dispatch_brief carries the memo elements the campaign briefs carried: the forecast, read-X-for-Y, and handed-down work marked as derived-quickly-check-rigorously. (3) review_prompt carries the plan gate's named risks as attack-here-first; compatible with the no-pre-judging lint, which bans suppression directives and not targeting. (4) the shared evidence-discipline block gains state-what-this-is-not and report-credence-separately.
payload.title: Make a dispatched agent state its expected reading before it measures

payload.description: curator binds claims to evidence at SHIP and .scripts/docs_claims.py checks documented claims, but a capability claim added to README or the repo description outside a release path is uncovered. This repo has shipped two false claims in one session. Claim detection is judged rather than deterministic, so this belongs beside docs_claims as a verify check and not in a git hook, whose job is a deterministic floor.
payload.title: Extend the docs-claims check to consumer surfaces outside a release

payload.description: Two surfaces the campaign's coordinator had and this repo does not. basicly brief <bead> emits the research-memo brief for one bead, sharing the dispatch_brief assembler rather than forking it. basicly usage outcomes reports what each lane returned - result, no-go, ceiling, or reduction - so the kill rate is visible and a wall is distinguishable from a door; it goes under the existing usage command beside report/tracker/forecast/tuning, not at top level.
payload.title: Emit a dispatch brief for one bead and report per-lane outcomes

payload.description: skill.schema.json already allows license, compatibility, allowed-tools and metadata; skill_source.py validates them and skills.py projects them into SKILL.md frontmatter. The catalog-authoring skill mentions none of the four (0 hits against a working control of 1 for 'invocation'), and no skill source in the catalog sets metadata (0 against a control of 9 sources setting technologies). The plumbing is complete and unused because the authoring guidance never taught it. Fix the guidance, not the schema.
payload.title: Teach catalog authoring the four frontmatter fields it never documented

payload.description: metadata is an arbitrary string-to-string map that reaches projected SKILL.md frontmatter, which makes it the one place a skill can carry structured facts that scripts, hooks, the loop, dispatched agents and the tracker can all read without parsing prose. Unused today. Needs a designed key vocabulary before adoption rather than ad-hoc keys per skill: candidates are the loop phase a skill serves, a stability level, the bead that introduced it, and a supersedes pointer for retirement. Joins naturally with usage telemetry, which currently reports skills as used or never-used with no way to ask why a given skill should have fired.
payload.title: Give skill metadata a key vocabulary the harness can query

payload.description: The decomposer's output contract asks each child for the reading its demonstration should print, but implementation-plan.schema.json carries no such field (acceptance, budget_tokens, demonstration, depends_on, integrity, issue_id, scope, title) so the plan gate cannot refuse a child that omits it. Instruction without enforcement is this repo's own named defect class: a closed bead proves code exists, not that a gate binds. Either add the field to the schema and the plan gate, or stop claiming the practice is in force.
payload.title: Bind the expected reading in the plan schema so the gate can refuse a child without one

payload.description: The campaign's briefs pre-wrote literal verdicts - VIABLE, EMPTY, PARTIAL - and the agent returned one, so the coordinator could tell a route that was empty from a route that failed. Here the only agent-declared verdict is VALIDATION PASS/FAIL (dispatch_brief.VERDICT_PREFIX, consumed by validate_gate). Because of that basicly usage outcomes can only report dispatch outcomes - whether the process finished - and prints its own boundary saying so. A lane verdict is what would make the kill rate real, and it is the piece usage outcomes was built to consume.
payload.title: Let a dispatched lane declare a verdict the engine records

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the same guidance is projected with and without conditional relevance blocks the adherence difference shall be measured and reported with the arm each figure came from - check: the eval reports both arms and states whether the difference exceeds its own noise
payload.description:
## Context

`humanlayer/skills` `improve-claude-md` (**MIT**) claims Claude Code's system reminder -
this context may or may not be relevant - makes the model ignore parts of a CLAUDE.md, and
proposes wrapping conditional guidance in `<important if="condition">` blocks.

## Why this is ours to test and not to assume

We measured **recall**: 98% claude, 93% copilot (`basicly-agzx.1`). Their claim is about
**adherence**. Those are different quantities, and this repo's own standing rule is that
recall is an upper bound that may not be cited as evidence of quality. So our data neither
supports nor refutes them, and we have the instrument - `.scripts/recall_eval.py` plus the
path-scoped tier - that would settle it.

## Two constraints on the answer

1. **Claude root only.** `<important if>` is Claude-specific XML, and `basicly-a3ab.5`
   forbids one target's instruction file naming another target's enforcement mechanism. If
   it wins it becomes a projection detail in `.claude/rules/`, never `AGENTS.md`.
2. **The premise is an assertion about a vendor's internals.** Per the `interface-facts`
   rule, check the vendor's current documentation for what it says about instruction
   weighting before attributing a mechanism to the result. A measured difference with no
   explanation is still a finding; a claimed mechanism is not.

## Also adopt regardless of the outcome

Two portable rules from the same source, neither Claude-specific: cut any instruction a gate
can enforce, and cut code snippets in favour of file-path references. Both belong in
`basicly-a3ab.1`'s baseline audit.

## Scope

- `.scripts/recall_eval.py`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/**`
- `tests/**`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Measure whether conditional relevance blocks improve claude adherence

(Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2) the skill is present in the catalog and absent from

payload.text:
Investigated 2026-08-07, read-only against the live tracker (all reproduction attempts ran in a scratch copy under /tmp, never on `.beads/`). Three findings, and the first is a discrepancy that should be resolved before anyone builds on this bead.

## 1. THE MECHANISM DID NOT REPRODUCE on the pinned binary

Attempted three ways against `br 0.2.16` build `5cf4310` - the same binary installed since 12 July, i.e. unchanged since before the 2026-08-06 incident - in a scratch repo with the reported precondition (a smaller/stale local DB beside a larger committed export):

- clean stale DB
- stale DB carrying local unflushed edits
- stale DB beside a corrupted JSONL line

In every case `br create` and `br update` **auto-imported the newer JSONL first** and then proceeded without loss, and the explicit paths refused outright:

```
br sync --flush-only
Error: Configuration error: Refusing to export stale database that would lose issues.
Database has 3 issues, JSONL has 7 unique issues. Export would lose 4 issue(s)...
Hint: Run import first, or use --force to override.
```

`br sync --merge` also refused with a ConvergentCreation conflict.

So br carries its own Stale DB Guard and an auto-import-first behaviour, and both defended exactly the precondition this bead describes. This does **not** show the bead is wrong - a real incident was measured with concrete before/after record counts (426 over 612, 187 deleted, 47 open) - but the bead does not record the exact command and DB state that triggered it, and the obvious reading of its account is not reproducible today. Treat the mechanism as UNCONFIRMED rather than understood, and do not build a fix on the assumed trigger until it is reproduced or the trigger is narrowed.

## 2. A REAL, VERIFIED GAP, which is not the deletion itself

This repo launders a guard refusal into a silent commit. Verified at main:

- `merge.py:466` `reconcile_beads` - `br.try_run_br(repo_root, ["sync", "--merge"])`, return value discarded.
- `merge.py:520` `commit_tracker_state` - `br.try_run_br(repo_root, ["sync", "--flush-only"])`, return value discarded, then immediately `scrub_export`, `git add .beads`, `git commit`.
- `rg 'sync --status' src/basicly/` returns **zero call sites**. Nothing in the engine ever consults the status the `harness-loop` skill tells a human to check.

So when br's own guard refuses - as it demonstrably does - the engine does not notice and commits whatever `.beads/issues.jsonl` already held. That is a stale-commit correctness bug on a path that runs on every landing, and it is independently fixable regardless of how finding 1 resolves. Filed separately.

## 3. THE CUTOVER DOES NOT RETIRE THIS, and claiming it would be a false claim

Worth stating plainly because it is easy to assume otherwise:

- Dual write does not touch it. `_UNMIRRORED_WRITES = {"init", "sync"}` (`br.py:497`) excludes `sync` deliberately, so the mirror neither protects nor worsens these call sites. The risk is **orthogonal** to step 3, not exacerbated by it - which is the sequencing answer: dual write is safe to flip with this open.
- The flip to `owned` does not retire it either. `read_record`'s own docstring says br "is still written" at `MODE_OWNED`, and none of the four design steps removes `merge.py`'s two `sync` calls.
- It retires only when br invocations are actually eliminated. That is `basicly-wpc8` class 3, which names both call sites - not any of the four steps in section 5.

One mitigation is now real and was not before: since the 2026-08-07 import, records captured in the append-only ledger survive a shrink of br's export, so recovery no longer depends solely on `git show <good-ref>`. Incidental, not a designed mitigation.

## Recommended next step

Reproduce or narrow the trigger before fixing. The cheap, unambiguous work - checking the two `merge.py` return codes - is filed separately and does not depend on this question.

## Context

Found by the lane-D measurement survey 2026-08-14.

```text
decompose._quantile_high   decompose.py:1425-1440
tuning._quantile           tuning.py:365-375
```

The two bodies are the same algorithm character for character: `index = math.ceil(quantile * len(ordered)) - 1`, a clamp, and the observed-sample rule. `tuning.py:369-371` states the duplication is deliberate, because `tuning` sits above `decompose` in the declared tiers.

## The specific risk

`tuning` recommends values for the working-set maximum and the ceiling with its copy. `decompose` enforces the unsized bound with the other. If one is edited, for example to interpolate, then the recommendation and the enforcement diverge in silence. That is the context-ceiling failure shape this repository already paid for. No test asserts the two agree.

## The fix is a test, not a refactor

Do not move the function to satisfy a layering preference. A ten-line statistics module at the bottom tier costs more than the test.

## Acceptance

- When the suite runs, then a test asserts the two quantile functions return equal values over a shared sample table.
- When the table is read, then it includes a single-element input, both extreme quantiles, and tied values.

## Scope

- `tests/test_tuning.py`

## Depends on

The extraction of the spend forecast out of `decompose`, which moves `_quantile_high`. Write the test against its new home.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_tuning.py -q`.
payload.title: one quantile recommends a bound and a second quantile enforces it

payload.description:
## Context

`decisions.py:416` builds every escalation prompt from
`intake_corpus(repo_root, root_issue)` — **the root issue's own bead text**. So an epic's
"what is wrong today" list is not commentary; it is the fact base a machine reasons from,
and it is the one part of a bead nothing ever revisits. A child closes, the defect it
named is gone, and the parent's problem statement still asserts it.

Measured 2026-08-08 on `basicly-u2hl`. Four of its eight problem bullets were superseded by
its own closed children, and one was not merely stale but **refuted**:

```text
"park (Hold) exists as a word and re-admits the lane - a fail-open"   REFUTED by u2hl.3
"supervised rework dispatches a fresh agent instead of repairing"     SHIPPED  u2hl.4
"no gate anywhere measures module length"                             SHIPPED  u2hl.5
"CI gates guard one boundary of six"                                  SHIPPED  u2hl.1
```

## What it cost

Two escalations, `basicly-u2hl.14#c72fd936ab` and `basicly-u2hl.23#c72fd936ab`, quoted the
refuted `park` bullet verbatim and reasoned from it:

```text
"park (Hold) exists as a word and re-admits the lane - a fail-open on a human control
 point ... means park would not actually hold the lane. That leaves retry as the only
 unrefuted option"
```

Both abstained to a human. Both lanes then sat in `build` holding live worktrees while the
supervisor seeded three fresh lanes, and both were in fact already mergeable —
`git merge-tree` reported each branch clean onto `main`. The decider was not wrong given
its corpus. Its corpus was wrong.

## Why the design document does not save it

`docs/design/factory-loop-requirements.md` §5 corrected the `park` claim on 2026-08-08 and
**deliberately left the wrong row in place** with the correction beneath it, on the stated
grounds that "the wrong claim is the more useful record". That is sound for a human reader
and actively harmful once the same prose is seeded into a bead a decider consumes: the
decider reads the row and never reaches the correction. The convention needs a stated
boundary — a corrected claim in a machine corpus is edited in place and dated, never
annotated elsewhere.

## Steps to Reproduce

```text
$ uv run br show basicly-u2hl | grep -n 'park'
28:- `park` (Hold) exists as a word and re-admits the lane - a fail-open on a human control point

$ grep -n 'never re-admitted' docs/design/factory-loop-requirements.md
215:was never re-admitted to anything.

$ grep -n 'intake_corpus' src/basicly/decisions.py
416:    prompt = decider_prompt(item, intake_corpus(repo_root, root_issue))
```

Observed: the bead asserts a claim its own design document refuted, and the decider reads
the bead. Expected: a claim contradicted by a closed child cannot reach a decider unflagged.

`basicly-u2hl`'s text was hand-corrected on 2026-08-08 (commit `c71940a`). This bead is the
gate; that commit is one instance and proves nothing about the next epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an epic whose problem statement names a defect a closed child claims to have fixed,
  when a decider escalation is built for that epic, then the corpus marks the bullet as
  superseded rather than presenting it as current — check: a test seeds an epic with a
  bullet naming a closed child's defect and asserts `intake_corpus` output flags it.
- Given the same epic, when a human runs a check command, then the suspect bullets are
  listed with the child that supersedes each — check: a `[[verify.checks]]` entry (or
  `basicly policy` subcommand) exits non-zero naming the epic and the bullet.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly policy corpus-drift basicly-u2hl` (or the equivalent verify check) names
each problem bullet contradicted by a closed child, and exits non-zero while any is
unmarked.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `tests/test_cli_policy.py`
- `src/basicly/corpus_drift.py`
- `src/basicly/decider_contract.py`
- `.scripts/check_corpus_drift.py`
- `tests/test_corpus_drift.py`
- `tests/test_check_corpus_drift.py`
- `tests/test_decider_contract.py`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `.importlinter`
- `changelog.d/basicly-b9ef.fixed.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `100000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Keep an epic problem statement honest because the decider reads it as fact

payload.description:
## Context

Two open beads give opposite instructions about the same 106-record gap and nothing reconciles
them, so step 2 of the five-step cutover cannot be licensed and therefore neither can step 4.

- `basicly-vkh0.23` (P0): the import is a one-shot - `migrate.import_snapshot`
  (`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/migrate.py:573`) has no caller, no `main()` and no CLI surface
  (`basicly tracker` registers only `shadow`, `cli.py:4707-4712`) - so the ledger cannot be
  brought current and no fresh consumer can build one at all.
- `basicly-u4xu` (P1): "Do not fix this by re-importing. `import_snapshot` is upsert, so a
  re-import would quietly add the missing records and make the differential look cleaner - but
  the owned side would then be tracking the external side, and the agreement would prove
  nothing."

Measured 2026-08-13: `.basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl` holds 643 distinct records against
749 in `.beads/issues.jsonl` - **106 behind**, up from the 24 `vkh0.23` recorded on 2026-08-08.

**Both are right about different things, which is why this is a scope defect rather than a
disagreement.** `vkh0.23` is right that a consumer needs a re-runnable entry point. `u4xu` is
right that closing *this repo's* historical gap by re-import destroys the differential's
evidentiary value.

## The resolution this bead records

The step-2 differential's job is to prove **the dual write agrees**, not that history agrees.
Scope it to records whose first event postdates the flip, and record the pre-existing delta as
a declared, dated baseline rather than something to be closed. Then:

- `vkh0.23` builds the entry point, for consumers and for `fsck --rebuild`, with a refusal to
  run against a ledger that already holds post-flip events.
- `u4xu` flips to `dual` with the differential scoped as above, and the 106 historical records
  stay unimported and named.

Also settles what the differential's first run already reported: `clean: no, conclusive: yes`,
because 331 of 643 records carry a passing `verify` gate on the live tracker and none on the
ledger, "because no export carries a gate field for the import to have read"
(`basicly.toml:66-69`). That is a history artifact, not a dual-write disagreement, and the
scoping above is what stops it blocking the cutover forever.

## Proposed check

`basicly tracker shadow` takes the flip point from recorded config and reports agreement over
post-flip records only, naming the excluded historical count in its output. A test asserts a
pre-flip-only divergence does not make the run unclean, and that a post-flip divergence
does.
payload.title: Scope the shadow differential to writes after the flip so the cutover can proceed

payload.text:
[harness-info] the flip boundary landed, 2026-08-14

## What it resolves

`vkh0.23` and `u4xu` gave opposite instructions about the same 106-record gap and both were
right, because they are about **different records**. Step 2 proves the dual write agrees, not
that history agrees, so the pre-existing delta is now declared rather than closed.

## Two populations, two discriminators, and only one needed a decision

**The ledger side is free.** `migrate.py` stamps every extracted event with `imported_from`
(`migrate.SOURCE_KEY`), so a record whose `created` event carries it is history by
construction - no config, no flip point to keep in step with the tree. Measured: **643 of 643
created events carry it**, and `events.py` never writes it, so absence means native by
construction of today writers. This is the population-discriminator rule applied: bind on the
marker the producer writes.

**The reference side needed the owner decision.** A record br holds and the ledger lacks has
no ledger event to classify. `basicly tracker shadow --declare-history` captures that set once
into a committed sidecar beside the ledger. Owner chose the baseline file over a config flip
point, and the reason the flip point loses is that it cannot classify that population either -
the record has no event to place against it.

## The two acceptance halves, and four more directions

```text
history-only divergence  clean: True   (expect True)
post-flip divergence     clean: False  (expect False)
empty scope         conclusive: False  (expect False)
non-empty scope     conclusive: True   (expect True)
undeclared unknown       clean: False  (expect False)
declared unknown         clean: True   (expect True)
```

## Two controls the bead did not ask for, and both are load-bearing

**An empty in-scope population is inconclusive, never clean** - owner decision. Scoping leaves
it empty until the flip happens, so without this the bead would have handed `u4xu` a green
light computed over zero records, which is the failure `differential.py` separates `clean`
from `conclusive` to prevent.

**A second declaration is refused.** Re-declaring after the dual write has begun would absorb
a genuine failure into history and report the run clean - the same shape `u4xu` refuses
re-importing for, one artifact over. The set may only shrink.

## A defect the suite caught in my own design

The first `ScopedReport` **dropped `refusals`**, so a differential run against a derivative of
the owned ledger would have reported clean. `test_tracker_shadow_names_the_refusal_beside_the_agreement_it_voids`
failed and named it. Refusals are now carried through unscoped, with their own test: the
boundary decides which records are judged, never whether the reference was real.

## Placement was forced by measurement

`differential.py` has **+3 tokens of size headroom and 0.0pt of density headroom**, so the
scoping could not go there. `baseline.py` is a new kit module with one nameable
responsibility, and `differential.py` is untouched.

## The live run

```text
0 record(s) in scope; 643 imported, 0 declared (no date recorded)
  ... 200 undeclared and absent from the ledger
  ... 375 excused as history
  inconclusive: scope: 0 post-flip record(s) compared
clean: no   conclusive: no   exit 1
```

## What was deliberately NOT done

**The baseline is not declared on this repo.** It must be captured **at** the flip: records
created in br between now and `u4xu` would be historical but outside a baseline declared
today, and would read as dual-write failures. The declaration path was tripped in a scratch
copy instead - it declares, writes the file, refuses the second declaration, and clears
`undeclared`.

## Verification

`pytest -q` 3986 passed, 9 new. module-size, comment-density, test-naming, wired-or-deleted
and docs-claims all green.

payload.description:
## Context

`read_cost._text_tokens` is `len(text) // 4`. `basicly-u2hl.32` measured it against
`tiktoken` `o200k_base` on real payloads and recorded the error band in the estimator's own
docstring:

```text
prose (skill bodies)              +1.6%
beads issue json                 -10.7%
run-record json                  -16.4%
run-record markdown headings     -28.9%
run-record tsv                   -39.5%
```

That bead's remedy was a **prohibition** - document the band, forbid the one use the unit
cannot support - because a tokenizer was a confirmation-gated dependency change. The owner
gave that confirmation on 2026-08-08: a real tokenizer is worth a dependency.

The number matters beyond format comparison. Every figure the factory reasons about is
denominated in this unit: `SCOPE_FILE_READ_CAP` (4,000), the govern band (8K-132K), the
module-size ratchet's 79 frozen baselines, and every scope read-cost that decides whether a
lane dispatches. All of it is **code**, which is the population the estimator is worst on.

Measured 2026-08-08 with the estimator itself: `src/basicly` reads as ~453,800 tokens over
40,549 lines. If the code error sits anywhere in the structured-text band, that figure is
wrong by 45,000-180,000 tokens, and nothing downstream can tell.

## The two constraints that make this not a one-line swap

**1. It re-bases the module-size ratchet.** `.scripts/check_module_size.py` imports
`_text_tokens` from this module deliberately, "rather than respelling chars/4 a second
time" (`read_cost.py:18`). So changing the function changes the gate's measure, and all 79
entries in `[tool.module_size.frozen]` were recorded in the old unit. This is exactly the
failure shape section 9.3 of the requirements doc already documents for the import
exclusion: run against baselines computed on a different measure, the gate reported a clean
tree because every module had silently gained an allowance. **The baselines must be
recomputed once, in the same commit, and a control assertion must separate the recompute
from a fail-open** - the existing
`test_a_module_that_grew_by_code_still_fails_after_the_import_exclusion` is the pattern.

**2. The kit cannot have the dependency.** `.basicly/core/kit` imports the standard library
and nothing else, enforced by the `kit-boundary` verify check. Anything the kit needs must
keep a stdlib path.

## Design constraints

- **Determinism.** A tokenizer present in one environment and absent in another must not
  produce two different band verdicts for the same tree. Either the dependency is required
  and the fallback removed, or the fallback is retained and every consumer records *which*
  unit produced its number. A silent fallback is the worst of the three and is refused.
- `tiktoken` downloads its BPE vocabulary on first use by default. An offline or
  air-gapped consumer must not have a gate fail on a network call - the encoding file needs
  a vendored or cached path, and that behaviour needs a test.
- `read_cost` imports nothing from the package (`read_cost.py:16`); keep that.
- Encoding choice is a capability constant about a vendor, so per the plan's standing
  constraint it is **declared with recorded provenance and made falsifiable**, never pasted
  in as a fresher literal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a text payload, when its tokens are counted, then the count equals the tokenizer's
  own count - check: a test asserts `_text_tokens` equals
  `tiktoken.get_encoding(<declared>).encode(s)` length for prose, json, tsv and Python
  source fixtures.
- Given the module-size ratchet after the unit changes, when it runs on an unmodified tree,
  then it passes, and when a module grows by real code it still fails - check: the existing
  control assertion is retained and a test grows a module by code and asserts the failure.
- Given a repo with no network access, when any gate that counts tokens runs, then it
  completes without a network call - check: a test monkeypatches the network to raise and
  asserts the count still returns.
- Given the kit, when `kit-boundary` runs, then it still passes - check:
  `uv run basicly verify --mode full` reports `kit-boundary: PASS`.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly verify --mode full` passes all 20 checks with the recomputed baselines, and
`uv run python -c "from basicly.read_cost import _text_tokens; print(_text_tokens(open('src/basicly/cli.py').read()))"`
agrees with a direct `tiktoken` count of the same file.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/read_cost.py`
- `tests/test_read_cost.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Measure tokens with a real tokenizer instead of the chars per four estimate

payload.description:
## Context

Session 2026-08-14. The handover carried the trap in plain words - "measure headroom before writing
prose, not after a gate refuses you" - and it was still paid for **three times in one session**,
because there are two ratchets and measuring one feels like having measured.

Each time, `module-size` headroom was measured and `comment-density` was not:

```text
basicly-jn1x   runner.py 59.9% vs frozen 59.8, run_record.py 58.0% vs 56.9
               two rounds of prose-trimming after the gate refused
basicly-c357   differential.py had +3 tokens AND 0.0pt density; the placement
               had to be redesigned into a new kit module
basicly-ejdm.2 lane_split.py landed at 56.5% against a 50% cap on a new file
```

The module-size trap is the one this repo has written down most, which is probably why it is the
one that gets measured.

## The shape of the fix

One command that takes a path and reports **both** ratchets in one answer - tokens against the
frozen baseline or cap, and prose share against the frozen share or cap - so "measure headroom"
is a single call rather than two an agent will half-do. `check_module_size.tracked_modules` and
`check_comment_density.tracked_modules` already produce both halves; nothing composes them.

Neither script currently takes a path argument either, so today the measurement is a python
one-liner importing both from `.scripts/`, which is why it is skipped under time pressure.

## What this is not

Not a new gate. Both ratchets already bind at commit time. This is the read that lets a change be
sized before it is written, which is the only point at which the information is cheap.

The rationale at `claude_settings.py:191-192` says every managed hook script is stdlib only, so none of them needs the project environment. That reasoning applies to both families equally.

- When the Copilot hook host runs a projected hook in a repository with no usable project environment, then the hook runs.
- If the Copilot host cannot accept the flag, then the divergence is recorded at the composition site with the vendor evidence.

```text
contention.py:61   path not in scopes.get(lane, ())     literal string membership
merge.py:942       merge._scope_covers                  decompose.globs_overlap
```

So a lane that declares `docs/**` or `*.md` covers a configured append-only `CHANGELOG.md` at the landing, and the preflight counts it as a lane that contends without declaring.

Nothing refuses on this surface. The cost is a false `contend:` line. This repository records that an advisory `contend:` line is a finding an operator acts on: one such line named the exact collision under a green verdict and four hand-resolved rebases followed. A false one spends the same attention.

- When no lane declares coverage, then the report is unchanged.

`basicly-u2hl.54.1` made `validate-as-consumer` a required gate for a unit whose recorded

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly loop advance <id>` at the build to verify boundary briefs a repair and dispatches a
metered `claude -p` implementer when the landing gate failed. It does this without checking
whether a grant with remaining budget covers the dispatch.

Observed 2026-08-13 on `basicly-ef7t`. The L3 grant on `basicly-u2hl` was already spent
(315,547,342 of 300,000,000) and a decision saying so was sitting in the queue
(`basicly-u2hl#201ea56f76`, "the session is human-only until re-granted"). The advance
briefed and spawned the repair agent anyway. It ran for over 10 minutes and had written
nothing when it was killed; the spend is unmeasured because the run recorded no entry.

`--runner manual` is the workaround and it works, but it has to be remembered per
invocation.

Related but not the same defect: `basicly-rupz` covers the ceiling not stopping a dispatch
already started. This one is about never starting it.

## Proposed check

A test that puts a spent grant on the root, drives a unit to a failed landing gate, runs the
advance, and asserts no runner subprocess is spawned and the escalation names the missing
budget instead.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a spent grant on the root, with the decision already queued saying so - observed
   2026-08-13, `basicly-u2hl#201ea56f76`: "L3 grant token_budget spent (315547342/300000000
   tokens under this grant); the session is human-only until re-granted".
2. Drive a unit to a failed landing gate, then run the advance:

   ```sh
   uv run basicly loop advance <issue>
   ```

3. Observed on `basicly-ef7t`: the first advance reported
   `[blocked] build -> build: merge failed: verify full failed: pytest (rework 1/2); briefed a
   repair for gate 'merge'`, and the **second** advance spawned
   `claude --agent implementer --model claude-opus-5 -p ...` as a subprocess. It ran for over ten
   minutes, had written nothing when it was killed, and the spend is **unmeasured** because the
   run recorded no entry.
4. `--runner manual` prevents it, which is the workaround, not the fix: it has to be remembered
   per invocation and nothing warns when it is forgotten.

Distinct from `basicly-rupz` (closed), which covered a ceiling not stopping a dispatch already
started. This is about never starting one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a root whose grant has no remaining token budget, when an advance would brief and
  dispatch a metered repair, then no runner subprocess is spawned - check: a test puts a spent
  grant on the root, drives a failed landing gate, runs the advance, and asserts the runner was
  never invoked.
- Given that refusal, when the advance reports why, then it names the missing budget rather than
  the gate - check: assert the reported detail names the grant, so an operator is told what to do
  next.
- Given a root with a covering grant, when the same advance runs, then the repair dispatches as
  it does today - check: the false-positive case, asserted so the refusal cannot swallow a
  legitimate dispatch.
- Given a runner that is a manual handoff, when the advance runs with no grant, then the outcome
  is unchanged - check: a handoff spends nothing, so it must not be refused on budget.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop advance <issue>` on a unit with a failed landing gate and a spent grant
reports the missing budget and exits without spawning a runner, and the ledger gains no record.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop_repair.py`
- `tests/test_loop_repair_grant.py`
- `changelog.d/basicly-dbbh.fixed.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`
payload.title: Refuse a metered repair dispatch when no grant covers it
