payload.description:
## Goal

Cut unnecessary complexity, dead code and ambiguous concepts out of basicly, and leave behind the deterministic and non-deterministic mechanisms that make a one-off pass unnecessary ever again.

## Why the mechanism half is not optional

**This analysis has already been run once.** `basicly-tcmy` is the 2026-08-01 architecture and code review: three read-only passes over the engine, the projector and the instruction catalog. Its own baseline reads *43 modules in a six-tier DAG*. Measured 2026-08-14: **86 modules, 42,966 lines**, and **13 of its children are still open**.

So a read-only pass that emits a prioritised list is a thing this repo can already produce. What it cannot do is **drain the list against feature pressure**. Commissioning a second audit without the draining mechanism buys a second backlog with the same fate, which is why pass 2 below is a precondition of the work being worth paying for rather than a follow-on.

The supporting measurement: `src/basicly/` went **36,641 to 42,966 lines in one week** with the module-size ratchet, the comment-density ratchet, the noqa ratchet, vulture, lint-imports and wired-or-deleted all live and green. **A ratchet bounds a file. Nothing bounds the tree.**

## The three passes

**Pass 0 - re-verify the inherited backlog.** Take `basicly-tcmy`'s 13 open children against today's tree and classify each done, moot, still-real or worse, with the check that decides it. A finding cites a `path:line` and code moves; an unverified inherited finding is a claim, not evidence. Adding new findings on top of an unverified backlog is how you get two backlogs.

**Pass 1 - the survey.** The `architect` role, at its declared maximum tier, over the tree. Output is a dependency-ordered backlog shaped so the plan gate admits it unchanged, so the loop can dispatch it without translation.

Scope exclusions, each with a reason rather than an exemption:

- `br.py` and the 32 `run_br` call sites across 12 modules - they leave the tree at the tracker flip (`basicly-u4xu`). Auditing a scheduled deletion spends budget the calendar already spends.
- `runner.py`'s subprocess dispatch path - replaced by `basicly-xjd2`.
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/` - no frozen surface, no declared schema, no cache decision. An audit needs a specification to judge against, and `work-tracker.md` section 7 now records that one does not exist.

**Pass 2 - the mechanisms.** Deterministic and non-deterministic, both, because each covers what the other cannot: a gate binds without judgement and cannot read intent; a role judges and cannot bind.

Non-deterministic, all already specified and none of them new inventions:

- `basicly-feje` - map `reviewer` to a phase so the per-lens adversarial review runs on every lane instead of never.
- `basicly-u2hl.22` - derive `change-shape` from an AST. This is the call-chain instrument; without it "a call chain that does not make sense" is a thing only a human notices.
- RETROSPECTIVE as a state with the special-cause trigger, so the system decides *when* a structural finding is worth acting on instead of tampering on every single occurrence.

Deterministic:

- `basicly-u2hl.27` - the controller and actuator. Set point, four sensors and the dampener already exist; what is missing is the thing that selects the next target and dispatches it. **This is the bead that decides whether any of the rest lands.**
- A tree-level size budget, because the per-file ratchets were all green through a 17%-in-one-week growth.
- `basicly-r343` - the dead-code gate reads English prose in a schema as a field reference, so it can pass a real finding.
- `basicly-plhx` - the agent schema lets a role ship with no tier, so D26's routing rule can be defeated silently.
- `basicly-a3yi` - resolve a declared tier into the projected surface, so a tier declaration reaches a spawn at all.

## Ranking rule for the backlog

Dependency order, not severity order. Severity decides what is in; dependency decides what is next. The finding that unblocks the most other findings goes first.

## Acceptance

- Given `basicly-tcmy`'s 13 open children, when pass 0 completes, then each carries a recorded verdict of done, moot, still-real or worse together with the command that decided it, and no finding is restated without re-verification.
- Given the survey scope and its three exclusions, when pass 1 completes, then every emitted item passes the plan gate unchanged and carries the measurement that found it.
- Given the emitted backlog, when it is ordered, then the order is by declared dependency and the graph is acyclic.
- Given pass 2, when it completes, then a controller selects and dispatches the next remediation target without a human choosing it, and a tree-level growth signal exists that the per-file ratchets cannot mask.
- Given this epic closes, when the next release boundary arrives, then the survey is re-runnable as a dispatch rather than reconstructed as a session.
payload.title: Architectural and design analysis, and the mechanism that retires it

payload.text:
[harness-info] the epic hid its own children for twenty minutes, 2026-08-14

Recorded because the trap is cheap to repeat and the symptom looks like nothing.

I wired this epic with five blocks-edges to the pass-2 mechanism beads that live in other epics: u2hl.27, feje, u2hl.22, r343 and a3yi. The intent was to say the epic cannot close until those land.

Effect: all 32 children became invisible to br ready. The ready set held 110 issues and not one of them was mine.

The discriminator was a comparison, not a theory. Three other open epics - tcmy, u2hl and jr0l - have 36 ready children between them, and every one of the three carries ZERO blocks-edges of its own. This epic carried five. Removing them took the ready set from 110 to 131 and surfaced 17 of the 28, which is exactly the number that carries no declared dependency.

Two probes were wrong before that one. My reimplementation of br's readiness rule gave 43 with parent-child counted as a blocker and 139 with it ignored; br reported 110, so neither model was right and neither could explain the absence. Do not diagnose this from the export.

The rule, stated so the next reader does not re-derive it: an epic used as a fan-out root declares no blockers. Record the dependency in the epic body instead. The five mechanism beads are named in the pass-2 section of this epic's description and they lose nothing by not being edges.

[harness-info] what the five surveys judged CLEAN, 2026-08-14

The 28 filed items are what the pass-1 surveys found. This is the other half: the modules they read and declined to file against, with the reason. Without it the next audit re-reads all of them from scratch and re-derives the same verdicts.

Every verdict below is one lane's judgment at `main` around 027e903. Treat it as evidence with a date, not as a permanent property.

## Essential complexity, deliberately not split

- `loop.py`, 29,816 tokens. Its sections are one responsibility: advance one track. The previous pass already cut `dispatch_brief`, `repair_brief` and `plan_entry` out of it, and the remaining seams are thin and coupled to `advance`. Splitting it now would be a metric-driven cut, which this repo's own rules forbid.
- `merge.py`, about 15,400 frozen tokens, 3.8 times the cap. No divergence found between its halves, and its attribution seam is deliberately the one both landing paths share. No split proposed.
- Marker parsing across `run_record.marker_payloads`, `decision_marker._marker_parts` and `artifact_record`. Three wire formats with three parsers, each cross-referencing the others and owning different header semantics. Unifying them would trade three simple parsers for one configurable one.
- `policy`'s grant, spend and marker-counter machinery. The additive-never-reset counters, the two-baseline grant metering and the refund bounds are one coherent invariant set that fragments badly if cut mid-family.
- Single-responsibility and left alone: `lane_log`, `working_set`, `landing_gate`, `rebase`, `checkout`, `contention`, `planner`, `state`, `dropin`, `catalog`, `scaffolds`, and the write half of `projection`. Several carry their own split provenance in the module docstring. `planner`'s containment reasoning is load-bearing security.

## Looks like a duplicate and is not

- `GRANT_COVERAGE` against `PROPOSAL_COVERAGE` in `policy`. Approval against origination, deliberately one level apart, documented at both sites.
- The two landing paths, `merge.merge_queue` and the supervisor's `route_outcomes`. They share their primitives through `merge.landing_order` and `merge.record_pass_couplings`, whose docstring names itself the one seam both go through. Composition, not reimplementation.
- `tuning.read_dispatches` against `run_record.dispatch_history`. Documented, with provenance as the stated reason, and the one behavioural difference argued in place. Watch, do not fix.
- `mirror.py`. Its only consumer is `br.py`, which is excluded. It is the dual-write mechanism the tracker flip activates, so it is pre-wired rather than dead.
- The per-target template files. They genuinely differ where they differ. Only the five-line `agents_md.j2` is byte-identical across families, and the renderer-shim question stays with `basicly-tcmy.21` and its Codex and Cursor counter-argument.

## Measured consolidated, no action

- **Token counting.** Exactly two `chars/4` sites repo-wide, `read_cost.py:74` and `runner_usage.py:88`. Both cite the design and `_text_tokens` carries its measured per-format error table.
- **Pricing a dispatch.** One site, `spend_calibration.calibrate_spend`, reached everywhere through the documented re-binding shim. One converter, `decompose.spend_from_working_set`.
- **Units at production.** Every producing site states its unit. The one genuinely dangerous pair, dollars against credits, already has separate fields and a warning comment.
- **Layering.** No undeclared upward import in any surveyed module. The only function-level imports carrying the `PLC0415` suppression are the two cycles `.importlinter` declares, and its alerting mode forces their removal when a cycle goes.
- **Constant-argument dead branches.** An abstract-syntax-tree scan over twelve modules re-found only the known `PassSpendAdmission.unforecast` and nothing else. The scan re-finding the known case is its positive control.
- **One name, one meaning.** `lane`, `pass` and `track` each carry exactly one meaning across the supervision layer. `model tier` against `capability tie

## Context

Found by the `basicly-9rv0` lane 2026-08-14 while fixing the acceptance-heading predicate, and
deliberately left out of that lane's scope rather than widened into it.

`basicly-9rv0` established one definition of the acceptance heading in `plan_record` and made both
readers ask `plan_record.has_heading`. Three more sites still spell a plan-section heading
themselves, and each is the same drift risk one step weaker.

```text
supervise.py:1058     spells the acceptance heading as a dict key
decompose.py:1891     respells it, while using plan_record.SCOPE_HEADING and
                      plan_record.PLAN_HEADING in the same dict literal
policy.py:255         _SCOPE_SECTION = "## Scope", duplicating plan_record.SCOPE_HEADING
```

## Why this is weaker than the bug it came from, and still worth closing

The first two only **write** the heading, and they write it as a whole line, so neither can
currently disagree with the reader that parses it. `policy.py:255` is a second **definition** of a
literal `plan_record` already owns, which is the same shape `9rv0` just removed one instance of.

So the failure mode is not live today. It is that the next edit to any one of these four literals
has three silent twins, and this repository has paid for two-copies-that-disagree three times
already: `session_issue_ids` disagreed by 14 beads, and the context ceiling had two implementations
that reached opposite conclusions about a bead's fate.

## Headroom, measured before this bead was filed

`policy.py` carries 9 tokens of module-size headroom against its frozen baseline and 57.5 percent
prose against a 57.6 percent frozen share. `decompose.py` and `supervise.py` are both frozen too.
Removing a literal and importing the shared name is a net reduction in every one, so the ratchets
help rather than block here. Do not add explanatory prose to any of the three.

## Acceptance

- When a plan-section heading literal is searched for under `src/basicly/`, then exactly one
  definition of each exists and it lives in `plan_record`.
- When `supervise`, `decompose` and `policy` name a plan-section heading, then each reads it from
  `plan_record` rather than respelling it.
- When the change lands, then the module-size and comment-density figures for all three modules are
  at or below their frozen baselines.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_plan_record.py`

## Demonstration

A test in `tests/test_plan_record.py` that asserts every plan-section heading literal reachable from
`src/basicly/` resolves to the `plan_record` constant, plus `uv run pytest -q` and
`uv run basicly verify --mode fast`.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When loader declares the fragment source vocabulary then it names one constant and the guard reads it with no inline set literal left at that site
payload.description:
## Context

Left as a residual by the `basicly-3oxp` lane 2026-08-14, which tripwired five of the six schema and
Python vocabulary pairs and could not reach the sixth without a source change outside its scope.

Two schemas declare the same two-value vocabulary:

```text
.basicly/core/schemas/fragment.schema.json   "source": {"enum": ["core", "user"]}
.basicly/core/schemas/agent.schema.json      "source": {"enum": ["core", "user"]}
src/basicly/loader.py:256                    if fragment.source not in {"core", "user"}:
```

The Python side is an **inline set literal inside a guard**, not a named constant, so there is nothing
for a tripwire to import and compare against. The pair is the only one of six that stays uncovered,
and the new module's docstring records the gap so it does not read as covered.

## Why the one-line change is the whole fix

Hoist the literal to a module constant - `SOURCES = frozenset({"core", "user"})` - and use it at that
guard. `tests/test_schema_vocabularies.py` then takes the pair as a sixth row in its `SCHEMA_ENUMS`
table and both mutation directions become checkable, exactly as the other five already are.

This is the same defect class the lane's own bead names and that this repository has now paid for
four times in one session: two declarations of one vocabulary that can drift apart silently. A
tripwire on five pairs and nothing on the sixth reads as covered, which is worse than no tripwire at
all.

## A second, differently shaped restatement the bead never named

All four schemas - `fragment`, `skill`, `agent` and `block` - declare
`"schema_version": {"const": 1}` against `schema.SOURCE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`. Same two-declaration
shape, but a **const rather than an enum**, so it needs a differently shaped row than `SCHEMA_ENUMS`
carries. Both halves belong in this bead because the fix is one table gaining two kinds of row.

## Acceptance

- When `loader` declares the fragment source vocabulary, then it names one constant and the guard
  reads it, with no inline set literal left at that site.
- When `tests/test_schema_vocabularies.py` runs, then the `source` pair is compared in both
  directions like the other five.
- When any of the four schemas restates `schema_version`, then a check compares it against
  `schema.SOURCE_SCHEMA_VERSION` and fails if they disagree.
- When a member is added to either side of any pair without the other, then the test fails - proven
  by mutation in both directions, with each probe reverted by hand.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loader.py`
- `tests/test_loader.py`
- `tests/test_schema_vocabularies.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_schema_vocabularies.py -q` passes with six enum rows and four
`schema_version` rows; then add `zzprobe` to one side of each new pair, read the failure, and revert
by hand. Paste both failures - a tripwire nobody has watched fail is a claim.

## Headroom, measured at main 866b821

`tests/test_schema_vocabularies.py` is new and well under the 4000-token cap. `loader.py` is not
frozen for size. Measure before writing prose anyway; a lane today lost that argument twice.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When a landing rebases a lane that changed a declared generated path then the path is rebuilt from the merged tree regardless of whether the rebase raised a conflict
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-14 when lane `basicly-2j5a` bounced on `docs-claims` at its landing, hours after
`basicly-3w51` shipped the per-path rebuild that exists to prevent exactly that bounce.

The rebuild is triggered by a **rebase conflict**. Two lanes that each increment the same counter to
the same value produce **identical text**, so git auto-merges them cleanly, no conflict is raised, the
rebuild never fires, and the merged value is wrong by one.

Observed, not reasoned:

```text
base after basicly-3oxp landed          Test files | 163
lane basicly-2j5a's own block            Test files | 163   (correct in its pre-rebase tree)
after the rebase, no conflict raised     Test files | 163
the true value with both files present               164
```

The landing then failed on `docs-claims`, and regenerating in the rebased worktree produced 164.

## What worked and what did not, stated separately

**The gate failed safe.** `docs-claims` refused the landing rather than committing a false count, which
is the behaviour that matters most. Nothing wrong reached main.

**The mechanism did not do its job.** `basicly-3w51` exists so a lane does not bounce on a file it did
not author. Here the lane bounced anyway, and a human had to regenerate the block by hand and commit
it. That is the cost `3w51` was bought to remove, and it returns for every pair of lanes that move a
counter by the same amount - which for a counter incremented by one is the *common* case, not the rare
one.

## Why the conflict trigger is the wrong predicate

A conflict means the two sides disagree textually. What a generated block actually needs is a
rebuild whenever **its inputs changed**, and its inputs are the tree, not the file. Two lanes each
adding one test file change the input twice while writing the same text once.

So the predicate wants to be *the path is declared generated and this landing touched anything its
command reads*, or more simply: rebuild a declared generated path on every landing, unconditionally.
The command is deterministic and cheap - `docs_claims.py --fix --block` runs in well under a second -
so an unconditional rebuild costs almost nothing and removes a whole class of near-miss.

Note the tension to resolve rather than assume: `3w51` deliberately scoped the rebuild to conflicts
because the file is only **partly** generated and discarding both sides of the whole path would
destroy hand-authored prose. An unconditional rebuild must therefore stay block-scoped, which
`--block` already makes possible. That is why this is filed as a change to the trigger and not to the
resolution.

## Acceptance

- When a landing rebases a lane that changed a declared generated path, then the path is rebuilt from
  the merged tree regardless of whether the rebase raised a conflict.
- When two lanes each add one test file and land in sequence, then the second landing produces the
  true count without a human regenerating anything.
- When a rebuild runs, then hand-authored prose outside the marked block is unchanged, asserted
  against a lane that edited both.
- When the rebuild command fails or leaves a conflict marker, then the landing still bounces to the
  lane, as it does today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/rebase.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_rebase.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`

## Warning

`tests/test_rebase.py` sits at exactly the 4000-token cap with zero headroom and is unfrozen -
`basicly-e2mz.2` is filed against precisely that. Sequence this after it, or expect the gate to refuse
the first line you add.

## Demonstration

Land two lanes that each add one test file, in sequence, with no human intervention between them, and
read the generated block on main: it must equal the tree. Then land a lane that edits the
hand-authored prose beside the block and confirm the edit survives.
payload.title: the generated block rebuild is triggered by conflict so identical increments slip through

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the two fields are compared then the population and time window each covers is stated and whether they are comparable at all
payload.description:
## Context

Surfaced 2026-08-14 by the board solution design and **verified by hand at main**:

```text
$ uv run basicly loop session basicly-kjc5 --json
token_budget     4,000,000
spent_tokens     177,970,761
```

44.5x over. Alongside it, over 357 dispatches: $953.82 spent, a $24.64 single-dispatch maximum,
1.25B tokens, and 12 `[harness-overrun]` markers.

## The figure is unclassified, and that is the whole bead

Two readings fit the same number and they call for opposite responses.

**Unenforced ceiling.** The grant spend halt did not fire for this root, and a control this repo
counts as working is not working. That is a P0.

**Scope mismatch.** `token_budget` is a per-grant figure while `spent_tokens` accumulates over every
grant the root has ever held, so the two are measuring different populations and the ratio is
meaningless. That is a reporting defect, and a smaller one.

The evidence points at the second without settling it: `stopped_bound` shows **9 `spend` firings** in
the run records, so the ceiling demonstrably does fire, and `factory-loop.md` section 15.7 keeps it as
a control on exactly that ground. But a control that fires nine times can still have a root it never
covers.

This is the same shape as two findings already recorded here: a band figure is not a spend figure,
and a delegated measurement can use the wrong unit. Re-derive the number against the unit the claim
is denominated in before calling it either thing.

## Why it gates other work

`basicly-rn0o.3` puts a spend panel on a wall display, and unwatched spend is the argument that
carries that whole project. **A board built over an unclassified number is observability over a
possibly-broken control.** Settle this first.

## Acceptance

- When the two fields are compared, then the population and the time window each covers is stated,
  and whether they are comparable at all.
- If they are not comparable, then either the reported pair changes so a reader cannot form a false
  ratio, or the surface states the window each covers.
- If the ceiling genuinely did not cover this root, then the gap is named with the code path that
  skips it, and this bead is re-filed as a P0.
- When the answer is recorded, then it names the command that produced it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop session basicly-kjc5 --json` prints a pair a reader cannot misread, and the
recorded answer names the command that settled it.
payload.title: classify the kjc5 budget figure as an unenforced ceiling or a scope mismatch

payload.acceptance_criteria: When requirement 10 is read then the original restatement and its reason are still present beside the amendment
payload.description:
## Context

Owner decision 2026-08-14, taken with the board solution design (`basicly-rn0o`).

`work-tracker.md` section 4.3 requirement 10 currently reads **restated** - *on-demand, not
real-time* - with the reason recorded at the site: *"A generated Mermaid/DOT graph and a static HTML
board rebuilt on write is not real-time, and calling it that would be the same overclaim one notch
smaller."*

The board's wall mode attaches to a live source. The owner re-opened the requirement **explicitly
rather than routing around it**, and the amendment is deliberately minimal.

## The amendment

Requirement 10 stays exactly as written. One sentence is added permitting a live-attached mode, under
two conditions that keep the original overclaim guard intact:

- it must display its own age, and
- it must never use the words "real time".

The first is enforced mechanically rather than by discipline: `harness-board/v1` makes `freshness` a
**required** top-level key, so there is no code path that renders a value without rendering its age.
That is why the amendment is safe - the guard moved from a word in a document into a schema.

## Why this is filed rather than just edited

The restatement is a recorded decision with an argument attached. Overwriting it silently is the
defect this repository keeps naming: a document that outlives the decision it records sends the next
reader to re-derive it. The amendment must land with its own reasoning beside the original, and the
original must stay legible.

## Acceptance

- When requirement 10 is read, then the original restatement and its reason are still present.
- When the amendment is read, then it names both conditions and points at the schema that enforces
  the first.
- When the words "real time" are searched for in any board-facing surface, then they do not appear as
  a claim about what the board delivers.

## Scope

- `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md`

## Demonstration

`rg -n 'real.time' docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` returns the amendment's prohibition and no
claim, and the section reads coherently to someone who has not seen this bead.
payload.title: amend work tracker requirement 10 to permit a live attached mode that shows its age

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the full suite runs to completion then git config of the repository under test is byte identical before and after asserted by a test that reads it
payload.close_reason: fixed: conftest drops ambient GIT_* at import and a session guard holds the shared config bytes (c0dc86d)
payload.description:
## Context

**The test suite corrupted the developer's real working repository on 2026-08-14.** Found when
`basicly worktree create` failed and `git status` began answering *"this operation must be run in a
work tree"*.

Three keys were written into `<redacted:posix-home-path>`, and a branch and a
worktree registration were created in the real repository:

```text
core.bare = true                              detached the entire working tree from git
user.name = Test
user.email = test@example.com
basicly.identityAllowEmail = @company\.com$    made every real commit fail identity-guard
branch harness/wt -> 15786c4                  a fixture commit, in the real repo
worktree registration -> /tmp/pytest-of-<redacted:machine-username>/pytest-67/popen-gw3/
                          test_check_ignores_a_hook_edit0/repo.worktrees/wt
```

Timestamps place it inside one `pytest -q` run and exonerate the harness's own command:

```text
19:40:42   .git/worktrees/wt appeared
19:40:57   .git/config gained bare = true
19:41:18   basicly worktree create ran - the victim, not the cause
```

## Blast radius, and why it is a P0

Nothing was lost - all files were on disk throughout and `main` was intact - but for roughly one
minute the repository was unusable and **every gate in it was answering about the wrong tree**. A
developer who did not notice would have committed under a test identity, or been blocked by an
identity pattern no committed file declares.

It is also the sharpest possible violation of this repository's own rule that a fix must live in the
repo and never in the machine around it. Here the *tests* changed the machine around them.

## What is observed and what is hypothesis, kept apart

**Observed.** The leaked worktree path names `test_check_ignores_a_hook_edit_in_a_sibling_worktree`
(`tests/test_hooks.py:331`). At least seven test modules run `_git(repo, "config", "user.email",
"test@example.com")` - `test_verify.py:389`, `test_commit.py:581`, `test_checkout.py:29` among them.
The real repository gained a branch named `harness/wt`, which is the sibling-worktree naming those
tests use.

**Hypothesis, and it is the one that would make this a class rather than an incident.** A linked
worktree **shares `.git/config` with its parent repository**. So a test that creates a sibling
worktree and then runs `git config` against that worktree writes to the *shared* config - and if the
worktree was ever created against the real repository rather than a tmp fixture, the write lands
here. That would make every `_git(repo, "config", ...)` call in a worktree-creating test a loaded
gun, and it explains all three keys arriving together.

**Establish this before fixing it.** The wrong repair is to change the three call sites; the right one
depends on whether the fixture repo resolves correctly and the config write escapes anyway, or the
fixture repo itself resolved to the real root.

## Do not reproduce this carelessly

Running the full suite may corrupt the repository again. Reproduce inside a throwaway clone, and
snapshot `.git/config` before and after.

## Acceptance

- When the full suite runs to completion, then `.git/config` of the repository under test is
  byte-identical before and after, asserted by a test that reads it.
- When the suite runs, then no branch and no worktree registration exists in the real repository that
  the suite did not clean up.
- When a test needs a git identity or a config key, then it writes it to a fixture repository that
  cannot resolve to the developer's checkout, and a guard proves the resolution.
- Given the recorded incident, when the guard is applied to today's suite, then it names the site
  that produced it.

## Scope

- `tests/conftest.py`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `tests/test_commit.py`
- `tests/test_checkout.py`
- a new guard test

## Demonstration

Snapshot `.git/config`, the branch list and the worktree registry of a throwaway clone; run the full
suite; diff all three. All must be unchanged. Read the diff, do not assert it.
payload.title: the test suite writes git config branches and worktrees into the real repository

payload.text:
[harness-info] the mechanism is established and the trigger is `git push`, 2026-08-14

The bead was filed from one incident. It reproduced within ten minutes and the second occurrence
identifies the mechanism exactly.

## The trigger

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` wires `pre-push-script` to `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-push.py`, which runs the
`[[verify.checks]]` declared for mode **full** - and `full` includes the whole pytest suite. So **every
`git push` runs the suite, and the suite corrupts the repository it is pushing from.**

Observed twice, with different fixture identities each time, which is why this is a class and not one
stray write:

```text
first   user.name = Test           user.email = test@example.com
        branch harness/wt

second  user.name = Harness Test   user.email = harness@example.invalid
        branches harness/one, harness/two, harness/three, harness/wt
```

## The mechanism, now established rather than hypothesised

The leaked worktrees were checked out at **739eec0 - real main**:

```text
/tmp/.../test_three_lanes_each_adding_a0/worktree-one     739eec0 [harness/one]
/tmp/.../test_three_lanes_each_adding_a0/worktree-two     739eec0 [harness/two]
/tmp/.../test_three_lanes_each_adding_a0/worktree-three   739eec0 [harness/three]
```

A fixture repository of its own would carry a seed commit, not this repository's tip. So the test's
repo root resolved to the **real checkout**, and from there everything follows without needing a
second bug: `git worktree add` creates its branches in the real repository, and a linked worktree
**shares `.git/config` with its parent**, so every `git config` the test runs against that worktree
writes into the developer's config. That is how `core.bare`, the identity and
`basicly.identityAllowEmail` all arrived together.

`core.bare = true` is the one that bites hardest: it detaches the working tree, so `git status`,
`git add` and every worktree command answer *"this operation must be run in a work tree"*.

## What this changes about the fix

The earlier framing - audit the `_git(repo, "config", ...)` call sites - is the wrong layer. Those
calls are correct if `repo` is a fixture. **The defect is the resolution**: something lets a test's
repo root become the real checkout. Fix that and every downstream write is contained; fix the call
sites and the next test to create a worktree re-opens it.

Two candidate sites carry the evidence: `test_three_lanes_each_adding_a*` and
`test_check_ignores_a_hook_edit_in_a_sibling_worktree` (`tests/test_hooks.py:331`).

## Operational consequence until it is fixed

**Do not push without checking afterwards.** A push leaves the repository bare, with a test identity
and fixture branches. The repair is three `git config --local --unset` calls plus
`git worktree prune` and a branch delete - nothing is lost, but nothing warns either.

The acceptance criteria already written cover this; the demonstration must now include a push, not
only a bare suite run.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the producer is identified then it is named with the command and the environment dump that shows the variable set
payload.description:
## Context

Left open by `basicly-e2mz.15`, which fixed the damage and could not identify what caused it.

That lane established the mechanism beyond doubt: **git resolves which repository it is talking to
from the environment first and from `cwd` only afterwards**, so one inherited `GIT_DIR` retargets
every `git init`, `git config` and `git worktree add` the suite makes, whatever tmp path a fixture
passed. Reproduced exactly - `GIT_DIR=<clone>/.git pytest -q -n 4` produced the incident's signature
including the same two test names, and moved `main` itself.

**What it could not establish is who sets the variable.**

## What has been ruled out, each by probe rather than by reasoning

```text
pytest -q            in a clean clone   all three instruments byte-identical
pytest -q -n 4       in a clean clone   all three instruments byte-identical
a real gated push    from a clean clone clean, pre-push-script Passed
this git's hook env  pre-push receives GIT_EDITOR, GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_PREFIX only
                     commit-stage adds GIT_AUTHOR_*, GIT_INDEX_FILE - never GIT_DIR
the driving shell    `env | grep ^GIT_` returns GIT_EDITOR=true and nothing else
our own code         no GIT_DIR reference in src/basicly, .scripts or .basicly/core/hooks
```

So the suite is correct given a clean environment, and nothing obvious sets the variable.

## The claim that was wrong, recorded so it is not inherited

While the incident was live I wrote that **every `git push` corrupts the repository**, because both
observed corruptions followed a push. The lane's controlled push refutes it: a real gated push from a
clean clone left every instrument unchanged. Two events that both follow a push is correlation at
n=2, not a mechanism. The trigger is still unknown and must not be re-asserted as "push".

## Why this still matters now that the damage is fixed

`e2mz.15`'s guard is defensive: it drops the ambient git environment at import and holds the shared
config bytes for the session, so the *consequence* cannot recur. That is the right control and it
binds - it was probed by disabling the drop and watching it fail.

But an unknown producer of `GIT_DIR` in a developer's environment is a hazard beyond this suite. Any
tool that shells out to git inherits it, and the next thing it retargets may not have a guard in front
of it.

## Where to look, in order of prior

- `pre-commit` itself: it manipulates the git environment when running hooks, and both incidents
  happened while a pre-commit-managed stage was running.
- The harness's own subprocess spawns: `runner.py`, `worktree.py`, `merge.py` - check what environment
  each passes to a child rather than assuming it passes `os.environ` untouched.
- A shell snapshot or wrapper in the invoking environment.

## Acceptance

- When the producer is identified, then it is named with the command and the environment dump that
  shows the variable set.
- If no producer can be found, then that is recorded as an unresolved cause with the probes that
  excluded each candidate, and this bead closes as unexplained rather than silently.
- When any harness code spawns a git subprocess, then whether it sanitises the environment is stated
  and tested.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/`

## Demonstration

Reproduce a corruption from a clean clone by running the real workflow that produced it, with the
environment dumped at every subprocess boundary. Read the dump. If it cannot be reproduced, say so
with the attempts listed.
payload.title: the git dir variable that retargeted the suite has no identified producer

payload.acceptance_criteria: When check_module_size runs then wired_or_deleted.py and every module split out of it are at or under the 4000 token cap with no waiver
payload.description:
## Context

Split out of `basicly-kr7t` by owner decision 2026-08-14, after a lane proved the cap unreachable in
one cut.

`kr7t` now removes the r343 waiver and lands the reference-index extraction near 5,022 tokens. **This
bead reaches the 4,000-token cap**, and it needs a different shape than an extraction.

## Why one more extraction cannot do it

`field_findings`, `command_findings` and `suppression_findings` each construct `Finding`, which is the
gate's output vocabulary. Moving any one into its own module makes
`wired_or_deleted -> surface -> wired_or_deleted`, and the gate runs as `__main__`, so the cycle is
real rather than a lint opinion. Moving `Finding` into a surface module instead is a token shuffle
with no nameable responsibility behind it.

So the cut is: **`Finding` and `WiringError` into a shared substrate**, each of the three surfaces
becomes its own module, and `wired_or_deleted.py` is left as baseline plus rule plus `main`.

## The floor this has to clear, measured

The residual gate module cannot be all prose. Its docstring is 938 tokens at essentially 100 percent
prose and `BASELINE` is 1,121 tokens at 48.7 percent - a 1,483-token prose floor - so it needs **at
least 1,940 tokens of content below 27 percent prose** beside them or it fails the comment-density cap
even after passing module-size. Design against that number rather than discovering it.

## The trap carried over from kr7t

`basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml` carries both `".scripts/wired_or_deleted.py" = -6554` and
`count_delta = 1`. Dropping only the `count_delta` leaves the path with **no frozen entry at all**, and
any result over 4,000 then fails `_over_cap` immediately. Both go together or neither does.

## Acceptance

- When `check_module_size.py` runs, then `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` and every module split out of
  it are at or under the 4,000-token cap with no waiver.
- When `check_comment_density.py` runs, then each of those modules is under the 50 percent cap with no
  waiver, or carries one whose reason is cohesion and says so.
- When `wired_or_deleted.py` runs before and after, then it reports the same finding count from the
  same baseline, proven by mutation on each of the three surfaces.
- When the split lands, then no module imports back into `wired_or_deleted`, asserted rather than
  reasoned.

## Scope

- `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py`
- three or four new modules under `.scripts/`
- `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/test_wired_or_deleted.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- a test module per new module

## Depends on

`basicly-kr7t`, which removes the waiver and must not find this file changed underneath it.

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` reports the same count as before; `check_module_size.py`
and `check_comment_density.py` both report one fewer waiver; `uv run pytest -q` green.
payload.title: bring the dead code gate under the size cap by giving its surfaces a shared substrate

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a lane that writes only its own bead-named per-lane artifacts when the scope check runs then no scope-violation marker is recorded for those paths - check: uv run pytest tests/test_loop.py -k scope_violation -q
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
br comments list basicly-4f5g --json | rg scope-violation
br comments list basicly-0p8n --json | rg scope-violation
```

Observed, measured over the three lanes of session `basicly-u2hl:f9c58c11` on 2026-08-15 -
**3 of 3 lanes recorded a scope violation**, and two of them name an artifact the harness
itself requires that lane to write:

```
4f5g   basicly.d/basicly-4f5g.toml, tests/test_cli_loop.py, tests/test_loop.py
0p8n   changelog.d/basicly-0p8n.added.md, src/basicly/cli.py, tests/test_claude_settings.py
```

Expected - a lane is not reported for writing the file the engine told it to write.

## Context

`basicly.d/<bead-id>.toml` and `changelog.d/<bead-id>.<category>.md` are this repo own
per-lane conventions, introduced by `basicly-4746` and `basicly-ef7t` precisely so two lanes
can never write one file. They are named for the bead, so by construction they appear in no
bead `## Scope` - the same "a path every lane writes and no bead declares" class that
`[worktree] append_only_paths` exists for, except these need no serializing because each is
already bead-unique.

The cost is not a wrong landing - section 12.6 records an out-of-scope path and lands it, which
is correct. The cost is that the marker fires on every lane whatever the lane did, so a reader
learns to skip it, and the genuine finding in the same session is buried beside two false ones.
`tcmy.19` extracted a new module and repointed two callers at it - six undeclared paths that a
reviewer should see - and it reads identically to `4f5g` writing its own config fragment.

A gate that reports on every run reports nothing.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
payload.title: The harness records its own per-lane conventions as scope violations

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
uv run basicly loop supervise basicly-u2hl --label u2hl-pass-2
rg "^(wip|routed):" <the pass log>
```

Observed, two passes on 2026-08-15:

```
pass 1  wip: 0/5 unlanded downstream of build; 2 lane(s) admitted
        routed: provisioned 2 of 3 lane(s) selected by label
pass 2  wip: 0/5 unlanded downstream of build; 1 lane(s) admitted
        routed: provisioned 1 of 2 lane(s) selected by label
```

Both passes had **zero** work in flight against a headroom of five, and both left a
selected lane unprovisioned with no line saying why. Pass 2 then provisioned the
remaining lane on a later tick, after the first had shipped - so the two lanes ran
serially despite disjoint declared scopes and a wholly empty WIP bound.

Expected - when a selected lane is not provisioned, the pass says which lane and on
what rule.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug

The visible cost is throughput: pass 2 was two lanes with no scope overlap and it ran
them one after the other, so the pass took the sum rather than the maximum.

The invisible cost is worse and it is what happened here. A reader who sees
"provisioned 1 of 2" cannot tell a deliberate refusal from a defect, so the first
reading of pass 1 attributed it to `basicly-0p8n` being a `feature` and therefore not
a leaf track - which was true of that bead and does not explain pass 2, where both
`ho3t` and `u2hl.30` are leaf types with a readable `## Scope`. One plausible cause
was tested and refuted: `br blocked` does **not** propagate a blocked parent to its
children - measured, 45 entries against 32 with a real open blocks-edge, and every one
of the 13 extra is an epic with open children, with zero false negatives. So the cause
is still unknown, and that is the point.

`wip.py:169` admits `ready[:headroom]`, so the remainder is upstream of the WIP bound
in whatever produces `ready`. The line already prints on the admitted path
deliberately (`wip.py:105`); it needs to print on the withheld one too.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/wip.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: When module-size runs then it names any tracked module whose headroom against its cap or frozen baseline is below a declared threshold
payload.description:
## Context

Reported by the `basicly-3w51` lane 2026-08-14 and confirmed by hand at main after the merge.

```text
tests/test_rebase.py    tokens=4000   cap=4000   headroom=0
```

The module-size gate reports PASS, because 4000 is within the 4000-token cap. It is at the cap
exactly, and it is **not frozen** — so there is no baseline to fall back on. The next line added to
that file fails `module-size` outright, and the failure lands on whoever touches `rebase` next
rather than on whoever filled it.

## Why this is not the ordinary ratchet obligation

A frozen module above the cap may only shrink, and the first touch below 2x the cap must bring it
under. Both rules give the next author a payable move. A file resting on the cap with no freeze
gives none: it is green today and red on the next character, with nothing in the gate output saying
so. `module-size` prints a count of modules within cap or baseline; it does not print headroom, so a
file at zero is indistinguishable from one at two thousand.

Two separable pieces of work, and the second is the one that generalises.

## Acceptance

- When `tests/test_rebase.py` is split along a nameable responsibility, then each part is under the
  cap with room to add a test, and no assertion or fixture is deleted to buy the room.
- When `module-size` runs, then it names any tracked module whose headroom against its cap or its
  frozen baseline is below a declared threshold, so a file about to block the next lane is visible
  before it blocks one.
- When the headroom report exists, then it reports rather than blocks, because it has no firing
  history yet.

## Scope

- `tests/test_rebase.py`
- a new test module under `tests/`
- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `tests/test_check_module_size.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` prints a headroom line naming every module below the
threshold, and adding one assertion to each split part of `tests/test_rebase.py` passes the gate.

## Note on the population this belongs to

Measured at main on 2026-08-14, three other modules sit at or near zero: `tests/test_decompose.py`
0 against a frozen 28885, `src/basicly/policy.py` 9 against 32482, `src/basicly/decompose.py` 11
against 24498. Two lanes in this session each had to cut their own added prose to land, and one
moved its regression test to a different file because the natural home had 1 token free. That is the
recurring shape, not a single file.

payload.acceptance_criteria: While a run record carries stopped_bound when the health report scores that agent then the run is excluded from the failure rate and counted under its bound instead
payload.close_reason: fixed: a bounded stop leaves the failure-rate corpus, matching izpi's exclusion; claude 18 to 13 percent, no false regression (ab7f996)
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-14, minutes after `basicly-zdtx` wired `health_coverage` onto the supervisor pass
line. The first thing the newly-wired report printed was a regression flag, and chasing it found a
defect in the report rather than in the runner.

```text
drift:  REGRESSED claude: fail 80% over the recent 5 vs 16% over 158 baseline runs (+0.64)
```

The recent five, ordered by timestamp through `health._agent_entries` — the reader's own path, not a
re-implementation:

```text
2026-08-13T09:23:19  executed
2026-08-13T09:26:15.529625  failed
2026-08-13T09:26:15.553781  failed
2026-08-13T09:26:15.556898  failed
2026-08-13T09:26:15.625860  failed
```

Four failures inside 96 milliseconds is not four lane failures. It is one event. The records name it:
`basicly-ca42`, `basicly-ef7t`, `basicly-efw2` and `basicly-rrah`, each `phase: lane`, each after
about 2,256 seconds of real work, and each carrying `stopped_bound: spend`. The session grant was
exhausted and the ceiling stopped every live lane at the same instant.

## The defect

`health` counts `outcome == failed` without reading `stopped_bound`, so a lane our own spend ceiling
halted is scored as an agent that failed. Over the whole ledger:

```text
claude failures                 29
  of which stopped_bound=spend   9   our budget stopped the lane
  of which no bound             20   the dispatch actually failed
```

So the reported 18 percent failure rate is really 12.3 percent, and the flagged regression is
**entirely** the ceiling: the recent window holds one executed run and four grant halts.

That matters more now than it did yesterday. Yesterday the number lived behind a command nothing
invoked. Today it prints on the pass line an operator reads before every dispatch, and it says a
runner is degrading when the ledger says the budget ran out. A signal that fires on the wrong cause
is worse than one nobody reads, because somebody acts on it.

## Why this is the health report's bug and not the ceiling's

The ceiling behaved correctly. `factory-loop.md` section 15.7 keeps it as a control precisely
because it has recorded correct firings, and that count is now **9 rather than the 5 measured on
2026-08-08** — four of them the event above. Nothing here argues for changing the ceiling.

It is also the same population question `basicly-izpi` answered this morning one layer down:
`decompose.unsized_lane_tokens` and `spend_accuracy` both exclude `FAILED` from the corpus, because
a lane that never finished is not evidence of what a lane costs. `health` is the third reader of the
same field and the only one that does not separate the causes.

## Acceptance

- While a run record carries `stopped_bound`, when the health report scores that agent, then the run
  is excluded from the failure rate and counted under its bound instead.
- When an agent's report is printed, then the count stopped by a bound is stated beside the failure
  rate rather than folded into it, so neither number hides the other.
- When drift is computed, then the recent and baseline windows apply the same exclusion, and the
  minimum sample rule is checked after it — a window emptied by the exclusion must not flag.
- Given the four `stopped_bound` records of 2026-08-13, when the report runs, then claude is not
  flagged as regressed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/health.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_health.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly health` prints a failure rate that excludes bounded stops and names them separately,
and a supervised pass line reports no regression for claude against the committed ledger. A
regression test seeds four bounded stops in one window and asserts no flag, with a control of four
unbounded failures that does flag.

## Headroom, measured at main 3207fc6

```text
src/basicly/health.py     2404 / cap 4000     headroom 1596
tests/test_health.py      2860 / cap 4000     headroom 1140
src/basicly/supervise.py  frozen              check before adding a line
```
payload.title: the health report scores a lane our own spend ceiling stopped as an agent failure

payload.acceptance_criteria: While a unit rests in validate with its consumer gate red and rework below the cap when a pass runs then a repair is dispatched carrying the brief
payload.close_reason: fixed: _on_validate repairs in the lane worktree and re-lands the commit, split on the same ancestry proof _on_ship uses (00bed66)
payload.description:
## Context

Found by the `basicly-w88t` lane 2026-08-14 and verified by hand at main before filing. That lane
made the repair brief carry per-lens reviewer findings. It then reported that nothing dispatches
against the brief while the unit rests in `validate`, which makes the improvement unreachable on the
path it was built for.

Three observations, each read from the tree rather than reasoned:

```text
loop.py:374            the ONLY call to _repair_in_place, inside _on_build (starts 358)
loop.py:438            _on_validate calls _rework on a failed gate
loop.py:2114           _rework records an attempt and blocks, escalating at the cap
loop_state.py:191-192  ("ship", landed and not validating) precedes ("validate", landed and
                       validating), so a landed validating unit pins at validate
supervise.py:1577      ready_lanes takes _phase_of(...) == "build" only
```

So a failed `validate-as-consumer` spins on `_rework` to its cap and escalates to a human. No repair
is dispatched, and the brief the reviewer findings now populate waits in the worktree until the unit
is returned to build by hand. The composition itself works — the `w88t` lane demonstrated the brief
being consumed once the unit is at build — so this is a missing route, not a broken brief.

## Why the obvious fix is not obviously right

Two routes exist and each has a named hazard, which is why this is filed rather than taken.

Changing `derive_phase` so a failing validate falls back to `build` returns the unit to a phase whose
work is already merged into base. A repair commit then lands on a branch whose content is upstream,
which is the shape that lost committed work before `basicly-5vu4`.

Adding a re-land step to `_on_validate` keeps the phase and needs the same spend gate the validate
dispatch already carries. Note `basicly-xab3` landed the grant root into both supervised drives on
2026-08-14, so that gate now binds there — that half is done and should not be redone.

## This is the third defect from one landing, and that is the finding

`basicly-u2hl.54` made VALIDATE a real phase on 2026-08-13 under five acceptance criteria. Three
separate defects have since been found downstream of it, none of which any criterion named:

```text
basicly-xab3   a unit parked in validate was counted by the wip bound and advanced by nothing
basicly-w88t   reviewer findings reached a human and no code
this bead      no repair is dispatched from validate at all
```

Each close was correct against its criteria and incomplete against the system. Under
`factory-loop.md` section 3.2 a run of three is a special cause rather than three common ones, so
the disposal is a control and not three fixes. `basicly-xmhc` builds the state that would have fired
it. Recorded here because the pattern is the evidence and it lives in no single bead.

## Acceptance

- While a unit rests in `validate` with its consumer gate red and rework below the cap, when a pass
  runs, then a repair is dispatched carrying the brief, and the phase the repair commits against is
  named in the record.
- When a repair is dispatched from validate, then it checks `policy.spend_status` under the session
  grant root before it spawns, on the path `basicly-xab3` already gated.
- When the repair commits, then the commit is not stranded on a branch whose work base already
  holds — asserted against a landed unit, not only a pre-landing one.
- Given the rework cap is reached, then the escalation still fires as it does today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop_state.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Demonstration

Seed an L3 unit landed with `validate-as-consumer` red and reviewer findings on both lenses, run a
supervised pass, and read the dispatched repair prompt from the record. `uv run pytest -q` and
`uv run basicly verify --mode fast` green.

## Warning on headroom, measured at main 48ecc67

`tests/test_supervise.py` had 43 tokens of headroom before this session and `loop.py` is
comment-density frozen at 52.4 percent with the `w88t` lane having just spent its margin. Measure
before writing prose in either. Do not delete a pre-existing comment to buy room.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the catalog is built then code-reviewer is absent from every projected agent root and from the vendored set and reviewer is present in both
payload.close_reason: superseded: code-reviewer removed, the retired name resolves to reviewer, and reviewer carries an ad-hoc route (c3cdb33)
payload.description:
## Context

Owner decision 2026-08-14, settling the question `factory-loop.md` section 6.3 has carried open since
2026-08-08 under the heading *"Unresolved, and section 6.2 requires it resolved"*. The question was
carried by no bead at all, which is why it survived three sessions.

`code-reviewer` and `reviewer` differ in invoker and artifact but not in job. Section 6.2 requires
that overlap resolved rather than left as two things with one job, and D5 admits a role only when it
differs in tier, tools or artifact.

**The owner supersedes `code-reviewer`.** `reviewer` is the stronger definition and section 6.3 says
why: per-lens, adversarial stance, severity-bounded, and no cross-lens ranking. `basicly-feje` made
it reachable on 2026-08-14, dispatched once per lens at VALIDATE, and `basicly-w88t` made its
findings reach a repair. It is a live role with a contract; `code-reviewer` is a prompt.

## This is a breaking change to a shipped surface, and that is the whole difficulty

`code-reviewer` is projected into every agent root and **vendored to consumers by `basicly install`**.
Removing it deletes an agent a consumer may invoke by name today. Section 6.3 records exactly this as
the reason the decision was the owner's rather than the document's.

So it is not a delete. Three things have to happen together, and the order matters.

- The commit carries a `!` marker and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer naming the removed agent and its
  replacement. The `v0.6.0` audit exists because zero of 535 commits carried a marker, and plan
  section 7 makes the marker a gate after the freeze.
- A deprecation window ships before the removal, not with it. A consumer who invokes
  `code-reviewer` gets told what replaced it, on the surface they used, rather than getting nothing.
- `reviewer` must be invocable the way `code-reviewer` was. Today it is engine-invoked at VALIDATE
  only. A human who typed `code-reviewer` needs a route, or the supersession removes a capability
  instead of relocating one.

That third point is the one that can turn this into a regression, and it is where the work is.

## What must not be taken from the removal

The two lenses are `correctness` and `security`, chosen deliberately in section 6.5 because a lens
whose axis a gate already covers spends tokens to restate a green check. Maintainability was refused
because ruff, pyright, vulture, `lint-imports`, `module-size`, `comment-density` and `noqa-debt`
ratchet it mechanically. Do not widen the lens vocabulary to cover what `code-reviewer` used to say.

## Acceptance

- When the catalog is built, then `code-reviewer` is absent from every projected agent root and from
  the vendored set, and `reviewer` is present in both.
- While a consumer invokes the superseded name, when the harness resolves it, then it reports the
  replacement rather than failing silently or resolving to nothing.
- When a human wants an ad-hoc review, then a documented route to `reviewer` exists that does not
  require a VALIDATE dispatch.
- When the change lands, then the commit carries a breaking marker and a changelog fragment naming
  the removed agent.
- When the lens vocabulary is read after the change, then it is still exactly `correctness` and
  `security`.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/agents/code-reviewer/`
- `.basicly/core/agents/reviewer/`
- `src/basicly/roles.py`
- `tests/test_roles.py`
- `tests/test_agents.py`
- `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` section 6.3
- `changelog.d/`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly agents-check --all-default-roots` passes with `code-reviewer` gone, a fresh
`basicly install` into a scratch repo writes `reviewer` and not `code-reviewer`, and invoking the old
name reports the replacement. Read that output rather than asserting it.

payload.close_reason: Gap 1 closed: .github/workflows/improvement-loop.yml is an independent call site and test_the_workflow_alone_credits_the_improve_command proves the credit is non-circular by passing the workflow as the entire wiring corpus, tripped in four directions. Gap 2 was already met and recorded (basicly-j73p); the one-lane bound re-observed against real tracker state. The schedule trigger is deliberately deferred by owner decision and filed as basicly-www5, so a closed bead is not read as an unattended loop.
payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-u2hl.27` landed the controller and the actuator on 2026-08-14 (`95974ec`). Its acceptance
criterion is met and the command works — reproduced independently on merged main:

```text
improve: set point: 4000 tokens (read_cost.SCOPE_FILE_READ_CAP)
improve: sensor:    .scripts/check_module_size.py measured 317 tracked module(s)
improve: error:     69 above the set point, worst first; 2 waived
improve: lanes:     0/1 unlanded lane(s)
improve: selected:  tests/test_supervise.py - 60089 tokens, 56089 over the cap (1 of 69)
improve: dropped:   68 candidate(s) not selected; the next run re-ranks them
```

Two gaps remain, both disclosed by the lane rather than found afterwards. Neither is a defect in what
landed; each is a thing the bead's own framing implies and the narrowed scope could not reach.

## Gap 1 — nothing schedules it

The bead says the loop "runs on a schedule". There is no cron entry and no workflow step, because
`.github/workflows/*` and `basicly.toml` were outside the dispatch scope. Today
`basicly loop improve` is a front door an external scheduler must call, and nothing calls it.

**The wiring credit is circular and that is the tell.** `wired-or-deleted` passes this module because
`.scripts/*` is a `COMMAND_SITE_GLOB` and the controller's docstring names `basicly loop improve`.
The script names the command and the command runs the script. A real schedule entry is what makes
that credit non-circular, and until then the gate is reporting a wiring that does not exist — the
same fail-open shape the plan's own risk table names first.

## Gap 2 — the actuator has never filed a real bead

`dispatch()` is covered with a faked `br.run_br` and was never run non-dry, because the dispatch that
built it was forbidden from mutating `.beads/`. A later attempt to exercise it from the base checkout
was refused by the host's permission classifier, correctly: it writes to the live tracker.

So the `br create` argv shape follows `decompose._create_child` and the body goes through
`policy.compose_body` by construction, and that is **derived, not observed**. This repository's
standing rule is that a closed bead proves code exists and not that a path works, and that entering a
forward path is the only way to learn what it accepts.

The first real run is also the cheapest test available: the controller already selects
`tests/test_supervise.py` at 60,089 tokens against a 4,000 cap, which is a legitimate target, so the
bead it files is work worth having rather than a probe to prune.

## Gap 3, smaller — one property of four

The bead's table lists four sensors: module size, the noqa count, C901, and unmatched test files. The
controller drives module size only. It says so in its own output rather than implying wider coverage,
which is the honest form, but three sensors the repo already owns are unused.

## Acceptance

- When a scheduler entry exists, then `basicly loop improve` runs without a human invoking it, and
  `wired-or-deleted` credits the command from that entry rather than from the script's own docstring.
- When the actuator runs non-dry for the first time, then the bead it files is read and recorded here
  with its id, and it passes the plan gate unchanged.
- When a target is selected under the bound, then a second run before that lane lands no-ops, observed
  against the live tracker rather than a fake.
- If a sensor beyond module size is added, then the output names which property it drove.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/`
- `basicly.toml`
- `.scripts/improvement_controller.py`
- `tests/test_improvement_controller.py`

## Demonstration

A scheduled run files one lane against the live tracker; its id is recorded on this bead; a second run
before that lane lands prints the no-op line and its reason. Read the filed bead, do not assert it.
payload.title: the improvement loop has no scheduler and its actuator has never filed a real bead

payload.text:
[harness-info] the actuator ran non-dry for the first time, 2026-08-14

Owner approved the tracker write. Both halves of the acceptance criterion are now **observed against
the live tracker** rather than derived from a fake `br.run_br`.

## The dispatch

```text
improve: sensor:    .scripts/check_module_size.py measured 319 tracked module(s)
improve: error:     69 above the set point, worst first; 2 waived
improve: lanes:     0/1 unlanded lane(s)
improve: selected:  tests/test_supervise.py - 60089 tokens, 56089 over the cap (1 of 69)
improve: dispatch:  basicly-j73p filed, labelled improvement-loop
```

## The bound, second run, against real tracker state

```text
improve: lanes:     1/1 unlanded lane(s): basicly-j73p
improve: no-op:     bound to 1 open lane; land basicly-j73p before the next run selects another
```

That is the half the fixture could only simulate. It holds.

## The filed bead passes the real gates

`policy.definition_of_ready(repo_root, "basicly-j73p")` returns `ready=True, missing=()`, and
`plan_record.section_entries` parses all three sections: four scope globs, four plan entries
(integrity `L2`, budget `70000`, no dependencies, a backticked demonstration), and one acceptance
criterion carrying its own check. So the `br create` argv shape and `policy.compose_body` produce a
bead the plan gate admits unchanged, which was previously derived from `decompose._create_child`
rather than observed.

## What the live run found that the fixture could not

The third scope glob is malformed: `tests/test_test_supervise*.py`. It is generated at
`.scripts/improvement_controller.py:179`, which prefixes `test_` to the stem unconditionally, so a
target that is already a test module gets the prefix twice. Filed as its own bead.

This matters more than one bad line. The plan's own section 9.3 measurement records tests as the
larger half of the over-cap population — 42 of 95 test files over the cap, holding the worst
offender — so most of this controller's future targets are test modules and most of its future beads
will carry the same dead glob.

**The glob is inert rather than harmful today**, and the reason is worth stating so nobody
over-corrects: the real file is covered by the first glob, so the lane's scope is complete. What is
lost is that a scope entry matching nothing is a declaration the contention preflight cannot use, and
a lane whose declared scope contains dead entries reads as wider than it is.

[harness-decision] manual dispatch first, cron later - owner 2026-08-14

The bead says the improvement loop "runs on a schedule". The owner takes the smaller step first.

**Build `workflow_dispatch` only. No `schedule:` trigger yet.**

Two reasons, and the first is the one that makes this bead worth doing at all. It makes the wiring
**non-circular**: today `wired-or-deleted` credits `basicly loop improve` because `.scripts/*` is a
command-site glob and the controller's own docstring names the command - the script names the command
and the command runs the script, which is a gate reporting a wiring that does not exist. A workflow
entry is a real, independent call site.

Second, the actuator has filed exactly **one** bead ever (`basicly-j73p`, 2026-08-14, its first live
run). Watching it file a few more under a human's hand before it runs unattended is cheap, and the
one-lane bound means an unattended loop that misbehaves would still only produce one bad bead at a
time - but only if the bound holds, which is itself only observed once.

Note this would be the repository's **first** scheduled workflow: `.github/workflows/` holds
`basicly.yml`, `pages.yml`, `quality-gates.yml` and `release.yml`, and none carries `schedule:`.
Adding cron later is a one-line follow-up on this same file.

CI files are on the confirmation list. This comment is the confirmation for `workflow_dispatch` and
**not** for a cron trigger.

[harness-info] the workflow_dispatch call site landed, 2026-08-14

## What landed

`.github/workflows/improvement-loop.yml` - `workflow_dispatch` only, per the owner decision on
this bead. It installs `br` (the controller reads its one-lane bound off the live tracker even
when it files nothing, so `br` is a requirement of the dry run and not only of the actuator) and
runs `uv run basicly loop improve --dry-run`.

## Gap 1 is closed, and the control assertion is what closes it

The complaint was a **circular** wiring credit, not an absent one, so a workflow that merely
mentions the command would leave the same defect with a second cause. The proof is
`test_the_workflow_alone_credits_the_improve_command`: it passes the workflow file as the
**entire** wiring corpus, so nothing under `.scripts/` contributes, and asserts
`wired.command_findings([("loop", "improve")], wiring) == []`.

Tripped in four directions before it was trusted, because an assertion that only ever returns
"credited" cannot tell a real wiring from an empty string:

```text
as written        credited      (expect credited)
command removed   NOT credited  (expect not)
empty corpus      NOT credited  (expect not)
loop supervise    1 finding     (expect 1)
```

The last is its own test - the negative half - so the corpus is not a blanket pass.

## Why the workflow dry-runs, stated at the site rather than inferred

A live run in CI files a bead into an ephemeral checkout. Persisting it needs `contents: write`
and a push to `main` from CI, which is far past what this entry was confirmed for. Filing stays a
human running `basicly loop improve` from the base checkout, which is exactly the "under a
human`s hand" the owner decision asks for.

## The bound re-observed

Running the workflow`s exact command on merged main:

```text
improve: sensor:    .scripts/check_module_size.py measured 323 tracked module(s)
improve: error:     69 above the set point, worst first; 2 waived
improve: lanes:     1/1 unlanded lane(s): basicly-j73p
improve: no-op:     bound to 1 open lane; land basicly-j73p before the next run selects another
```

Exit 0. The bound holds against real tracker state a second time.

## What is deliberately NOT met

Acceptance bullet 1 reads "runs **without a human invoking it**". `workflow_dispatch` cannot
satisfy that by construction - it is a human pressing a button. The owner deferred the `schedule:`
trigger on this bead and the comment above is explicit that it confirms `workflow_dispatch` and
**not** cron. The deferred half is filed rather than left in this bullet, so a reader does not
score a closed bead as an unattended loop.

Gap 3 (three unused sensors) is untouched and was never in this scope.

## Verification

`pytest -q` 3974 passed - two new. `wired-or-deleted` 39 known findings, none new. `module-size`,
`comment-density`, `ruff`, `ruff format`, and the 9 commit hooks all pass.
