payload.close_reason: fixed: a derived scope entry is kept only if it resolves, or is the target's own split pattern; 214 dead entries removed (306bf7f)
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-14 by the first non-dry run of the improvement actuator, which is what
`basicly-e2mz.6` exists to exercise. A fixture could not have found it: the fake `br.run_br` never
rendered a scope for a target whose name already begins with `test_`.

```text
.scripts/improvement_controller.py:178   f"{path.parent.as_posix()}/{path.stem}_*.py"
.scripts/improvement_controller.py:179   f"tests/test_{path.stem}*.py"
```

Line 179 prefixes `test_` unconditionally. For the target `tests/test_supervise.py` the stem is
already `test_supervise`, so the rendered glob is `tests/test_test_supervise*.py`, which matches
nothing. `basicly-j73p`, the first bead the loop filed, carries it.

## Why this is not one bad line

The plan's section 9.3 measurement records tests as the larger half of the over-cap population - 42
of 95 test files over the cap, holding the worst offender. The controller ranks by distance above the
cap, so most of its future targets are test modules and most of its future beads carry the same dead
entry.

## What is actually lost, stated so nobody over-corrects

The glob is inert rather than harmful. The target itself is covered by the first glob, so the lane's
scope is complete and no file is left undeclared. What is lost is that a scope entry matching nothing
is a declaration the contention preflight cannot use, and a lane whose declared scope carries dead
entries reads as wider than it is - which is the over-declaration the plan already records as the
reason nine u2hl children are band-refused on read cost.

## Acceptance

- When the target's stem already begins with `test_`, then the rendered scope carries no
  double-prefixed glob.
- When any scope is rendered, then every glob in it either matches a path in the tree or is the
  target itself.
- Given `tests/test_supervise.py` as the target, when the scope renders, then it is exactly the
  target, its sibling split pattern, and `pyproject.toml`.

## Scope

- `.scripts/improvement_controller.py`
- `tests/test_improvement_controller.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop improve --dry-run` against a tree whose worst offender is a test module, with
the rendered scope read from the output; and a regression test that asserts every rendered glob
resolves to at least one path.
payload.title: the improvement loop renders a double prefixed test glob that matches nothing

payload.acceptance_criteria: While a projected agent has no catalog source when basicly agents-build runs then the projection is removed from every agent root it was written to
payload.close_reason: fixed: agents-build prunes an orphan projection and agents-check reports it, keyed on the same generated marker uninstall uses (18f371f)
payload.description:
## Context

Found by the `basicly-e2mz.5` lane 2026-08-14 while removing `code-reviewer`, and confirmed by
reading `agents.sync_agents` rather than reasoning about it.

`sync_agents` prunes a projected agent only when a **technology selection** excludes its source. It
never prunes a projection whose source has simply been deleted from the catalog.

So a consumer who already installed `code-reviewer` keeps
`.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` and `.github/agents/code-reviewer.agent.md` after upgrading, and
`basicly agents-check` never notices, because it iterates catalog **sources** and a deleted source has
nothing to iterate.

## Why this is worse than an untidy file

The orphan is a live agent definition on the consumer's host. It carries the retired contract, it is
matched for delegation by description, and it will be selected in preference to nothing. The harness
side of the supersession works - `roles.SUPERSEDED_ROLES` redirects the retired name - but that
redirect is only consulted when the harness resolves a role. A human or a host that spawns the orphan
by name bypasses it entirely.

It also generalises past this one removal. Every future catalog deletion has the same shape: the
authoring repo goes clean, every consumer keeps the artifact, and the projection gate reports up to
date on both sides. That is a fail-open gate, and the plan's own risk table names believing a gate
because its bead closed as the first risk.

## What the removal shipped instead, so this is not re-derived

The limit is stated in three places rather than hidden: the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer on `c3cdb33`,
the `changelog.d/basicly-e2mz.5.removed.md` fragment as a manual step, and `factory-loop.md` section
6.3. None of those is a mechanism.

## Acceptance

- While a projected agent has no catalog source, when `basicly agents-build` runs, then the projection
  is removed from every agent root it was written to.
- When `basicly agents-check` runs against a tree holding such an orphan, then it reports the orphan
  rather than reporting up to date.
- Given a consumer tree carrying `code-reviewer.md` in both roots, when the consumer upgrades, then
  both files are gone and no other projected agent is removed.
- When a projection is pruned, then the generated-marker rule still governs it - a hand-written file
  a consumer added is never deleted.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/agents.py`
- `tests/test_agents.py`

## Demonstration

Install into a fresh scratch repo at an older catalog, delete a source, upgrade, and read the agent
root: the orphan is gone and every other agent survives. Then run `basicly agents-check` against a
hand-planted orphan and read it fail. Exercise both; the second is the gate half and it is the half
that was silent.
payload.title: a projected agent whose catalog source was deleted survives on every consumer

payload.acceptance_criteria: When sync_agents removes a projection then it returns the reason it removed it rather than the path alone and the command line prints the returned reason
payload.description:
## Context

Found by the `basicly-e2mz.8` lane 2026-08-14 and confirmed by hand at main after the merge.

`cli.py:1808` hardcodes one reason for every path `agents.sync_agents` returns:

```text
cli.py:1808   print(f"Removed {...} (excluded by technology selection)")
cli.py:1693   the identical string on the skills path
```

`e2mz.8` gave `sync_agents` a second reason to remove a file - a projection whose catalog source was
deleted. The path printed is correct; the parenthetical is not. A consumer watching an upgrade is
told a technology selection removed the file when the source was deleted instead.

## Why this is not cosmetic

The two causes have different consequences for a reader. *Excluded by technology selection* means the
file will come back when the selection changes, so nothing is lost. *Orphaned* means the source is
gone and the artifact is retired. A consumer who reads the first and means the second will wait for a
return that never comes.

It is also the same defect class this session has now paid for three times: one string standing for
two facts. `basicly-9rv0` was two predicates that disagreed, `basicly-7jb5` was one gate name spelled
three times, and this is one message covering two causes.

## The skills path already had it

`cli.py:1693` prints the same string for resources `_prune_orphans` removed **because they left the
source**, so this is a pre-existing shape rather than one `e2mz.8` introduced. That matters for the
fix: correcting only the agents site would leave the skills site lying, which is how a defect class
survives its own bead.

`check_synced_agents` already returns `(path, reason)` pairs and words them correctly - the check half
is right and only the build half is wrong. The reason vocabulary therefore already exists; nothing
needs inventing.

## Acceptance

- When `sync_agents` removes a projection, then it returns the reason it removed it rather than the
  path alone, and the command line prints the returned reason.
- When `sync_skills` removes a resource, then the same holds on that path.
- Given a consumer whose technology selection excludes an agent and a second whose source was
  deleted, when each upgrades, then the two removals print different reasons.
- When the check half runs on the same trees, then its wording and the build half's agree.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/agents.py`
- `src/basicly/skills.py`
- `tests/test_agents.py`
- `tests/test_cli_catalog.py`

## Demonstration

Install into two fresh scratch repos, deselect a technology in one and delete a source in the other,
upgrade both, and read the two lines. They must differ and each must be true. Read the output; do not
assert it.
payload.title: the build prints one removal reason for two different causes

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-08 on the five-lane pass `basicly-u2hl:bc7cc925`. **Three of five lanes
bounced on the merge queue**, and every bounce was a shared anchor no bead declares:

```text
docs/plan/implementation-plan.md   the docs-claims generated block (module count, test count)
basicly.toml                       [[verify.checks]] - .12, .14 and .15 each appended an entry
pyproject.toml                     [tool.module_size.frozen] and [tool.noqa_debt]
```

Any lane that adds a module, adds a test file, or wires a check rewrites all three.
`loop preflight` printed the warning before the pass and it was dispatched anyway:

```text
contend:   no append-only path declared ([worktree] append_only_paths)
```

## Why the existing mechanisms do not cover it

`[worktree] append_only_paths` is empty **on purpose** - its own comment records that
`CHANGELOG.md` was the whole list and that serializing every lane was the price of
detecting one collision. `basicly-4746` replaced it with one fragment file per lane, so
the collision became **impossible by construction** rather than detected. That is the
pattern to apply here; serialization is the second-best answer and is explicitly
deprecated in the config comment.

## Cost this bought

Re-dispatch does not discard work - the worktree keeps its commits - but each bounce costs
a fresh process boot and re-orientation. On `basicly-u2hl.14` the three re-dispatches were
5.6M tokens (16% of the bead) and roughly 19 minutes of a 51-minute lane (37% of its wall
clock). Pass slot utilisation was 42%.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given three concurrent lanes that each add a source module and wire a verify check, when
  the pass lands them through the merge queue, then none bounces on `basicly.toml`,
  `pyproject.toml` or `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` - check: a test provisions three
  branches each adding one check entry and one frozen-list entry, runs the merge queue over
  all three, and asserts zero rebase conflicts and zero rework recorded.
- Given a consumer running `basicly verify`, when the checks are assembled from per-lane
  fragments rather than one array, then the same check set runs as before - check:
  `uv run basicly verify --mode full` reports the same check names and count as on the
  parent commit.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly verify --mode full` lists the identical check set, and a three-branch merge
queue test lands all three with no bounce.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `.scripts/check_noqa_debt.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Make the three shared landing anchors collision proof by construction

payload.description:
## Context

A bead's `## Scope` is read by two gates that want opposite things:

```text
merge scope-collision   wants the declaration COMPLETE  - every path the diff touches
decompose band          wants the declaration SMALL     - it prices what the scope READS
```

Declaring honestly for the first necessarily inflates the second. Measured on
`basicly-u2hl.14`, 2026-08-08, inside a single landing:

```text
13 scope entries   78,709 est   -> merge refused: 16 undeclared paths
27 scope entries  197,646 est   -> band ceiling 132,000 exceeded; raised to 200,000
35 scope entries  245,466 est   -> band ceiling 200,000 exceeded; raised to 248,000
```

**Nothing about the change grew.** The same diff was always that wide; only the
declaration moved. The lane chased its own tail between two gates, and the operator
raised `DEFAULT_WORKING_SET_MAX` twice in one landing to let it through — which is a
ratchet being moved by an artifact rather than by evidence.

## Why the existing beads do not cover it

`basicly-esxp` argues read-cost never predicted change cost, and `basicly-tcmy.34`
fixed the forecast unit. Both take for granted that one scope field feeds both
consumers. This bead is that assumption: even a perfect estimator over a complete
declaration reports a number that grows with declaration completeness, so the two
gates cannot both be satisfied by one field however well either is calibrated.

## Steps to Reproduce

```text
$ uv run basicly loop run <bead> --autonomy L3
[blocked] ... changed <paths> outside its declared scope ... the plan is wrong, not the merge
# declare those paths, then:
[blocked] ... completed at an estimate of N, above working_set_max M; raise it to at least K
# raise M, re-run, and the collision gate names the next undeclared path
```

Observed: two ceiling raises in one landing, neither earned by a larger change.
Expected: declaring a path completely does not make the lane look bigger.

## Shape

Separate the two readings. `## Scope` stays the ownership declaration the merge gate
reads and the collision graph learns from — complete by construction, and free. The
band reads a distinct input: either a declared working set (what the lane must *read*,
a subset), or a derived one (`basicly-agzx.2`'s AST localisation), or the diff-size
forecast `basicly-esxp` wants. Which of the three is the design question; that they
must not be the same field is the finding.

The two ceiling derivations recorded in `config.py` must then be re-read as measuring
declaration completeness, not working set, and the comment there says so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bead whose scope is widened to declare paths it already touched, when the
  band sizes it, then the estimate does not increase - check: a test sizes one lane at
  two declaration completenesses over an identical diff and asserts the band verdict is
  unchanged.
- Given the merge scope-collision gate, when a lane declares every path it touches,
  then it lands without a band refusal caused by that declaration - check: a test lands
  a lane whose complete declaration exceeds the old ceiling and asserts no ceiling
  violation is recorded.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop preflight <epic>` reports the same band verdict for a bead before
and after its scope is completed against the merge gate's own finding.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/working_set.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`
- `tests/test_working_set.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none

## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
The defect holds verbatim: `loop.py:867-879` still passes only the issue id, with no
requirement, scope, plan or prior finding. **The evidence and the remedy are both stale.**

**The 254x is two incomparable populations.** Re-measured over 346 records on 2026-08-13 it is
now 320x - and it compares a `decide` dispatch averaging **12 seconds** to a `lane` averaging
**979 seconds**. That is a one-turn classification against a multi-hour build, so it cannot
isolate briefing from work type. This repo's own recorded lesson is "a cost prior from the
wrong population"; do not cite this ratio as the cost of a short prompt. The causal claim that
a ~1.1M-token floor is "bought by the instruction" has **no instrument behind it**: there is no
per-lane split between context acquisition and implementation.

**Two mechanisms are now recorded as if they were one fix.** `factory-loop.md` section 8.3
still names the engine-assembled durable brief. `implementation-plan.md:224` substitutes
`--resume --fork-session`, calling the floor "a cache miss, not tokens". These are different
designs with different costs and the choice must be made explicitly, not inherited.

**The fork figure does not hold in our shape.** Probed on claude 2.1.231, 2026-08-13: 19.06x
same-directory, but the denominator is the ~21k-token host floor, not a repo corpus - against a
lane's 8.66M mean that floor is 0.24% of a lane. And a fork from a **different working
directory degrades to 5.4x**, because cwd and a git-status snapshot sit inside the cached
prefix, worktrees of the same repository included. Every lane is dispatched at
`cwd=worktree_path` (`supervise.py:2623`), so fork-per-lane plus worktree-per-lane **is** the
degraded case. See `basicly-w20y` for the documents-side correction.

**Acceptance criterion 3 was unmeasurable when written** and is now measurable:
`basicly-i4gg` (closed 2026-08-13) landed the claude cache split that a before/after ratio
needs.

---

## Context

**A dispatched lane is told to go and read; a dispatched decider is handed its corpus. The
same model on the same repo costs 254x more for the first.** Measured 2026-08-08 over the
whole of `.basicly/usage/run-records.json`:

```text
phase    n    mean tokens   mean $   mean s   failed
lane    77      8,124,617    6.28      942    16/93 = 17.2%
build   28     11,564,149    8.70     1163     4/153 =  2.6%
decide  24         31,991    0.23       14     5/29  = 17.2%
```

`loop.dispatch_prompt` (`loop.py:858`) is ~90 words and passes **only the issue id**:

```text
"You are in a git worktree dedicated to the tracked issue <id>. Read AGENTS.md for the
 repo rules, run `br show <id>` for the requirement and acceptance criteria, implement
 the work, and commit it on the current branch referencing that issue id. ..."
```

No requirement text, no scope, no plan, no architecture, no prior finding. The prompt
*instructs* the agent to rebuild what the dispatching session already holds, and the
~1.1M-token floor every lane pays before its first edit is bought by that instruction.

Observed cost of the same waste twice in one session: `u2hl.15`'s lane independently
re-derived pyright's dot-directory behaviour that had been measured, written down and
committed to its own bead an hour earlier.

Per unit of output, the floor dominates small work: `u2hl.16` cost **\$0.077 per changed
line**, `u2hl.14` **\$0.010**.

## What this bead is NOT

It is **not** "make the prompt longer". `factory-design.md` §D6 records a deliberate
decision that every dispatch pays fresh context priming, grounded in Laban et al.'s
measured **-39% on multi-turn** degradation. That decision is about *conversation* history,
not about *facts the engine already knows*, and this bead must not overturn it by accident.

The docs already contain the shape that resolves the tension: the **report file**
(`agent-roster-design.md:664-670`, `gates-and-rework-design.md:219-235`) — an agent
inherits through a durable, structured artifact rather than through a replayed window.
`basicly-u2hl.18` already shipped two such artifacts (`implementation-plan`,
`change-summary`) as typed records, so the mechanism exists and has a schema.

## Shape

Give the dispatch prompt a **brief assembled by the engine** from what it already has:
the bead's requirement and acceptance criteria (already read to gate it), the declared
scope, the plan artifact, and any finding recorded on the bead. Every one of those is a
tracker read the engine performs anyway.

Two constraints from this repo's own measurements:
- **Selection, not serialisation** (D21): `br ready --json` costs 36.9% of a lane and its
  five-field projection costs 1.7%. Assemble the brief from named fields, never by pasting
  a payload.
- **Our own vocabulary, not `br`'s** (D22): `br` is being removed; the brief names our
  record fields so only the adapter changes at the flip.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatched lane, when its prompt is built, then the requirement, acceptance
  criteria, declared scope and plan artifact are present in the prompt - check: a test
  asserts each field appears in `dispatch_prompt` output for a fixture bead.
- Given the same bead dispatched twice, when the briefs are compared, then they are
  identical - check: a test asserts prompt determinism, preserving D9's diffability.
- Given a measured pair of lanes before and after, when mean tokens-to-first-edit are
  compared, then the briefed lane is lower - check: recorded on the bead from
  `run-records.json`, with the before figure taken in base first.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop run <bead> --runner manual` prints the brief the lane would receive,
and it contains the bead's acceptance criteria and scope rather than an instruction to go
and read them.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none

payload.text: Investigated 2026-08-13 before dispatch - take this, do not re-derive. FEASIBLE: runner_envelope.stream_object returns json.loads(line) UNNARROWED, so StreamEvent.data already holds message.content including the tool_use block. Verified against a real captured fixture (tests/test_runner_subagent_stream.py:34-73, live Claude Code 2.1.226): a tool-calling turn carries {type: tool_use, name: Agent} AND its own usage block in the same event. payload.title: Report a lane token spend split into acquisition and implementation

payload.text: Two measured caveats that decide whether this child's number means anything - established 2026-08-13, do not re-derive. (1) ATTRIBUTION NEEDS A PAIRING RULE: a tool_use turn's usage is the cost of EMITTING the call; the tool's RESULT lands in the NEXT assistant turn's cache_creation_input_tokens. So summing tokens on tool_use turns measures the wrong thing - a read's cost is not on the turn that asked for it. State the pairing rule explicitly and test it. (2) USE SHARES, NEVER ABSOLUTES: per-turn usage over-reports against the run record by 1.46x to 1.79x (runner.py:1672-1678, measured over four lanes), so an absolute token figure derived from the stream is in a different denomination from the grant it would be compared against - this repo has already killed a lane by mixing those two. (3) The instrument is claude-only: codex emits no per-tool event this stack parses. That matches the ledger, which holds only claude and manual dispatches, but the report must say so rather than implying coverage.

[harness-info] the split instrument landed, 2026-08-14

## The demonstration found a defect the unit tests did not

The bead`s demonstration line asks for the command on **a repo holding one real lane
transcript**. This repo holds none - the engine has never written a lane `.jsonl` here - so it was
run against a transcript built by driving the **real** `lane_log` writer and `runner._emit` with
the live Claude Code 2.1.226 stream captured in `tests/test_runner_subagent_stream.py`.

The first pairing implementation paired against the **immediately preceding transcript line**. On
that real transcript it reported:

```text
basicly-demo: acquisition 0%  implementation 0%  unclassified 0%  unattributed 100% (52869)
```

A confident 100% measuring nothing. The cause is visible in the transcript itself:

```text
assistant  tokens= 26234 tools=[Agent]     <- the call
user       tokens=     0 tools=[]          <- the forwarded result, no usage
assistant  tokens=     0 tools=[]
assistant  tokens= 26635 tools=[]          <- the turn that pays for the answer
result     tokens=     0 tools=[]
```

The `user` event sits between the call and its answer, so a line-adjacent rule breaks every chain
in a real transcript. **Nine unit tests over hand-built turns all passed against it**, because
none of them interleaved a usage-free event. Corrected to pair against the last tools emitted
before a turn that carries usage, and pinned by
`test_a_usage_free_event_between_a_call_and_its_answer_does_not_break_the_chain`.

After the fix, on the same real transcript:

```text
basicly-demo: acquisition 0% (0)  implementation 0% (0)  unclassified 50% (26635)  unattributed 50% (26234)
```

The 26,635 that paid for the subagent`s result land in **unclassified**, which is correct: the
captured lane`s only tool is `Agent`, and bucketing a subagent spawn as either read or write would
put a guess inside the number `ejdm.4` is judged by.

## The three caveats, each carried into the artifact

1. **Pairing** - implemented as above, and the docstring names both wrong versions.
2. **Shares, never absolutes** - the report leads with shares and labels the tokens
   `stream-denominated, over-reports the run record by 1.46x-1.79x`.
3. **Claude only** - stated in the report`s own output, not implied.

## The classification is reused, not respelled

`copilot_tools.WRITE_TOOLS` is the write half, imported rather than copied, so a name added there
extends this classification. `READ_TOOLS` is declared beside it. A tool that is neither is
`unclassified` and a turn with no predecessor is `unattributed` - four classes, because two would
have forced a guess.

## Gates this change had to satisfy that the bead did not name

`lint-imports` is exhaustive, so the new module had to be declared a layer (above `lane_log`,
below `cli`). A docs tripwire requires every subcommand in architecture §8. And `wired-or-deleted`
refused the command until a catalog source named it - it is now part of the `session-finish` close
-out, which is where a spend question belongs.

## Verification

`pytest -q` 4002 passed, ten new. Each acceptance selector resolves: `-k classify` 2 passed,
`-k unclassifiable` 2, `-k missing` 2. module-size, comment-density, test-naming, wired-or-deleted,
lint-imports and docs-claims all green.

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
python3 -c "
import json
d=json.load(open(\".basicly/usage/run-records.json\"))
recs=[r for v in d.values() for r in v if isinstance(r,dict)]
have=[r for r in recs if \"cache_read_tokens\" in r]
nz=[r for r in have if (r.get(\"cache_read_tokens\") or 0)>0]
print(len(recs), len(have), len(nz))
"
```

Observed - 361 records, 206 carry `cache_read_tokens`, and **3 of those 206 are non-zero**,
all on claude. Expected - a claude dispatch that reads a cached prefix records what it read.

## Context

`factory-loop.md` section 15.5 makes the cache split the gate on everything else: without
it "a 40% apparent saving that actually broke a cached prefix is indistinguishable from a
real win". The document still says "0 of 297 dispatch records carry a cache split", which is
stale in the direction that hides this - the extractor now writes the field, so a reader
checking presence concludes the gap closed. Presence is not population.

This blocks the measurement `ejdm` exists for. The `--resume --fork-session` mechanism is
priced entirely in cache reads - 19x on a hit against a cold seed, ~10x on a corpus once the
denominator is corrected - so `ejdm.4`, which measures the briefed lane against the unbriefed
one, has no instrument for the quantity its remedy moves.

Not established here: whether the extractor drops the numbers or the dispatch shape genuinely
misses the cache. `claude -p` opens a fresh session per lane and this repo passes no
`--resume`, so a near-total cache miss may be the true reading rather than a parser fault.
Deciding which is the first work, and a positive control is available - a hand-run
`--resume --fork-session` dispatch is known to return a non-zero read.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner_usage.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `tests/test_runner_usage.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-08 across the five lanes of pass `basicly-u2hl:bc7cc925`. Cost is
Anthropic's own `total_cost_usd`, not the token figure - `CLAUDE_TOKEN_KEYS`
(`runner_envelope.py:71`) sums `cache_read_input_tokens` at full weight while cache reads
bill at 0.1x, so the token column overstates spend by roughly 3-10x.

```text
bead        dispatches   cost   lines changed   $/line
u2hl.16          1      $ 1.47        19        0.077   <- worst
u2hl.12          1      $ 6.29         -            -
u2hl.15          3      $10.43         -            -
u2hl.23          2      $27.07     1,736        0.016
u2hl.14          4      $25.62     2,575        0.010   <- best
```

**The small lane is the wasteful one.** A dispatch pays a fixed floor of roughly 1.1M
processed tokens / $1.47 - repo rules, always-on guidance, the skill index, the bead,
orientation, plus `uv sync` and `npm install` on a fresh worktree - before it edits
anything. A long lane amortises that against a stable cached prefix and gets cheaper per
line; a short one does not.

## The gap

`supervise._band_verdict` already computes a floor verdict -
`under the floor - dispatches, but merge it with a sibling` - and **the floor never
refuses; only the ceiling does**. So nothing stops a 19-line change from being dispatched.

It cannot simply be made binding as it stands, because the band is measured on
`decompose.scope_read_cost` - the cost of *reading* the scope, not of *changing* it -
and read cost did not predict change cost here either: `u2hl.16` measured 15,199 tokens
(above the 8,000 floor, so it dispatched) and produced 19 lines, while `u2hl.14` measured
78,709 and produced 2,575.

`basicly-tcmy.34` closed 2026-08-05 on the forecast unit, and `_band_verdict`
(`supervise.py:1387`) still reads a `WorkingSetAdmission` - a scope *read* figure. So the
floor was never in that bead's scope and does not inherit its fix; the measurement above
is fresh evidence taken 2026-08-08, not a restatement of it.

## What this bead does, and what it defers

Bind the floor on a **forecast of change size**, not read size, and record the rule in the
`harness-loop` skill so a driving session applies it before `supervise` is even called:
a unit expected to change under roughly 200 lines is done in session, not dispatched.
Calibrating the change-size forecast itself stays on `basicly-tcmy.34`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a child whose forecast change size is below the floor, when a pass is planned,
  then the band refuses it naming the in-session route rather than dispatching - check:
  `uv run basicly loop preflight <epic>` prints a refusal row for a seeded under-floor
  child, and a test asserts `_band_verdict` returns the refusing verdict for it.
- Given the same child, when a human overrides, then the override is recorded - check: a
  test asserts the override path writes a marker naming who allowed it.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly loop preflight basicly-u2hl` prints an under-floor refusal for a seeded
19-line child instead of `in band`.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop.skill.yaml`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none

payload.text:
[harness-sizing] the floor now has a measured value, 2026-08-14

`basicly usage tuning` at session close, over 359 recorded dispatches:

```text
policy.sizing.working_set_min   8000 tokens in force
                                69317 advised (measured, n=50)
                                observed 53580-317796 tokens
```

The advised figure is the 0.1 quantile of the working set a finished lane really occupied. **The
floor in force is 8.7x below the smallest lane ever observed** (53,580), which is why it never
refuses - it is not that the rule is advisory, it is that no package can be small enough to trip
it.

That is the number this bead was missing. It does not settle whether the floor should bind, which
is still the question here, but it removes the option of binding it at 8000: at that value a
binding floor and an advisory one behave identically.

Filed as evidence, not as a change - `basicly.toml` is on the confirmation list and the tuner is
advisory by design.

payload.description:
## Context

Verified against claude 2.1.231 on 2026-08-13 by probe, with a positive control.

`skills:` in an agent definition is a **documented, typed** frontmatter field: "Skills to
preload into the subagent's context at startup. The full skill content is injected, not only
the description."

It is honoured when the definition is spawned as a subagent - probed: a definition declaring
`skills: [probeskill]`, spawned via the Agent tool and told not to use the Skill tool,
returned the skill's canary token.

**It is not honoured under `claude --agent <name> -p`, which is this repo's dispatch shape.**
Probed twice: same definition, same skill, `NONE` returned, `num_turns 1`. The positive
control loaded the same skill via the Skill tool in the same mode and returned the canary, so
the probe discriminates. Corroborated by the vendor's own `--agent` section, which says the
session takes on the subagent's "system prompt, tool restrictions, and model" - skills are
not in that list.

Consequence today: `.claude/agents/implementer.md`, `decomposer.md`, `validator.md`,
`researcher.md` and `retrospector.md` all declare `skills:` and every one of them gets
nothing from it. The specialist runs without its specialism, and `catalog_lint` enforces a
pairing that has no runtime effect.

This also resolves the open half of `basicly-6vr6` and refutes `agents.py:372`, which calls
the key "deliberately untyped (its shape is the host's to define)". The shape is a documented
list of skill names; the defect is the spawn mode.

## Proposed check

Dispatch through a path that spawns the definition as a subagent (the Python Agent SDK's
`agents={name: AgentDefinition(skills=[...])}`), and assert the preload with a canary: a test
that dispatches a role whose skill contains a unique token and asserts the token reaches the
agent without a `Skill` invocation.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Project the agents (`basicly agents-build`), leaving `implementer.md` declaring
  `skills: [python-guidelines, repair-in-place]`.
- Dispatch it the way the engine does: `claude --agent implementer -p "<prompt>"`, with the
  prompt asking for a token that appears only inside one of those skill bodies.
- Observed: `NONE`, `num_turns 1` - probed twice on claude 2.1.231, 2026-08-13. The positive
  control loaded the same skill through the Skill tool in the same mode and returned the
  canary, so the probe discriminates between "absent" and "wrong probe".
- Expected: the agent holds the skill body without invoking the Skill tool.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/roles.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_roles.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
payload.title: Carry a role declared skill body into the dispatch prompt

payload.text: Kept as a blocker of basicly-xjd2 rather than refiled as its child: the blocks edge xjd2 -> ey58 already encodes the ordering the audit wanted, and br refused the parent-child edge as a cycle. The finding stands on its own - skills: is inert under claude --agent -p - and xjd2 builds on it.

OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13 - the fix is PROMPT INJECTION, not the Agent SDK. Measured before deciding: the largest role's declared skills are 3261 tokens (implementer: python-guidelines + repair-in-place) against a lane costing 8-11M, so injecting the bodies costs about 0.03% of a lane. The SDK route was rejected on two grounds: it is claude-only in a harness that advertises three families, and it is a new runtime dependency every basicly install consumer inherits, whose behaviour tracks the CLI product's release cadence rather than a pinned library's (basicly-ctdz's criterion). Named failure mode to measure, not assume: skills: injects at startup ahead of the first turn while a prompt prefix arrives as user text, so ADHERENCE may differ even though the content is identical - the canary test must assert the content arrives, and a follow-up should measure whether it is followed.

payload.description:
## Context

Step 2 of the cutover in `docs/design/work-tracker.md` §5. Step 1 ran 2026-08-07
(commit `b97a653`): the ledger now holds 3775 events over 643 records, imported with
provenance EXTRACTED, and `fsck` reports zero errors.

Step 2 is shadow mode - the owned tracker answers the same queries read-only and a
differential asserts identical verdicts for phase derivation, ready set and gate status.
Every piece of machinery exists and none of it is wired to anything real. Measured
2026-08-07: `differential.run_differential` and `differential.ReferenceSource` are
constructed in `tests/test_kit_tracker_differential.py` only. No engine module, CLI
command or script builds a source from the live tracker, so the differential has never
been run against this repo.

## The reference must be live, not a re-import

§5.1 records why, and the kit already enforces it: `import` upstream is upsert-only and
cannot express deletion, so comparing two derivatives of one lossy snapshot agrees with
itself and proves nothing. `ReferenceSource` carries `snapshot=None` for a live source
and `audit_reference` perturbs the owned event set to catch a source that is secretly a
derivative - a source that changes its answer when the ledger is perturbed is refused.
So the work is a `views` callable that reads the live `br` and ignores its argument
entirely.

Report `clean` and `conclusive` separately, as the kit already does. A refused reference
still runs the comparison, and the report must say in the same breath that the agreement
proves nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the imported ledger and a reference source built from the live br when the shadow differential runs then it reports clean and conclusive separately and a perturbed ledger makes the audit refuse the source rather than reporting a clean comparison

## Scope

- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`

payload.description:
Measured 2026-08-09 in base @ 5132143, while decomposing basicly-u2hl.54.

ROLE_BY_PHASE (roles.py:63) has seven entries and reviewer is not among them:

  classify -> decider          build -> implementer      retrospective -> retrospector
  decompose -> decomposer      validate -> validator     ship -> curator
                               repair -> implementer

`.claude/agents/reviewer.md` and `.agents/agents/reviewer.md` both exist and are projected,
and the reviewer agent's own description says it is 'invoked by the engine at VALIDATE, once
per lens, alongside the validator'. But VALIDATE maps to validator alone, so even after
basicly-u2hl.54 lands and VALIDATE becomes a real phase, nothing can reach reviewer.

The comment at roles.py:55-62 explains that VALIDATE, REPAIR and RETROSPECTIVE are recorded
without phases on purpose. It does not cover reviewer, which has no phase to be waiting for.

Two honest resolutions, and this bead is to pick one rather than to assume:

1. VALIDATE dispatches more than one role - validator plus one reviewer per lens - in which
   case ROLE_BY_PHASE is the wrong shape, because it is phase -> one role. That is a design
   change, and it should be settled against factory-loop.md section 6 rather than here.
2. reviewer is not an engine-dispatched role at all and the agent should be deleted or
   re-described, because an agent nothing routes to is context load with no reach - the same
   argument that just moved 15 tool skills to user-invoked (basicly-a3ab.12).

Do not resolve this by adding 'validate' -> 'reviewer' to the map. That would displace
validator, which basicly-u2hl.54.3 is being built to dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The repo shall either route reviewer from a named phase through `roles.resolve_role`, or
  carry no projected reviewer agent, and a test shall assert that every projected agent file
  under the loop-role set is reachable from `ROLE_BY_PHASE`.
- Where the answer is that VALIDATE fans out to several roles, the decision shall be recorded
  in `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` before `ROLE_BY_PHASE` changes shape.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/roles.py`
- `.basicly/core/agents/`
- `tests/test_roles.py`
- `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n 'ROLE_BY_PHASE' -A 10 src/basicly/roles.py` - seven entries, no reviewer.
2. `ls .claude/agents/reviewer.md` - the agent exists and is projected.
3. There is no phase string for which `roles.role_for_phase` returns 'reviewer'.
payload.title: Map the reviewer role to a phase or delete the agent

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-C survey 2026-08-14. The largest item in the backlog and the last in its chain.

After the owned extractions land, the command-line module still cannot be named without the word and. It is the projection and distribution command surface, lines 125 to 1930, and an interactive factory operations console.

```text
loop preflight printing     cli.py:2700-3070
session rendering           cli.py:3441-3560
decisions, answer, kill     cli.py:3561-3823
                            about 1,160 lines
parser wiring               cli.py:4048-4910, about 860 lines
```

The module is 4,911 lines and 51,691 tokens, frozen at 54,336 against a 4,000 cap.

## The seam is a responsibility, not a metric

The loop console has its own state, its own vocabulary and its own test files. The layering contract is exhaustive with the command-line module alone at the top tier, so the new module needs a declared tier between it and the supervisor. It imports the supervisor, the loop, the decisions module and the policy module, and only the command-line module imports it.

## The ratchet arithmetic

The command-line module is frozen on size and not on prose share, so it has prose headroom below the cap. The loop console is printer-heavy code, so the extraction raises the remainder's prose share. Measure both before choosing the exact cut. Record the shrink through the delta mechanism, never by editing the frozen line.

## Acceptance

- When a loop subcommand is invoked, then its handler resolves from a dedicated console module placed in its own declared tier.
- When the command-line module is read after the change, then it retains parser registration only for those commands.
- When any loop command runs, then its output is byte-identical to today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- a new module
- `.importlinter`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py` and its siblings

## Depends on

The supervisor pass extraction, the install lifecycle extraction, and the structured escalation routes. All three move code out of the same file.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -q` and a diff of `uv run basicly loop status` output against the pre-split output.
payload.title: extract the loop operations console out of the command line module

payload.description:
## Context

`rg -r` is `--replace`, not `--recursive`. It has already silently mangled a probe's output
in this repo, and it is recorded nowhere: a search for `rg -r` and `--replace` across
`.basicly/`, `docs/` and `.claude/` returns zero hits. Positive control: the same search
shape for `word.split` returns 3 files, so the probe discriminates.

`tool-ripgrep` does not carry it either, and that is the point - every footgun this repo has
actually captured was captured as an always-on fragment plus a hook, never as a tool-* card:

- zsh not word-splitting unquoted vars - `non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml` plus
  `.basicly/core/hooks/unsplit-loop-guard.py`
- `shlex.split` mangling Windows paths - `python/skill.yaml` plus
  `.basicly/core/hooks/shell_tokens.py`

A `user`-invoked tool card cannot be the carrier: nothing routes to it, which is why
`catalog_lint.py:304-308` refuses to let it carry a description at all.

## Proposed check

A hook that refuses `rg -r` used as if it meant recursive, following `unsplit-loop-guard.py`,
with a test for the false positive: a genuine `--replace` use must pass.
payload.title: Capture the rg dash r means replace footgun where the tooling enforces it

Where the skill mentions a waiver it shall say that a prose heavy extraction cannot stand alone under the fifty percent cap and that a new small module is where a density waiver is legitimate - check: rg -n "cannot stand alone|no frozen baseline" .basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml

payload.description:
Retro finding, session 2026-08-13. Proposed by the agent, not self-applied.

## Context

`module-size` counts tokens; `comment-density` counts the prose share. They can be
unsatisfiable together, and nothing in the catalog says so.

On `basicly-u2hl.54.3` the size ratchet forced 459 tokens out of `loop.py`. The honest
extraction available - the prompt builders - was **code**-heavy, so removing it raised the prose
share from 52.4% to 53.0% and broke the other gate. Six trim-and-remeasure cycles followed before
the pattern was named and the session stopped to ask the owner.

The rule that resolves it is arithmetic and cheap to state: **an extraction satisfies both gates
only if the extracted unit prose share is ABOVE the origin module share.** Extracting code raises
the origin share; extracting prose lowers it. The second extraction attempted that session - the
answered-escalation reader, at a higher prose share than `loop.py` - satisfied both in one pass.

The skill already carries the right stance ("Fix the metric, do not move the score", and the test
of stating what you did without naming the gate). What it lacks is the measurement that tells you
WHICH cut to make, so an author obeying the stance still cycles.

A second consequence belongs with it: **a prose-heavy extraction cannot stand alone.** A new
module has no frozen baseline, so a 66% module fails the 50% cap the moment it is created. That is
where a `comment-density-waiver` is legitimate and scoped, rather than on the 2600-line module it
came out of - which is what `landing_gate.py` records as the tree first such waiver.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Take any module over both caps, e.g. `loop.py`.
- Extract a code-heavy block to satisfy `module-size`.
- Run `uv run python .scripts/check_comment_density.py` - the origin now fails, and the skill
  offers no guidance on which block to have cut instead.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml`
payload.title: teach python guidelines that the two size ratchets pull opposite ways

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-07 while investigating `basicly-b2n2`. This is the verified, independently
fixable half of that bead: whatever the truth about br's internal auto-flush, **this repo
discards the exit code of every `br sync` it runs**, on the one path that commits tracker
state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Put the checkout in a state where `br sync --flush-only` refuses. br carries a Stale DB
   Guard and refuses with a non-zero exit and this message, measured 2026-08-07 against
   `br 0.2.16` build `5cf4310`:

   ```
   Error: Configuration error: Refusing to export stale database that would lose issues.
   Database has 3 issues, JSONL has 7 unique issues. Export would lose 4 issue(s)...
   Hint: Run import first, or use --force to override.
   ```

2. Drive any landing that reaches `merge.commit_tracker_state`.

Observed: the refusal is discarded and the engine commits whatever `.beads/issues.jsonl`
already contained.

Expected: a refusal from the tracker's own guard is surfaced, not laundered into a commit.

## The two call sites

- `src/basicly/merge.py:466` `reconcile_beads` - `br.try_run_br(repo_root, ["sync", "--merge"])`,
  return value discarded entirely.
- `src/basicly/merge.py:520` `commit_tracker_state` - `br.try_run_br(repo_root, ["sync",
  "--flush-only"])`, return value discarded, then **immediately** `scrub_export`,
  `git add .beads`, `git commit`.

The second is the damaging one: the three lines after the discarded call commit the export
unconditionally. A refusal there means the commit records tracker state that br declined to
produce, and the commit message still reads as a normal `chore(beads)` landing.

Also measured: `rg 'sync --status' src/basicly/` returns **zero call sites**. The
`harness-loop` skill instructs a human to run `br sync --status` before any write, and
nothing in the engine ever does. The skill is the only enforcement, which is why this is
worth closing in code.

## Why this is not basicly-b2n2

`b2n2` is about br's *internal* post-mutation auto-flush deleting records, and its mechanism
did not reproduce on the pinned binary (recorded there 2026-08-07). This bead makes no claim
about that. It is the narrower, fully verified point that the engine ignores an exit code it
is already collecting - true regardless of how `b2n2` resolves, and cheap.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given br sync exits non-zero on the tracker commit path when commit_tracker_state runs then the failure is surfaced and no tracker commit is created from the unflushed export, and a test proves the refusal is not committed
payload.title: Stop discarding the br sync exit code on the tracker commit path

payload.description:
## Context

`factory-loop.md` §15.5 reads as corrected on caching economics, but the extractor behind it
was never fixed. `runner_usage.py:57,75` declares a cache field and `:177` populates it for
codex only, so **0 of 345 dispatch records carry a cache split** - `cache_read_tokens` is null
in all 163 claude records and all 182 manual ones.

Every economic claim the factory makes about dispatch now depends on a number the ledger does
not hold. `basicly-ejdm`'s whole justification is a cache-hit ratio, and after it lands there
is no way to tell from our own data whether a lane hit the cache or paid cold.

The vendor's stream carries it: a top-level `-p` run reports
`cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens`, observed directly
during the 2026-08-13 probe session. The Python Agent SDK additionally emits per-subagent
usage (`TaskProgressMessage.usage`, `TaskNotificationMessage.usage`,
`TaskUsage{total_tokens, tool_uses, duration_ms}`), which is the metering `basicly-xjd2`
requires and which the hand-rolled parser does not read at all.

## Proposed check

A dispatch record carries `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_creation_tokens` for the claude
runner, asserted by a test that feeds a recorded stream fixture and reads the split back off
the record. The fixture must be an **observed** stream, not a composed one.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the ledger's claude records and ask for the cache split:

   ```sh
   uv run python -c "
   import json
   d = json.load(open('.basicly/usage/run-records.json'))
   rows = [r for rs in d.values() for r in rs if r.get('agent') == 'claude']
   print(len(rows), 'claude records;', sum(r.get('cache_read_tokens') is None for r in rows), 'null')"
   ```

   Measured 2026-08-13: 163 claude records, 163 null. All 182 manual records are null too.

2. Positive control, so the zero is not a property of the probe: run the same query for
   `agent == 'codex'`. Those records carry a populated split, which is what makes this a
   claude-side gap rather than a missing column.

3. Read the cause. `runner_usage.py:106` (`claude_json_usage`) and `:132`
   (`claude_turn_usage`) both construct `Usage(tokens=..., cost=..., estimated=...)` and leave
   `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens` at their
   `None` defaults. The codex path at `:171-179` passes all five from `_codex_usage_split`.

The vendor reports the fields; we drop them. `runner_envelope.CLAUDE_TOKEN_KEYS:71-76` already
enumerates exactly the four keys needed, and they are already summed into `tokens` - the split
is discarded on the way.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a claude result object whose usage block carries `cache_read_input_tokens` and
  `cache_creation_input_tokens`, when `claude_json_usage` parses it, then the returned `Usage`
  carries `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens` equal to those values - check: a test
  over an **observed** stream, captured from a real dispatch, not a composed one.
- Given a usage block that omits a cache key, when it is parsed, then that field is `None` and
  not `0` - check: a test asserts `None`, because a real turn that created no cache reports a
  genuine `0` and the two claims must stay distinguishable. This is the reason
  `_codex_usage_split` already states in its docstring.
- Given an `assistant` event forwarded from a subagent, when `claude_turn_usage` parses it,
  then it still returns `None` - check: the existing forwarded-turn assertion continues to
  pass, so the split does not become a route around `runner_envelope.forwarded`.
- Given a dispatch record written after this lands, when it is read back, then it carries the
  split - check: `uv run basicly usage report` reports a cache figure for claude rather than
  omitting the column.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_runner_usage.py -q` passes, and

```sh
uv run basicly usage report
```

reports a claude cache split instead of nothing. The unit is what makes `basicly-ejdm` and
`basicly-xjd2` measurable at all: both are justified by a cache-hit ratio this ledger cannot
currently express.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner_usage.py`
- `tests/test_runner_usage.py`
- `changelog.d/basicly-i4gg.fixed.md`
payload.title: Extract the cache split from a dispatch stream so a caching claim is measurable

payload.description:
## Context

`[[verify.checks]]` spells lint-imports as a bare command (`command = ["lint-imports"]`), so it
resolves from PATH. A landing runs verify as a subprocess of `basicly loop advance`, which was
launched with `uv run` from the base checkout, so PATH carries the base `.venv/bin` and
import-linter imports the `basicly` package the *base* editable install points at.

lint-imports is the only configured check that resolves its target by import rather than by path -
pyright and vulture read files under cwd - so it is the only one that follows the venv instead of
the worktree.

## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-08 on the basicly-u2hl.2 worktree, which adds `src/basicly/integrity.py`:

```text
VIRTUAL_ENV=<base>/.venv PATH=<base>/.venv/bin:$PATH lint-imports
  -> Missing layer in container 'basicly': module basicly.integrity does not exist.
uv run lint-imports
  -> Contracts: 2 kept, 0 broken.
```

## Impact

Any lane that adds a new module can never land: the gate reports a module-not-found the lane's tree
does not have, and the bounded rework loop cannot fix it. basicly-u2hl.2 escalated at rework 2/2
with the engine's own note that 'this round changed nothing it reports'. Two lanes' landings and
one rework round were spent on it.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Plan section 10's second owed owner decision, **taken 2026-08-14: design the arms now.** It had been
owed since the plan was rewritten on 2026-08-08 and had no owner; architecture section 14.4 names the
shape and nothing is built.

The owner chose this over deferring it past v1.0.0.

## What is owed

Two things, and the second is the sharper one.

**The four arms.** Architecture section 14.4 names the shape of a catalog eval but not the arms
themselves. An arm is a cell whose guidance configuration is declared, so a measured difference
between arms is attributable to that configuration and to nothing else.

**Whether the safety tier is a gate or a metric.** A metric reports; a gate refuses. This repository
has a recorded rule for exactly that call - D23: a control with no recorded correct firing becomes
observability, and one that has earned a firing keeps its teeth. A safety tier that has never fired
starts as a metric under that rule, and the decision is whether safety is the exception.

## The constraints this design must honour, each already recorded

- **The isolation assertion is the whole instrument.** Plan section 11 names the risk: *"a measurement
  is uninterpretable because an arm was contaminated"*, and the remedy already written is that the
  harness reads back what guidance is live in the cell and fails if it does not match the arm's
  declaration. Without that, every number the eval produces is unfalsifiable.
- **Stage by adding entries to the enforced set, never by lowering a threshold.** Also plan section 11.
  Tier-1 failure from the start.
- **8 of 34 skills had ever been exercised** when last measured, and that figure is now unsound
  (`basicly-4grf`) because `ey58` injects a role's skills into the dispatch prompt, so the never-used
  report cannot tell an uninvoked skill from an injected one. **The eval needs a sound exercised-count
  before it can measure anything about guidance**, so state whether this bead depends on `4grf` or
  routes around it.
- **An unmeasured behavioural claim costs context every turn** - the plan's third invariant. That is
  the argument for the eval and it is also the standard the eval itself is held to.

## Acceptance

- When the four arms are declared, then each names its guidance configuration and what a difference
  between it and its neighbour would establish.
- When an arm runs, then the harness reads back the guidance live in that cell and fails if it does not
  match the declaration.
- When the safety tier is decided, then the decision states whether it gates or reports and cites the
  rule that decided it.
- When the design lands, then it states what it depends on for a sound exercised-count and does not
  assume the 8-of-34 figure.

## Scope

Design only. `docs/architecture/architecture.md` section 14.4 is the target of the write-up; the
implementation is decomposed after.

## Demonstration

The four arms are readable by someone who was not in the room, and for each one a reader can say what
result would falsify it. A design nobody can falsify is the thing this eval exists to catch.

## Context

Found by the lane-D measurement survey 2026-08-14 and re-measured by hand with the repository's own reader.

Two functions in `decompose.py`, 240 lines apart, sample lane actuals from different populations under different rules.

```text
decompose.py:1400  unsized_lane_tokens   run_record.load_run_records   local only, .basicly/usage is git-ignored
                                         keeps outcome == failed
decompose.py:1644  spend_accuracy        run_record.dispatch_history   local records union committed markers
                                         excludes failed attempts, decompose.py:1652
```

`spend_accuracy` states its reason at decompose.py:1622: so a fresh clone measures the same thing. `unsized_lane_tokens` states no reason for the other choice.

## Measured

On a checkout with no local records, `unsized_lane_tokens` returns `UNSIZED_LANE_TOKENS_SEED = 4_000_000` (decompose.py:1336, 1419). Measured against 126 write-phase samples in the committed markers:

```text
seed          4,000,000
median        7,694,941
0.9 quantile 20,594,047
maximum      38,145,168
```

The seed sits 1.9 times below the median and 5.1 times below the 0.9 quantile.

## Why that is the dangerous direction

The comment above the constant, decompose.py:1333, reads: Deliberately high, this feeds a ceiling check, where erring low admits an unbounded pass and erring high only asks a human to widen the grant or scope the bead.

The seed now errs in the direction the comment names as dangerous. The repository's own ledger falsifies the rationale written above the number. This is the shape of `basicly-89hm` and of the stale context window: a constant that was correct when written and rots in silence.

## Consumers

`supervise.py:1322` at pass admission, `supervise.py:2602` where it writes `forecast_spend_tokens`, and `cli.py:2717`.

## Acceptance

- When `unsized_lane_tokens` computes a measured bound, then it samples the same corpus and applies the same outcome exclusion as `spend_accuracy`.
- When a checkout holds only committed markers and no local records, then the bound is measured and not the seed, and a test demonstrates it.
- While neither corpus holds a record, then the function returns the seed labelled as a seed. That behaviour is kept.
- When the seed value is next reviewed, then it is stated against a measured quantile or removed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_decompose.py`

## Depends on

Nothing. Coordinate the wording with `basicly-tcmy.15`, which owns the read amplification on the same path.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_decompose.py -q` plus a marker-only corpus test, and `uv run basicly usage forecast` on a checkout with no local records.

payload.description:
## Context

`.basicly/usage/run-records.json` holds 163 claude dispatch records. **Every one of them is
`claude -p <prompt> --output-format stream-json --verbose [--forward-subagent-text]`. Zero
carry `--agent` or `--model`.**

The role-injection wiring exists and is not in doubt: `runner.py:425` `_apply_role`, reached
via `roles.resolve_role`, and `basicly-4kdm` closed on it having been "verified against claude
2.1.226 and copilot 1.0.78 rather than recalled". A repair dispatch observed live on
2026-08-13 did carry `--agent implementer --model claude-opus-5`.

So the ledger and the code disagree about supervised lanes, and the ledger is the only
artifact a before/after measurement can use. Either lane dispatch does not apply the role, or
it does and the record does not capture it. **Both are defects, and they are not
distinguishable from the data we keep** - which is the actual finding.

Second defect in the same record shape, from the same probe session: `--agent` honours an
agent's declared model, and passing `--model` alongside it **overrides** that declaration
(measured: `--agent probeagent(model: haiku) --model sonnet` ran the turn on sonnet). The
observed repair dispatch passed both, so the declared tier was overridden - while the run
record for that shape reports `tier_honoured: true`.

## Proposed check

The dispatch record carries the resolved role, the resolved model, and the argv flags that
were actually applied. A test asserts a supervised lane's record names its role, and a second
asserts `tier_honoured` is false when `--model` overrode a declared tier.

## MERGED FROM basicly-tcmy.33 (2026-08-13)

The same defect from the opposite direction, and its acceptance criterion is the one this bead
needs and did not state.

tcmy.33: a `phase: decide` record's `command` ends in the usage-report flags, but
`decisions.py:655` dispatches with `capture_usage` unset - **so those flags were never on the
real argv**. Cause: `runner.record_dispatch` **re-derives** the command instead of copying
`result.command`, and hard-codes `capture_usage=True` in that re-derivation.

So the record asserts flags the dispatch never carried (tcmy.33) and omits flags it did carry
(this bead). One fix discharges both: thread the real argv onto the record.

**Carried acceptance criterion:** the recorded command matches the real argv, with only the
prompt redacted.
payload.title: Record the flags a dispatch actually carried so role injection is falsifiable

payload.text:
[harness-info] the recorded argv landed, 2026-08-14

## What changed

`runner.record_dispatch` **copies** `result.command` and elides the prompt by equality, instead of
re-deriving the argv from the spec with a hard-coded `capture_usage=True`. One change discharges
both directions, which is what the merge from `basicly-tcmy.33` predicted.

Before and after, on the claude builtin:

```text
OLD  claude -p <prompt-redacted> --output-format stream-json --verbose --forward-subagent-text
NEW  claude --agent implementer -p <prompt-redacted> --output-format stream-json --verbose \
       --forward-subagent-text          (lane, role resolved)
NEW  claude -p <prompt-redacted>         (decide, capture_usage unset)
```

The old form was wrong both ways at once: it omitted `--agent`, which the lane passes, and
appended usage flags the decider never carried.

## Three tests, each tripped against the old behaviour before it was trusted

```text
test 1  --agent present in the record      old False  new True
test 2  no usage flags on a decide record  old False  new True
test 3  unknown prompt records no argv                new True
leak    the prompt is absent, placeholder present     new True
```

Test 2 is the negative half and it is load-bearing: without it, a record that simply appended
every known flag would pass test 1.

## An unknown prompt records no argv

The redaction keys on the prompt the caller dispatched, so a caller that omits it leaves nothing
to key on. Recording the argv unredacted would publish a prompt into a committed ledger, which is
the one defect class that survives its own fix. It costs nothing: the only site that omits the
prompt is `record_unstarted_dispatch`, whose dispatch died before an argv existed.

## Three fixtures were asserting nothing, and that is the finding under the finding

`test_runner._copilot_run` and two `test_loop` stubs built their `RunResult` from
`tuple(spec.command)` - the **template**, `("claude", "-p", "{prompt}")`, with the placeholder
unsubstituted. Their redaction assertions therefore passed against a command that never contained
a prompt. They pass now because the fixtures build the substituted argv, which is what a real
dispatch carries.

## What this does NOT establish

The instrument exists; the reading does not. **The 357 historical records are unchanged and still
name no role**, so a before/after measurement of role injection begins with the next supervised
pass. Do not read this close as "role injection is observed".

The second defect on this bead - `--model` overriding the model an agent declares while
`tier_honoured` reports true - is **not fixed here**. Its precondition is unmet: D30 keeps a model
id out of every projected agent file, so nothing is overridden today, and `basicly-a3yi` is the
injection that changes that. Filed as `basicly-trxy`, blocked on `a3yi`. The co-occurrence is now
visible in the ledger, which is the part this change buys it.

## Verification

`pytest -q` 3977 passed, three new. `module-size` and `comment-density` both green - the first
attempt tripped both, and the prose was cut rather than a baseline moved.

Fixed and committed 93ec579 on 2026-08-06 (decompose.py +47, supervise.py +8, test_decompose.py +48); the bead was never closed. Tracker history shows this id as open in all 25 committed versions of issues.jsonl - never closed, so this is not a b2n2 resurrection.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the r343 module-size waiver is removed then wired_or_deleted.py carries no waiver and the gate reports the same finding count as before with no stale suppression
payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-r343` fixed the schema scan and could not land without a size waiver. This bead removes that waiver by doing the work the waiver stands in for.

```text
.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py   6,554 frozen, 6,525 used   29 tokens of headroom
the r343 fix adds                829 tokens
now                            7,432 tokens               1.86 times the cap
```

## Why the waiver is not the right end state

`factory-loop.md` section 9.3 states that the first change to a frozen file **under 8,000 tokens** must bring it under the cap, not merely reduce it. This file was 6,554, so the recorded obligation was to extract.

A waiver is for a module that is genuinely cohesive. The `r343` implementer named a real seam in its own report and then waived on cost rather than on cohesion. It said so plainly, which is why this bead exists rather than a silent concession.

## The seam it named

The reference index is a nameable responsibility that does not import back: `_iter_files`, `_read`, `_dotted`, `Index` and `build_index`. It is about a 2,000-token move and it touches every function in the file plus `tests/test_verify.py`.

## Measure before you cut

The two size ratchets pull opposite ways. Extracting code raises the remaining prose share, so an extraction fixes both gates only when the extracted unit's prose share is above its origin's. Measure both with the gates' own scripts before choosing the cut.

## Acceptance

- When the extraction lands, then `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` is under the 4,000-token cap.
- When the module-size gate runs, then the waiver count returns to 1 and the waiver comment is gone from the file.
- When `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml` is read, then it no longer carries a module-size waiver delta.
- When the dead-code gate runs before and after, then it reports the same finding count.
- When both size gates run, then neither baseline is raised.

## Scope

- `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py`
- a new module under `.scripts/`
- `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml`
- `tests/test_wired_or_deleted.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` reports the same count as before the split, and `uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` reports one waiver rather than two.
payload.title: the dead code gate carries a size waiver that must not outlive its extraction

payload.text:
[harness-info] dispatched 2026-08-14 and blocked before a commit; nothing landed

A lane took this bead, built the extraction the description names, measured it against both ratchets
and returned the worktree to baseline. No commit. `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` is byte-identical
to HEAD and the probe module was removed. The finding is why it stopped.

## The two ratchets are in direct conflict on this file

```text
wired_or_deleted.py at HEAD        7514 tokens   49.8% prose   frozen 6554, waived
same, waiver comment removed       7331 tokens   48.9% prose   the removal buys 183 tokens
reference_index.py as built        2359 tokens   50.6% prose   REFUSED by comment-density
origin after that extraction       5022 tokens   48.1% prose   passes module-size, 25% over the cap
```

The extraction the bead names is real and it was built: `SKIP_DIRS`, `KIT_DIR`, the template and
schema globs, `iter_files`, `read`, `relative`, `dotted`, the name readers, `Index`, `build_index`
and `WiringError`. It is the file's only unit that produces no findings. The gate refused it at
50.6 percent against the 50.0 cap, and the gap is 28 prose tokens — 112 characters. The only prose
in it is the three constants' comments, at 86, 92 and 84 percent prose, and each records a measured
masking incident: `basicly-jr0l.70`'s 48 modules indexed against 401 sites with all 44 baseline
entries stale, the kit `folded`/`holds` masking, and `basicly-r343`'s five schema descriptions.
Cutting any of it to pass is the gaming `python-guidelines` names.

## No other surface can be extracted at all

`field_findings`, `command_findings` and `suppression_findings` each construct `Finding`, the gate's
output vocabulary. Moving any one into its own module makes `wired_or_deleted -> surface ->
wired_or_deleted`, and the gate runs as `__main__`, so the cycle is real rather than a lint opinion.
Moving `Finding` into a surface module instead is a token shuffle with no nameable responsibility
behind it.

## The arithmetic was enumerated, not argued

With the waiver comment gone the file carries **no frozen comment-density entry**, so both halves of
any split must land under 50.0 percent on their own. The lane enumerated all 8.4 million subsets of
the file's 26 natural blocks using the two gates' own `module_tokens()` and `measure()`. **225,756
satisfy both ratchets and not one is a nameable responsibility** — every survivor is `BASELINE` plus
an unrelated mixture, landing at 49.8 to 50.0 percent on both sides. That is the shape a metric-driven
cut takes, which section 9.2 item 5 forbids.

## The blocker is `basicly-05g0`, and the dependency is now an edge

`check_comment_density.load_ratchet` reads `pyproject.toml` directly and composes no `basicly.d`
fragment, while `check_module_size:194` and `check_noqa_debt:216` both call `dropin.compose`. So a
lane cannot record a comment-density waiver without editing the shared landing anchor — the same
anchor that bounced three of five lanes on 2026-08-08. `basicly-05g0` is that defect, filed by the
lane-E survey, and it is worse than this lane knew: `dropin.py:109` accepts `int` only while density
baselines are floats, so the composer needs a type change and not merely a call.

## What this bead can and cannot reach

With `05g0` landed, this bead can take a comment-density waiver on the extracted index — the
legitimate case `python-guidelines` names, a module whose payload is provenance — and land the origin
at 5,022 tokens. **That still does not reach 4,000.**

Reaching the cap needs `Finding` and `WiringError` in a shared substrate so each of the three surfaces
becomes its own module, leaving baseline plus rule plus `main`. That is a three-to-four module
decomposition, and it has a floor: the docstring is 938 tokens at essentially 100 percent prose and
`BASELINE` is 1,121 tokens at 48.7 percent, so the residual gate module needs at least 1,940 tokens
of content below 27 percent prose beside them or it fails the density cap too.

## One trap for whoever lands the removal

`basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml` carries `".scri

[harness-decision] re-scoped by the owner 2026-08-14: waiver now, decomposition later

A lane proved this bead's first criterion unreachable in one cut. It enumerated all 8.4M subsets of
the file's 26 natural blocks against both gates' own functions: 225,756 satisfy both and **not one is
a nameable responsibility**. It returned the worktree to baseline rather than land a grab-bag, which
was correct.

The owner splits the bead rather than weakening it.

**This bead now**: take the comment-density waiver that `basicly-05g0` made recordable through
`basicly.d`, land the reference-index extraction, and **remove the r343 module-size waiver**. That
waiver is what the owner decided must expire - it was bought on cost, not cohesion - and removing it
is what this bead was really for. The file lands near 5,022 tokens.

**Reaching the 4,000 cap moves to its own bead.** It needs `Finding` and `WiringError` in a shared
substrate so each of the three surfaces becomes its own module, and it has a measured floor: the
docstring is 938 tokens at essentially 100 percent prose and `BASELINE` is 1,121 at 48.7 percent, so
the residual gate module needs at least 1,940 tokens of content below 27 percent prose beside them.

**The trap that survives the split**: `basicly.d/basicly-r343.toml` carries both
`".scripts/wired_or_deleted.py" = -6554` and `count_delta = 1`. Dropping only the `count_delta`
leaves the path with no frozen entry at all, and any result over 4,000 then fails `_over_cap`
immediately. Both lines go together or neither does.
