payload.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-11, copilot CLI 1.0.78, throwaway repo with one .agent.md each.

  tools: Read, Grep, Glob        -> 'no shell/bash tool is available to me (only view, grep, glob, sql, and skill tools)'
  tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash  -> ran the command, printed PROBE_OK
  tools: ["read"]                -> 'only view, sql, and skill tools'

So the comma-scalar form parses, the PascalCase names resolve through COPILOT_TOOL_ALIASES, and the
allowlist enforces. The second line is the positive control: without it the first is ambiguous
between 'the allowlist bound' and 'the agent declined for its own reasons'.

What is unbound is the table itself. src/basicly/copilot_tools.py:36 is pinned from one reading on
2026-07-31 and its own comment says copilot drops an unrecognised entry silently. lint_agent_sources
checks a declared name against the table; nothing checks the table against the CLI. A vendor rename
turns a read-only agent into a silently narrower or wider one with every gate green.

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the quality gate fragment states the check step then it names the command that runs every gate and the pass line to confirm, so a hand-picked subset cannot be reported as the gate.
payload.description:
## Context

Session 2026-08-14, and this is a user-visible mistake rather than a near miss: I reported "all
gates green" before committing `basicly-ejdm.2`, then the commit was **refused**. What I had run
was `pytest` plus five checker scripts I picked by name. What I had not run was the gate, which
then failed on `pyright` and `projection-skills`.

The `quality-gate` fragment says: *"Run the repo's checks on anything touched, re-run after the
final edit"*, and *"Point at gates, don't restate them."*

## Root cause, and it is in the wording

"The repo's checks" is a **set an agent has to assemble**, and an agent that has just run five
checkers has evidence it assembled it correctly. There is no moment at which a hand-picked subset
announces that it is a subset - it looks exactly like the whole.

The repo already has the one command: `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-commit.py` runs all 20 and prints
`checks passed: 20/20`. Nothing in the guidance names it, so the fragment describes an outcome
where it could name a command - which is the inversion of section 3.1, the rule that guidance
points at the enforcement rather than restating it.

## Proposed change, for a human to apply

Amend the `quality-gate` fragment so the check step **names the command** rather than the set:
run the repo's own gate runner, and confirm the pass line it prints. The count in that line is
what makes a subset visible - `18/20` cannot be misread as green, while five green scripts can.

D25 forbids an agent amending the catalog, so this is filed rather than applied.

## The second half, which the wording cannot fix

I also reported the result before running the gate. The fragment already carries
*"Confirm success from the explicit pass/fail summary line; truncated output hides failures"* -
that rule was right and I did not follow it. Only the first half is a guidance defect.
payload.title: the quality gate says run the repos checks so an agent assembles its own subset

payload.description:
Filed 2026-08-09 from a defect this session actually committed, at the owner's direction.

## What happened

A 15-file catalog edit was written as:

    MOVE="tool-ast-grep tool-curl ... tool-yq"
    for s in $MOVE; do ...; done

zsh does not word-split an unquoted scalar, so the loop ran ONCE with the whole 260-character
string as $s, touched nothing, and exited 0. The only reason it was visible is that the loop
body carried a `grep -q ... || { echo MISS; continue; }` guard, which printed one line. Without
that guard it reads as complete success and 15 files silently stay as they were.

## Why guidance did not prevent it

The rule already exists and is ALWAYS-ON. `.basicly/core/fragments/tools/
non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml` says verbatim: "Never loop over an unquoted variable
(`for x in $LIST`): zsh does not word-split, so it runs once with the whole string and the
silent no-op looks like success." It was projected into CLAUDE.md and in context from the first
token of the session. It did not bind.

This is not a discovery failure, so the two cheapest remedies are both refuted:

- Routing a tool skill would not have helped: `tool-zsh` has been `invocation: user` since
  before this session, because its content was already PROMOTED into the always-on fragment.
  That promotion is the fix that was already tried.
- Adding more always-on text is the one remedy with evidence against it. The always-on baseline
  is at cap and the open question recorded against it is adherence, not size.

What is left is a deterministic gate, which is this repo's stated doctrine for exactly this:
guidance that must bind becomes a hook.

## Why the matcher can be tight AND complete

Shell state does not persist between Bash tool calls in this harness, so the only reachable
form of the defect is an assignment and its loop in the SAME command. That means matching a
scalar assignment whose value contains whitespace, plus a `for X in $NAME` over that same name,
catches every instance that can occur here while firing on nothing else.

Deliberately NOT matched, each because it is correct or ambiguous:

- `for x in "\${arr[@]}"` - the correct form.
- `for x in a b c` - an inline list.
- `for x in $arr` where arr is an array - zsh DOES split an array; only scalars are the trap.
- `for x in $(cmd)` - also unsplit in zsh, but idiomatic and often intended; blocking it would
  make the gate cry wolf, and a gate that cries wolf gets switched off.
- a name assigned with no whitespace in its value - the loop correctly runs once.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a Bash tool call assigns a whitespace-containing scalar and then loops over it unquoted
  in the same command, the hook shall exit 2 and name both the variable and the corrected form.
- When a Bash tool call loops over an array, an inline list, or a quoted array expansion, the
  hook shall exit 0 and write nothing.
- Where the payload is malformed, absent, or not a Bash call, the hook shall exit 0, so a bug
  in the guard can never lock an agent out of running commands.
- The hook shall be declared in the catalog hook manifest for the claude manager at the
  pretooluse stage with a Bash matcher, and shall be projected into .claude/settings.json.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/unsplit-loop-guard.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/hooks.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/tools/non-interactive-shell.fragment.yaml`
- `tests/test_git_hooks/test_unsplit_loop_guard.py`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a Bash call containing `V="a b c"` and `for x in $V; do echo $x; done` under zsh.
2. Observe one line of output containing 'a b c', not three lines.
3. Observe exit code 0.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_git_hooks/test_unsplit_loop_guard.py -q` passes, and piping the
recorded payload of this session's own failing command into the hook exits 2 naming MOVE.

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-b9ef` landed a gate for a stale claim in an **epic's** problem statement, because a
decider reads that text as fact. The same failure exists one level up and nothing checks it: a
requirements document is read as fact by every human and agent that plans from it, and four of
its current claims are false against the tree. Each was verified 2026-08-13.

**1. `factory-loop.md:358-363` - "All seven are authored and dispatched as of 2026-08-09. The
gap this section had measured since 2026-08-08 - 'the projection works and nothing consumes it'
- is closed."**

Refuted. **0 of 346 recorded dispatch commands contain `--agent`**, against a positive control
of 163 containing `-p`. `resolve_role` has exactly one call site (`loop.py:745`) and the
supervised lane path passes no role at all (`rg role src/basicly/supervise.py` returns zero
hits). `implementation-plan.md:112-124` already carries the correction; this document does not,
and it is the document the roster work plans against.

**2. `factory-loop.md:404-407` - "`skills:` preloads a skill's full body at subagent startup."**

Half true, and the false half is the one that matters. Probed twice on claude 2.1.231 with a
positive control: preload happens for a definition **spawned as a subagent**, and does **not**
happen under `claude --agent <name> -p`, which is this repo's only dispatch shape. Five agent
definitions declare `skills:` and get nothing from it. Owned by `basicly-ey58`; the document
still states the unqualified claim.

**3. `implementation-plan.md:225` - xjd2's "open question is answered twice over ... a competing
harness runs exactly this split in production, host-runtime dispatch for the same vendor."**

The cited section says the opposite. `factory-loop.md:1115` records that harness's loop as
"**prompt assembly**: the verbs 'do NOT call any LLM', they emit a prompt to stdout. The loop is
prose in `SKILL.md` the model executes." That is an existence proof for the *re-scope* branch of
`basicly-xjd2`, not for engine-driven host dispatch. The row's justification therefore does not
support the row.

**4. `implementation-plan.md:132-135` - "validator, reviewer, retrospector and curator resolve
correctly today and can never be invoked."**

`roles.py:63-71 ROLE_BY_PHASE` has **no `reviewer` entry at all**, so `reviewer` does not
resolve; and `curator` maps to `ship`, which **is** a live phase with a live handler - it is
unreachable only because `_on_ship` (`loop.py:441`) never calls `_run_agent`. So the count and
the reason are both wrong. `basicly-u2hl.54`'s comment 2085 recorded this correction and the
plan never absorbed it.

Also unamended and already known false: `factory-loop.md:1163-1165` (section 12 / D6) still
carries "Context | one window shared by everything" and "The last row is why light cannot
replace dark", which D24 (`:100`) concedes architecture section 5 records as **isolated**.

**5. `factory-loop.md` section 15.5 asserts a defect that no longer exists.**

It reads "`runner_usage.claude_json_usage` never populates `cache_read_tokens`/
`cache_write_tokens` ... **0 of 297 dispatch records carry a cache split**". `basicly-i4gg`
landed the split on 2026-08-13 (`_claude_usage_split`, `runner_usage.py:201`, cited by bead id
in its own docstring) and shipped. Leaving the section as written arms exactly the failure mode
section 5.2 row 5 describes: a reader plans against a defect that was fixed.

**6. The document contradicts itself about the context ceiling, and a bead cannot be written
until one side wins.**

- `:1308` (section 15.6): "The context ceiling is **deleted, not retuned**."
- `:99` (D23, later and general): "**A sizing control with no recorded correct firing becomes
  observability** ... the runner timeout, the working-set band and the **context ceiling** have
  zero between them ... **Demotion is not deletion: the number stays recorded, surfaced and
  falsifiable**, because section 15.6's gate was wrong for months with the telemetry already
  contradicting it."

D23 names the context ceiling explicitly and postdates 15.6, so it should win - but
`basicly-u2hl.30`'s acceptance criterion is written to the 15.6 half and demands the constant,
its meter and its follow-up path be **absent**. A lane implementing it as written deletes a
number D23 requires kept. This is an owner decision, not a wording fix, and `basicly-89hm` now
depends on `u2hl.30`, so it blocks the context-window work too.

## The general defect, which is the reason this is one bead and not four

A committed requirements claim has no falsifiability gate. `docs-claims` checks generated
blocks; `corpus-drift` checks an epic's `## Context` bullets against its own closed children.
Neither reads a requirements document. So a decision recorded on 2026-08-09 can be refuted by
2026-08-11's code and the document keeps asserting it, which is how a session plans a P0 against
a remedy the plan replaced - measured today on `basicly-89hm`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n "All seven are authored and dispatched" docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`
2. Count `--agent` in the ledger:

   ```sh
   uv run python -c "
   import json
   d = json.load(open('.basicly/usage/run-records.json'))
   cmds = [r.get('command') or [] for rs in d.values() for r in rs]
   print(sum('--agent' in c for c in cmds), 'with --agent of', len(cmds))
   print(sum('-p' in c for c in cmds), 'with -p  <- positive control')"
   ```

3. Observe zero against a non-zero control, so the zero is a property of the population.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the four claims above, when each is read in its document, then it states what the tree
  does, or is deleted - check: a reviewer diffs each quoted line against the cited `file:line`.
- Given a requirements document asserting a checkable claim about the code, when a gate runs,
  then an unbacked claim is named - check: exercise the gate on a planted false claim and assert
  it fails, and on the corrected document and assert it passes.
- Given the corrected documents, when `basicly verify --mode full` runs, then `docs-claims` and
  `corpus-drift` still pass - check: the command's own summary line.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly verify --mode full` passes, and the reproduction above prints the corrected
count for whatever the claim is restated to.

## Scope

- `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

payload.description:
## Context

Found by the lane-C survey 2026-08-14 and reproduced by hand.

```python
# src/basicly/loader.py:191
def _infer_source_from_path(path: Path) -> str:
    parts = {part.lower() for part in path.parts}
    if ".basicly-local" in parts or "user" in parts:
        return "user"
    return "core"
```

`path` is absolute. Reproduced:

```text
<redacted:posix-home-path>   core
<redacted:posix-home-path>            user
<redacted:posix-home-path>               user
/srv/User/basicly/.basicly/fragments/x.yaml                 user
```

The lowercase fold makes `User` match too.

## Which root reaches it

`cli._fragment_roots` (cli.py:201-205) passes `None` as the source hint for the legacy root `paths.legacy_fragments_dir`. Any fragment loaded from there infers its source from the path. That root is absent in this repository, so the defect does not fire here. It fires in a consumer repository that still carries it, on a machine whose home directory is named user.

## What a wrong provenance permits

Provenance selects real semantics, both verified:

- `loader._validate_replacements` (loader.py:107-118) downgrades a `ValidationError` to a warning when `fragment.source == "user"`. A `replaces` that names an unknown id stops being an error.
- `planner._apply_user_replacements` (planner.py:132-147) drops any core fragment that a user fragment names in `replaces`.

So on such a checkout a fragment can silently remove an always-on rule from every agent in that repository.

## Why this repository forbids it

Behaviour varies by the absolute path of the checkout. The portability rule states that no committed artifact may depend on a machine path, and this is the same defect one layer in: the code reads the machine path at run time.

## Acceptance

- While a fragment loads from a root with no source hint, then the loader infers `user` only from the overlay marker directory, or from a component relative to the fragment root, and never from the absolute prefix of the checkout.
- When the loader runs against a fixture rooted under a path containing `user`, then it infers `core`.
- A regression test ships with the fix.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loader.py`
- `tests/test_loader.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_loader.py -q` with a fixture rooted under a temporary path that contains a `user` component.
payload.title: fragment provenance reads any path component named user as an overlay

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly loop supervise` runs `while True` (`cli.py:3265`) and returns only when
`state.done` — every child of the root closed. There is no `--once`, no pass limit and no
stop command. Measured 2026-08-08 on session `basicly-u2hl:bc7cc925`: the root had 21 open
children and a 300,000,000-token grant, so the loop was committed to spending the whole
grant with no operator control short of a signal.

**Lock takeover is not the stop control it looks like.** `supervise.acquire`
(`supervise.py:159`) steals a lock only when the holder's heartbeat is older than
`STALE_AFTER_S`, and a healthy supervisor beats continuously. Takeover is crash recovery;
a working supervisor cannot be handed over or asked to finish.

So the only available lever is a signal to the process, and that is exactly the action the
repo's own cost rule forbids: **cost is bounded by sizing the work, never by interrupting a
working agent**. When this was hit, three lanes were mid-dispatch at 16.4M, 18.2M and 8.3M
tokens — roughly \$40 of work that a stop would have discarded — and two further lanes had
just been unblocked and would have been stranded with live worktrees.

## Why a signal is not good enough even when it is safe

The lanes are `claude -p` subprocesses of the supervisor. A signal to the parent leaves
their disposition unspecified: killed mid-write, or orphaned and still spending against a
grant nothing is now metering. Neither is a documented outcome, and the operator has to
pick the moment by watching a log, which is the manual polling this harness exists to
remove.

## Shape

The beat callback already exists for precisely this kind of prompt interrupt — `hb.check()`
runs once per pass and raises when ownership is lost, and the dispatcher takes a `beat`
callback "so a takeover stops the pass promptly" (`supervise.py:265`). The stop wants the
same path: a sentinel the beat reads, so the supervisor finishes the round it is in —
landing everything already dispatched — and then returns instead of seeding another.

A pass bound (`--max-passes`) is the cheaper half and worth having as well, because it lets
an operator commit to a bounded spend at launch rather than having to intervene at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a supervisor with lanes in flight, when an operator requests a stop, then the
  current round completes and every dispatched lane lands before the process returns, and
  no further lanes are seeded — check: a test starts a session with a stubbed runner,
  requests a stop mid-round, and asserts every in-flight lane reached a terminal route and
  the next round seeded zero lanes.
- Given `--max-passes N`, when the Nth pass completes, then the supervisor returns even
  with open children remaining — check: a test with two open children and `--max-passes 1`
  asserts one pass ran and the process returned non-zero with the reason named.
- Given a stop request, when the operator inspects the session afterwards, then the reason
  and who asked is recorded — check: a test asserts the stop writes a marker naming the
  requester.

## Demonstration

`basicly loop stop basicly-u2hl` (or the equivalent surface) prints the lanes it is waiting
to land, then returns after they land; `basicly worktree list` shows no orphaned worktree
and `basicly loop status` on each lane shows a terminal phase rather than a live dispatch.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop.skill.yaml`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none

## Context

Found by the lane-E cross-cutting survey 2026-08-14. Three defects in the lists' own claims, each verified.

```text
pyproject.toml:90   says the two false positives sit at hooks.py:280 and :282
                    they are at precommit_config.py:127 and :129
                    hooks.py:280 is now a different function
pyproject.toml      says two of them are true false positives
                    a third is: tb, a protocol parameter at tracker_usage.py:286
.ruff.toml          records 111 hits for one ignored rule
                    measured today: 187
```

A maintainer who follows the first citation audits the wrong module.

The rule with the stale count keeps its rationale, which survives. What rots is the number, and nothing ratchets the growth of an ignored family. A second recorded count still measures correctly, so the rot is per entry rather than systemic.

## A fourth of the same class

`tracker_surface.py:51` points at a function in `tracker_usage`. The function lives in `tracker_invocation.py:62`. And `tracker_surface.py:52` re-spells a constant from `tracker_invocation.py:30`. The concept a token that can be a tracker surface word has two definitions.

## Acceptance

- When a suppression entry names a file and a line, then that citation resolves to the suppressed condition.
- When an ignored-rule entry records a count, then a check reports the count as stale once it drifts.
- When the surface-word concept is searched, then one definition remains.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml`
- `.ruff.toml`
- `src/basicly/tracker_surface.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_invocation.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run vulture src/basicly .scripts --min-confidence 60` and `uv run ruff check`.
payload.title: the suppression lists cite the wrong file and carry a stale count

payload.description:
## Context

An audit of 24 live work items on 2026-08-13 checked every `file:line` citation it relied on.
**14 of 14 had drifted.** This is one missing mechanism, not fourteen defects:

```text
runner.py:141-142        -> :151            basicly.toml:512 / :568   -> :619
supervise.py:2700        -> :2727           cli.py:3582               -> :3589
merge.py:466 / :520      -> :475 / :529     cli.py:3265               -> :3314
policy.py:560            -> :673            run_record.py:605         -> :742
supervise.py:1286        -> :1222           loop.py:327               -> moved module
supervise._band_verdict  -> working_set.py:285
```

Why it matters more than tidiness: a citation is how a work item makes its claim checkable, and
the repo's own rule is "re-check a cited `file:line` before fixing it"
(`implementation-plan.md`, section 1 item 2). When every citation is stale, that rule costs a
re-derivation per item and readers stop performing it - which is how `basicly-4xmu`'s
reproduction came to omit `_run_proposer`, and how a P0 was nearly built against a remedy the
plan had replaced.

Two live items show the failure in its worst form, where the **symbol** moved rather than the
line: `basicly-esxp` cites `supervise._band_verdict`, now `working_set.py:285`; and
`basicly-o40x`'s declared `## Scope` names `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop.skill.yaml`, a
path that **matches no file** (the real one is `harness-loop/skill.yaml`). A scope glob matching
nothing is what `basicly-a3ab.3` exists to catch for catalog entries, and nothing catches it for
a bead's own scope block - `basicly policy dor` warns only when a `## Scope` heading parsed to
zero globs, not when a declared glob matches zero files.

## Why a line number is the wrong thing to store

The durable identifier is the symbol, not the offset. A check that re-resolves
`module.function` and reports where it now lives survives every refactor; a check that compares
stored line numbers fails on the first unrelated insertion above them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick any live bead older than a week that cites a `file:line`.
2. Open the cited line. Positive control before reporting drift: confirm the file exists and the
   symbol is findable elsewhere in it, so "wrong line" is distinguishable from "deleted".
3. Observed: 14 of 14 sampled citations pointed at the wrong line or a moved module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a live work item citing a symbol that has moved, when the check runs, then it names the
  item, the stale citation and the symbol's current location - check: a test plants a bead
  citing a known-moved symbol and asserts all three appear.
- Given a work item whose declared `## Scope` carries a glob matching no file on disk, when the
  check runs, then it is named - check: `basicly-o40x` is reported today, and a corrected scope
  is not.
- Given a citation that is still correct, when the check runs, then it is silent - check: the
  false-positive case, asserted on a bead whose citation resolves.
- Given the check, when it cannot find the file at all, then it distinguishes deleted from moved
  - check: a bead citing a path removed in `28257e9` reports "deleted", not "drifted".

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/check_bead_citations.py` names the drifted citations across the live
tracker and exits non-zero, and `--strict` or a per-bead argument reports one item.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_bead_citations.py`
- `tests/test_check_bead_citations.py`
- `basicly.toml`
payload.title: Re-resolve a work items cited symbol so a stale line number is caught not inherited

## Context

A start-of-session sync check found five claims in docs/plan/implementation-plan.md, docs/requirements/factory-loop.md and docs/requirements/work-tracker.md that are false against the tree, and three of them name a closed bead as live work.

## What is false

- AGENTS.md is 14428 characters against a 16000 cap, not 1135 over. codex.yaml line 9 records the cap moving 12000 to 16000 on 2026-08-09 after the a3ab.1 audit found the overrun is the scoped tier Codex cannot receive as separate paths rules files. Three documents outlived that by five days and the plan named a3ab.1 as the gating item of the v0.10.0 row while a3ab.1, .10 and .12 are all closed.
- Plan section 3 asserts resolve_role is called from one site and implementer is the only role ever to reach an argv, citing basicly-4xmu. 4xmu is closed. Measured three call sites in src: loop.py 818, loop.py 1062 and supervise.py 2679, and the classify and decompose phases both resolve.
- Plan section 5.2 lists eleven plumbing rows in the present tense of a live defect. Five are closed, including every P0 the section 5.1 ordering argument rests on.
- Plan section 5.4 holds u6jq.1 on a stated precondition, after rrah and 5vu4, and both are closed.
- factory-loop section 12 says --forward-subagent-text is passed nowhere; it is passed at runner.py 179. Section 9 says cli.py is 5097 lines and src totals 36641; measured 4911 and 42966.
- work-tracker.md said no implementation starts from this document while eight kit modules totalling about 264 KB are committed under .basicly/core/kit/tracker/, and its own section 7 trigger, basicly-kjc5.22, is closed.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

Every one of these is the failure mode plan section 1.3 already names: a closed bead proves code exists, not that a claim is still true. The documents are the corpus a decider reads, and basicly-b9ef exists because a decider reasoned from a refuted claim in a bead and wedged two lanes.

## Context

D26 is explicit: **a dispatch with no resolved tier is a bug, not a default** - an omitted model inherits the session's, which is usually the most expensive one, so the routing rule defeats itself silently.

Found while running the admission test for a new role, 2026-08-14.

## Measured

- agent.schema.json required is [schema_version, name, purpose, triggers, returns, posture, tools, slots]. **tier is optional.**
- code-reviewer and security-auditor declare no tier. agents.py:307 reads str(data.get('tier') or '').strip(), so both resolve to the empty string.
- basicly catalog lint and basicly agents-check both pass on that tree, so no gate binds.
- Both are ad-hoc agents vendored to consumers by basicly install, so a consumer inherits the untier-ed pair.
- Nobody declares maximum at all. The ladder has four rungs and the roster uses three, which is the same dead-definition shape recorded for skills.

## What the fix is

Make tier required in the schema, assign one to the two roles that lack it, and let catalog lint refuse a source without it. Assigning the tiers is a judgement per role and is the part that needs a human.

## Relationship to basicly-a3yi

Different halves of the same rule and both are needed. a3yi resolves a **declared** tier into the projected surface that has a model slot. This bead is that a tier can be **undeclared** and nothing notices - so a3yi could land in full and these two roles would still spawn on whatever the session is running.

## Note on the third half

Verified 2026-08-14: the tier kit ships (.basicly/core/kit/tier/claude_tier_hook.py) and its hook is **not installed in this repo** - .claude/settings.json registers PreToolUse and PostToolUse only. So a declared tier reaches no spawn here today, by any path.
payload.title: the agent schema lets a role ship with no tier and two already do

## CORRECTED 2026-08-13

One claim below is wrong. It says the harness-loop skill does not mention `--runner manual`.
**It does, at `harness-loop/skill.yaml:432`**, in an unrelated context (the band verdict). The
real gap is narrower and still real: `grep -i repair` over that skill returns **zero**, so
nothing in it warns that a failed landing briefs and dispatches a metered repair.

Sequencing, added from the same audit: do this split **before** `basicly-u2hl.42`, which is a
trigger-gated content rewrite of the same two skills. Splitting afterwards pays that rewrite
twice. The edge is now recorded.

---

## Context

`.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml` is 32,423 characters - 2.3x the next largest
skill (`tool-br` at 14,084) and by far the most used (41 invocations, most recent
2026-08-13).

It covers two separable jobs: driving one unit with `loop run`/`loop advance`, and running a
multi-lane pass with `loop preflight`/`loop supervise` including the band table, grant
sizing, and lane watching. A session doing one never needs the other.

It is also incomplete in a way that cost real time on 2026-08-13: nothing in it warns that
`loop advance` dispatches a metered repair agent when the previous landing gate failed. That
gap produced an unbudgeted `claude -p` dispatch against a spent grant, and the fix is
`--runner manual`, which the skill does not mention.

## Proposed check

Two skills, each under the size of the current one, with no duplicated section; the
multi-lane half names the repair dispatch and `--runner manual`. `basicly skills-check
--all-default-roots` passes and the usage counter shows both reachable.

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-5p49` shipped the tree-growth signal and met four of its five acceptance criteria. This bead is the fifth.

The signal prints from `basicly verify`. It is not recorded on the run and it does not appear in the supervised pass line, so it is visible to whoever runs a gate and invisible to whoever reads a pass afterwards.

## Why the lane stopped rather than reaching

Two reasons, both stated by the implementer rather than discovered later.

The scope globs on `basicly-5p49` were `.scripts/`, `basicly.toml` and `tests/`. The pass line comes from `supervise._report_coverage`, beside the existing band and spend lines, and the run fields come from `run_record`. Both are outside those globs.

And there is a hard blocker. `src/basicly/supervise.py` is frozen by the module-size ratchet and may only shrink, so adding a report line to it fails the gate today. That is the same shape `basicly-r343` hit: a ratchet refuses a change to a file, and the real fix is a split that has nothing to do with the change.

## What that makes this bead depend on

`basicly-wotk` extracts the outcome routing sink out of `supervise.py` and is the item that gives that file headroom. Doing this one first means either a second waiver or a refactor bolted onto a reporting change.

## Why it is worth doing at all

The standing rule is that a demoted or advisory number must still be recorded on the run, surfaced in the pass line and kept falsifiable against the ledger. A signal that only prints during a gate run satisfies none of those. It also cannot earn the right to block, because earning it requires a firing history and nothing records one.

## Acceptance

- When a supervised pass completes, then its line states the tree-growth value and the window it covers, beside the existing band and spend lines.
- When a run record is written, then it carries the same value and window.
- When the value is read back from the ledger, then it is comparable across passes, so a trend is computable without re-running the gate.
- When the signal has no window to measure, for example in a shallow clone, then the pass line says so rather than printing a zero.
- When any of this is added, then `supervise.py` does not grow past its frozen baseline.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `.scripts/check_tree_growth.py`
- `tests/`

## Depends on

`basicly-wotk`, which gives `supervise.py` the headroom this needs.

## Demonstration

Run a supervised pass and read the tree-growth line beside the band line, then read the same value back out of the run record.
payload.title: the tree growth signal is not on the run record or the pass line

## Context

Found by the lane-A survey 2026-08-14, with the arithmetic closed.

`policy.py` carries at least four nameable responsibilities: gate and checkpoint policy, bead body scaffolding, autonomy grants and spend metering, human wait telemetry, and the confirm-code store.

It has 10 tokens of size headroom and 0.0 percentage points of prose headroom.

## Only one cut clears both gates

```text
slice                lines        tokens   prose    remainder
wait telemetry       2279-2609    3,405    45.7%    fails density
grants and spend     1455-2140    8,126    56.3%    fails density
confirm code         1204-1274      688    32.4%    fails density
body scaffolding      229-330     1,283    67.5%    passes, remainder 57.1%
```

A cut leaves the remainder green only above 57.6% prose. A new module passes only below 50%. The two windows do not overlap, so the move must land in an existing under-cap module.

## The measured home

`dispatch_brief.py` is 2,523 tokens at 37.4% prose. After the merge it is about 3,806 tokens at about 47.6%, under both caps. It is one tier above `policy`, so all four external callers stay legal: `cli.py:2174`, `supervise.py:1056`, `decompose.py:713` and `decompose.py:1888`. Its theme is prose the engine authors.

`scaffolds.py` is not the home. Its charter at `scaffolds.py:1-13` is installer file templates and it declines this content.

## Take the rename while the seam is open

`compose_body` means two things: bead bodies in `policy` and agent markdown at `agents.py:400`. Rename the bead-body one during the move.

## The honest boundary

The wait telemetry is the conceptually cleaner second cut and is not dispatchable today. Its 45.7% prose share fails the density ratchet from either direction. A further split of `policy.py` needs either prose reduction in the remainder or a deliberate frozen-share decision. Neither is in this scope.

## Acceptance

- When the scaffolding functions move, then both size gates pass with no new frozen entry and no raised baseline, and the `policy.py` entry shrinks in the same diff.
- When the four external call sites are compiled, then they resolve against the new home.
- When a bead body is scaffolded for a bug, then the printed body is byte-identical to today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`

## Depends on

The loop-core dead-symbol slice. Its deletions are the only size headroom available for the import line this leaves behind.

## Demonstration

Compare a scaffolded bug body before and after, run both ratchet scripts, and `uv run pytest -q`.

## Context

R6 in `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md:73` requires that "no committed artifact carries a
host path, username or hostname". It exists because the `br` export wrote
`source_repo_path` on 328 of 332 records.

`.basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl` is committed (confirmed with `git ls-files`) and **every
one of its 3,775 events carries `"actor": "<redacted:machine-username>"`**, with `"created_by": "<redacted:machine-username>"` inside
payloads. Absolute paths *are* correctly redacted - 3 hits, all of the form `/home/<user>/...`
- so the redaction pass works on paths and does not look at the actor field.

No gate sees this: `.basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py` scans for paths (`:42` scopes to
`^\.beads/.*\.jsonl$`) and not for usernames, and its scope does not include
`.basicly/ledger/`. No bead was found covering it.

So the artifact built to satisfy the nine paid-for requirements reproduces one of them, in the
one field the redactor does not read. This is the same class of defect as the `br` export
R6 was derived from.

## Open question this bead must settle first

Whether R6's requirement column is intended to bind the owned ledger's `actor` field at all,
or only host paths. If actor attribution is wanted, it needs a stable non-identifying form
(an opaque per-repo id, or the git author already in the commit) rather than the OS username.

## Proposed check

Extend the path scan to the owned ledger and to usernames, with a positive control: a test
plants a known username in a ledger event and asserts the gate fails, and asserts it passes on
a redacted equivalent.

## Context

`.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` treats `.basicly/core/schemas/**/*` as a field-consumer site
(`FIELD_SITE_GLOBS`, line 123) and indexes it with `_tokens()` (line 300), which returns **every
identifier-shaped word in the file**. A JSON schema is mostly `description` prose, so ordinary
English counts as a reference to a dataclass field of the same name.

Reproduced 2026-08-13 on `basicly-r4jm`: adding five schema files whose descriptions contained the
English word **holds** made `record-field:basicly.worktree.RemovalVerdict.holds` stop reproducing,
and the gate reported it as a stale baseline entry. `worktree.py` was byte-identical to main.

**The advice is the dangerous part.** The gate says "remove the entry from BASELINE". Obeying it
would delete a real dead-code finding because unrelated prose used a common word - and the entry
could never come back, because the prose stays. That is the same failure shape this script already
documents at lines 90-98 for parallel worktrees: "the gate advice on a stale entry is remove the
entry, so a maintainer following it would empty the baseline and blind the surface permanently".

Exposed field names are any that are also English: `holds`, `result`, `steps`, `level`, `reason`,
`gates`, `claims`, `output`, `delta`. Nine of the 45 baseline entries are words of this shape.

The intent of scanning schemas is sound - a schema **key** named for a field is a real reference.
The defect is scanning the whole file rather than its keys.

## Steps to Reproduce

- On a clean tree, `uv run python .scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` - passes, 45 known findings.
- Add any file under `.basicly/core/schemas/` containing the word `holds` in a description string.
- Re-run - `record-field:basicly.worktree.RemovalVerdict.holds ... no longer reproduces`.
- Observed: prose marks a field as wired. Expected: only a schema key or enum value does.

## Scope

- `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py`
- `tests/test_wired_or_deleted.py
payload.title: wired or deleted counts English prose in a schema as a field reference

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-07 landing `basicly-3ifz.1`, **hours after `basicly-69az` shipped**
(`a90585f`). That fix reads the lane tree's `config.py` schema via `ast` so a lane can add
a `basicly.toml` key and declare it in one commit. It covers exactly one config surface.
Here is the same mechanism on a second one.

1. A lane adds `src/basicly/tuning.py` and declares the module in `.importlinter`'s layer
   contract (`policy | tuning | verify`) in the same commit.
2. `basicly verify --mode full` inside the lane worktree passes: 16 gates PASS,
   `Contracts: 2 kept, 0 broken`.
3. `basicly loop run <id>` lands it from the base checkout.

Observed - the merge gate fails, twice, identically, and the convergence detector escalates:

```
Missing layer in container 'basicly': module basicly.tuning does not exist.
merge failed: verify full failed: lint-imports
```

Expected: a lane that adds a module and declares it in the import contract can land.

## Cause: same as 69az, different config surface

The landing runs verify from the **base** checkout, so `import_linter` resolves the
`basicly` package base has installed - which has no `tuning` module - while reading the
**lane tree's** `.importlinter`, which declares one. The contract names a module the
analyzed package lacks.

This is `69az`'s exact shape: a declaration in the lane's tree referencing something only
the lane's code provides, validated by the pre-merge process. `69az` fixed it for
`basicly.toml` by resolving the schema from the tree under test. `.importlinter` was not in
that fix's scope and resolves the package, not a schema, so the same remedy does not
transfer unchanged.

**The trap that makes this expensive**: running the gate inside the worktree passes,
because `uv run` there resolves the worktree's own package. So the lane, and any human
checking by hand, both see green. Only the landing sees it, and it reads as a flaky gate. I
diagnosed it as transient on the first occurrence and was wrong; the correction is recorded
on `basicly-3ifz.1`.

## Cost

Two full rework rounds plus one escalation on `basicly-3ifz.1`, then a hand landing. The
convergence detector fired correctly both times - "this round changed nothing it reports" -
which is right and still leaves the lane stuck, because the lane cannot fix a failure that
does not exist in its own tree.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a lane whose commit adds a module and declares it in the import contract when the landing runs verify from the base checkout then lint-imports analyses the tree under test rather than the pre-merge package, and a regression test proves the bare missing-layer refusal red first
payload.title: The import contract is checked against the pre-merge package so a lane adding a module cannot land

## Context

`.scripts/check_module_size.py` imports `COUNT_DELTA`, `FRAGMENT_DIR`, `RATCHET_SECTION` and
`compose` from `basicly.dropin`, so a lane records a ratchet move in its own
`basicly.d/<bead-id>.toml` and never edits `pyproject.toml`.

`.scripts/check_comment_density.py` does not. Its `load_ratchet` reads `pyproject.toml`
directly and composes nothing, so a lane that adds a `comment-density-waiver` has no drop-in
path and must edit `[tool.comment_density] waiver_count` in `pyproject.toml` by hand.

Found on `basicly-u2hl.54.3`, which wrote `basicly.d/basicly-u2hl.54.3.toml` with
`[ratchet.comment_density] count_delta = 1`, watched the gate ignore it, and edited
`pyproject.toml` instead. The fragment was deleted rather than left as config nothing reads.

This is the exact collision shape `basicly-ef7t` fixed for the other anchors: `waiver_count`
is a total, and a total does not compose. Two concurrent lanes each adding one waiver both
measure 0, both record 1, and the merged tree holds 2 with a gate neither rebase conflicted on.
Single-lane work does not hit it, which is why it survived.

## Steps to Reproduce

- Add a column-0 `# comment-density-waiver: <reason>` to any module over the cap.
- Record `[ratchet.comment_density] count_delta = 1` in `basicly.d/<bead-id>.toml`.
- Run `uv run python .scripts/check_comment_density.py`.
- Observed: `1 module(s) carry a waiver but waiver_count is 0`. Expected: the delta composed,
  as `check_module_size.py` composes its own.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py

Filed from OQ-18 (docs/requirements/factory-loop.md). The CLI half is settled and measured in section 6.3; this bead is the VS Code half only.

WHAT IS KNOWN [S, vendor doc, 2026-08-11]: VS Code discovers custom agents from .github/agents/ AND
.claude/agents/, and states it maps claude-specific tool names to VS Code tools, accepting both the
YAML array and the claude comma-separated string. It publishes no mapping table. Its own vocabulary
is namespaced and different again - 'search/codebase', 'edit/editFiles', 'web/fetch'.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: whether Read/Grep/Glob actually resolve there, and whether an unmapped name fails
safe (drops to nothing) or fails open (grants everything). Only the second matters for posture: an
agent this repo certifies read-only would hold write tools on that surface.

HOW TO SETTLE IT: the same three-probe shape used on the CLI - a restrictive list, the same list plus
a write/execute tool as the positive control, and a list of names known-good in VS Code's own
vocabulary. Record the transcript. Skills need no equivalent probe: .claude/skills/ is a documented
default discovery root for VS Code and was measured working on the CLI (34 of 34 listed).

## Context

Skill projection is gated only by `technologies:` detection: `tool-starship`, `tool-tmux`,
`tool-wezterm`, `tool-zsh` and `wsl` are in `.basicly/core/skills/` and are not projected
into `.claude/skills/` here, because their technology is not detected.

There is no way to express "ship this skill to consumer repos but do not project it in
basicly" for a skill with no distinguishing technology. Two skills need exactly that:

- `worktree-isolation` - the engine provisions worktrees itself at classify approval, so the
  skill is redundant here, but a consumer repo not running the loop still needs it.
- `tier-injection` - its own description is about installing a kit "in another repository",
  so it is consumer-facing by definition.

Both currently project here and are never used.

This is a budget question, not tidiness. Both are `invocation: model`, so both carry a
description and both occupy the host's model-invoked listing. Measured 2026-08-13: that
listing is 1,696 tokens against a 2,000-token budget (`catalog_lint.py:313-322`, 1% of the
adapter-default window) - 304 tokens of headroom. Two unreachable-here skills are spending
part of it, and the host evicts descriptions least-invoked-first when it overflows, so the
skills paying the cost are the first to be silenced.

## Proposed check

An opt-out declared in the catalog source or `basicly.toml`, verified by a test that builds
the projection and asserts the named skill is absent from `.claude/skills/` while still
present in the distributed catalog.

payload.description:
## Goal

An interactive web page anyone can run locally that visualises what the harness is doing: the work
tracker and its backlog, the factory while it runs, lane state, gates, spend and health. The target
is a wall display in an engineering room, full screen, so everyone sees what is happening and can
step in.

**The reusable part is the contract, not the page.** `harness-board/v1` is designed so any harness can
emit it, which is why unit A is L3 and comes first.

## The design

The full solution design is `01-solution-design.md` on this epic's own harness branch, per D33: no new
requirement or plan document is ever created under `docs/`. It carries the six D17 sections, the
contract, this decomposition, the library and licence findings, and the open questions. Read it before
working any child - the bead bodies are the plan gate's view of it, not a replacement for it.

## The argument, and the correction inside it

The framing this was commissioned under was that a wall display attacks the rendezvous cost
`factory-loop.md` section 7.4 measured. **That framing was partly refuted by its own author.** The
design replicated section 7.4 on today's ledger (n=154, 44.4 h, 83% in 19 tail events, replicating the
recorded 85%/17) and added the axis section 7.4 lacked - *when the engine asked*, in local wall clock.

```text
asked during plausible in-room hours    4 events   14,527 s   9% of all human wait
asked out of hours                                            74%
the 17% head                            60 s median, no display beats it
```

So the arrival mechanism is real and its ceiling is about 4 hours of 44.4, at n=4. Section 7.4 had
already said it: *"eight hours asleep, eighty-one seconds awake."*

**What carries the project instead is unwatched spend.** $953.82 over 357 dispatches, a $24.64
single-dispatch maximum, 1.25B tokens, 12 `[harness-overrun]` markers, and
`loop session basicly-kjc5 --json` reporting `spent_tokens 177,970,761` against
`token_budget 4,000,000` - in a JSON surface nobody watches, behind a command that costs 11 seconds
to run. **That figure is unclassified**: it is either an unenforced ceiling or a scope mismatch
between a per-grant budget and a lifetime total, and `basicly-e2mz.13` settles it. A board built over
an unclassified number is observability over a possibly-broken control, so that probe gates unit C.

## Owner decisions taken 2026-08-14

1. **Phased.** Ship A, B, C and G only, then run four weeks against the real factory before deciding
   D, E and F. Roughly 470,000 tokens, zero long-lived processes, and it satisfies
   `work-tracker.md` requirement 10 exactly as recorded.
2. **Requirement 10 is amended, not overridden.** It stays as written; one sentence permits a
   live-attached mode that must display its own age and must never use the words "real time".
   `basicly-e2mz.14` carries the edit.

payload.description:
## Context

**The factory keeps no record of what its agents did.** A dispatched lane is a `claude -p`
subprocess whose `stream-json` output `runner.py` reads line by line into an **in-memory
sink** and spends entirely on token accounting. When the process exits the transcript is
gone. Measured 2026-08-08 on session `basicly-u2hl:bc7cc925`:

```text
.basicly/usage/run-records.json      token and cost totals per dispatch
.basicly/usage/tool-usage.json       counts
.basicly/usage/tracker-usage.jsonl   tracker calls
.basicly/usage/verify-*.json         gate results
                                     <- no lane transcript, anywhere
```

So the harness records **how much** every lane cost and **nothing about what it did**. The
only narrative is the supervisor's own stdout, which is written to a terminal and, if the
operator does not redirect it, is lost when the pane closes.

## Why this is a P0 and not an ergonomic wish

The repo's own rules are unsatisfiable without it:

- `quality-gate` requires evidence for a claim. A claim about what a lane did cannot be
  evidenced after the lane ends.
- `factory-loop-requirements.md` section 11 item 2 wants **termination-condition and
  step-repetition detectors** and calls them "trace-level detectors an engine with a
  dispatch ledger can implement cheaply". There is no trace to detect on.
- Section 12 records that the stream is already read and "spends it entirely on token
  accounting" - this bead is the other half of that observation.
- D6's dark-factory column says progress is "stream exists, unused".

Recorded live on 2026-08-08: the owner asked how to see what a lane was doing and there was
no answer to give. Every statement about lane behaviour that session rested on an operator
having happened to redirect stdout, to a path outside the repo. That is auditing by luck.

## What already exists to build on

`runner.py` already parses the stream into `StreamEvent`s and already hands them to a sink
(`runner.py:1397` and around `:1138`); `event_text` already extracts the prose a progress
line shows, with thinking blocks excluded because their signature blobs dwarf the text. So
the plumbing is present and only the durable sink is missing. Redaction already applies to
the sink's copy (`:1268`), which is what makes a persisted copy safe to write.

## Steps to Reproduce

```text
$ ls .basicly/usage/
checkpoint-confirms.json  run-records.json  supervisor.lock  tool-usage.json
tracker-usage.jsonl  verify-checks.json  verify-run.json

$ grep -n 'transcript\|log_path\|logfile' src/basicly/runner.py | grep -c 'open(\|write_text'
0
```

Observed: 32 dispatches recorded on 2026-08-08 costing $122.41, and zero recoverable
transcripts. Expected: each dispatch leaves a readable, greppable record of what it did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a dispatched lane, when the dispatch ends by any route - success, timeout kill, or
  error - then its forwarded text is on disk under a path naming the bead and the session
  - check: a test dispatches a stubbed runner, kills it mid-stream, and asserts the partial
  transcript exists and contains the events emitted before the kill.
- Given a completed pass, when an operator greps the transcript directory, then every
  landing route and every lane's step sequence is recoverable - check: a test asserts the
  written file contains each routed outcome for a two-lane pass.
- Given a lane whose output contained a secret-shaped string, when the transcript is
  written, then the value is redacted - check: a test asserts a planted token is absent from
  the file while its surrounding line is present.
- Given transcripts accumulating over many passes, when the directory grows past its bound,
  then old ones rotate - check: a test asserts the retention bound is enforced.

## Demonstration

```text
$ basicly loop supervise <epic>
$ ls .basicly/usage/lane-logs/
<session>/basicly-u2hl.18.jsonl  <session>/basicly-u2hl.20.jsonl  <session>/pass.log
$ grep '^routed:' .basicly/usage/lane-logs/<session>/pass.log
```

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/lane_log.py`
- `tests/test_lane_log.py`
- `changelog.d/basicly-rrah.added.md`
- `.importlinter`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `100000`
- depends on: none

payload.description:
## Context

Step 5 of the cutover, and the one that actually removes `br` from the engine. Measured
2026-08-07 against `main` @ `b97a653`.

`comments` is the single largest remaining dependency: 26 of the engine 55 `_run_br` call
sites, and 714 of 1568 recorded br invocations (45% of all traffic) per
`docs/design/work-tracker.md` §3.0. Split by direction it is 22 `comments add` and 6
`comments list`.

## The surface is 89% harness transport

Measured over the live tracker (1834 comments across 427 of 644 beads):

| | count | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[harness-*]` markers | **1646** | **89%** |
| human prose | 188 | 10% |

By kind: policy 828, wait 259, run 225, cost 154, decision 113, info 36, sizing 19,
overrun 12. Every one is harness-owned state - checkpoint approvals, grants, gate
records, rework counters, needs-input, the human-wait clock, dispatch records, spend
rollups - using a beads comment purely as transport.

This is what plan §10 standing constraint anticipated: "Land evidence as `[harness-*]`
comment markers - a format we own, which migrates with us - not as tracker fields." The
markers were chosen so this migration would be possible. It is now due.

## The destination already exists and already holds the data

`events.py` declares `KIND_COMMENT` and a dedicated `KIND_DISPATCH`, and the step-1
import (commit `b97a653`) already wrote **1831 comment events** into the ledger. So this
is not a data migration - the facts are in both stores. It is a seam change: the engine
must write and read its own markers natively rather than spawning br.

`br.py` records why that is tractable: the write surface is one funnel
(`run_br`/`try_run_br`) and the record-read surface is one function (`read_record`), so
this is an edit to a seam rather than to 26 callers.

## Deliberately out of scope

The 188 human comments. A human writing prose on a bead runs `br` directly; the engine
never spawns that. Removing the engine dependency does not require removing the human one,
and conflating them is how this grows into a general-purpose tracker - an explicit
non-goal (plan §2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the engine at tracker mode owned when a checkpoint approval or gate record or grant or rework counter or dispatch record is written then it is written as a ledger event and read back from the ledger with no br comments spawn, and a test proves the engine completes that write and read with br absent from PATH

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`

payload.acceptance_criteria: When a role declaring a tier is dispatched and a model pin is also in force then the model the turn runs on is the one the role declared, or the record reports tier_honoured false with the override named.
payload.description:
## Context

Second defect recorded on `basicly-jn1x`, **not fixed there** because its precondition is not met.

`runner.py` applies both flags on one argv: `_apply_role(spec, _apply_model(spec, ...), role)`.
Measured on the probe that filed `jn1x`: `--agent probeagent(model: haiku) --model sonnet` ran the
turn on **sonnet**, so `--model` overrides the model an agent definition declares.

The run record then reports `tier_honoured: true` for that shape, because the field means
something narrower than a reader assumes - `run_record.py` documents it as False "only when a tier
was asked for and the family could not pin one at all". A role whose declared tier was overridden
is not that case, so the record is not wrong by its own contract and is misleading against the
question a reader asks it.

## Why it is not actionable yet

Decision D30: a provider model id never appears in an agent file, generated or not. So **no
projected agent carries a `model:` today** and there is nothing for `--model` to override. The
injection that would put one there is `basicly-a3yi`, still open.

Filing a fixture for the override now would be inventing the shape rather than observing it, which
is the failure this repository has already paid for twice.

## What changed under it

`basicly-jn1x` landed the recorded argv, so the co-occurrence is now **visible in the ledger**: a
record whose command carries both `--agent` and `--model` is exactly the shape at risk. Before
that, 0 of 357 records named either flag and the question could not be asked of the data at all.

## When to take this

After `basicly-a3yi`. Then decide whether the fix is to drop `--model` when a role declares one,
or to widen `tier_honoured` to mean "the tier that was asked for is the tier that ran" - the
second is the honest reading of the name and changes an existing contract, so it is a decision
rather than a patch.

## Context

Found by the lane-C survey 2026-08-14. The most expensive class here, and this repository has paid for it twice already.

Which routes an escalation offers is composed as free prose in five wordings, at `policy.py:638-640`, `supervise.py:2730`, `:3709`, `:3717` and `:3842`. It is then re-derived by parsing on the consumer side.

```text
cli.py:3608   _OFFERS_PARK = "or park?"        suffix match
cli.py:3576   _RETRY_ANSWER                    leading-token regular expression
policy.py     gate_from_rework_escalation      question-regex gate extraction
policy.py     gate_from_unreliable_escalation  applied at cli.py:3672
```

## Two shipped defects of exactly this shape are already on record

The docstrings themselves record them at `cli.py:3585-3587` and `cli.py:3627-3631`. `basicly-4tjt` offered three routes and implemented none. `basicly-vkjt` offered a park route whose answer silently did nothing.

## The second half

The consequence carriers `_carry_out_rework_retry`, `_carry_out_rework_hold` and `_announce_land_anyway` are at `cli.py:3582-3680`. They are engine semantics that live in the command-line tier, reachable and tested only through the argument parser. That is the shape `basicly-tcmy.16` names for the install lifecycle.

Today the three answer sites stay consistent only because the engine sites self-answer with a marker the carriers happen to refuse.

## Acceptance

- When an escalation is enqueued, then the decision item carries structured route and gate fields written by its composer.
- When an answer is recorded, then the consequence is selected on those fields, from a module below the command-line tier.
- When the suffix and regular-expression parsers are searched, then none remains.
- When a new escalation wording is added, then its routes cannot detach from their consequences.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/landing_gate.py`
- `src/basicly/working_set.py`
- their tests

## Depends on

Serialize with `basicly-tcmy.12`, which touches the same region of the command-line module.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_policy.py -q`, then answer a real escalation on a fixture session and read the recorded consequence.

payload.description:
## Context

Found while landing two lanes on 2026-08-14.

Each ratchet gate ratchets its own waiver count. Nothing counts them together, and nothing reviews one after it is granted.

```text
module-size waivers      1 -> 2   basicly-r343, bought on cost, expires under basicly-kr7t
comment-density waivers  1 -> 2   basicly-feje, bought on cohesion, no expiry needed
```

Two waivers in one session, from two lanes that were not about size. Both were argued honestly and both are defensible on their own. The pattern is the finding, not either grant.

## Why a per-gate count is not enough

A waiver is the one escape every size rule leaves open, so it is where pressure goes when a ratchet blocks unrelated work. The `basicly-r343` case is the shape to watch: the ratchet refused **any** change to a file, so the fix could not land without either a waiver or a refactor that had nothing to do with the bug.

The design already says waivers are ratcheted so the count may not grow silently. It grows visibly and nobody reads the number, because it is a parenthetical inside one gate's pass line.

## The distinction that must survive

Not every waiver is debt. Two kinds exist and they need different handling.

- **Bought on cohesion.** A genuinely small module whose prose is the contract it carries. Correct, permanent, and no follow-up is owed. `lens_review.py` is this.
- **Bought on cost.** The ratchet refused a change and the real fix was out of scope. Debt, and it must expire. `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` is this, and `basicly-kr7t` retires it.

Today the record cannot tell them apart. A reader sees a count.

## Acceptance

- When any waiver is granted, then its record states which of the two kinds it is.
- When a waiver is bought on cost, then it names the bead that retires it, and a check fails once that bead closes and the waiver remains.
- When the gates report, then one line states the total waiver count across all gates and how many are debt.
- Given today's four waivers, when the check runs, then it reports two cohesion and two cost, and it does not fail.

## Scope

- `.scripts/`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `basicly.d/`
- `tests/`

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly verify --mode fast` prints one waiver total with its split, and a fixture whose retiring bead is closed while its waiver stands fails the check.

payload.description:
## Context

The loop is specified in prose across `docs/design/factory-design.md`, the agent roster design and
the `harness-loop` skill. The engine implements a smaller, different thing. Measured 2026-08-07 by
a line-by-line read: **the loop is a two-state machine wearing seven labels** — real enforcement
happens at build→verify, and every other boundary is a checkpoint or a lint.

The full delta, the decisions taken, the research behind them and the open questions are
externalised in `docs/design/factory-loop-requirements.md`. That document is the input to this
epic, and this epic is how it gets built.

**This epic dogfoods its own subject.** It is decomposed and driven through the loop it specifies,
so each state's gaps are felt while the state is being built.

Headline measured gaps, each with evidence in the requirements document:

- decompose emits no dependency graph; ordering is derived from scope overlap only
- validate never runs for plain leaves, and its only deterministic check is re-running verify
- SHIPPED 2026-08-08 (basicly-u2hl.4): repair now runs in the lane's own worktree, briefed with
  the gate's actual findings
- CI gates guard two boundaries of six as of 2026-08-08 (basicly-u2hl.1 added the plan gate on
  entry to BUILD, alongside build->verify)
- zero of seven personas are implemented
- retrospective does not exist in the engine
- CORRECTED 2026-08-08 (shipped, basicly-u2hl.3): the original claim here — that `park` (Hold)
  re-admits the lane, a fail-open — was REFUTED. `deferred` was always excluded from
  `DISPATCHABLE_STATUSES`, so a held lane was never re-admitted. The real gap was that no
  answer carried the verb out, and both writes now exist (`policy.hold_lane`,
  `basicly loop kill`). Do not reason from the refuted claim
- SHIPPED 2026-08-08 (basicly-u2hl.5): module length is gated as a token ratchet with a
  per-file waiver

## Success Criteria

- Every loop state has an entry predicate, an exit gate and a schema-validated handoff artifact
- Verify and validate are separate states with distinct agents, and validation exercises the change
  as a consumer would rather than re-running the gate suite
- Three integrity levels select the gate set, model tier and token budget per unit of work
- All four gate verbs are implemented, with an answered Hold actually deferring the lane and
  recording its reason
- Repair happens in the existing worktree, briefed with the gate's actual findings
- The retrospective fires on a computed special-cause signal rather than on judgement
- Deterministic code-quality gates cover complexity and module length; the non-mechanical half
  ships as an agent-facing skill
- The catalog's projected output conforms to the Agent Skills specification

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the requirements document when this epic is decomposed and built then every state named in it has an implemented entry predicate and exit gate, verify and validate run as separate states, integrity levels select the gate set and budget, all four gate verbs carry out their stated behaviour, and a fresh consumer repo can be driven through the whole loop with the gates binding at every boundary

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `docs/design/factory-loop-requirements.md`

## Corpus note

This description is the decider's `intake_corpus` for every escalation on this epic, so a
stale problem statement here is read as a current fact by a machine. Two escalations on
2026-08-08 (`basicly-u2hl.14#c72fd936ab`, `basicly-u2hl.23#c72fd936ab`) abstained after
reasoning from the refuted `park` claim above. Correct a superseded bullet in place, dated,
rather than leaving it with a correction elsewhere - the design document's convention of
keeping a wrong claim as the more useful record does not survive being fed to a decider.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a child plan is loaded the plan gate shall refuse it unless every child carries a non-empty acceptance list at least one scope glob a declared dependency list a token budget and an integrity level - check: uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -q
- If the declared dependency graph contains a cycle then decompose shall refuse the plan naming the members of the cycle and create no issue - check: uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -k cycle -q
- When decompose creates children from a plan carrying dependencies it shall record each declared edge on the tracker so br dep tree shows the graph rather than deriving order from scope overlap alone - check: uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -k edges -q
- When a lane is about to be dispatched the build entry predicate shall refuse a unit whose plan fields are absent naming the missing field - check: uv run pytest tests/test_plan_gate.py -k entry -q

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/plan_gate.py`
- `tests/test_plan_gate.py`

## Context

Requirements doc section 9.2 lists nine judgement calls no linter can check: where a
module splits, naming quality, docstring usefulness, whether an abstraction earns its
keep, fixing the metric versus gaming it, noqa legitimacy, exception design, 3.14 idiom
selection and free-threading safety.

The skill exists to prevent rework: an agent that discovers a violation only when the
hook fails has already spent a round.

OQ-9 is resolved inside it - paren-free `except A, B:` is the house direction, since the
repo is 3.14-only and no linter enforces either way.

Test quality is out of scope, `test-discipline` owns it.

- `.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/**`
- `.claude/skills/python-guidelines/**`
- `.agents/skills/python-guidelines/**`
- `.basicly/generated-manifest.json`

- depends on: none

    test_decompose.py::test_the_spend_forecast_lands_within_an_order_of_magnitude_of_recorded_spend
    basicly-u2hl.14 spent 1,512,403 tokens against a recorded forecast of

That is this lane's own dispatch record, not a regression from this diff. Proof: `git diff --name-only main HEAD -- src/basicly/decompose.py src/basicly/run_record.py tests/test_decompose.py` is empty, and `git diff --name-only 8908d09 HEAD -- .beads/` is empty, so decompose, run_record, the test and the ledger are all bit-identical to main. The failure reproduces on main against the same tracker state.

Mechanism, and it is not either of the two unit errors already fixed in-engine: the band is symmetric on purpose (decompose.py:1464-1466, "one order of magnitude, either way") and both sides here are whole-lane spend, so no unit is mixed. The forecast 26,320,290 was sized for the lane's *first* dispatch, which spent 30,139,416 (1.14x, in band). Every re-dispatch of an already-complete lane is then held to that same whole-lane forecast while doing a fraction of the work: 2,785,270 (0.106x, barely in) and now 1,512,403 (0.057x, out). So a lane that is re-dispatched enough times necessarily turns main red, and the third dispatch is the one that crossed. This is a third failure shape for that gate, distinct from the two unit errors.

Not fixed here, deliberately. The only in-scope-looking repairs are widening or exempting the band, which is defeating a gate; the real fix is that a re-dispatch should not be paired against the original whole-lane forecast, and that is decompose.py work belonging to its own bead, colliding with paths this lane must not touch. ## Context

pyright's default `exclude` is `**/.*`, so `.scripts/` (9 modules) and `.basicly/core/`
(26) are not type checked at **either** mode - including the hooks that ship to consumers
and run in the dispatch path, which is the code with the widest blast radius.

Measured 2026-08-08 with a scratchpad config: 150 files analysed today, 185 with them
included, **9 errors at standard**. Four of the nine are `reportMissingImports` and may be
an `extraPaths` artifact of that probe, so **re-measure against a real in-repo include
list before treating the count as the work**.

## Scope

- `pyproject.toml`
- `basicly.toml`
- `.scripts/docs_claims.py`
- `.scripts/generate_model_map.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/kit-boundary.py`

payload.title: Type check the scripts and kit that pyright silently excludes

payload.text:
measured 2026-08-08 in base at main 96d005a, and the bead's premise is half wrong.

An `include` alone does NOT bring these trees under pyright. The default `exclude` (`**/node_modules`, `**/__pycache__`, `**/.*`) is applied on top of `include` and wins, and it also filters files named explicitly on the command line:

    uv run pyright .scripts/check_module_size.py   ->  filesAnalyzed 0
    (same file copied outside the project root)    ->  filesAnalyzed 1

So the fix must override `exclude`, not merely add `include`. Measured with a probe config at the repo root carrying include=[.scripts, .basicly/core] and exclude=[node_modules, __pycache__]:

    filesAnalyzed 37   errorCount 4   warningCount 0

The count is 4, not 9 — the handover's guess that 4 of 9 were an extraPaths artifact is inverted; 4 is the real figure and the other 5 were the artifact. The four:

    .basicly/core/hooks/kit-boundary.py:240   reportAttributeAccessIssue   Cannot access attribute lineno for class AST
    .scripts/docs_claims.py:503               reportOptionalMemberAccess   splitlines is not a known attribute of None
    .scripts/generate_model_map.py:145        reportOperatorIssue          not in unsupported for Literal['text']
    .scripts/generate_model_map.py:657        reportOptionalMemberAccess   splitlines is not a known attribute of None

pyright 1.1.411. Scope narrowed to the three files that actually carry an error plus the two config files.

payload.description:
## Context

Requirements doc D17 and section 8.1. INTAKE today records **one enum value** - `loop._on_intake`
calls `classify.classify(repo, id, work_type)` and that is the whole artifact.

Five sections, machine-checked, markdown not JSON (the `## Plan` section and
`needs-input.json` are the two proven precedents here):

```text
## Problem            the requirement in the requester's terms
## Success            an observable, not a feeling
## Consumer transcript  the command as it will be typed, and what it prints
## Out of scope       what this deliberately does not do
## Constraints        what the solution may not violate
```

## Why a transcript and not a mockup

This product has no screens. Its consumer surface is the CLI, `basicly.toml`, the catalog
schemas, the generated-file contract and the ledger format. The transcript does a mockup's
job: a reader disputes the surface before it exists, the agent receives the exact strings it
must produce, and the `quality-gate` fragment's existing rule - exercise the change as it
will really be used - checks the same thing from the shipping end.

## Ratchet

Follow `basicly-u2hl.1`: bind on the presence of the heading block, so beads filed before
this exists are admitted and one that carries the block incompletely is refused naming the
section. Do not bulk-transform the 667 existing beads.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/**`
- `tests/**`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none

- When a unit of work declares scope globs the engine shall assign exactly one integrity level by a deterministic rule over those paths - L3 for the five consumer surfaces the implementation plan section 9 names L2 for other src/basicly paths L1 for docs and test-only paths - check: uv run pytest tests/test_integrity.py -q
- If a scope classifies L3 but the change diff is under the configured line threshold and changes no public signature then the level shall downgrade to L2 and record the reason - check: uv run pytest tests/test_integrity.py -k downgrade -q
- The assigned level shall select the gate set the model tier and the rework allowance through one function a caller reads rather than re-deriving them - check: uv run pytest tests/test_integrity.py -k selects -q
- The rule shall be total - every path the repo can hold resolves to a level and no path resolves to two - check: uv run pytest tests/test_integrity.py -k total -q

## Scope

- `src/basicly/integrity.py`
- `tests/test_integrity.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Requirements doc D18 and section 3.3. The plan gate checks five fields and acyclicity. It
would pass a horizontally sliced plan - add the model, add the service, add the CLI - and
every such child has no consumer-visible behaviour, so **D10 cannot derive a check for it**.

## Why this happens by construction

`decompose` groups children by **scope-glob overlap**, which is file adjacency. Slicing by
file *is* horizontal slicing. The decomposer slices that way because scope globs are the
only structure it can see (see basicly-agzx.2 and requirements section 8.2 for the
whole-change structure that would fix the cause rather than the symptom).

This bead is the checkable proxy: a child that cannot say how it is exercised end to end is
refused at plan time, when splitting is cheap.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/plan_gate.py`
- `src/basicly/plan_record.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `tests/test_plan_gate.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none

payload.description:
## Context

Requirements doc D20 and section 8.2. Named `change-shape` here: it pairs with
`change-summary`, which is what BUILD hands back - shape it, build it, summarise it.

## The defect it fixes

`decompose` groups children by **scope-glob overlap**, which is file adjacency, and
slicing by file *is* horizontal slicing. Every horizontal child has no consumer-visible
behaviour, so D10 cannot derive a check for it and D18 must refuse it. The decomposer
slices that way because scope globs are the only structure it can see.

## Derived, never authored

`basicly-agzx.2` proposes exactly this artifact from an AST - tree-sitter, no model, no
tokens. That bead and this one are the same decision and are taken together.

**Not a state.** A state holds an entry predicate, an exit gate and a persona; a derivation
has none of those and cannot fail a judgement - it parses or reports that it could not.
CLASSIFY emits it and DECOMPOSE's entry predicate gains it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/classify.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/**`
- `tests/**`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `150000`

payload.description:
## Context

Requirements doc section 3.1 states BUILD's entry predicate as **plan gate green and
downstream WIP below limit**. Measured 2026-08-08: **nothing implements it.**

```text
grep -rn "wip|work_in_progress" src/basicly/*.py   -> nothing
basicly.toml:78  concurrency = 5
```

`concurrency` bounds **parallelism** - how many lanes run at once. WIP bounds **unlanded
work** - how much finished-but-unreviewed output exists. They are different quantities and
we only have the first.

A specced gate that does not exist is the fail-open shape this repo keeps paying for
(`jr0l.22` was shipped and inert for 67% of the tracker).

## Why it matters beyond conformance

Our bound is denominated in tokens and slots. The quantity that actually runs out is
**review capacity**: a pass that lands five lanes faster than anyone reads them produces
merge conflicts and unreviewed surface, and neither the spend ceiling nor the concurrency
cap can see it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
