payload.description:
## Context

Requirements doc section 10 records the plugin channel as a **total gap by absence**: no
`plugin.json`, no `skills/` at plugin root. Confirmed still true 2026-08-08 - `ls
.claude-plugin` finds nothing. D16 makes the plugin a **second distribution channel**
packaging the same projected output as `basicly install`.

## A reference we may legally follow

`humanlayer/skills` is **MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 HumanLayer** and ships three conforming
packages:

```text
plugins/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
plugins/<name>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
plugins/<name>/skills/<name>/references/*.md
```

Manifest keys observed: `name`, `description`, `version`, `author{name,email}`,
`repository`, `license`, `keywords`.

MIT permits reuse of expression with attribution, so this is a conformance reference rather
than a thing to infer. Attribute it.

## Do not build

Section 10.2: the seven FUTURE_CONSIDERATIONS items. Encode integrity levels and gate
evidence in skill `metadata` or an `extensions` namespace, never as invented top-level
manifest fields, so migration is a rename.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/projection.py`
- `.claude-plugin/**`
- `tests/**`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none

## Context

Requirements doc section 7 sets the discipline: encode only what a second party can check.
Our skills state ordered steps with **no exit condition**, so nothing says when a phase is
done.

A completion criterion per phase is ETVX at skill granularity - the same thing D4 does for
states. Sourced from `humanlayer/skills` (**MIT**, attribute it), whose skills carry
`Completion criterion:` on every phase and `Read the following references:` naming what
to load when.

Apply to `harness-loop` first: it is our longest skill and our least checkable.

## One thing that does not transfer

Those skills are **interactive** - their phase B is literally "This is an interview". That
does not transfer to a dark-factory lane. It does transfer to INTAKE, which D6 already says
is inherently light.

- `src/basicly/catalog_lint.py`

## Context

Requirements doc D17 as amended, section 8.1.1. Sixth section of `solution-design`.

## The defect

`needs-input.json` is the block-don't-guess protocol and it fires **when a lane is already
blocked mid-build** - after a worktree is provisioned, after a dispatch has started, after
tokens have been spent reaching the wall. The unknowns surface at the most expensive moment
available.

This section moves the **anticipable** ones to the cheapest moment, before CLASSIFY. A
design whose unknowns are written down can be reviewed for whether they matter; one whose
unknowns are found at build time can only be escalated.

`needs-input.json` is unchanged and stays - a fact nobody anticipated will still be reached
mid-build, and blocking is still right then.

- `.basicly/core/schemas/**`
- `tests/**`

- budget: `40000`

payload.description:
## Context

A **second loop shape** we do not have: set point -> sensor -> controller -> actuator, under
disturbances, with a dampener holding the line while the loop chips at it. Sourced from
`humanlayer/skills` `design-control-loop` (**MIT**, attribute it).

It is not the delivery loop. The delivery loop takes a requirement and ships a change; this
one drives a **property of the codebase** toward a target on a schedule.

## We already own most of it

```text
set point   the 4000-token cap                          have
sensor      check_module_size.py, the noqa count,       have, four of them
            C901 at 10, the unmatched test files
dampener    the frozen-baseline ratchet - literally     have, and best named
            keeps the problem from getting worse
            while the loop improves it
controller  selects the next target                     MISSING
actuator    dispatches a lane to do it                  MISSING
```

On 2026-08-08 the controller was played **by hand**: read the module-size output, dispatch
five lanes. It worked, which is the argument for mechanising it.

## Flow control is not optional

Bound to **one open lane**. A scheduled loop that outruns review produces conflicting and
duplicate work. Note this bound is the same quantity `basicly-u2hl.23` adds to BUILD, so
build that first or share the mechanism.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `.scripts/**`
- `tests/**`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-u2hl.23`

payload.description:
## Context

`.basicly/core/kit/` held one foldered kit (`tracker/`) and three loose modules
(`claude_tier_hook.py`, `install_hook.py`, `tier_resolver.py`). Found by the owner
2026-08-08.

## Why it is not cosmetic

Both kit gates scope themselves by directory:

```text
.scripts/kit_deployment.py:75   KIT_DIR = .basicly/core/kit/tracker
kit-boundary.py                 walks KIT_ROOT
```

So the three loose modules had **no deployment gate looking at them at all**. Foldering
is what brings a kit under a gate.

## What it exposed

The move broke `find_map`'s kit-adjacent fallback: it computed the catalog root as
`here.parent`, correct only while the kit sat directly under `core/`. After foldering it
resolved `core/kit/models/` and found nothing. Two tests caught it. Fixed to
`here.parents[1]`.

## Breaking, and how

`install_hook.py` writes the resolved path of `claude_tier_hook.py` into the consumer's
Claude settings - absolute at `--user` scope. An installed consumer's hook stops resolving
until they re-run the installer from the new path. Mitigating: the installer matches
existing entries by filename, so a re-run repairs it.

## Also in this change

- The kit README split: kit-wide constraints stay at `kit/README.md` (the tracker modules
  cite it), tier-specific content moves to `kit/tier/README.md`.
- `docs/design/tier-injection-kit.md` renamed to `tier-kit.md` so one concept has one name.
  The **skill** stays `tier-injection`: it installs the kit, and the kit injects the tier -
  the skill names the technique, the kit names the domain, matching `tracker`.
- **The repo's first module-size waiver.** `tier_resolver.py` went 1 token over because
  `parents[1]` is a character longer than `parent`. Waived rather than split, with the
  reason in the file: the kit's contract is that a foreign harness can copy the file and its
  hook flat into one directory, so splitting it along the seam the cap wants would break the
  thing the module exists for. Approved by the owner per D14.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/**`
- `docs/design/tier-kit.md`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `tests/test_kit_*.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Fold the tier injection kit into its own directory

payload.acceptance_criteria: When a lane reads the tracker it shall receive only the fields its phase declares and the claude dispatch record shall carry a cache split - check: the projected ready query costs under a tenth of the unprojected one on this repo and a claude run record carries cache_read_tokens
payload.description:
## Context

Requirements doc section 15, D21 and D22. Measured 2026-08-08 with tiktoken o200k_base on
real repo payloads.

```text
br ready --format json   223961 chars   55751 tok   36.9% of a p50 lane
projected to 5 fields      9613 chars    2507 tok    1.7%      22x
```

A p50 lane occupies 151099 tokens and **basicly authors 3812 of them - 2.52%**.
Re-serialising everything we author into the best format saves **1.01% of one lane**.
Selection beats serialisation by roughly 500x, so this bead is selection.

Our own `tool-br` skill instructs every agent to run the unprojected query.

## Three parts, one landing

1. **Field projection** (engine). A declarative per-phase allowlist applied before tracker
   output reaches a lane. This is `read_cost`'s existing cap-what-a-lane-reads principle
   applied to the tracker surface, which is uncapped today. **A filter, not a codec** -
   deliberately lossy, and it must be labelled so; only part 2 carries a zero-loss claim.
2. **The bijective codec** (kit, stdlib only, parses on 3.9). Uniform record arrays only,
   read-only, never nested data and never anything the model must emit - the accuracy
   evidence in section 15.3 is why. Round-trip gate over this repo's 682 beads, 3775 events
   and 297 run-records, plus a committed adversarial fixture covering the six measured loss
   modes: null vs empty string, int vs str, bool vs str, embedded tab, embedded newline,
   absent key vs null key.
3. **The claude cache split**, folded in per the owner. `runner_usage.claude_json_usage`
   never populates `cache_read_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens` though `runner_usage.py:177`
   does for codex, so 0 of 297 records carry one. Cache reads cost 0.1x, so until this
   lands a 40% apparent saving that actually broke a cached prefix is indistinguishable
   from a real win - on the agent doing 76 of 77 dispatches.

## D22 - build it so the tracker swap does not break it

`br` and `bv` are being removed. **The allowlist names our own record vocabulary, never
br's JSON keys**, and an adapter maps them. At the flip only the adapter changes. A
projection written against br's payload shape would have to be rewritten, which is the
major refactor this constraint exists to prevent.

## Measure it, do not assert it

Accuracy A/B before the codec reaches a lane, using `.scripts/recall_eval.py`'s existing
two-arm three-rep design. If the intervals overlap - as the one honest third-party
benchmark found - ship the token win and claim nothing about quality.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/context.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/context/**`
- `src/basicly/runner_usage.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `tests/**`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `200000`
- depends on: none
payload.title: Project tracker payloads to the fields a phase needs

payload.description:
## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — owner decision, read before the text below

**The acceptance criteria below are written to the losing side of a contradiction inside
`factory-loop.md`, and the owner has now resolved it.**

- `:1308` (section 15.6): "The context ceiling is **deleted, not retuned**."
- `:99` (**D23**, later and general, naming the context ceiling explicitly): "A sizing control
  with no recorded correct firing becomes observability ... **Demotion is not deletion: the
  number stays recorded, surfaced and falsifiable**, because section 15.6's gate was wrong for
  months with the telemetry already contradicting it."

**Owner decision, 2026-08-13: D23 wins. Demote to observability, do not delete.**

So the criterion below - "the ceiling constant its meter and its follow-up path are **absent**"
- is wrong as written and a lane implementing it deletes a number that must be kept. Restate as:

- The ceiling no longer blocks a dispatch and no longer spawns an overrun follow-up.
- `ceiling_tokens` and the occupancy it is compared against **stay recorded per dispatch,
  surfaced, and falsifiable** - the 18 overrun beads it produced remain explicable from the
  ledger.
- Section 15.6 is corrected to match D23 (see `basicly-miqr`).

`basicly-89hm` now depends on this bead, so this restatement gates the context-window row too.
`basicly-jr0l.12` fixes the follow-up machinery and is now blocked on this bead: under a
demotion it survives, under a deletion it was void.

---

## Context

Requirements doc section 15.6. Measured 2026-08-08.

```text
DEFAULT_CONTEXT_CEILING = 0.6  x declared 1000000 window = 600000
lanes crossing it: 0 of 79        max observed occupancy: 403051
```

Against the stale hardcoded 200000 the threshold was 120000 and **51 of 79 lanes crossed**,
which is where the twelve overrun follow-ups came from.

A gate that has never once fired correctly - first at a fifth of its intended point, then
never - is removed rather than given a third hand-picked constant. Its follow-up machinery
goes with it.

## Watch for

`supervise` and `loop` both reach the meter (`loop.py:594`, `supervise.py:1089`, `:1118`).
The overrun follow-up path and its `[harness-overrun]` marker family are downstream; decide
whether the marker history is read anywhere before deleting the writer.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`

## Context

Seven design decisions were taken by the owner on 2026-08-09 while scoping v0.9.0, and
establishing them refuted three claims committed in this repo. Both halves land together
because the decisions rest on the corrected facts.

## Decisions recorded (factory-loop.md section 2)

- D27 thin engine: the catalog defines agents/skills/hooks, the host runtime executes them
- D28 amends section 6.4: an agent may spawn only a role the engine authored, gated by host hooks
- D29 spend caps compose: our grant ceiling outer, the host cap inner, per dispatch
- D30 a provider model id never appears in an agent file; tier is injected at spawn
- D31 a tier resolves by declared vendor order, verified at install
- D32 handoff artifacts are files on harness/<issue>, deleted at teardown; ledger keeps the digest
- D33 docs/ carries only architecture, tutorial, how-to and a contributor guide

## Claims corrected

- section 15.5 said the cache split is unavailable. It is in claude's result event today
  (cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, modelUsage.<id>.contextWindow),
  verified on a live probe of 2.1.226, and copilot's is already extracted by copilot_store.
  The blocker was our own extractor, not the stream.
- section 6.4's Conductor refusal read "no agent spawns agents", which both installed
  runtimes contradict by construction.
- run_record.credits said summing cost and credits would be an accounting defect. GitHub
  documents 1 AI credit = 0.01 USD, so a USD rollup is sound at a fixed published rate.

## Measured, from four real dispatches of one seeded session

cold seed and a cache-missing resume each cost 0.2165 USD at 21578 cache-creation tokens;
a cache-hitting resume cost 0.0112 and --fork-session 0.0115 while carrying the parent's
context and issuing a fresh session id. 19x on a cache hit. This answers basicly-ejdm and
basicly-xjd2 with one mechanism and relocates the per-dispatch floor to a cache miss.

## Follow-on, not in this unit

D31 needs vendor_order in anchors.yaml plus an install-time entitlement probe. D32 needs the
harness branch created at INTAKE rather than at worktree provisioning (loop.py:327). D33
needs a docs/ path gate and a contributor guide, which does not exist.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a tier whose first declared vendor is unavailable on the surface in effect when the tier is resolved for that surface then the next vendor in the declared order is returned with the vendors it skipped recorded and never a different tier's model
payload.description:
## Context

D31, taken 2026-08-09. Owner constraint from D30: a provider model id never appears in an
agent file, so a tier must resolve to a model at spawn time. Today `TierResolver.resolve`
takes exactly one vendor - `HOST_SURFACES[host]` yields a `(surface, default_vendor)` pair -
and reads exactly one cell. If that cell is unavailable the spawn gets no model and falls back
to the host default, which is the tier silently not binding.

The owner's example: tier `maximum` on claude resolves to Fable 5; on a copilot surface where
Fable is not served it must resolve to the next vendor's `maximum`, not to a lower tier and not
to nothing. `model-map.json` already carries every cell needed to answer that
(`tiers.<tier>.vendors.<vendor>.surfaces.<surface>`) and already refuses to substitute another
tier's model. What is missing is an order to walk.

## Scope

- `anchors.yaml` declares a `vendor_order` per tier, reviewed and diffable, listing every vendor.
- `generate_model_map.py` copies it into `tiers.<tier>.vendor_order` and fails when the order
  omits or misspells a declared vendor, so the order cannot drift from the vendor list.
- `TierResolver.resolve` walks that order when no explicit vendor is given and returns the first
  cell the map marks available. An explicit `vendor=` argument still reads exactly one cell.
- The `Resolution` records which vendors were tried, so a resolved model is explainable without
  the map.

## Out of scope

The install-time entitlement probe is its own unit: the map's `available` is a claim from the
generator about what a surface serves, not about what this consumer is entitled to, and probing
needs a live host. Filed separately.

## Constraints

The kit imports nothing from `basicly` and is gated by `.basicly/core/hooks/kit-boundary.py`, so
this reads committed data and takes everything else as an argument. Resolution runs in the spawn
path, so a malformed map must resolve to None with a reason rather than raise. A tier must never
resolve to another tier's model.

## Demonstration

`uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tier/tier_resolver.py --host copilot --tier maximum` prints a
model and the vendor it came from, and prints the vendors it skipped when the first was
unavailable.
payload.title: Resolve a tier by declared vendor order instead of one hardcoded vendor per host

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given three modules exceed the size ratchet when the anchor and resolution layers are extracted into their own modules then check_module_size reports every tracked module within the cap or its frozen baseline and the committed model map is byte identical to what the generator rendered before the split
payload.description:
## Context

The module-size ratchet (D7, factory-loop section 9.3) refused three modules while
basicly-u2hl.35 was in flight. Each was frozen under 8000 tokens, so the amended OQ-12
rule applies: the first change to such a file must bring it under the 4000-token cap
rather than merely not grow it.

  .scripts/generate_model_map.py   7438 -> 8101
  tests/test_kit_resolver.py       6859 -> 8242
  tests/test_model_map.py          6708 -> 6834

Taken as its own unit so the D31 vendor walk lands as a small reviewable diff on top of
a refactor that changes no behaviour, rather than mixed into it.

## The seam

The same one twice: the reviewed anchor source versus the generated artifact.

  .scripts/generate_model_map.py -> .scripts/model_map_anchors.py    load and validate
  tests/test_model_map.py        -> tests/test_model_map_anchors.py  mirrors it
  tests/test_kit_resolver.py     -> tests/test_kit_resolver_walk.py  the walk aspect

Extraction is along a nameable responsibility, not to satisfy the metric: anchors.yaml is
hand reviewed input with its own validation rules, model-map.json is derived output with
its own shape. Trimming comments to duck the gate is refused as gaming under section 9.2.

## Constraint

No behaviour change. The generator's CLI, its drift check and the committed map must be
byte identical before and after, which the existing byte-compare test already asserts.

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` reports every tracked module within the cap
or its frozen baseline, and `uv run pytest -q` is green.

payload.text:
SWEPT 2026-08-09. 15 sources across two dispatches. Result: 0 adoptions from the third-party list,
2 concept-level adaptations, 10 declines. The authoritative half produced 6 corrections to committed
claims and 2 mechanisms that change the loop design.

Landed in docs/requirements/factory-loop.md: section 6.3 (agent count, dispatch contract, hot-reload
refutation, competitor contract comparison), section 7.1 (paths trigger, listing budget, scope
precedence inversion), section 7.2 (D35 supersedes the fragment demotion), new sections 7.3 and 7.4,
section 11 items 4 and 8 plus the two cheapened capabilities, OQ-15 through OQ-17.

AUTHORITATIVE - what changed:

- Agent AND hook definitions HOT-RELOAD. Refuted in 3 committed places -> basicly-u2hl.43.
- A skill takes a `paths:` glob. This refutes the premise under the python-guidelines fragment
  demotion -> D35, implemented by basicly-a3ab.9.
- Skill scope precedence is enterprise > personal > PROJECT, the INVERSE of agents. basicly install
  writes the lowest-priority writable scope -> basicly-u2hl.46.
- Skill listing is budgeted at 1% of the context window, descriptions capped at 1536 chars, and
  overflow drops LEAST-INVOKED skills first -> basicly-u2hl.45.
- A Stop hook returning decision:block fires and continues a turn under our own `claude -p` -
  probed, 2 firings. Capped at 8 consecutive blocks (OQ-16). Engine work, not catalog:
  claude_settings.py:51 maps 2 of 31 documented hook events.
- Hook types `prompt` and `agent` give section 11 item 4 a host-native fresh-context verifier.
  `type: agent` is vendor-flagged experimental.
- Nesting depth 3 CONFIRMED - and the Anthropic blog in this reading list is the stale source,
  still saying five. Our own document was right. Rung ordering caught it.

ralph-wiggum: DECLINED. Its termination is an exact literal string the model writes about itself,
which is MAST's "unawareness of termination conditions" rather than a fix for it. No phases, no
artifacts, no gates, no bounded rework. Licence is all-rights-reserved under Anthropic Commercial
ToS - mechanism learnable, code not portable. Its one good idea (loop state on disk, prompt never
mutated) we already do better in loop_state.py plus br.

THIRD PARTY - 10 declines. aipatternbook and agentic-ai-systems both fail the "what does the author
sell" test outright. multica-ai duplicates our baseline and is unlicensed. The rest are rung 6 with
nothing our fragments lack. Two adaptations: tjboudreaux's counterfactual test (basicly-u2hl.47) and
Piebald as a READ-ONLY research input for the reviewer role - MIT (c) Piebald cannot license the
vendor's prompt text, so read never paste.

VISUAL-EXPLAINER: DECLINED, premise unestablished. Measured against our own ledger, n=129 human
answered checkpoints: median 95s, p25 12s, 54% under 2 minutes, but 17 events over 30 min carry 85%
of the 40.5h total. Two of those were answered in the SAME SECOND; another waited 29012s while the
next decision from the same human took 81s. The clock starts when the ENGINE asks, not when the
human ARRIVES, and CONFIRM_TTL_SECONDS is 900. Root cause: the checkpoint clock measures RENDEZVOUS,
not reading. A renderer cannot move a quantity the instrument does not contain. Recorded as section
7.4 with the branch not taken (decision quality, unmeasurable - checkpoint_approved is a boolean
with no un-approve). One datum on the other side, stated honestly: wait-decompose, the only
checkpoint with a real artifact, ran 2490s at n=1. Settled by one field -> OQ-15.

The full wait distribution was independently re-derived by the session from .beads/issues.jsonl
before landing.

payload.title: Research claude-code-harness as a competing harness

payload.text:
RESEARCHED 2026-08-09. Chachamaru127/claude-code-harness v5.6.0, main at 9736a5b4 (2026-08-08).
Landed as factory-loop section 11.7 plus section 11 item 8 and section 6.3.

LICENCE, read first and in full: SPDX MIT. Two licence-bearing files, both read - LICENSE.md and
LICENSE.ja.md, the second a Japanese translation, not a rider. A repo-wide probe for
LICENSE/NOTICE/COPYING/THIRD-PARTY returned exactly those two, with a positive control confirming
the probe discriminates. No NOTICE, no per-directory licence, no field-of-use restriction. Go deps
all standard permissive, none vendored. One diligence item: the copyright line asserts a second
holder, "Manus AI & Chachamaru", with no CLA or provenance note explaining it. That matters only if
we ever vendor code; it does not restrict learning facts.

VERDICT: a live competitor on the GATING axis, a non-competitor on the LOOP and TRACKER axes.

Their gates run at the AGENT RUNTIME - 27 hook events, PreToolUse and PermissionRequest, a
5-category floor, R01-R15, a tamper check that refuses to adjudicate rather than fail open, and a
redacted JSONL audit that writes hash-and-length only and NOTHING for the two most sensitive
categories. Ours run at commit, push and landing. They gate the action before it happens; we gate
the artifact after. That is the single biggest capability gap found and it is now section 11 item 8.

Their loop is PROMPT ASSEMBLY, not orchestration - the verbs explicitly do not call any LLM, they
emit a prompt to stdout, and the loop is prose in SKILL.md the model executes. Their tracker is
Plans.md, a Markdown table parsed by regex, with status as a text marker.

This is EVIDENCE FOR a decision we already took. architecture.md:86-106 records phases as engine
code and deliberately not configuration, decided 2026-07-30 after reviewing two projects that made
them declarative. This is a third, larger, better-resourced instance, and the cost is observable:
their own issue #269 is a Stop hook blocking infinitely because it keys on Plans.md WIP counts. A
marker ledger is remembered; a graph is derived, and a compacted session can only re-derive the
second.

Solved there, open here: basicly-0p8n is their entire product; basicly-66ix has a working shape as
one policy kernel plus N host codecs with a golden-file check gate; basicly-a3yi is solved with
declared precedence; basicly-u2hl.24 is shipped; basicly-tcmy.20 is enforced at write time.

Not attempted there: derived phase from a graph, engine-held authority (theirs can veto a tool call
but cannot refuse to advance a phase, enforce a checkpoint, cap rework or rank a ready set - all
four are prose), guidance projection from one source into three families, multi-lane supervision
with a serial merge queue, install/upgrade convergence preserving a consumer overlay.

Their agent files are hand-written with no schema, no projection and no vendoring - strictly weaker
than our section 6.1 as a SOURCE. But each names tools, disallowedTools, model, effort, maxTurns,
isolation and a versioned output schema, and each is actually spawned. That is exactly the gap
section 6.3 measures. Their test-wiring-auditor contract (fresh context, inherits no conversation
state, emits one JSON object) is a clean model for our validator. Their SKILL.md shape/role/pair/
base quadruple is a machine-readable skill graph - the pairing section 7.2 states in prose and
cannot check. Concepts only; nothing ported.

THE EXTERNAL-REVIEW RULE CAUGHT THE INVERSE OF THE GASTOWN CASE, and the check was different.
gastown advertised an UNREACHABLE feature, found by looking for callers. Here the code is more
honest than the README: a REACHABLE feature described too strongly. The README says the runtime
floor is "Overridable: No. Not by any config, env var, or permission mode" - and two documented
escape hatches were exercised live, each flipping a deny to an allow, with the source file's own
comment conceding the exceptions. Finding it required EXERCISING THE OVERRIDE, not finding the

## Context

Owner asked twice for a five-whys skill. The first ask was deferred on factory-loop section 7.2
- "a loop skill is blocked on its state" - and on the repo's own sourced caution against
iterated-why (Card, BMJ Quality and Safety 2017). The owner asked again, so it ships.

The deferral was answerable rather than correct. Section 7.2's failure mode is a skill with **no
invoker**, not a skill whose state is unbuilt. `root-cause` has two invokers today: a human
running the retro under `session-finish`, and the `researcher` agent whose method section defers
to it. So the rule is sharpened rather than broken - name the invoker before authoring - and
section 7.2 now records the amendment.

## What shipped

`.basicly/core/skills/root-cause/skill.yaml`, model-invoked, projected to `.claude/skills/` and
`.agents/skills/`. It carries the method and both of the method's failure modes, which is the
whole reason it is a skill rather than the one-line instruction that already exists in three
places (`core-rules`, `self-improvement-retro`, `session-finish`) and taught nothing.

- Runs on a **signal, not an incident**: section 3.2's common-cause guard, with the ledger
  queries that answer "has this shape happened before" before any analysis starts.
- Every link cites an observation, never an inference.
- Stops at a cause inside our control; a chain that terminates on a person stopped early.
- Records the **branch not taken**, which is the direct answer to Card 2017 - the method yields
  one path chosen by the asker and is not reproducible between analysts.
- Output is section 3.2's contract: a named control, its tier, the class it covers - and under
  D25 it lands as a diff against catalog YAML, never as advice.

## Also corrected

Section 7.2 carried three claims this invalidates: "1 of 5 exist", `root-cause` "missing", and
the blanket blocked-on-its-state paragraph. All three corrected in place rather than restated
beside the stale version.

## Follow-on, not in this unit

The skill becomes RETROSPECTIVE's unchanged when that state exists. `validate-as-consumer`,
`decompose-plan` and `repair-in-place` remain missing and still fail the invoker test.
payload.title: Ship the root-cause skill ahead of RETROSPECTIVE with the invoker test that licenses it

## Context

Re-probed 2026-08-09 against copilot CLI 1.0.78. The tier kit's copilot installer installs
nothing and explains that copilot "exposes no hook surface that fires for a spawn, so its
working path is static frontmatter plus copilot --model". Both halves of that explanation are
now false:

- copilot ships hooks, including one that intercepts a subagent finishing **before its results
  return to the parent** (`.github/hooks/*.json`, plus inline definitions in config)
- copilot carries per-subagent selection in **config**, at
  `subagents.agents.<name>.{model, effortLevel, contextTier}`, configurable with `/subagents`

The second is the load-bearing one. It means a copilot spawn is pinnable **without a
frontmatter `model`**, which is exactly what D30 requires and what the installer currently
reports as impossible.

## Scope

- Resolve the declared tier through the D31 vendor walk and write the result into copilot's
  per-subagent config at install time, not into the agent file.
- The installer stops reporting a no-op for copilot and reports what it wrote.
- `effortLevel` and `contextTier` have no equivalent in our tier vocabulary. Decide whether
  they are derived from the tier, declared separately, or deliberately left unset - and record
  which, because an unset field on a multi-vendor surface is a silent default.

## Constraint

No provider model id in any agent file, generated or not (D30). The projected `.agent.md` must
stay model-free; the resolved id lives in config, which is generated and rewritten on install.

## Correction already landed

The stale explanation is corrected in the `tier-injection` skill in place rather than left
beside the new claim, and it names this bead as the fix.

## Demonstration

Install into a scratch repo, then show the generated copilot config carrying the resolved model
for a `tier: low` agent while `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` carries no model line.
payload.title: Pin a copilot subagent spawn through per-subagent config instead of reporting no-op

payload.description:
## Context

Audited 2026-08-09 against the seven decisions taken that day. Both skills are **correct as
written today** and both go stale the moment D32 and D27 are implemented. Filed so the coupling
is not rediscovered by a reader who trusts a skill that has quietly stopped describing the code.

- `worktree-isolation` documents provisioning on `harness/<name>`, which is what `loop.py:327`
  does: the branch and the worktree are created on entry to BUILD. D32 moves branch creation to
  INTAKE, because INTAKE, CLASSIFY and DECOMPOSE all emit artifacts before any worktree exists.
- `harness-loop` is the runbook for driving the loop and carries 14 dispatch references. D27
  makes the host runtime the thing that spawns a role, with the engine supervising lanes rather
  than processes, and D28 replaces the blanket no-agent-spawns-agents rule with a
  roster-bounded one gated by host hooks. D32 also adds `.factory/<issue>/` as where a state's
  artifact is written and read.

## Why this is not doable now

Rewriting either skill today would make it describe a factory that does not exist. That is the
same failure as authoring a skill with no invoker, applied to documentation - and this repo has
paid for a stale document being believed over working code twice in one session.

## Trigger

Land this with the implementing change, not before and not after: the commit that moves branch
creation to INTAKE, and the commit that moves dispatch to the host runtime.

## Check

`basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` is green and the skill's own commands, run verbatim,
produce what it says they produce. A skill's claim about a command is exercised, not asserted.

Refuted 2026-08-09 against claude 2.1.226 vendor documentation, and independently corroborated by
this repo: the researcher agent authored this session registered without a host restart.

Claude Code watches ~/.claude/agents/ and .claude/agents/ and picks up an added or edited definition
within seconds. Hook config in settings files is watched too, and a ConfigChange event exists for
exactly this. There are two exceptions and both are narrow: the FIRST agent file in a newly created
agents/ directory, and --disable-slash-commands.

The first exception is the first-install case, which is what the tier kit targets - so the notice
survives in sharpened form rather than being deleted. Do not simply remove the lines.

## Sites

- .basicly/core/kit/tier/install_hook.py:115 - the RESTART_NOTICE constant and the comment above it
- .basicly/core/kit/tier/README.md:72 - consumer facing, same claim
- .basicly/core/skills/tier-injection/skill.yaml:50 - third copy

## Note on the original measurement

The claim cites basicly-wbsz.3 and pins no version, so it cannot be adjudicated as wrong-then or
stale-now. That is itself the finding: a capability claim without a version pin cannot be
re-checked, only re-argued. Whatever replaces it carries the version and the date.

## Demonstration

Create a new agent file in an existing .claude/agents/ during a live session, do not restart, and
show the host dispatches it. Then the same in a directory that did not exist, and show it does not.

src/basicly/loop_state.py:38 declares

as it exists today.

Measured 2026-08-09 at claude 2.1.226, vendor documentation.

- A skill's `description` plus `when_to_use` is capped at 1536 characters per entry.
- The whole skill listing is budgeted at 1 percent of the context window.
- On overflow, descriptions are dropped starting with the LEAST INVOKED skills.

## Why this is a defect and not trivia

Those three compose with a fact this repo already measured - 8 of 34 skills had ever been exercised -
into a feedback loop. A rarely invoked skill is the first whose description is truncated, which makes
it harder to invoke, which makes it more truncated. It converts the catalog eval in factory-loop
section 11.6 from hygiene into a measurable context cost.

We ship 37 skill sources, 32 projected.

## Scope

- `basicly catalog lint` fails a source whose description plus when_to_use exceeds 1536 characters.
- Report total projected listing size against the 1 percent budget for each target's context window,
  as a warning with the arithmetic shown.

## Positive control

Skills with long descriptions already exist, so the probe can be shown to discriminate before any
zero is reported. Do not ship a check that has only ever returned clean.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly catalog lint` fails on a deliberately over-length fixture description and passes on
the real catalog, with the listing total printed.

Skills resolve:  enterprise > PERSONAL > PROJECT

.claude/skills/, which is the lowest priority writable scope - so any developer's
~/.claude/skills/<same-name> silently overrides a skill we shipped them, while an agent of the same
name would not.

For a distribution tool that is a supply chain shaped surprise, and consumers cannot discover it
from anything we ship today.

- Record both orders in docs/architecture/architecture.md, with the install consequence stated.
- Decide whether `basicly install` should warn when a same-named personal skill already exists on

  outside the repo, which the install path deliberately avoids elsewhere.

D37, decided 2026-08-09.

claude_settings.py:51 is `AGENT_HOOK_EVENTS = {"pretooluse": ..., "posttooluse": ...}` - two of the
thirty-one documented host events. No catalog source can name a stage the engine map lacks, which is
why basicly-0p8n has nothing to bind to and why the in-dispatch termination gate cannot be expressed.

## The rule that comes with it

A stage is added by the change that consumes it. Widening to all thirty-one was refused: twenty-nine
stages with no consumer is the dead-definition problem this repo already measures elsewhere (8 of 34
skills ever exercised), and each is a surface to keep true against a vendor that moves.

## Two consumers exist today

- `Stop` returning `decision: block` - probed reachable under our own `claude -p` on 2.1.226, two
  firings observed, stop_hook_active flipping. Capped at 8 consecutive blocks (see the OQ-16 bead).
- basicly-0p8n's tool-call-boundary enforcement.

## Constraint

Claude-only. hooks.py:55 shows copilot accepts preToolUse and postToolUse and nothing else, so a
widened stage projects to one family. Declare the parity gap rather than leaving it silently uneven.

## Demonstration

A catalog hook source naming the new stage projects, fires, and its blocking behaviour is asserted by
a test on the real exit-code contract - exit 2 blocks, exit 1 does not.

payload.text:
TWO RESEARCH QUESTIONS SETTLED AGAINST THIS BEAD rather than filed separately, because both are
about the same mechanism and both resolve without a probe.

1. "Is /goal reachable under `claude -p`?" - DECLINED, not worth establishing. /goal is documented
   as an interactive slash command that installs a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook. This bead
   gives us the underlying mechanism directly, so the answer changes nothing we would build. If the
   reachability ever matters it is one dispatch, but it is not on the path.

2. "Is --forward-subagent-text output parseable by our usage accounting?" - OPEN, and it belongs to
   section 12 observability rather than here. Established: the flag exists at 2.1.226 and section 12
   records it as passed nowhere. Not established: whether runner_usage handles messages tagged with
   parent_tool_use_id. Settled by passing the flag on one dispatch and reading what the parser does
   with the extra frames - do not infer it from the schema.

PARTIAL, DELIBERATELY, 2026-08-09 in 04945c4. The vocabulary is NOT widened, and D37's own rule is
why.

D37 says a stage lands with the catalog source that uses it. Applied to itself, neither named
consumer is ready:

- The stop stage is probed reachable under our own `claude -p`, but it is capped at 8 consecutive
  blocks and that bound is UNMEASURED. basicly-u2hl.51 is the probe. Designing a termination gate on
  an unmeasured ceiling is how a control ends up looking like it binds - the repo's sharpest
  recurring lesson.
- basicly-0p8n is the other consumer and is parked on the wiring track until the account usage
  window resets 2026-08-12.

So widening now would have created exactly the dead-stage population D37 refused when it declined
all 31.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD: the rule's enforcement, which did not exist. Nothing stopped a stage being
added to AGENT_HOOK_EVENTS with no consumer.
`test_every_declared_agent_hook_event_has_a_catalog_consumer` runs over the real catalog and fails
on a mapped stage no hook uses, and it ships with a positive control asserting the check
discriminates - a widened map containing `stop` is shown to be caught. A rule that happens to hold
today reads identically to one that can never fail.

The map also now carries the reasoning at the point a future reader would widen it: which two
consumers are known, why neither has landed, and that whatever lands next is claude-only because
hooks.COPILOT_EVENTS accepts preToolUse and postToolUse and nothing else.

CORRECTED, and it removes work rather than adding it: the research suggested the blocking hook's
exit-code contract should be asserted by a test rather than assumed. It already is -
tests/test_git_hooks/test_protect_generated.py asserts returncode 2 on a block and 0 on all three
fail-open paths, and a live probe against the real hook returned 2. No action needed.

REMAINING on this bead: the actual widening, once basicly-u2hl.51 measures the block cap or
basicly-0p8n starts. The gate above will then force the consumer to land with it.

arrives. Measured over 129 human-answered checkpoints: median 95s, p25 12s, p90 2090s, max 29012s,
with 17 events over 30 minutes carrying 85% of the 40.5h total - two of them answered in the same
second, and one waited 29012s while the next decision from the same human took 81s.

So the interval is rendezvous, not reading, and arrival latency and comprehension are fused in one
number. That is why factory-loop section 7.4 records the rendered-artifact question as unestablished
rather than refuted.

## Scope

One field: a marker written when the operator first VIEWS a checkpoint, so wait decomposes into
arrival and comprehension. CONFIRM_TTL_SECONDS is 900, so a view event also tells us how often a
challenge has already expired by the time anyone reads it.

## Why it is worth one field

It decides a whole class of proposals - any rendered or restructured checkpoint artifact - that
cannot otherwise be evaluated. The single datum on the other side is wait-decompose, the only
checkpoint with a real artifact to read, at 2490s and n=1.

## Demonstration

A checkpoint answered after a delay records three timestamps, and the wait report separates arrival
from comprehension on real data rather than on a fixture.
payload.title: Record when the operator first views a checkpoint so wait splits from reading

payload.text:
DONE AND PARKED 2026-08-09 on branch `harness/basicly-u2hl.50`, commit d59ddfa. Full suite 3600
passed, all 17 gates green on that branch. Not merged: it grows two modules already many times the
size cap, and the ratchet correctly refuses. basicly-u2hl.53 is the extraction that unblocks it.

WHAT IT MEASURES. waited_s fuses arrival latency and comprehension. The split records the first VIEW
of a challenge, so `basicly loop status` can now print:

  wait:       2h 30m human, 0s delegated (dispatch 14m)
    of which: 2h 21m before anyone looked, 9m reading (3 measured)

FOUR DESIGN CALLS, each with its reason:

- Machine-local, under the gitignored usage dir. A view is a fact about one operator's screen, not
  about the work. Committing it would publish one machine's habits to every consumer clone and
  conflict between two people answering the same checkpoint. It is also NOT a tracker comment: that
  would be a `br` write per printed challenge, on the path already measured to republish
  machine-specific paths on every write.
- FIRST view, never latest. A challenge reprints on every expired code and every re-run advance, and
  a later print is evidence AGAINST the arrival it would overwrite. Same reasoning that makes
  wait_id_for_checkpoint derive rather than mint. Proved by mutation - disabling the guard reddens
  the test.
- -1, never 0, when unmeasured. A wait nobody was shown and a wait seen instantly are different
  facts; averaging the second into a population containing the first is how the fused number stopped
  meaning anything.
- Stamped at the challenge PRINT, not inside approve_checkpoint_guarded. That function also runs on
  paths that render nothing, and a view nobody had would put a fabricated arrival into the very
  population this exists to measure.

TWO GATES CORRECTED THE FIRST DRAFT, both rightly:
- wired-or-deleted refused `viewed_at` as a record field nothing reads. It was right: the derived
  intervals are what anything consumes. The raw stamp is now payload provenance only, and arrival_s
  and read_s reach a human through WaitSummary and the status line.
- module-size refused the growth, which is this bead's parked state.

The status line prints only when something was measured: a zero there would read as "nobody spent
time reading" when it means "nobody was measured" - the exact conflation the split exists to end.

payload.description:
OQ-16, accepted for settling 2026-08-09.

Established: a `Stop` hook returning `decision: block` fires and continues the turn under our own
`claude -p` dispatch. Two firings observed on 2.1.226, stop_hook_active moving false to true.

Not established: whether many iterations are reachable, or only the documented override after 8
consecutive blocks.

## Why it must be measured before anything is designed on it

It bounds any in-dispatch termination gate to 8 turns per dispatch. A gate designed for unbounded
iteration that silently stops at 8 is a control that looks like it binds and does not - the failure
shape this repo already names.

## Method

A hook that blocks unconditionally and counts its own firings to a file. Run one dispatch. Read the
count. Do not infer the limit from the documentation; the point is what our dispatch actually gets.

## Constraint

One cheap dispatch. Not to be run before the account usage window resets on 2026-08-12 unless the
budget says otherwise.

payload.close_reason: Delivered as the agent-to-skill preload check rather than the four skill fields: measured first, the catalog has three skill-to-skill references and none is a pair or base, so the fields would have had no user. The real pairing is agent->skill, the host already carries it through our fence, and the missing half was the check - now shipped with the extractions the ratchet forced.
payload.description:
Accepted 2026-08-09 from the competing-harness comparison. Concept only; nothing ported. That repo
is MIT, and this is a schema idea rather than an expression, so it would be usable even under a
restrictive licence.

factory-loop section 7.1 states "an agent is a dispatch contract; a skill is a method that contract
can load" as prose, and nothing checks it. Observed working elsewhere as four front matter fields:

- `shape`  workflow or delegate
- `role`   executor or orchestrator
- `pair`   the counterpart skill
- `base`   the skill this one delegates to

That makes "which skill answers which, and which one this delegates to" a graph a gate can walk -
for instance to refuse a skill whose declared pair does not exist, which is the loop-skill pairing
rule section 7.2 currently enforces by hand.

## Sequencing

Composes with D36 (basicly-a3ab.11). These fields are ours rather than host-specific, so they belong
in the portable part of the schema, not behind the vendor fence - but land the fence first so the
two schema changes do not collide.

## Constraint

Do not add a field with no consumer. Each of the four ships with the check that reads it, or is left
out. That is the same rule D37 applies to hook stages.
payload.title: Make the skill pairing machine-readable with shape role pair and base

payload.text:
DELIVERED DIFFERENTLY, 2026-08-09 in 1349aeb, and the bead's own constraint is why.

MEASURED FIRST: the catalog holds exactly 3 skill-to-skill references and none is a `pair` or a
`base` - session-finish -> root-cause, tool-br -> harness-loop, wsl -> node, all see-also pointers.
So shape/role/pair/base would have been four fields with no user, which is the dead-definition
problem the constraint exists to prevent. None landed.

THE PAIRING THAT IS REAL IS AGENT->SKILL, not skill->skill. factory-loop section 7.1 says "an agent
is a dispatch contract; a skill is a method that contract can load" and states it in prose. The host
expresses exactly that as a `skills:` key in subagent front matter (confirmed 2.1.226 in the
2026-08-09 mechanics research), and a probe showed OUR AGENT FENCE ALREADY CARRIES IT with zero code
change - .claude/agents gets the key, .github/agents does not.

So the mechanism existed and the CHECK did not. The host preloads what it finds and says nothing
about what it did not, so a typo yields an agent silently missing its method - the same failure shape
as an unrecognised copilot tool (basicly-8sxf) and the same remedy: restore the loud failure at
authoring time. lint_agent_sources now refuses a claude.skills name that is not a skill in the
catalog. Verified by planting `root-cuase` and watching the lint name it.

The researcher agent now declares the root-cause skill it already deferred to in prose, so the
pairing section 7.2 records is mechanical for the one case that exists.

TOLERANCE: both shapes the host accepts (a YAML list and a bare string) are handled, because the
passthrough is deliberately untyped and a checker understanding only one would report a false unknown
on a source the host reads fine. A value that is neither is left to the schema rather than reported
as an unknown skill - blaming the wrong thing.

SCOPING FIX the catalog-lint suite caught: skill discovery is a REFERENCE TABLE here, not a subject.
A malformed skill was producing two diagnostics for one defect, so it is now reported by the skill
lint alone and this check skips rather than blaming every agent.

TWO EXTRACTIONS, both forced by the module-size ratchet, both nameable without an "and":
- src/basicly/copilot_tools.py - GitHub's pinned tool vocabulary, data plus one lookup. agents.py
  7299 -> 5908 against its frozen 6893.
- tests/test_agent_lint.py plus tests/agent_helpers.py - the semantic lint suite and the shared
  factories, the shape model_map_helpers already uses. test_agents.py 7507 -> under its frozen 7027.
- tests/test_copilot_tools.py - required by the test-naming gate, which refuses a source unit with no
  test file named after it. That gate is what stopped the tests being left in the file named after
  the module they were extracted from.

pyright caught what pytest did not: the passthrough value is typed `object`, so it is not statically
iterable. Narrowed rather than iterated.

REMAINING: nothing on this bead. shape/role/pair/base stay unbuilt until a skill graph has more than
three edges and a check that reads them.

payload.description:
basicly-u2hl.50 is DONE and PARKED on branch `harness/basicly-u2hl.50` (commit d59ddfa), behind a
module-size waiver that must die with this bead rather than be renewed.

## Why it is parked

The split adds ~1350 tokens to policy.py and ~1300 to tests/test_policy.py. Both were already many
times the 4000-token cap, so the ratchet's rule is "may only shrink". Trimming the change's own prose
recovered 178 tokens - the rest is code.

## The extraction, measured

The wait block in policy.py is 4739 tokens over 447 lines: WAIT_MARKER, WAIT_KINDS, WaitEvent,
wait_id_for_checkpoint, record_wait, record_first_view, _take_view, wait_events, WaitSummary,
_wall_clock_seconds, split_waits, session_wait_summary. Moving it takes policy.py from ~34000 to
~29300, under its frozen 32482.

## What blocks it, and it is a design call not a move

The block shares `_parse_ts`, `_add_comment` and `_now` with the rest of policy.py. A naive move
makes wait_ledger import policy while policy still imports the wait API, which cycles. Decide where
those three live first - most likely a lower tier alongside the other shared primitives, since
`.importlinter` declares an exhaustive layer stack and a new module must name its tier.

Note the test suite must split with it, or tests/test_policy.py stays over.

## Constraint

Do not renew the waiver. It names this bead as its expiry and says so in both files. A waiver that
survives its own extraction is how these two modules reached 34k and 37k.

## Demonstration

`uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` reports no waiver for policy.py or tests/test_policy.py
and both are under their frozen baselines; `uv run lint-imports` keeps both contracts; the branch
merges to main with the full suite green.

payload.description:
## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — read this before the text below
The description below overstates which roles this unblocks. **Comment 2085 on this bead is the
correct text and this note records it where a decider meets it first.** Verified 2026-08-13:

- `roles.py:63-71 ROLE_BY_PHASE` has **no `reviewer` entry at all**, so `reviewer` does not
  resolve; the plan's claim that it "resolves correctly" is wrong (`implementation-plan.md`
  132-135).
- `curator` maps to `ship`, which **is** a live phase with a live handler - it is unreachable
  only because `_on_ship` (`loop.py:441`) never calls `_run_agent`.
- So **only `validator` is unblocked by this work**, not four roles.

The load-bearing claim is unchanged and still true: `config.py:380` and `loop_state.py:38`
carry no `validate`, while `factory-loop.md:144` and `integrity.py:178` both still require
`validate-as-consumer` at L3. D1 (`factory-loop.md:79`) still makes VERIFY and VALIDATE two
sequential states.

Also still true and still a trap: appending a required gate today would drop a landed L3 unit
back to the `build` rung, because `loop_state.py:181-182` derives `verified`/`landed` from the
aggregate `gates.can_advance`. And child `.3`'s acceptance criterion points at the repair
dispatch, which already reaches `_run_agent` - the **supervised lane** path
(`supervise.py:2669`) passes no role, so wire that one too or `.3` fixes the path that already
works.

---

Section 5.3 of the plan names this and it is the item that unblocks four of the seven loop roles:
validator, reviewer, retrospector and curator resolve correctly today (basicly-4kdm) and can never
be invoked, because VALIDATE, REPAIR and RETROSPECTIVE are not phases.

## The design question that was blocking it is answered

Adding a phase changes the advance sequence for every in-flight issue, so it needs a population
discriminator or it refuses work already under way. **Section 4 already supplies one and it does not
need inventing**: `validate-as-consumer` is an L3-only gate. L1 (docs, comments, test-only) and L2
(engine code, no consumer surface) do not require it.

So VALIDATE is a state every unit passes through, whose GATE is required only at L3. L1 and L2 enter
and exit it without a validation dispatch. That satisfies D1 (validate is a state, sequential after
verify) without refusing the existing population, which is mostly L1 and L2.

## Blast radius, measured 2026-08-09

- 11 engine modules read PHASES or LOOP_PHASES: loop, loop_state, config, policy, wip, decompose,
  commit, run_record, spend_calibration, dispatch_phase, roles.
- 8 test modules carry 10-91 phase references each: test_policy 91, test_loop 36, test_supervise 14,
  test_loop_lane 14, test_br_seam 12, test_loop_state 11, test_kit_tracker_differential 10,
  test_integration_loop 10.

This is a decomposition, not an edit. Use `decomposer` with the `decompose-plan` skill.

## Corrected while scoping, so nobody re-derives it

The plan recorded "the two phase tuples disagree" as a defect. They do not. They differ by exactly
one element - the terminal `done`, absent from LOOP_PHASES because it has no transition out - the
reason is documented at config.py:369, and tests/test_loop.py:2811 pins loop._HANDLERS to
LOOP_PHASES so a handler cannot drift from the set that validates it. Do not "reconcile" them.

## Sequencing

`derive_phase` reads recorded signals downward, so VALIDATE needs a signal. The natural one is a
gate verdict, which reuses `policy.gate_status` and the required-gates config rather than waiting on
`validation-transcript` - one of the four handoff schemas still unbuilt. Deciding gate-versus-artifact
is the first thing the decomposition must settle.

## Demonstration

An L3 unit advances build -> verify -> validate -> ship and cannot reach ship with the validate gate
red; an L2 unit advances build -> verify -> ship unchanged; `basicly loop status` reports the phase
for both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a unit classified L3 whose build has landed and whose verify gate is green, when
  `basicly loop advance` is run, then the derived phase is `validate` and not `ship`.
- Given that same L3 unit with its validate gate recorded failed, when `basicly loop advance` is
  run, then the advance is refused naming the validate gate, and `br` shows the unit still open.
- Given a unit classified L2 or L1 whose verify gate is green, when `basicly loop advance` is run,
  then it advances to `ship` without any validation dispatch being made.
- Given any unit in the new state, when `basicly loop status <id>` is run, then it reports
  `phase: validate` and names the gate that phase is waiting on.
- Given the phase set, when `loop._HANDLERS` is compared against `config.LOOP_PHASES`, then every
  phase that has a transition out has a handler, so `tests/test_loop.py` still pins the two
  together with `validate` present in both.
- Given a unit that enters VALIDATE, when the engine resolves the role for that phase, then
  `roles.resolve_role` returns `validator` and it reaches the dispatch argv as `--agent validator`.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/config.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/roles.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_phase.py`
- `src/basicly/wip.py`
- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `src/basicly/commit.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `src/basicly/spend_calibration.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_loop_state.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_loop_lane.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
- `tests/test_loop_state.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_differential.py`
- `tests/test_integration_loop.py`

Decomposed 2026-08-09. Design decisions settled, and three claims on this bead corrected.

## Settled: the two validates are two halves, not one thing (owner's call)

loop.py:1839 _integrate_lane already runs a validate step, deliberately BEFORE the landing
merge - 'the landing merges the moment its verify passes, a validate failure has to stop the
lane while its work is still unmerged'. A phase between verify and ship is necessarily AFTER
it. Owner decided these are different jobs:

  lane (unmerged)                     base (merged)
  build -> _validate_lane -> LAND -> verify -> VALIDATE -> ship
           rubric                             validate-as-consumer
           rubric-judged                      run it as a consumer would
           acceptance criteria met?

Evidence: integrity._SELECTIONS L3 (integrity.py:178) lists 'full' and 'validate-as-consumer'
as separate gates. The pre-merge rubric pair is not moved or renamed by this work.

## Settled: gate, not artifact - but not by the mechanism this bead proposed

handoff._validator (handoff.py:114) returns None when the schema is not installed, adopted()
is public so producers skip work in an un-adopted repo, and entry_verdict ADMITS a unit
carrying no artifact. .basicly/core/schemas/ holds 7 schemas and none is a handoff transcript,
so inert-by-default is universal today. A rung derived from an inert signal is a phase that is
silently skipped.

CORRECTION to this bead's 'Sequencing' section: appending the gate to config.required_gates
does not add a rung, it DELETES one. derive_phase reads the single aggregate gates.can_advance
for both the verify and ship rungs (loop_state.py:181-182), and policy.py:448 sets
can_advance = not failed and not missing. So a second required gate that is missing collapses
verified to False and drops an L3 unit with a green verify gate back to the build rung, which
re-runs the build->verify landing - the basicly-k35r / basicly-jr0l.49 defect class the
derive_phase docstring warns about. The rungs must be rewritten against the per-gate fields
GateStatus already carries: required_passed / required_failed / required_missing.

Gate name is validate-as-consumer, taken from integrity._SELECTIONS rather than invented.
evidence-binding, the other L3 extra, is deliberately NOT promoted - it is unimplemented and
promoting the whole tuple would block every L3 unit.

## CORRECTION: this bead's headline claim is wrong

'validator, reviewer, retrospector and curator resolve correctly today and can never be
invoked' - verified against roles.py:63 and it is wrong three ways:

- reviewer has NO entry in ROLE_BY_PHASE at all. .claude/agents/reviewer.md exists but is
  mapped to no phase, so VALIDATE does not unblock it and nothing in this bead will.
- curator IS mapped to ship, which is a live phase with a live handler. It is unreachable
  because _on_ship (loop.py:441) tears down and closes without ever calling _run_agent.
- retrospective is not in either phase tuple and is not this bead's phase.

Only validator is unblocked by this work. Sharper still: _run_agent (loop.py:709) takes
phase='build' by default and of its three call sites (594, 1642, 1758) only one passes
anything else (phase='repair', which also maps to implementer). classify and decompose
dispatch through paths that never reach resolve_role. So today only implementer ever reaches
an argv, and decider/decomposer are equally unreached. That is a separate bead.

## CORRECTION: the blast radius was over-counted

commit.py (_WORK_PHASES), run_record.py, spend_calibration.py and dispatch_phase.py read
DISPATCH phases (WRITE_PHASES), not loop phases. Inserting a loop phase requires no edit in
any of them. run_record.py enters child 3's scope only because a new dispatch phase value is
a ledger-format change.

## The population discriminator exists half-built

classify._record_classification writes '[harness-classification] level=... gates=...'
(CLASSIFICATION_MARKER, classify.py:40, written :93) and NOTHING in the tree reads it back -
verified, zero readers outside classify.py, and integrity

## Acceptance Criteria

- The loop shall list `validate` between `verify` and `ship` in both `config.LOOP_PHASES` and `loop_state.PHASES`, and `loop._HANDLERS` shall carry exactly one handler per `config.LOOP_PHASES` entry.
- The loop shall derive the verify and ship rungs from the per-gate fields of `policy.GateStatus` rather than from the aggregate `can_advance`, so a second required gate cannot drop a landed unit back to the `build` rung.
- Where a unit's recorded `[harness-classification]` marker names level L3, the engine shall classify that unit's recorded gates against the base required set plus `validate-as-consumer`, and shall not promote `evidence-binding`.
- When a unit whose recorded level is L3 has a green engine-provided `verify` gate and no engine-provided `validate-as-consumer` result, `loop_state.derive_phase` shall return `validate`, and shall return `validate` rather than `ship` even where the ship checkpoint is approved and the branch has landed.
- When a unit whose recorded level is L1 or L2 has a green engine-provided `verify` gate, `loop_state.derive_phase` shall return the phase it returns today and the engine shall dispatch no validation agent.
- While a unit rests in `validate`, `basicly loop status` shall print `phase: validate` and shall name `validate-as-consumer` among the gates the unit is waiting on.
- If a unit carries no `[harness-classification]` marker, then the engine shall treat `validate-as-consumer` as not required for it, so an issue already in flight neither gains a rung nor is refused.
- The engine shall admit `validate` as a `[policy.evidence]` key and `wip.DOWNSTREAM_PHASES` shall count a unit resting in `validate` as parked downstream.

- `src/basicly/config.py`

## Context

Measured 2026-08-08 on the basicly-u2hl.1 lane. Extracting `contention` out of

bounded rework cannot act on. This is OQ-12's failure mode reached in the first lane after

payload.description:
## Context

Step 3 of the cutover in `docs/design/work-tracker.md` §5. Steps 1 and 2 landed 2026-08-07
(`b97a653`, `17be554`).

**This is a config flip, not a code change.** `br._mirror_write` is already called on every
accepted write and is a no-op only in `MODE_EXTERNAL`, so setting `[tracker] mode = "dual"`
in `basicly.toml` activates it.

## Why it is now urgent rather than merely next

The first real shadow differential (2026-08-07) reported `clean: no, conclusive: yes` with
three records **unknown to the ledger** - `basicly-f6th`, `basicly-s5li`, `basicly-wpc8`,
all filed that same day, after the import. Nothing keeps the ledger current in `external`
mode, so that count grows with every bead filed. Three in a single working day.

**Do not fix this by re-importing.** `import_snapshot` is upsert, so a re-import would
quietly add the missing records and make the differential look cleaner - but the owned side
would then be tracking the external side, and the agreement would prove nothing. That is the
§5.1 self-agreement trap reached by a second route. Dual write is the answer, and until it is
on, every day in shadow mode adds noise the differential cannot distinguish from a real
defect.

## Pre-flight, measured 2026-08-07 - the flip will not hard-fail

A mirror failure **raises** rather than logging (`_mirror_write` docstring: "Every failure
below is raised, never logged, and that is the acceptance criterion"), and an unknown write
surface or unknown `br update` flag raises `TrackerDivergenceError`. So the flip is safe only
if every write surface the engine spawns has a translator. Checked:

- `_MIRRORED_WRITES` covers `close`, `comments add`, `create`, `dep add`, `gate report`,
  `update`.
- Those are exactly the six surfaces `classify_access` calls `write` among everything the
  engine spawns. Every other spawned surface - `comments list`, `dep cycles`, `gate list`,
  `show`, `blocked`, `lint`, `where` - classifies `read` and returns no drafts.
- `sync` and `init` are in `_UNMIRRORED_WRITES` deliberately; they are br-only surfaces with
  no owned equivalent. Note `init` classifies as `unclassified`, so it is excluded by the
  list rather than by classification - correct today, but it depends on the list.
- `br update` is spawned with only `-t` and `--external-ref`, exactly the two flags the
  mapping declares plus status.

## Sequencing constraint

Do not flip while a lane is mid-flight. Because a mirror failure raises, an uncovered write
would fail a running lane tracker write rather than degrading. Flip from a clean base with no
live worktrees, then exercise it before dispatching anything.

## Acceptance Criteria

payload.title: Flip the tracker to dual write and stop the ledger drifting

payload.text:
Sequencing note: this is step 3 in the design and it is blocked on basicly-s5li, which is step 5. The inversion is deliberate, for two reasons.

Technical: s5li changes how the harness markers are written - from br comments to native ledger events. Dual write mirrors the write path, so flipping first would spend a window mirroring a shape we are about to replace, and every mirrored comment written in that window becomes history in the ledger under the old shape.

Operational: the flip is unsafe while a lane is in flight, because a mirror failure raises rather than degrading, so an uncovered write surface would fail a running lane rather than logging. s5li was dispatched before this bead was filed.

The design numbering is a narrative order, not a dependency. Step 2 (shadow) genuinely had to precede this one and did.

[harness-info] the cutover sequence is now buildable, 2026-08-14

`basicly-vkh0.23` landed `basicly tracker import` and `basicly-c357` landed the flip boundary.
Together they resolve a tension that reads like a contradiction in the two beads and is not one.

## The apparent contradiction

This bead says do not re-import, because the owned side would then be tracking the external side
and the agreement would prove nothing. `c357` says the 200 historical records stay unimported and
named. Read together those imply the ledger reaches `owned` **missing 200 real beads**, which
would be data loss rather than a design.

## The sequence that resolves it

The order is what matters, not whether an import ever runs:

```text
1  basicly tracker import                  bring the ledger current, while still `external`
2  basicly tracker shadow --declare-history declare whatever delta remains (ideally none)
3  flip to `dual`                           the dual write begins
4  basicly tracker shadow                   now judged over a non-empty post-flip scope
```

Importing at step 1 is **not** the re-import this bead refuses. What it refuses is closing the gap
*after* the dual write has started, when the agreement being measured is the dual write. Before
the flip there is no dual write to prove anything about, so bringing the ledger current is
housekeeping. The controls make that distinction mechanical rather than a matter of discipline:

- `basicly tracker import` **refuses a ledger that already holds a post-flip record**, so step 1
  cannot be re-run after step 3 to tidy a failure away.
- `shadow --declare-history` **refuses a second declaration**, so the baseline cannot be widened
  after step 3 either.

## What this bead still owes

Whether to run step 1 at all is this bead`s call, not `vkh0.23`s. Running it makes the declared
baseline empty and the differential`s scope the whole post-flip population; skipping it leaves 200
records declared as history and absent from the ledger at `owned`, which needs an answer for where
they then live.

**The import was deliberately NOT run on this repo** by the lane that built it, for exactly that
reason: it is a cutover step and this bead owns the cutover.

basicly-jk3l closed 2026-08-13 as discharged; its survivability and observability preconditions were its four blockers, all closed: yvx9 (a killed lane commits its work), rupz (the dispatch event stream is read not discarded), 1lpo (a release epic can fan out), lpsf (the wall clock retired as a lane bound). Its edge to this bead was backwards - jk3l existed to enable this run, not to wait on it - and was removed rather than satisfied. Carry its criteria here: a pass is survivable and observable before this proof is attempted.

## Context

`projection.py:1-7` claims the comparison contract lives in exactly one place. That is true of the write half only. The inverse operation, compare planned bytes against disk and classify missing, stale or orphaned, is written four times.

```text
skills._check_projected_skill    skills.py:391-424
agents.check_synced_agents       agents.py:478-498
hooks.check_copilot_hooks        hooks.py:190-215
cli.cmd_check                    cli.py:400-461
```

## The fourth copy already diverged and was paid for

Build compared bytes and check compared decoded text. The comment at `cli.py:429-430` records the line-ending drift incident that forced a hand realignment.

The copies also disagree on report shape. Three emit a path and a reason through `cli._report_mismatches`. `cmd_check` emits a path with two hashes through a bare print to standard error at `cli.py:451-458`.

`sync_hooks` merges a precommit config and `claude_settings` merges a deny list. Both are co-owned semantic merges, genuinely different, and stay out of the shared kernel.

Four copies of repo-relative path formatting: `schema.display_path:194`, `catalog_source.rel:43`, `agents._rel:501`, `cli._format_path:158`. Fold onto the lowest tier copy.

`ui.py:3-4` claims every command routes user-facing lines through that module. Measured: 50 `ui.` calls against 296 `print(` calls in `cli.py` alone. Correct the claim or converge the check reports while the seam is open.

## Acceptance

- When a projection family checks its outputs, then it classifies each planned path through one shared function whose comparison is byte-identical to the write half.
- When the four check paths report a mismatch, then they use one reason vocabulary.
- When repo-relative path formatting is searched under `src/basicly/`, then one implementation remains.

## Context

**Corrected 2026-08-08.** The first version of this bead claimed the cutover could not
start because the import had never run. That was wrong - it was inherited from a stale
handover note and not probed. The import ran on 2026-08-07 in commit `b97a653`, by hand:
`.basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl` holds 3775 events over 643 records, every one
carrying `imported_from: beads-export` and provenance `EXTRACTED`.

The real defect is one step over, and it is sharper.

## The defect

`migrate.import_snapshot` (`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/migrate.py`) has **no caller in
`src/`, `.scripts/` or `.basicly/`**, no `main()`, and no CLI surface -
`basicly tracker --help` lists `shadow` only. So the import is a one-shot that was
performed once by hand and **can never be repeated**.

## Impact - it has already drifted

```text
records in .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl : 643
records in .beads/issues.jsonl               : 667
```

The ledger is 24 records behind one day after it was written, and every bead filed since
is missing from it. A shadow differential run today compares a stale ledger against a
live tracker and reports divergence that is age, not defect. No consumer can build the
ledger at all.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/migrate.py`
- `tests/test_cli_tracker.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
