payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the tracker kit is copied into a repository that has never installed the engine when its entry point is run then it creates reads and queries a work item without importing the engine, and given the kit boundary check runs then it confirms the kit imports nothing from the engine package
payload.description:
## Context

The tracker kit must work standalone. A repository that copies the kit and never installs the engine has to be able to create, read and query a work item with it.

The kit already holds events, snapshot, ids, scheduler, fsck, provenance, differential and migrate. What it has is no entry point.

The one-way boundary is already enforced by a pre-commit hook: the kit may not import the engine. The redaction function is injected rather than imported. Keep both properties.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`
- `tests/test_kit_boundary.py`

payload.description:
## Context

The flip. Step 4 of the cutover.

The acceptance criterion is deliberately harsh: with the external binary absent from the machine entirely, the loop still runs a unit of work from intake to a merge. Nothing weaker proves the dependency is gone rather than merely unused.

Three defects in the external binary are the argument for finishing this, and all three are upstream so none can be fixed in place:

- br doctor health printed db=ok while sqlite called the image malformed.
- br doctor --repair rebuilds the database from the JSONL export, and that export carries zero gate results against 386 in the database, so the vendor's own repair path destroys the gate ledger.
- br exited CONFIG_ERROR: Invalid JSON at line 562 on an export line that parses without error under Python, intermittently. Recorded in this bead's comments 2026-08-17.

## Why the scope was narrowed rather than split

This bead was REFUSED by the working-set band at 1487370 tokens, and the refusal was over-declaration and not size [measured 2026-08-17 with read_cost.scope_read_cost]:

- declared as filed, with tests/** : 497551 read tokens
- the same scope without tests/** : 9803
- tests/** alone accounts for 487748 of it, which is 98 percent

The named test files below cost 21913 read tokens, which is about 65739 working-set tokens at the task factor of 3, inside the band of 8000 to 264000. So the remedy was to name the tests this work actually touches. A split would have cut one unit of work into parts that each carry the same over-declaration.

If the build finds a test file this list does not name, add it here and re-check the band. Do not widen it back to a glob.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `src/basicly/tracker_cutover.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `tests/test_tracker_cutover.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
- `tests/test_owned_store.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_invocation.py`

payload.text:
Owner decision 2026-08-17: go on the flip, in the order vkh0.27 then this bead. vkh0.27 is dispatched as a lane on the vkh0 grant.

This bead is not dispatchable as written. basicly loop preflight refuses it: 1487370 working-set tokens against a band of 8000 to 264000, verdict REFUSED - too large, split it. Every other ready vkh0 child sits in band, the largest at 77454, so the refusal is this bead's scope and not the band.

Two further constraints on it, both measured today:

1. Its declared scope includes docs/architecture/architecture.md, which an architect pass is rewriting for the comment-kind split. Dispatching it now would put two writers on one file.
2. The grant on vkh0 has 46489485 tokens remaining and a lane costs about 33 million measured, so one lane at a time. The full five-lane fan-out forecast is 105672805, which the grant cannot pay.

Next action on this bead is a decompose, not a dispatch.

A third upstream defect, observed 2026-08-17 during the architecture pass. br exited with CONFIG_ERROR: Invalid JSON at line 562, naming .beads/issues.jsonl. Line 562 of that file parses without error under Python. The failure was intermittent: an earlier invocation in the same session read the same file successfully.

That makes three, and the pattern is the argument rather than any one of them: the binary's own reader, its own health check and its own repair path have each now been observed to misreport or destroy state that the owned ledger holds correctly. None is fixable in place.

Not investigated further, and no reproduction is recorded. It is handed on as evidence for this bead, not as a bug to chase upstream.

Operator reading of the acceptance criterion, recorded before dispatch so the build does not have to guess.

"With the external binary absent from the machine entirely" is not satisfiable by a lane and must not be attempted literally. Removing br from the machine is not a change to this repository, and under dual mode the base checkout's tracker still depends on it, so a lane that uninstalled it would break the store its own claim is written to.

Read it as hermetic absence inside the lane: the loop runs a unit of work from intake to a merge with the binary unreachable from the environment the engine spawns into. A PATH that excludes it, or an equivalent injected lookup failure, satisfies the criterion. The proof must be a committed test, not a manual session, because the criterion has to keep holding after the lane closes.

If hermetic absence turns out to be untestable at this layer, block with needs-input rather than weakening the criterion to "unused".

payload.description:
## Context

The citation ratchet reports a stale `file:line` only when the cited line happens to be **blank or past end of file**. A citation that has drifted onto a different line of real code passes, and stays passing.

Measured 2026-08-17 on one block, `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` around line 124, which tabulates three call sites:

| Cited | Actually at | Off by | Gate said |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loop.py:869` `_run_agent` | 858 | 11 | passed |
| `loop.py:1119` `_run_proposer` | 1108 | 14 | **stale**, but only after an unrelated edit shifted it onto a blank line |
| `supervise.py:2651` `_dispatch_lane` | 2651 | 0 | passed, correctly |

Two of the three were wrong. The block was written 2026-08-15 in f8f6d34, so both survived two days and an unknown number of gate runs. The one the gate caught, it caught by luck: a three-line comment added elsewhere in `loop.py` pushed line 1119 onto a blank line.

## Why this is the worse failure mode

A citation pointing at nothing is an obvious defect. A citation pointing at the **wrong but existing** line reads as verified and is not — the same class the architecture rewrite hit, where three section references pointed at a real but wrong section. A reader who follows one lands on unrelated code and has no signal that the pointer, rather than their understanding, is what is wrong.

## What would fix it

The convention already exists and this repository states it: name the symbol, not the line. A symbol citation is checkable by search and survives every edit above it. The three entries above already name their symbol in the next column, which is why dropping the numbers cost nothing — that is the repair applied to the two stale ones in 1f3162b.

So the gate's own rule can be stronger: a `file:line` citation in a document is refusable on sight when the same entry names a symbol, and checkable against the symbol's definition line when it does not. What it must not do is treat a line's non-blankness as evidence.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_docs_citations.py`
- `tests/test_check_docs_citations.py`

## Context

Two committed and pushed files carry a person's username and a personal e-mail address. Architecture §32.7 claimed absolutely that no committed artifact carries a username, and the claim is false.

Measured 2026-08-17, twice by paths sharing no step — a field-wise count over the parsed records and a raw-line regex over the bytes — and both agree on the substance:

    .beads/issues.jsonl, 924 records
      created_by: <redacted:machine-username> 846, <redacted:machine-username> 78
      assignee:   niksavis@live.com 56, <redacted:machine-username> 26
      lines holding an e-mail address: 58

    .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl, 5616 lines
      lines holding an e-mail address: 59
      lines holding the redaction placeholder: 4944   <- positive control, the rule does fire

Both files are tracked, committed and pushed to a public remote, so this is published rather than merely present.

## Why every gate is green over it

`tracker-path-scan` builds its identity rule from `getpass.getuser()`, which on this machine is `<redacted:machine-username>`. The identity in the stores is a **different** one. So the gate is not broken and its green result is correct — it is answering "does this artifact carry *your* identity" when the requirement is "does it carry *anyone's*".

That is the general defect, and it is worth stating separately from the data: an identity gate keyed on the running user cannot see another user's identity, and a repository that several machines write to will accumulate identities no single machine's gate can find.

## What is bounded and what is not

Every identity-bearing event in the owned ledger carries the import's own source marker; no live write path produces one. So the population is inherited from the pre-cutover import and is not growing. That bounds the remedy to a backfill plus a format rule — it does not make the published values unpublished.

## The three remedies, and which needs an owner

Removing the values from the current files is a corrective append or a rewrite, and the rewrite of a committed append-only log is the exception architecture §4.2 reserves for an explicit owner decision. Removing them from **history** is a force-push, which is an owner decision of a different order and is not this bead's to take. Preventing the next one is the format rule and the deny-list configuration, which is ordinary work.

Note the deny-list the hook already names, `[[privacy.denied]]`, belongs in the gitignored `basicly.local.toml` — 787 bytes, all comments, parsing to an empty table. The mechanism exists and was never configured.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/migrate.py`
- `src/basicly/redact.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/internal-info-scan.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `docs/architecture/status.md`
- `tests/test_br_scrub_ledger.py`

A flip blocker found 2026-08-17 while clearing the binary out of the scripts, and it is not in the flip bead scope.

At mode owned the improvement loop raises. owned_write.create refuses a parentless create - "A root mint needs the ledger id prefix, and nothing owned declares one" - and the improvement controller files a root lane with no parent. So either the ledger declares an id prefix, or the improvement loop gives its lanes a parent. Either is a decision, not a port.

Measured separately: improvement-loop.yml will fail when dispatched now that its binary install is gone. With the binary off PATH, supervise.lane_selection raises RuntimeError: br is not on PATH, on the dry run, before any lane starts. The read is the engine own and the mode is dual, so this is blocked on this bead rather than on the workflow. It is workflow_dispatch only, so nothing fires until a human dispatches it, and the file records the state.

Partly landed 2026-08-17. Both binary installs are deleted: quality-gates.yml and improvement-loop.yml.

The path filter is not landed, and the reason is a three-place contract. tests/test_cli.py asserts exact equality of the ignore list against three sources at once: basicly.yml, quality-gates.yml and scaffolds.CONSUMER_CI_WORKFLOW. Any edit to one turns that test red and cannot be fixed inside the workflows. Landing it takes one commit touching scaffolds.py, tests/test_cli.py and both workflows together.

And it is not a move but an addition, measured over the last sixteen tracker-state commits: each touches the owned ledger and the external export together, so the ignore list must name both until basicly-vkh0.42.7 removes the second. A straight move would start running the full three-OS matrix on every tracker commit.

Coverage cost of the install deletion, measured: the five integration modules are 37 passed with the binary on PATH and 37 skipped without it. A skip, never a failure - but 37 tests stop running in CI until the flip removes the need for them.

One of three landed 2026-08-17. shell_tokens.py no longer names the binary in its incident example, with every measurement and bead reference kept.

Also landed, and worth more than the de-naming: tests/test_git_hooks/test_tracker_path_scan_staged.py, which runs the path-scan hook as git runs it over a repository holding only the owned ledger. Nothing previously exercised staged_tracker_files at all - the existing tests call findings on text handed to them. Proven to discriminate by narrowing the glob to the external directory alone, which turned it red.

Two are blocked, each on a coupled file outside the working fence. tracker-path-scan.py glob and docstring are one atomic change and tests/test_tracker_path_scan.py asserts the external paths match. tool-usage.py cannot drop its tracker-recording half while tests/test_tracker_surface.py asserts its two-word subcommand set equals tracker_usage.GROUP_SUBCOMMANDS - the hook half and the engine module are one unit split across two fences.

Transcript proving the constraint this bead exists for: over a repository with no external directory at all, the hook still blocks a machine path in the owned ledger and exits 1, and exits 0 on a clean ledger.

One of three landed 2026-08-17. improvement_controller.py reaches the tracker through the seam - br.create_record - rather than spawning it, so the whole-tree spawn count is now the src count.

Deleting install_br.py is blocked on five references outside the fence: tests/test_install_br.py loads it by path in nine tests, README and a how-to page cite it, and br.py and worktree.py name it in their own repair advice. Deleting the script alone hands over a red suite. Its CI precondition is met, so it is one atomic commit away.

check_corpus_drift.py is blocked on a missing capability rather than a fence: there is no bulk record read out of the owned ledger. export_records is export-only, owned_record answers one id at a time, and the kit fold sits behind a boundary a script may not cross. export_records has four other call sites in the engine, so the fix is a ledger-first export_records - the same shape the commit-message gate got at basicly-vkh0.42.1.

The pre-flip differential, taken 2026-08-17 immediately before the mode change, as this bead third criterion requires:

    64 record(s) in scope, 18 of them adopted; 866 imported, 0 declared (2026-08-15)
    clean:      yes
    conclusive: yes
    not compared: a record title, description, type, priority or acceptance criteria - the
    three queries read its status, comments, edges and gate rows only, so a clean verdict
    does not say the owned ledger can reproduce a record
    The owned ledger agrees with the live tracker, and the agreement means something.

Clean and conclusive over a non-empty scope of 64 records, which is step 4 own precondition in basicly.toml. The body half the verdict does not cover is closed separately: basicly-vkh0.41 backfilled the nine records the ledger held no body for and ledger-bodies is now a blocking check reporting all 923 carrying one.

Clause 1 and clause 2 were both demonstrated before the flip rather than after, by the wpc8 port. With the binary stripped from PATH, mode owned, and a temp consumer repo seeded through the kit own CLI, the real basicly decompose created two children and every engine query answered - labels, lane set, blocked, ready, cycles, record, gates - with no process spawned. The negative control is what makes that attributable: the same three queries at mode dual with the binary unreachable each raise RuntimeError, br is not on PATH.

payload.value:
Roughly 45 places in tests/test_supervise.py and 3 in tests/test_rubrics.py pass Path() as the repository root, so the engine under test resolves to the developer own checkout rather than a temp directory.

They pass today because they never reach the store. That is the whole risk: each is one seam change away from writing to the real ledger. Measured rather than reasoned - during the flip repair a traceback showed repo_root PosixPath(.) reaching owned_write.append, and the only thing between the test and a write to the live ledger was an invalid record id. Giving that id a valid shape, which the repair required, removes the brake.

Six further tests in the same modules were passing for the wrong reason: they assert an absence, and a fake installed at a seam the owned mode no longer calls produces exactly that absence. Those six are fixed; the repo roots are not.

The fix is mechanical - tmp_path rather than Path() - and the value is that a test can no longer write to the repository it is testing.

This record was minted by a probe of the owned create path and repurposed rather than tombstoned.

- `tests/test_rubrics.py`

payload.name: title
payload.value: the write seam still speaks the retired binary argument grammar

payload.name: description
payload.value:
Nothing spawns the external binary any more, and its vocabulary has not left. `basicly tracker write -- <argv>` takes the binary own argument grammar - comments add, close --reason, dep add, update --acceptance-criteria - and the seam translates it into owned events.

So every human tracker write, every skill that documents one, and every agent instruction still teaches a command language named after a tool the repository no longer runs. That is the same defect shape as the overloaded comment event kind, one layer up: a name inherited from a dependency outliving the dependency.

The choice is a design decision rather than a port. Either the seam grows a vocabulary of its own and the old grammar becomes an alias with a deprecation window, or the argv form is declared the permanent interface and the naming is accepted. Both are defensible; leaving it undecided means the next reader cannot tell which.

Filed from a retro rather than from a failure: no defect is attributable to it yet.

This record was minted by a probe of the create output path and repurposed rather than tombstoned.

Given a skill or an instruction documents a tracker write then it names the vocabulary this repository declares

payload.text:
[harness-info] the external store is deleted, and the engine spawns nothing

Landed in one pass rather than as the seven filed children, because each was blocked on a
file outside its own fence and the fences were the reason the track stalled.

What went, measured after:
- `.beads/` and its four tracked files. Verified first: 930 export records, 935 ledger
  records, **zero export-only**, against a positive control that reported a fake id.
- `run_br`/`try_run_br` and every spawn helper. `br.py` fell 1843 -> ~700 lines,
  22,940 -> ~8,000 tokens.
- Nine engine modules: tracker_surface, tracker_invocation, surface_report,
  tracker_cutover, edge_adoption, and the external halves of dependency_graph,
  gate_source and label_source.
- The `external` and `dual` modes. `owned` is the only one, and the default.

What replaced the parts that were load-bearing:
- `.beads/redirect` -> `.basicly/ledger/redirect`, naming the checkout rather than a
  directory, so two readers cannot disagree.
- `export_records` -> `br.all_records`, one fold of the ledger rather than a file read.
- The clock-step defect signature left with the process that produced it; the lock
  contention one was repointed at `events.LedgerLock`'s own wording.

Two defects the walk found, neither of which the flip's partial demonstration could:
- `owned_record` rendered `dependencies` and never `dependents`, so
  `supervise.derive_session` derived an empty session from a root whose children were all
  in the ledger. Every supervised pass was broken at `owned`.
- A test wrote four events into the committed ledger. Repaired, and a conftest guard now
  fails any test that touches it — proven to fire against a deliberate violation.

[harness-info] clause 2 met: a whole walk with nothing spawned

The clause asked for a full intake-to-merge walk with the external binary absent. What
had been demonstrated was `decompose` plus every engine query, not a walk.

The walk now runs as a test rather than as a one-off: `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
drives 12 scenarios end to end — claim, provision, build, verify, land, close — against a
real ledger, with a spawn wired to fail the test. All 12 pass. They were skipped
entirely before, because the fixture required the binary on PATH.

The walk found a defect no partial demonstration could: `br.owned_record` rendered a
record's `dependencies` and never its `dependents`, so `supervise.derive_session` derived
an **empty session** from a root whose children were all in the ledger. Every supervised
pass was broken at `owned`. Fixed at the read seam, with the title carried on each edge
because the sub-task report has no second read to reach for.

## Context

The cross-project `development` workspace still tracks its own coordination work in an
external tracker. `basicly`'s owned tracker replaced that here (basicly-vkh0.42), and the
kit is deployable on its own: `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/` imports nothing from `basicly`,
enforced by the `kit-boundary` hook, and its CLI walks a whole unit of work under an
engine-import blocker (`tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`).

**The kit alone, not the harness.** The workspace coordinates across repos; it does not
run lanes, worktrees or gates, so it needs the ledger and the CLI and nothing else.

## Open questions this must answer first

- Where a kit-only consumer declares its root id prefix. Here it is `[tracker] prefix` in
  `basicly.toml`, which a workspace with no `basicly.toml` does not have.
- Whether the workspace's existing records are imported or the ledger starts empty. The
  kit's `migrate.py` reads a foreign export; whether the workspace has one is unmeasured.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the development workspace when a coordination record is filed then it lands in a
  ledger under that workspace, with no `basicly` package and no tracker binary present
- Given that ledger when `cli.py ready` is run then it answers the ranked ready set
- Given the workspace's prior records when the cutover is done then every one is in the
  ledger, proven by an id-set comparison with a positive control

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`

## Context

The first install of the full harness — loop, gates and owned tracker — in a repository
that is not `basicly` itself. This is the real test: everything until now has been
exercised on the repository that authors it, where the catalog, the kit and the engine
are the same tree.

smaller half of the same claim.

## What this is expected to surface

A consumer install has never been walked end to end with the tracker owned. The install
now creates the ledger directory and reports a derived prefix rather than writing one
(`cli._setup_tracker`); whether that is enough for a consumer to mint its first root is
untested outside this repository.

  the projected hooks, skills and instructions land, with no tracker binary present

payload.description:
## The failure this comes from

I ran `git checkout HEAD -- tests/test_cli.py` during basicly-vkh0.42 and lost two of my
own uncommitted edits. Nothing refused it. The `require-explicit-confirmation` fragment
names the family in as many words, and the permissions comment
(`.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml:34`) names these three commands *specifically*
as undenied — so the rule was written, read and still not followed.

**Root cause: the rule lives only in prose, and prose is advisory at the moment of the
call.** Every neighbouring family in that file has a mechanical backstop —
`destructive-rm`, `destructive-git`, `bypass-gates`, `force-push`. This one has a comment
explaining why it does not. The asymmetry is what made it the family that got through.

## The control

A `destructive-restore` deny entry beside `destructive-git`:

```yaml
  - id: destructive-restore
    description: block path-restore and stash, which discard uncommitted work silently
    claude:
      - "Bash(git checkout --*)"
      - "Bash(git checkout*--*)"
      - "Bash(git restore*)"
      - "Bash(git stash*)"
    copilot:
      - "shell(git restore)"
      - "shell(git stash)"
```

`git checkout <branch>` and `git checkout -b` stay allowed, which is what the loop's own
branch handling needs. The engine drives git through `subprocess`, not through the Bash
tool, so no deny rule reaches it — verify that before landing rather than assuming it.

Then rewrite the comment at lines 33-37: it currently teaches the reader that these three
are undenied, which will be false.

**Editing the permissions catalog is on the confirmation list.** This record is the
proposal; a human disposes of it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the projected `.claude/settings.json` when it is read then it carries a deny rule
  matching `git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore` and `git stash`
- Given `git checkout -b <name>` and `git checkout <branch>` when either is attempted then
  neither is denied, proven by a matcher probe rather than by inspection
- Given `permissions-check` when it runs then it passes with the new entry projected

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/permissions/permissions.yaml`
- `.claude/settings.json`
- `tests/test_permissions.py`
payload.title: deny the path-restore family in the permissions backstop

payload.description:
## The failure this comes from

A multi-line regex I ran over `tests/test_decompose.py` during basicly-vkh0.42 removed
**1644 lines**. The pattern was `(?:    .*\n)+?(?=\n\n)`, intended to cut one indented
block; the lazy quantifier still spanned every blank-line-separated run in the file. The
module was restored from HEAD and every edit reapplied by hand.

## Why the existing rule did not catch it

The `non-interactive-shell` fragment already says to name the expected site count before a
scripted multi-site replace and reconcile after. It did not bind here, for two reasons:

- **A deletion's site count was right.** One match, as predicted. The match was the wrong
  *size*, and a count of matches cannot see size.
- The rule reads as being about replacement, so an edit framed as a cut does not obviously
  fall under it.

## The control

Extend that fragment with the magnitude clause: after any scripted in-place edit, compare
`wc -l` before and against after, and name the expected delta first. A delta larger than
the change described is a stop, the same way a site-count delta is. One line, in the
fragment that already carries the site-count rule, so it lands in every agent's always-on
baseline — check the character budget before adding, since that baseline is at its cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the `non-interactive-shell` fragment when it is read then it names the line-delta
  reconciliation for a scripted in-place edit, distinct from the site-count rule
- Given the projected instruction files when `basicly check` runs then every per-target
  character cap still passes

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/fragments/non-interactive-shell.yaml`
payload.title: reconcile the line delta after a scripted in place edit, not just the site count

payload.description:
## What the residue sweep found

A whole-tree probe over tracked files (2026-08-18) for the binary, the store directory and
the export filename. The probe:
`(^|[^a-zA-Z<._-])(br|bv)([ .]exe|\s+[a-z][a-z-]+)`, `\.beads`, `\bbeads\b`, `issues\.jsonl`.
Positive control: the probe returns 5130 hits in the ledger, so a zero elsewhere is a real
zero.

| Population | Files | Hits | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.basicly/ledger/` | 1 | 5130 | keep — the history is the record |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | 1 | 102 | keep — a released entry describes what shipped then |
| `tests/` | 66 | 282 | prose in fixtures and rationale; low value |
| engine `src/` | 34 | 206 | prose; three false claims already fixed |
| `docs/` | 4 | 62 | basicly-vkh0.42.6 owns these |
| **`.basicly/core/kit/`** | **8** | **25** | **this record** |

## Why the kit is the one that matters

The kit ships to a consumer by copy. A repository that installs it gets
`differential.py` explaining its own row shape in terms of `br gate list`, `scheduler.py`
citing `br schema issue` for the priority default, `migrate.py` describing `.beads/issues.jsonl`
as "the export the current tracker already writes" — a tracker the consumer has never had.
Every other population above is read only by people working in *this* repository, who have
the history. The kit's readers do not.

`migrate.py` is the exception to check rather than rewrite: it genuinely reads a foreign
export in that format, so its references are a live input contract, not a stale citation.
Establish which before editing it.

## Already fixed under basicly-vkh0.42, not part of this

Three user-facing false claims, found by the same sweep:
`commit.py` told the user to run `br sync --flush-only` against an `issues.jsonl` that no
longer exists; `cli.py`'s `policy dor` help said "via br lint"; `policy.py`'s module
docstring said the same and contradicted its own line 177.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the kit sources when the probe above is run then every remaining hit is a live
  input contract of `migrate.py`, and each is named in that module's docstring as one
- Given `kit-boundary` and the kit CLI's own walk when they run then both still pass
- Given a consumer reading a kit module cold when it cites a behaviour then that behaviour
  is one the kit itself has

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/`

payload.description:
## The defect

`.basicly/core/skills/work-tracker/skill.yaml` contradicts itself. Its Writes section at line 72 shows `basicly tracker write -- update <id> --add-label phase-7` as a working call and line 76 explains that it accumulates under the ledger lock. Its Refuses section at line 112 says the opposite:

> There is no owned label write. `update --add-label` (and every other label flag) raises at the seam ... Any instruction to label a record, a lane or a cut is therefore false: select work by id.

## Which half is true

The Writes section. Read 2026-08-18:
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py:53` `_resolve_labels` reads the record's own labels and rewrites the argv into `--labels` before translation, and line 117 documents the write as a read-modify-write under the lock.
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py:130` calls `mirror.drafts(kit_module, _resolve_labels(...))`, so the resolver always runs first.
- The raise at `src/basicly/mirror.py:117` is an internal guard on the un-resolved entry point. Its own message names the resolver that handles the case. A user never reaches it.

The false bullet is residue from before the label write landed under basicly-vkh0.42.

## Why it is priority 1

The consumer is a dispatched agent, not a human. The bullet does not merely confuse: it instructs the reader that every labelling instruction is false. `basicly loop supervise --label` is the multi-lane selection mechanism, so an agent that obeys this bullet refuses the parallel path. Nothing tests skill prose, so no gate sees it.

## Acceptance criteria

Given a reader of the work-tracker skill, then no passage states that a label write is refused, and the skill's Writes and Refuses sections do not contradict each other.
Given the corrected skill, when the label write is exercised against a scratch ledger, then the record carries the label and the transcript is recorded on this bead.
Given the projected copy at `.claude/skills/work-tracker/SKILL.md`, then it is regenerated from the source rather than hand-edited.
Demonstrated by: uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/work-tracker/skill.yaml`

payload.description:
## The defect

`basicly tracker show <id>` and `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py show` both return the kit fold shape and render **no edges at all**. Neither a `dependencies` nor a `dependents` key appears. So no command-line surface answers what a record blocks, what blocks it, or what its children are, one record at a time.

The engine itself has the answer. `src/basicly/tracker.py:155` `owned_record` returns `br show --json`'s shape, and `_rendered` at line 191 fills **both** directions. Its own docstring at line 202 records why the inverse direction is load-bearing: rendering only the outgoing half left `supervise.derive_session` deriving an empty session from a root whose children were all in the ledger (basicly-vkh0.29).

## Measured 2026-08-18

Same record, `basicly-vkh0.42`, three readers:

```text
basicly tracker show          keys: comments fields max_seq record status tombstoned totals
kit cli.py show               keys: comments fields max_seq record status tombstoned totals
tracker.owned_record          keys: comments dependencies dependents description id
                                    issue_type priority status title
                              dependencies: 1    dependents: 12
```

Positive control: the internal reader returns 12 dependents on that record and 1023 `edge` events exist in the ledger, so the fold has the material and a zero from the CLI is the CLI's zero, not the store's.

## Why it is priority 1

1. **An agent orients through the CLI.** The work-tracker skill points every reader at `basicly tracker show <id>` and describes the folded record as carrying exactly the seven keys above. An agent asking what a record depends on has no command that answers, and the skill does not say so.
2. **It is on the dashboard's critical path.** basicly-rn0o renders the backlog and its dependencies. A snapshot producer built over this surface would emit a graph with no edges.
3. **Two read surfaces disagree in shape.** `owned_record` and the CLI fold are separate renderings of one store. That is the drift `owned_record`'s own docstring says the kit loaders exist to prevent.

## Acceptance criteria

Given a record with at least one incoming and one outgoing edge, when `basicly tracker show <id>` runs, then the output carries both directions, each edge naming its type and the other record's status.
Given a record with no edges, then both keys are present and empty, so absence is distinguishable from a surface that never renders them.
Given the kit CLI's own `show` on a repository that copied only the kit, then it answers the same question in the same shape.
Given the two readers, when the same record is read through each, then a test asserts the edge sets are equal, so the shapes cannot drift apart again.
Demonstrated by: uv run basicly tracker show basicly-vkh0.42 printing 12 parent-child dependents, against a positive control record printing none

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`

payload.description:
## The finding

Reported by the lane that built the guard (basicly-vkh0.46), and left unfixed because it sits outside that record's acceptance criteria and its scope fence.

`write_snapshot` is now the single refusal point for a shrinking publish. It has three call sites. On the third, `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/fsck.py:736` in `fsck.rebuild`, the guard **cannot fire**: `rebuild` `unlink()`s every derived file before writing, so the target the guard would compare against is always absent, and the publish lands on the deliberate nothing-to-compare branch.

## Why it matters

`rebuild` is the path most likely to lose records, not least. The incident that bought R9 deleted 187 records, 47 of them open, and reported success. 3. Accept it, and record at the unlink why the guard is deliberately bypassed there.

Option 1 preserves both contracts and is the recommendation.

## The defect

`basicly tracker show <id>` and `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py show` both return the kit fold shape and render **no edges at all**. Neither a `dependencies` nor a `dependents` key appears. So no command-line surface answers what a record blocks, what blocks it, or what its children are, one record at a time.

The engine itself has the answer. `src/basicly/tracker.py:155` `owned_record` returns `br show --json`'s shape, and `_rendered` at line 191 fills **both** directions. Its own docstring at line 202 records why the inverse direction is load-bearing: rendering only the outgoing half left `supervise.derive_session` deriving an empty session from a root whose children were all in the ledger (basicly-vkh0.29).

## Measured 2026-08-18

Same record, `basicly-vkh0.42`, three readers:

```text
basicly tracker show          keys: comments fields max_seq record status tombstoned totals
kit cli.py show               keys: comments fields max_seq record status tombstoned totals
tracker.owned_record          keys: comments dependencies dependents description id
                                    issue_type priority status title
                              dependencies: 1    dependents: 12
```

Positive control: the internal reader returns 12 dependents on that record and 1023 `edge` events exist in the ledger, so the fold has the material and a zero from the CLI is the CLI's zero, not the store's.

## Why it is priority 1

1. **An agent orients through the CLI.** The work-tracker skill points every reader at `basicly tracker show <id>` and describes the folded record as carrying exactly the seven keys above. An agent asking what a record depends on has no command that answers, and the skill does not say so.
2. **It is on the dashboard's critical path.** basicly-rn0o renders the backlog and its dependencies. A snapshot producer built over this surface would emit a graph with no edges.
3. **Two read surfaces disagree in shape.** `owned_record` and the CLI fold are separate renderings of one store. That is the drift `owned_record`'s own docstring says the kit loaders exist to prevent.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run basicly tracker show basicly-vkh0.42` — read the top-level keys.
2. `uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py show .basicly/ledger basicly-vkh0.42` —
   read the top-level keys.
3. Positive control, the same record through the engine's internal reader:
   `uv run python -c "from pathlib import Path; from basicly import tracker;
   r=tracker.owned_record(Path('.'),'basicly-vkh0.42'); print(sorted(r))"`
4. Second control, that the store holds the material:
   `grep -c '\"kind\":\"edge\"' .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl` returns 1023.

Observed: steps 1 and 2 return `comments fields max_seq record status tombstoned totals` —
no edge keys at all. Step 3 returns `dependencies` with 1 entry and `dependents` with 12.
Expected: every reader of one record answers what it depends on and what depends on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a record with at least one incoming and one outgoing edge, when `basicly tracker show <id>` runs, then the output carries both directions, each edge naming its type and the other record's status.
Given a record with no edges, then both keys are present and empty, so absence is distinguishable from a surface that never renders them.
Given the kit CLI's own `show` on a repository that copied only the kit, then it answers the same question in the same shape.
Given the two readers, when the same record is read through each, then a test asserts the edge sets are equal, so the shapes cannot drift apart again.
Demonstrated by: uv run basicly tracker show basicly-vkh0.42 printing 12 parent-child dependents, against a positive control record printing none

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`

## The defect

basicly-vkh0.45 moved the per-work-type required sections into `[policy.type_sections]` in `basicly.toml`. It moved the **reader** that judges a record, not the **writer** that scaffolds one.

`policy.compose_body` and `policy.scaffold_body` hold no repository root, so they cannot reach the configuration. Their two callers — `decompose._child_body` and `cli._cmd_policy_scaffold` — were outside that record's scope fence, and the lane deliberately declined to add a `repo_root` parameter nothing passed.

The result is a split brain. A repository that declares `bug = ["## Repro Steps"]` gets a Definition-of-Ready that demands that heading, and a `basicly policy scaffold --type bug` that emits the built-in one instead. The scaffold's own output then fails the gate the scaffold exists to satisfy, and the failure message points the user back at the same command.

1. In `basicly.toml`, set `[policy.type_sections]` `bug = ["## Repro Steps", "## Impact"]`.
2. `uv run basicly policy scaffold --type bug` — read the headings it emits.
3. Create a record from exactly that scaffold output.
4. `uv run basicly policy dor <id>` on it.

Given a repository that declares `[policy.type_sections]`, when `basicly policy scaffold --type <t>` runs, then it emits exactly the headings that work type's configured rule requires.

## The defect

The `work-tracker` skill carried **three** false statements at once (basicly-7wlhlp), each describing a refusal the code does not make. Every gate in the repository was green throughout. Skill prose is projected, linted for format, and checked for drift against its own source — and never checked against the behaviour it describes.

This is the population a green suite protects least: the consumer is a dispatched agent, so a false claim is not confusion, it is a lane that follows a wrong instruction and files no bug about it. One of the three told the reader that every labelling instruction is false, which would make an agent refuse `loop supervise --label`, the multi-lane path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `.basicly/core/skills/work-tracker/skill.yaml` before commit fbf844ba.
2. Note the Refuses section claims `update --add-label` raises, `create` without `--json` is refused, and the ready set is the open records.
3. Check each against `src/basicly/owned_write.py`, `src/basicly/tracker_write.py` and `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py`.
4. Run `uv run basicly verify --mode fast`, `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` and `uv run basicly catalog lint`.

Observed: all three claims are false, and every gate reports PASS.
Expected: a claim a skill makes about a refusal is checked against the table that implements it.

## The control that would have caught all three

Proposed by the lane that fixed them. `.scripts/docs_claims.py` already carries the mechanism: an `Assertion` that reads a catalog source and fails when it disagrees with an engine symbol. `_skill_work_types` is the working example, and `tests/test_docs_claims.py` has its anchor-vanished test.

Add an assertion that parses the skill's refusal section and fails when it names an `update` flag that `tracker_argv.UPDATE_LABEL_FLAGS` or `tracker_argv.UPDATE_FIELD_FLAGS` actually translates. That binds the prose to the tables whose change made it false, costs nothing per run, and is a deterministic gate rather than a judged one — which the standing constraints prefer.

## The scope question this raises, and does not answer

34 skills ship. This audited one. Whether the other 33 carry the same class of residue is **unmeasured**, and a per-skill hand audit does not scale. The generalisable form is: a skill that states a refusal names the symbol that implements it, and the gate checks the pair. That is a catalog-schema change, and it is larger than this record. Decide the narrow gate first and let its firing history argue for the general one.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the work-tracker skill states a refusal for an `update` flag, when the flag tables translate that flag, then the gate fails and names both the passage and the table.
Given the pre-fix text of all three claims, when the gate runs against it, then it fails — proven by restoring that text temporarily, not by reasoning.
Given the corrected text, then the gate passes.
Given the flag tables gain an entry, then no gate change is required.
Given a skill with no refusal section, then the gate passes rather than erroring on an empty match.
Demonstrated by: uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check, red against the reverted passage and green against HEAD

## Scope

- `.scripts/docs_claims.py`
- `tests/test_docs_claims.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Three decision records rest on premises the tracker flip expired, and one of them was false the day it was written. Everything in T2 to T6 cites the replacement, so this lands first.

**D-28** says a handoff artifact travels as a comment marker, never a ledger append, because the landing advance sweeps base-checkout dirt only under the tracker path. Measured 2026-08-18: `merge.py` calls `commit_tracker_state` and only then `_assert_base_ready`, so ledger dirt is swept before the clean-tree check. `git log -L` dates that behaviour to `b20a0b5a`, 2026-08-15. D-28 was authored in `e0b38e7f`, 2026-08-16. Its reason was carried over from the requirements document, where it correctly named the external store, and the noun was updated without re-running the measurement.

**D-23**, the seam is the only place where both stores move together. There is one store. Its own table row already reads `expires at the flip`. The rule survives with a different reason, which the configuration already names: the read-only guard, the argv classification and the event translation all live at the seam.

**D-35**, the external binary is transitional. It is gone. Section 37 describes it in the present tense throughout and its cutover table still marks the flip step not dispatchable.

**Section 32.10's first rule** claims only free-text keys truncate and never a field the fold reads. The allow-list contains `value`, and the fold reads `value`. One record has already lost 365 bytes of its description permanently.

## The decision to record, D-36

A handoff artifact is one typed `artifact` event in the owned ledger, body under a key the per-event cap does not name, never truncated. Its size is bounded by removing what the ledger can already derive; where nothing is derivable the body is stored whole. D32's branch-file alternative is rejected: its premise expired at the flip, and deleting the body at teardown leaves a digest whose preimage is gone, which proves bytes existed and nothing about what they said. Refusal is also rejected, on three measured grounds carried in the analysis.

The accepted cost is stated, not waved: every artifact body is in every clone forever, measured at 478311 bytes against a 5.7 MB log, about 8 percent.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the decision table then D-28 reads superseded by D-36 rather than accepted, and D-23 and D-35 no longer read as live.
Given D-28's body then it names the commit and the date its reason expired, and keeps the record rather than deleting it.
Given D-36 then it states the rejected alternatives with their reasons and the accepted permanence cost with its measurement.
Given section 32.10's first rule then it names `value` as the fold-read key the allow-list contains.
Given section 33 then it no longer asserts the marker mechanism as the design.
Given no heading is renumbered then every existing intra-document anchor still resolves.
Demonstrated by: uv run basicly verify --mode fast

## Scope

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`

payload.description:
## The defect

The per-event size cap dispatches on the payload key's name, from a closed four-member allow-list, and the event kind is never passed to the preparer. Two consequences, both provable.

A key outside the allow-list is not capped at all. So a new typed kind is exempt from the cap **by accident of naming** rather than by any decision. That is the state a typed `artifact` kind would ship into.

And `value` is on the allow-list while the fold reads it, which contradicts the rule section 32.10 states about itself. The same logical field carries two different bounds depending on which event shape holds it: a description on a `created` event is stored whole, and the largest is over 7000 bytes, while a description on a `field` event is cut at 4096.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the truncatable-key set and the cap constant in the kit's events module. Note the set has four members and no kind appears in it.
2. Read the preparer's call site in the append path. Note the draft's kind is not passed.
3. Call the preparer with a 10000-byte value under `text`, under `body`, and nested under `artifact`. Observe 4096, 10000, 10000.
4. Read the fold's field handler. Observe it reads `value`.
5. Scan the committed ledger for truncation flags.

Observed: one record's description is permanently cut to 4096 of 4461 bytes in the store of record, and any key the allow-list does not name is unbounded.
Expected: the bound is a property of the kind, declared, and a fold-read field is never cut.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a payload key the fold reads then the preparer never truncates it.
Given a payload key outside the allow-list then the preparer applies the bound the kind declares rather than none.
Given a kind that declares no bound then the preparer refuses the draft rather than storing an unbounded body.
Given an existing event already carrying a truncation flag then the fold derives the same field state as before.
Demonstrated by: uv run pytest tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py -q, plus a fold over the committed ledger deriving an identical phase for every record against a snapshot taken first

## Cost to know before starting

The kit's events module is frozen at its module-size baseline and has no headroom, so this needs an offsetting cut **in code, not in comments** — its comment density is already above the cap and only frozen. It serialises with basicly-vkh0.30, which writes the same file.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py`

## The defect

The producer validates the in-memory payload, the transport truncates it, and the consumer re-reads the stored body and refuses it. The producing function's own docstring claims it is validated before the write so a producing state can never hand on an artifact the consuming state will refuse. That sentence is false.

Measured over the committed ledger 2026-08-18: 31 of 54 handoff artifacts are cut, 337353 bytes lost. **23 record and kind pairs are refused by their own entry predicate and the bodies are unrecoverable**, because the external binary is deleted and the log may not be rewritten. 20 of 21 artifacts written live by the engine were truncated, so this is not an import artefact.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call the entry predicate for the implementation-plan of `basicly-ejdm`.
2. Call it for the change-summary of `basicly-0p8n` as a positive control.
3. Scan the ledger for artifact markers and compare their stored length against their recorded original length.

Observed: step 1 returns not admitted, with a reason quoting JSON cut mid-token. Step 2 returns admitted. `basicly-ejdm` is open and in decompose.
Expected: a body the producer validated is the body the consumer reads.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a producing state records an artifact then the engine appends one `artifact` event carrying the kind as a typed field and the body under a non-truncatable key.
Given the stored body is read back by the entry predicate then it is byte-identical to what the producer validated.
Given a legacy artifact marker on disk then the reader resolves it to the `artifact` kind through the delegated-kind alias rather than the skip path.
Given a repository that has not installed the schemas then neither end runs.
Demonstrated by: uv run pytest tests/test_artifact_record.py tests/test_handoff.py -q, plus recording a 20000-byte artifact and asserting the entry predicate admits it, which is red today against 23 real pairs

Two module docstrings assert the external tracker mode as a live fact. Both are defects under the comment-divergence decision.

Dropping it makes the artifact constant-size in the diff rather than linear, which is the correct bound: the decision on diff size already rules that a large diff is sometimes right, so refusing the artifact would refuse a correct landing for being correct about a large change.

## Context

**No record absorbs or deletes this document.** A search of every record for `factory-loop` returns 44 that cite it and none that removes it, against a positive control that finds the sibling record for the work-tracker document by the same query. The plan's register ties its deletion to an epic with 16 open children, which is the wrong precondition: absorbing the claims does not require the work they describe to be finished.

The document holds 37 decisions. 31 have a counterpart in the architecture. Five do not: the light and dark factory modes, the waiver rule at the lower integrity levels, the plugin package as a second distribution channel, the authority order which is obsolete because the document it ranked is deleted, and the vendor order which is only partly shipped.

**This record must not run before T1.** D32 lives here and is being withdrawn. If the file is deleted first the decision vanishes and the next reader re-derives its consequence from nothing.

payload.description:
## Context

The owner's standing goal: reading the ledger at session start, plus `architecture.md` in context, must become the best and most complete way to prepare an implementation session. `HANDOVER.md` then stops being mandatory.

**No command does that today.** Measured 2026-08-18:

- `basicly brief` takes a required issue id, so it briefs a unit and cannot open a session.
- `basicly status` reports engine version, install state, projection drift and hook wiring. It never reads the backlog.
- `basicly health` reports per-agent run counts, failure and rework rates. It never reads the backlog.
- `basicly tracker ready`/`blocked`/`stats` each answer one question and none carries the release ladder, the live decisions, or what the previous session learned.

So the three things a new session actually needs - what is ready and why it is ranked that way, which decisions are live or recently reversed, and which traps cost the last session time - have no home but a hand-written file that nothing gates and that goes stale silently.

## Why the handover cannot simply be deleted

It currently carries load nothing else does: unpushed-commit state, the dependency order among open records, and the operating traps. Two of this session's traps were discovered the hard way and would have been avoided by reading them. Deleting the file without a replacement loses that; keeping it without a gate means the next reader trusts a stale claim.

## The shape to consider, not a design

A read-only `basicly session start` (name to be decided) that composes existing readers rather than inventing a store: the ranked ready set with its scores, the blocked set with its blockers, records changed since a given ref, the live grant and its remaining budget, and any decision records marked TARGET or recently superseded. Every line derived, so it cannot go stale.

The open question this record must answer first, before any code: **which parts of a handover are derivable and which are irreducibly human.** A trap learned by a session is not in the ledger unless something puts it there. If the answer is that some part is irreducibly human, then the honest outcome is a smaller handover with a gate on its freshness, not no handover.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a new session in a harness-enabled repository, when the orientation command runs, then it prints what is ready and why, what is blocked and by what, the live grant and its remaining budget, and the decisions currently marked as targets.
Given every line it prints, then that line is derived from the ledger, the configuration or the git history, and no line is hand-maintained prose.
Given the command runs in a repository with an empty ledger, then it says so rather than printing an empty frame that reads as nothing to do.
Given the analysis of what is irreducibly human, then it is recorded as a decision, and either the handover is retired or its remaining scope is named and gated for freshness.
Demonstrated by: running the command in this repository and in a fresh consumer repository, and comparing its output against the current hand-written HANDOVER.md to show what it does and does not replace

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`

## Context

Owner decision 2026-08-19. `docs/requirements/` is **not** deleted. A long-lived design branch was refused, and a ledger event was refused as the home for a 1178-line design. The folder stays as the place a requirement is born, and every requirement created there from now on carries **one identifiable structure** an agent, a skill and a script can each act on.

This **amends** the v1.0.0 rule `basicly-vkh0.42.6` cites. The rule now reads: a requirements document that describes **shipped** work is absorbed into the architecture and deleted; a document that states work **not yet built** lives in `docs/requirements/` in the register form until its acceptance criteria close.

## What is missing

Nothing structures or identifies a requirement document today. The two that exist are 1568 and 1585 lines of mixed claim, decision and measurement, with no shared section set, no id and no gate. The marker roster and requirement register read `architecture.md` after basicly-vkh0.42.8, not this folder, so a malformed requirement is invisible to every gate.

The six machine-checked sections architecture section 33 already specifies for `solution-design` are the obvious candidate format rather than a new invention.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a new requirement document then it carries a machine-checkable section set and a record id that resolves in the tracker.
Given a requirement document whose sections do not conform then a verify check fails and names the missing section.
Given an author asks for a new requirement then a scaffold command writes the conforming skeleton rather than the author copying an existing file.
Given every acceptance criterion a requirement carries is closed then a check reports the document as absorbable rather than deleting it.
Given the folder holds no requirement document then no gate changes behaviour.
Demonstrated by: uv run basicly verify --mode fast with a deliberately malformed requirement present, showing the check fail and then pass once corrected

## Open question the owner left open

Whether an implemented requirement is deleted or kept forever. The owner said whichever is better. A recommendation is recorded as a comment on this record.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/`
- `.scripts/`
- `src/basicly/`
- `docs/requirements/`

payload.description:
## Context

`docs/research/2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md` is findings, not a plan, and says so. A whole-tracker search for `sota|deepseek|cordis|revertible` over all 951 records returns one unrelated hit, so **nothing carries this work** — it exists only as research prose and as point 6 of the owner plan.

Two framing corrections the research establishes, both of which a proposal must respect. The paper formalises **Cordis**, not the harness; `deepseek` occurs once in it, as an author affiliation. And `dsh` is a **runtime, not a factory**: zero hits for `decompos`, `depends_on` and `blocked_by` across its packages, five for `worktree`, three for `git commit`, against a control of 3385 for `subagent`. It has no work graph, no decomposition and no landing, so it cannot teach us the loop. What it can teach us is composition, effect tracking and gated documentation.

## What must be settled before any adoption argument

Section 8 of the research lists eight open questions, each with a stated method. Two of them decide whether adoption is even possible, and they are this record.

**Q1 — does the revertible-effect guarantee survive contact with a filesystem?** The paper confines it to locations the system can modify exclusively and restore. A coding agent principal effects, files in a user repository, spawned processes and network calls, are outside that boundary by the paper own test. Method: enumerate `ctx.effect` call sites in the fs, shell and subprocess packages and classify each inverse as restore, compensate or no-op.

**Q4 — would the paradigm survive translation to Python?** The paper names the descriptor protocol as the `Proxy` analogue and requires a module registry supporting eviction. Neither claim is tested against CPython import machinery. Method: a spike that introduces a Python component and then **retracts** it, such that its registrations and its module both go away.

A proposal written before Q1 and Q4 are settled is unfalsifiable, which is why this record produces the answers first and the proposals second.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given Q1 then every `ctx.effect` call site in the three named packages is classified, with a count per class and the file and line for each.
Given Q4 then a runnable Python spike exists that introduces and retracts a component, and the transcript states which half failed if either did.
Given each settled question then a proposal names what basicly adopts, what it refuses, and the evidence for each, with a refusal reason stronger than taste.
Given a proposal that would change an invariant then it cites the invariant by architecture section number.
Given a question that could not be settled then it is listed as not established rather than answered from recall.
Demonstrated by: the spike script run end to end with its output pasted into the record, and a proposal set each item of which carries an evidence rung

## Scope

- `docs/research/`
- the tracker only. **This record writes no architecture text**; the architecture update is a separate record so the two do not collide.

## Context

Point 3 of the owner plan. Two research documents totalling 2123 lines hold findings no architecture section carries: `2026-07-26-sota-review.md` and `2026-08-17-deepseek-harness.md`. The first states where basicly is ahead, where it is behind ranked by cost, and a rejection table with a reason per row; the second states the plugin paradigm and its comparison table against our own sections.

The research files are the durable evidence base and stay. What is missing is the **absorption**: an architecture reader today cannot find out that a competing project converged on our thesis, or that eight named gaps were measured and ranked, without opening a research file the architecture never cites.

## The rule that binds this absorption

Architecture D-36 generalisation, landed 2026-08-18: an absorbed *Because* inherits a measurement that can expire, so it is **re-run or it is not absorbed**. The SOTA review is dated 2026-07-26 and every number in it is now three weeks old against a field that moves. Any figure carried into the architecture is re-measured first or carried as a dated sourced claim, never as a bare assertion.

## Ordering

This record writes `architecture.md`. So do basicly-vkh0.42.6, basicly-1hp91f and basicly-e2mz.37. **They run one at a time.** This one runs last of the four, because the absorptions delete two documents whose claims this record would otherwise have to re-place.

Its input is basicly-e2mz.45, which settles the two questions that gate any adoption argument. Do not start before that record answers them.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a finding the architecture adopts then a section states it with its source and the date it was verified at.
Given a rejection the review recorded then the architecture carries it as a decision with the reason, so it is not re-proposed.
Given a number carried from a research file then it is re-measured or marked sourced with its date, never restated bare.
Given a research claim that merely restates shipped code then it is dropped rather than moved.
Given the absorption is complete then a reader can reach every adopted finding from the architecture contents without opening a research file.
Demonstrated by: uv run basicly verify --mode full, plus a citation probe showing each adopted finding resolves from an architecture section number

## Context

Two owner decisions reshape the design that lives as `01-solution-design.md` on `harness/basicly-rn0o`, 1178 lines.

**Owner decision 2026-08-18.** The 2026-08-14 decision to ship units A, B, C and G only is **superseded**: wall mode and the action surface are in scope. And the design is **not implementation-ready** as written; a reviewer and an architect pass clean it up before any unit is built.

**Owner decision 2026-08-19.** The board must work across harnesses **and** across trackers, in every combination: copilot with an external tracker, claude with an external tracker, claude with the basicly ledger, copilot with the basicly ledger. The chosen cut is **the `harness-board/v1` snapshot schema is the interface**. The board becomes a kit that renders any conforming snapshot. basicly ships **one reference producer**, not the only producer. A foreign producer gets a documented adapter contract and the conformance kit.

## What that changes in the existing design

Unit B is currently the file-only snapshot producer, described as *the* producer. It becomes **a** producer, and the schema in unit A stops being an internal wire format and becomes a published contract with its own compatibility rule. Unit G, the adoption seam and conformance kit, moves from last to **first-class**, because it is now what makes the interface real rather than a later courtesy. Unit C onward consume the schema and must not reach past it into the ledger.

The named failure mode is the one the plan already records for the hybrid dispatch shape: the native path carries the features and cross-producer parity rots quietly. A conformance kit that only the native producer is ever run against does not detect that.

Given the revised design then the snapshot schema is specified independently of any producer, with its versioning and compatibility rule stated.
Given a consumer unit then it reads only the snapshot and no unit reaches the ledger directly.
Given a foreign producer then the design states the adapter contract it satisfies and the conformance kit that proves it.
Given the two superseded scope decisions then the revised design carries wall mode and the action surface in scope, with the superseded decision recorded rather than deleted.
Given a reviewer and an architect pass then each finding is dispositioned in the design or recorded as refused with a reason.
Given the revision is complete then the decomposition names which unit publishes the schema and which units consume it.
Demonstrated by: the revised design passing the six-section solution-design check, and a walkthrough naming for each of the four harness and tracker combinations which component supplies the snapshot

## Scope

- `01-solution-design.md` on the harness/basicly-rn0o branch
- the tracker records under basicly-rn0o

payload.description:
## The defect

`basicly-vbl35a` made the cap stop cutting any key the fold reads, which acceptance criterion 1 required. The consequence it names rather than buries: `field`.`value` and every `created` payload key are now stored **whole** where `value` was previously cut at 4096 bytes, and **nothing in the tree bounds them**.

That is not a regression against the old behaviour for `created` — a description under `description` was always uncapped, and 31 are stored above 4096 with the largest at 7043. It **is** a new hole for `field`.`value`, which the cap did bound, wrongly, and now bounds not at all.

The reason the cap exists is section 32.10 first paragraph: git compression, the ship-time rollup and a change-sized write all assume bounded events, and none of them bounds a single pasted payload. An agent that pastes a multi-megabyte log into a description now puts it in every clone, compressed and unremovable, because true removal is the history rewrite section 32.8 forbids.

## Why the cap cannot be the answer

Cutting a folded field makes a derived value depend on the cap, which breaks the determinism section 32.2 asserts. So the bound has to move to the **producer**, which is D-36 derivability argument applied to a field rather than to an artifact: a body is bounded by dropping what the ledger can already derive, not by a byte count.

`basicly-gvlpxm` does exactly this for `change-summary`. It does not cover a folded field, so this record is the sibling case and not a duplicate.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Write a field event whose value is a 5 MB string through the engine seam.
2. Read the stored event. Observe the whole 5 MB, no truncation flag, and no refusal.
3. Confirm no gate refuses it: run the verify suite and observe every check pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a folded field whose value exceeds a declared producer bound then the write is refused at the seam with the field named, rather than stored.
Given a folded field within the bound then the write is unchanged and the fold derives the same state.
Given a refusal then it says which field and what the bound is, so the caller can drop what is derivable instead of guessing.
Given an existing oversized value already in the log then the fold derives the same state as before and nothing rewrites it.
Demonstrated by: uv run pytest tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py -q plus a seam-level test that a 5 MB field value is refused, against a positive control that a small one is accepted

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/`

payload.description:
## The defect

The shipped board schema and its consumer refuse the **document** on any violation anywhere. The design promises the opposite: only `meta` is required, and an absent section renders as not emitted by this producer. `board_schema.verdict` returns INVALID on any violation and `readable` goes false, so one bad section blanks the screen.

That was tolerable while basicly was the only producer. Under the owner decision of 2026-08-19 the snapshot schema is a **published contract** and a foreign producer is expected. A real external tracker whose first honest attempt carries one over-long title gets a blank board, so **a producer that emits nothing is better off than one that tries**. That inverts the adoption story the contract exists to create.

## Falsified directly, four refusals against one control

Each of these is refused with exit 1, whole document:

- `freshness.source` = `producer-push` — the enum has no member for a producer that writes on a state transition.
- `generated_at` = an RFC3339 `+00:00` offset — the pattern admits only the `Z` form, while Pythons `datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()` produces the offset form. The design own annotation says RFC3339 UTC, so the design is wrong about what it ships.
- `asks[].actions` = `approve-pr` — a closed enum of basicly CLI verbs, so a foreign producer that names any action of its own loses the board rather than the buttons.
- `units[].title` at 250 characters — the 200 bound is right and refusing the document is the defect, not the bound.

**Positive control:** an undeclared *key*, `quotas`, validates ok with exit 0 and reports `unknown 1 key(s)`. So the four refusals are properties of the constraints, not of the probe.

## The rule the compatibility clause is missing

Keys may be added; permitted values may never be widened within a major. Widening an enum, loosening a pattern or raising a maxLength produces documents an already shipped consumer of the same major refuses. The design borrows the ledger additive-only rule, and that rule does not transfer, because the ledger readers are all ours and a board readers are not.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a snapshot whose units section violates the schema and whose backlog section does not then backlog is reported renderable and units is reported not conformant naming its violations.
Given a partly renderable document then the exit code distinguishes it from a refused one.
Given a value added to a v1 enum then the documented rule predicts the refusal rather than promising tolerance.
Given a foreign extensible value set then it is not a closed enum, and a label the consumer does not implement is ignored rather than fatal.
Given the minimal and full fixtures then both still validate exactly as before.
Demonstrated by: uv run pytest tests/test_board_schema.py -q plus the four falsifying snapshots above, each rendering its valid sections and naming its invalid one

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_schema.py`
- `.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`
- `tests/test_board_schema.py`
- `tests/fixtures/board/`

## The defect

`01-solution-design.md` lives on `harness/basicly-rn0o` and its producer half reads `.beads/issues.jsonl`. **That file does not exist on main.** The branch is 248 commits behind and the deletion is not an ancestor of it, so the design was written against a tree that has since changed underneath it.

Verified four ways:

- `git ls-tree main .beads/` is empty; `git ls-tree harness/basicly-rn0o .beads/` holds four blobs.
- `git log --diff-filter=D -- .beads/issues.jsonl` names `db5619d6`, make the owned ledger the only work store.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor db5619d6 harness/basicly-rn0o` answers no.
- `git rev-list --count harness/basicly-rn0o..main` answers 248.

The data survived at a different path, in a different shape, reached through a different module: 354 `harness-wait` occurrences in the owned ledger against a positive control of 1075 `harness-policy`. So this is a re-basing job, not a lost capability.

## What it invalidates

Every source path, every measurement and every acceptance number in the producer half. Named specifically: the contract section, unit B first acceptance criterion and its 500 ms cap, the 0-against-132 ask derivation, constraint C5 and constraint C6. Two headline ratios are load-bearing and both cite a file nobody can open.

Constraint C5 timing figure is also **root dependent**, which a single number was never the right shape for: `loop session basicly-rn0o --json` takes 4.45 s and `loop session basicly-kjc5 --json` takes 20.29 s, measured 2026-08-19. The direction of C5, build from stored state and never from a live observation, survives and is strengthened, because the worst case got worse.

## The rule this is an instance of

A design that lives only on a branch decays against main at the rate main moves, and nothing measures it. The loop deletes a lane branch at teardown, so this design survives only because its lane never shipped.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the revised design then no source path names the deleted external store outside a block marked superseded.
Given each named source then it carries its read cost measured on or after 2026-08-19.
Given the ask derivation criterion then it states both the naive count and the paired count as re-measured numbers, with the positive control that proves the low number is a property of the world rather than of the probe.
Given the timing claim then it is stated as root dependent with at least two roots measured, not as one number.
Given a superseded measurement then it stays in the document dated rather than deleted.
Demonstrated by: a search for the deleted store path over the revised design returning only occurrences inside a superseded block, and uv run basicly board validate on the minimal fixture still exiting zero

## Scope

- `01-solution-design.md` on harness/basicly-rn0o

## Context

`basicly-rn0o.10` names the failure mode in its own words: the native path carries the features and cross-producer parity rots quietly, and a conformance kit that only the native producer is ever run against does not detect that. **The design contains no unit that detects it.**

The gate that exists already concedes the gap. The `board-schema` verify check comment says it proves nothing about a snapshot the engine produced, because no producer exists yet. So today the contract is checked against fixtures, and after unit B it would be checked against exactly one producer.

The same shape has already bitten this project once and it is measurable: the dispatch ledger holds 423 run records over 313 items, distributed 229 claude and 194 manual, and **zero copilot**, while three agent families are advertised. A capability nothing exercises reads as working.

## What is missing

A unit whose whole job is to run the conformance kit against a producer that is **not** the basicly reference producer. The cheapest honest second producer is a small script in the fixture tree that reads a checked-in fake external-tracker export and emits a snapshot. It imports no basicly module, which is the point.

The ongoing cost must be stated rather than hidden: the second producer is a maintained artifact.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the conformance suite then it runs against at least two producers, one of which imports no basicly module.
Given a section the reference producer emits and the second producer does not then the parity check fails and names the section, unless the asymmetry is declared.
Given a foreign fixture derived from a non basicly tracker shape then the page renders and every absent section is named as not emitted by this producer.
Given the second producer is added then the design states its maintenance cost rather than omitting it.

payload.description:
## The defect

Two halves, and the second is the one that is wrong rather than untidy.

**The cycle.** The board design has the producer read the supervisor lock file directly, and unit F has the supervisor write the snapshot on its tick. The supervisor is a band 2 driver, so the snapshot module must sit below it for unit F to import it, and above it to call the lock reader. That is a cycle, and the import contract declares itself **exhaustive**, with only two function level exemptions.

**The duplication.** The supervisor own lock reader carries a non-obvious invariant in its docstring: a corrupt payload still reports the heartbeat age, because **staleness is mtime only by design**, with the identity fields absent. A second reader written from the file format will very likely take the heartbeat from the payload timestamp instead of the file mtime. The two then disagree about whether a supervisor is alive, silently, and only when a supervisor crashes.

## The two shapes, and neither is obviously right

Either the lock info type and its reader move to a leaf module both bands may import, which is a real extraction along a nameable responsibility and touches a frozen module with 1503 tokens of headroom. Or the supervisor **injects** the holder into the snapshot producer, which is the pattern the kit already uses for redaction. The second makes the producer unable to answer the lock question on its own, so the on-demand mode must render not supervised rather than reading the lock, which is arguably more honest and matches the design own transcript.

The design must pick one and give the reason. This record does not pick for it.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the revised design then exactly one module parses the supervisor lock and the design names it.
