body.post_ship_action:
Declared before the tag moves, and the first item is a pre-tag action rather than a post-ship one, because curating changelog.d after `basicly release` never publishes — the workflow reads the tagged commit. (1) BEFORE the tag: correct changelog.d/basicly-rn0o.1.added.md to say the three required keys are `schema`, `generated_at` and `freshness`, delete the `meta` sentence, and narrow the verify-pipeline sentence to "checks the shipped fixture on every run". (2) BEFORE the tag: write changelog.d/basicly-rn0o.11.fixed.md covering section-by-section ruling, the new exit code 3, the four opened value spaces, the `asks[].actions` retype, and the compatibility rule. (3) If the owner tags without (1) and (2): the tag stands, no re-tag — file an errata record to amend the released `## [v-next]` section in a follow-up commit, and state in it that the released text was wrong rather than editing it silently. (4) File one record against the gate gap the second reader exists to cover: no check reads changelog.d, so a false capability claim on the assembled changelog reaches consumers unopposed; the cheapest binding is to extend .scripts/docs_claims.py with an assertion that any fragment naming a schema's required keys matches .basicly/core/schemas/*.json. (5) basicly-rn0o.13 stays open and blocked-by this record; it is the unit that would detect the parity rot item (3) above concedes. All edits are the owner's — I changed no file, moved no tag, and pushed nothing.

Coverage boundary: I read the full diff of a3db99b2 across all five files, board_schema.py at HEAD for the changed regions, the schema's required/properties, basicly.toml's board-schema and docs-claims entries, changelog.d/README.md and the full changelog.d listing, and the named tests. I ran pytest on tests/test_board_schema.py, the validate command on three fixtures plus two hand-built documents, and docs_claims.py --check. I did NOT inspect: c79b1589's manifest regeneration beyond its stat line, the other 30 changelog.d fragments against code, the verify pipeline's handling of exit code 3 by callers other than the shell, docs/architecture/architecture.md's row for this command, or README.md and the repository description.

unsupported.claim: changelog.d/basicly-rn0o.1.added.md:4, the exact words a consumer will read when `basicly release` folds this fragment in: "A snapshot carries only `meta` as required; every other section is optional, so a producer declares what it can supply rather than filling fields it cannot know."
unsupported.why: False, not merely unevidenced, on two independent counts. The shipped schema's required list is ['schema', 'generated_at', 'freshness'] and `meta` is not among its 15 properties at all (verified: python3 -c "import json;s=json.load(open('.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json'));print(s['required']);print('meta' in s['properties'])" → ['schema','generated_at','freshness'] / False). A consumer following this sentence emits {"meta": {...}}, takes three required-key violations, and now — because of this very lane — gets INVALID with "The required part does not validate, so no section renders", exit 1. `meta` is design-era vocabulary that never reached the schema. Nothing catches it: changelog.d/README.md states `basicly release` folds every fragment into `## [Unreleased]` and deletes it in the same commit, no gate in basicly.toml reads changelog.d, and docs-claims passes clean right now (uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check → "4 generated blocks current, 5 assertions current", exit 0) while scanning only targets/, skills/, tests/ and src/ globs. Confidence: high on the fact — I read the schema JSON directly. Confidence: high that it publishes unless the fragment is edited before the tag. This finding is NOT about the rn0o.11 diff, which is correct; it is a stale sibling fragment that this release carries. It does not imply any other fragment is wrong — I checked only this one against code.

unsupported.claim: The section-by-section ruling itself — the entire user-visible behaviour change in basicly-rn0o.11, including the new exit code 3.
unsupported.why: There is no changelog.d/basicly-rn0o.11.*.md fragment (ls changelog.d/ shows 31 fragments plus README.md; the only rn0o entry is basicly-rn0o.1.added.md). Under changelog.d/README.md the release assembles only what is in the directory, so a consumer will read the old fragment's description of the contract and nothing about the change that altered it. A caller wrapping `basicly board validate` in a shell will meet exit code 3 with no released note announcing it. This is an omission rather than a false claim; confidence: high, it is a directory listing. It is NOT a defect in the code and NOT a reason to hold the merge — only a reason to write the fragment before the tag.

unsupported.claim: changelog.d/basicly-rn0o.1.added.md:3, "a `board-schema` entry in the verify pipeline checks it on every run", read by a consumer as "emit a conforming snapshot ... and have it checked".
unsupported.why: Narrower than it reads. The gate exists and binds (basicly.toml:402), but its command validates one checked-in fixture, tests/fixtures/board/minimal-v1.json — it exercises no producer output. basicly-rn0o.13, the open dependent of this record, states the gate's own comment concedes it "proves nothing about a snapshot the engine produced, because no producer exists yet". The consumer-facing checking mechanism is `basicly board validate` run by the consumer, which does work; the pipeline entry is a contract-rot guard, not coverage of anyone's snapshot. Confidence: high that the gate runs only minimal-v1; medium that a consumer misreads the sentence. Recommend narrowing the wording, not deleting it.

unsupported.claim: Implicit in "permitted values may never be widened within a major": that v1 changed only by widening.
unsupported.why: `asks[].actions` was retyped, not widened — from an array of strings to an array of objects. Probe: taking full-v1.json and restoring the pre-diff value `"actions": ["checkpoint-approve"]` now yields "invalid $.asks[0].actions[0]: 'checkpoint-approve' is not of type 'object'", withheld asks, exit 3. That is a narrowing, which the stated rule does not license. It is harmless here and the harmlessness is evidenced — the schema is absent from the v0.9.0 tag, so no released consumer holds the string form — but the release note should say the shape changed rather than leaving "widened" to cover it. Confidence: high on the probe, which I ran. This is NOT a compatibility break against any shipped consumer, and NOT an argument to revert; it is a wording gap on a consumer surface.

payload.description:
## The defect

The gate failure ledger detected a real special cause and the analysis produced for it was refused as malformed, so the signal was found and then lost.

Observed verbatim during a landing on 2026-08-19:

```
retrospective fired (beyond-limits on basicly-vkh0.26): basicly-vkh0.26 carries 3 gate
failures, beyond the upper control limit: 3 failures on one unit is one special cause,
not 3 common ones [147 units, centre 0.21, sigma 0.46, upper limit 1.59]; outcome:
refused: no control is named; tier is not one of control, warning, documentation; no
class of defects is named
```

**The detection half is correct and should not be touched.** It computed a centre of 0.21 and a sigma of 0.46 over 147 units, put the upper limit at 1.59, and correctly refused to treat three failures on one unit as three common causes. That is the instrument working.

**The producing half has no contract enforced where it is written.** The retrospector is required to name a control, a tier drawn from a closed three member set, and a class of defects the control covers. It returned none of the three. The refusal is correct and it is also terminal: the special cause is consumed, the analysis is discarded, and no record carries what was learned.

So a rare and valuable signal, one point beyond three sigma across 147 units, produces nothing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Find a unit carrying gate failures beyond the computed upper control limit.
2. Advance a lane so the retrospective fires on it.
3. Read the outcome. Observe the analysis refused for a missing control, a tier outside the closed set, and a missing defect class.
4. Search the tracker for a record carrying the analysis. Observe none.
5. Observe the special cause is not re-offered on a later advance.

Observed: the detector fires, the analysis is refused, and the signal is neither recorded nor retried.
Expected: a refused analysis is either retried against the same signal, or recorded as a refused attempt naming what was missing, so the special cause is not silently spent.

## Two fixes, and they are separable

The narrow one: the role prompt states the three required parts, and the reply is validated before the signal is marked consumed.

The one that matters more: **a refused analysis must not consume the signal.** A special cause beyond three sigma is rare, so spending one on a malformed reply is the expensive half.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a special cause when the analysis it produces is refused then the signal remains unconsumed and is re-offered.
- Given a refused analysis when the refusal is recorded then a tracker record carries the attempt and what was missing from it.
- Given the retrospector reply when it names no control or a tier outside the closed set then the refusal names each missing part, as it already does.
- Given a well formed analysis when it is produced then the signal is consumed exactly once.
- Given the detection arithmetic then it is unchanged, and a test pins the centre and sigma and limit it computes for a known failure set.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/retrospective.py`
- `.basicly/core/agents/retrospector/agent.yaml`
- `tests/test_retrospective.py`

## Context

Plan §4 Phase 0. Depends on nothing. Size 2-3 sessions.

The 2026-07-26 dogfood met its acceptance criterion but needed one human intervention, caused by two defects that interact. - A supervised multi-lane pass on real work completes with zero human interventions attributable to a harness defect, as opposed to a checkpoint the autonomy level requires. `basicly-u6jq.1` is that run; it closes on a record naming every intervention it did need and why each was policy rather than a defect.
- `tracker-path-scan` reports no absolute path, OS username or drive letter over the committed ledger and the committed export, against a positive control that reports a planted one. This record measured 365 of 366 records leaking at c175c1a on 2026-07-26; `basicly-vkh0`'s 2026-08-15 note records 4,812 of 5,081 events rewritten and 0 findings after.
- An answered escalation clears the rework counter and a flaky gate does not spend a lane's rework budget - `basicly-4tjt` and `basicly-55yh`, both closed - each with a test that fails when the mechanism is disabled.
- A pass is admitted against the same number provisioning spends: `basicly-u6jq.3` closes when the forecast reads the room rather than the cap, so no fundable pass is refused.

## Context

Plan §4 Phase 1. Depends on Phase 0 for 1b and 1c. Size 3-4 sessions.

Three assumptions carry large downstream work and each has a cheap test; at least one could cancel a whole phase. 1a (recall) is independent and can run first. 1b (7bur, cost per landed package) is the hub - the design documents defer four further decisions to it, and kjc5.29 must land first so tier economics are not measured against an unpinned model mapping. 1c (localisation) must precede Phase 5 because it changes what the decomposer scope declarations have to carry.

- Each of the three Phase 1 measurements carries a number, its method and its date on the record that owns it, and the document that consumes it cites that record rather than restating an estimate: recall against a no-guidance control (`basicly-agzx.1`, closed), localisation effect on pre-first-edit tokens (`basicly-agzx.2`), conditional-relevance effect on adherence (`basicly-agzx.3`).

## Context

Owner, 2026-08-01: **"If you need to go search your memory to run basicly correctly, we are doing
it wrong."** A consumer who installs basicly inherits the engine, the projected instructions, the
skills and the hooks — and none of an operator's accumulated recollection. So any knowledge required
to run basicly correctly that lives only in an agent's private memory is an undocumented runtime
dependency, and the consumer hits the failure the operator learned to avoid.

Externalize in this priority order, owner-specified:

1. **Deterministic** -> a script, a command, or a gate. The engine answers it; nobody recalls it.
2. **Semi-deterministic** -> a script plus a skill (the skill carries the judgment and references
   the script).
3. **Non-deterministic** -> instructions and skills.

## Audit, 2026-08-01

An operator memory of 58 entries was classified against what the repo actually enforces. Three
groups came out.

**Group A - required to run basicly, NOT externalized.** These are the defects.

- The **supervised-run runbook** does not exist in the catalog. `loop supervise` appears only in
  `docs/design/factory-design.md` and `docs/architecture/architecture.md` (which describe the
  system, not how to drive it) and in the `harness-client` skill (which is about attaching as a
  second observer). The `harness-loop` skill, 271 lines, barely mentions supervise, grants or
  budget. Everything about starting a run - mint a grant, size the budget from measured cost, check
  the base is clean, know which runner will meter spend - was operator memory.
- **`FORCE_COLOR` breaks the piped-output test: zero mentions anywhere in the repo.** Pure memory.
- Budget sizing from measured per-lane cost: the numbers exist in run records, but nothing reads
  them and says "a 5-lane pass needs about this much".
- `br` read patterns: `br list --json` caps at ~50 and drops closed rows, so a whole-tracker
  question must read `.beads/issues.jsonl`. A zero-finding audit was silently wrong once because of
  this.
- The tracker export re-adds `source_repo_path` on every write, so a scrub is required before
  staging. Loop landings scrub automatically; an out-of-loop write does not, and the operator
  remembers.

**Group B - required, and ALREADY externalized.** The memory entry is redundant history, which is
fine and needs no work: the loop landing guards (`4psl`, `9niw`, `o0q3`), the commit-message rules
(the `commit-msg` and `beads-commit-msg` hooks plus `basicly commit`), the lint rules (ruff,
markdownlint), the deny-list, `--all-default-roots`.

**Group C - not about running basicly.** Agent working discipline and project state: verification
habits, session history, measurements, Claude-Code-specific facts. These legitimately stay in an
agent's memory or a handover, and are out of scope here.

## Scope

Children, one per tier. Filed separately so each can be prioritized on its own.

- **Tier 1, done in this session**: `basicly-f3mi` (projected Claude hooks used a relative script
  path, so every consumer's hook broke outside the repo root - the exact defect an operator was
  papering over with a "never use a bare cd" note) and `basicly loop preflight <root>`, a read-only
  command that answers the whole pre-run checklist and exits non-zero when a run would be blocked.
- **Tier 1, remaining**: environment preconditions the engine should assert rather than an operator
  recall - `FORCE_COLOR`, the node resolution that differs in non-interactive shells, and an
  automatic export scrub on the out-of-loop `br` write path.
- **Tier 2**: a `harness-supervise` runbook skill (or a `harness-loop` section) that carries the
  judgment around a run and points at `loop preflight` for the facts.
- **Tier 3**: fold the verification-discipline rules into `test-discipline` and `harness-loop`.

## Measuring it

`.scripts/recall_eval.py` already measures whether an agent recalls the always-on baseline **with
every file read denied**, which is the right shape for this question: can an agent operate correctly
from what the repo projects and nothing else? Extending it to cover the operational runbook, rather
than only the always-on rules, is how this epic gets a number instead of an opinion.

## Success Criteria

- An agent can drive a supervised run with file reads denied: every fact the run needs comes from `basicly loop preflight <root>`, a projected skill, or the always-on instructions, and the preflight exits non-zero when a run would be blocked.
- `.scripts/recall_eval.py` is extended from the always-on rules to the operational runbook and returns a number for that question, so this epic closes on a measurement rather than on a judgment about coverage.
- Each Group A entry is discharged or retired with a recorded reason: the supervise runbook (`basicly-xxom`), `FORCE_COLOR` (now named in `src/basicly/checkout.py` and `tests/conftest.py`, checked 2026-08-19), budget sizing from measured per-lane cost, and the out-of-loop export scrub (`basicly-4ovq`).
- The two `br` read-pattern entries in Group A - the `--json` cap and reading `.beads/issues.jsonl` - are retired by the store change rather than externalized. `.beads/` is absent from the tree and `TRACKER_MODES` is `("owned",)` (checked 2026-08-19), so closing them means recording the retirement, not writing a skill.
- No Group A entry is discharged by prose where a command or a gate could answer it, per the owner's tier order in this description.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a fresh consumer repo with basicly installed and no operator memory when an agent is asked
  to drive a supervised run then every fact it needs is available from a command, a skill or the
  projected instructions, and no step depends on knowledge that exists only in an agent's private
  memory

## Goal

An interactive web page anyone can run locally that visualises what the harness is doing: the work
tracker and its backlog, the factory while it runs, lane state, gates, spend and health. The target
is a wall display in an engineering room, full screen, so everyone sees what is happening and can
step in.

**The reusable part is the contract, not the page.** `harness-board/v1` is designed so any harness can
emit it, which is why unit A is L3 and comes first.

## The design

The full solution design is `01-solution-design.md` on this epic's own harness branch, per D33: no new
requirement or plan document is ever created under `docs/`. It carries the six D17 sections, the
contract, this decomposition, the library and licence findings, and the open questions. Read it before
working any child - the bead bodies are the plan gate's view of it, not a replacement for it.

## The argument, and the correction inside it

The framing this was commissioned under was that a wall display attacks the rendezvous cost
`factory-loop.md` section 7.4 measured. **That framing was partly refuted by its own author.** The
design replicated section 7.4 on today's ledger (n=154, 44.4 h, 83% in 19 tail events, replicating the
recorded 85%/17) and added the axis section 7.4 lacked - *when the engine asked*, in local wall clock.

```text
asked during plausible in-room hours    4 events   14,527 s   9% of all human wait
asked out of hours                                            74%
the 17% head                            60 s median, no display beats it
```

So the arrival mechanism is real and its ceiling is about 4 hours of 44.4, at n=4. Section 7.4 had
already said it: *"eight hours asleep, eighty-one seconds awake."*

**What carries the project instead is unwatched spend.** $953.82 over 357 dispatches, a $24.64
single-dispatch maximum, 1.25B tokens, 12 `[harness-overrun]` markers, and
`loop session basicly-kjc5 --json` reporting `spent_tokens 177,970,761` against
`token_budget 4,000,000` - in a JSON surface nobody watches, behind a command that costs 11 seconds
to run. **That figure is unclassified**: it is either an unenforced ceiling or a scope mismatch
between a per-grant budget and a lifetime total, and `basicly-e2mz.13` settles it. A board built over
an unclassified number is observability over a possibly-broken control, so that probe gates unit C.

## Owner decisions taken 2026-08-14

1. **Phased.** Ship A, B, C and G only, then run four weeks against the real factory before deciding
   D, E and F. Roughly 470,000 tokens, zero long-lived processes, and it satisfies
   `work-tracker.md` requirement 10 exactly as recorded.
2. **Requirement 10 is amended, not overridden.** It stays as written; one sentence permits a
   live-attached mode that must display its own age and must never use the words "real time".
   `basicly-e2mz.14` carries the edit.
3. **Unit H is deferred.** It is the only part touching a surface v1.0.0 freezes, and a passive wall
   would close OQ-15 falsely by rendering every checkpoint instantly.

## Success Criteria

- A producer exists. `basicly board --help` lists `validate` only (checked 2026-08-19), so the consumer half is built and nothing emits a snapshot; the criterion is a `harness-board/v1` document produced from files with no subprocess (`basicly-rn0o.2`) that `basicly board validate` accepts, plus the supervisor-tick emission (`basicly-rn0o.7`).
- Units A, B, C and G land with no long-lived process: the board is a single on-demand HTML artifact, and `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` requirement 10 holds as recorded with the one-sentence live-attached amendment (`basicly-e2mz.14`) rather than an override.
- No rendered value appears without its age. There is no code path that renders a value without its freshness, proven by a test over the renderer, and the words "real time" appear nowhere in the output.
- A snapshot carrying only `meta` renders and names every absent section instead of failing, per-section rather than per-document (`basicly-rn0o.11`, closed).
- The spend figure this epic was argued from is classified before unit C ships: `loop session basicly-kjc5 --json` reporting `spent_tokens 177,970,761` against `token_budget 4,000,000` is settled by `basicly-e2mz.13` as either an unenforced ceiling or a per-grant-versus-lifetime scope mismatch. A board over an unclassified control is observability over a possibly-broken one.
- The D, E and F decision is taken on four weeks of recorded use against the real factory - view events from `basicly-rn0o.8` - and not on the n=4 in-hours arrival figure this design already refuted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a foreign harness that emits only `meta`, when the board renders it, then it renders what is
  present and names every absent section rather than failing.
- Given any snapshot, when a value is displayed, then its age is displayed with it - there is no code
  path that renders a value without its freshness.
- Given the phased scope, when A, B, C and G have landed, then no long-lived process exists and
  requirement 10 holds as recorded.
- Given the four-week trial, when it ends, then the decision on D, E and F rests on recorded use
  rather than on the n=4 arrival assumption.

## Context

Opened 2026-07-25 on the owner's direction. The tracker is not a peripheral integration - it is the harness's state. br is the single source of truth for every phase derivation, gate, checkpoint, dependency edge, decision item and run record, and the engine deliberately keeps no side-state, so every guarantee the harness makes is downstream of it. That dependency is unowned: beads_rust and bv are MIT and excellent today, but licenses change, maintainers move on, and a breaking change upstream lands in our critical path. We already carry a version floor and version-specific workarounds.

Design doc: docs/work-tracker.md, opened as an initialization rather than a build plan. The tractable part is that the harness's tracker surface is narrow and enumerable - roughly twenty subcommands - so this is not rebuilding a general-purpose issue tracker. Telemetry comes first: no schema is designed from memory of our own usage.

## Success Criteria

- No process the engine starts spawns an external tracker binary, and the mode set names exactly one mode: `src/basicly/owned_store.py` has `TRACKER_MODES = (MODE_OWNED,)` and `src/basicly/tracker.py` re-exports it (checked 2026-08-19). Owner clarification 2026-08-13 (`basicly-ctdz`): the criterion is absence from the runtime path, not deletion of `br`/`bv` support, which other projects use.
- A fresh consumer repository installs basicly and drives a record to shipped with no external binary on `PATH`. `basicly-vkh0.49` (the terminal repository) is that test and `basicly-vkh0.48` is the same proof for the development workspace; neither has run, so this epic's acceptance is unmet whatever the child count says. 47 of 60 children are closed as of 2026-08-19.
- The ledger is the only store: `.beads/` is absent from `main` (checked 2026-08-19), and the kit's own entry point - `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py` with `fsck` and `rebuild` - reproduces the fold from the log with no basicly import and nothing on `PATH`.
- A write reports its own outcome truthfully. `basicly-vkh0.50` is open - the write seam prints `recorded:` and exits 0 whether or not the write landed - so until it closes, no criterion on this epic may be verified from that line; the field is read back instead.
- The store can remove a record and cannot silently lose one: `basicly-vkh0.34` (neither store can remove a record), `basicly-b2n2` (a stale auto-flush deletes committed records) and `basicly-dx2ngn` (the shrink guard is inert on the rebuild path) each close with a test that fails when the guard is made inert.
- The surface list is frozen on a current usage sample rather than the 2026-07 one (`basicly-vkh0.47`). The shadow differential that justified the flip left with the external half, so the flip's evidence is the record it wrote, not a command anyone can re-run - any further claim about store agreement needs a new instrument, named on the child that makes it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a full factory session including a supervised multi-lane run when its telemetry is reviewed then docs/work-tracker.md carries a frozen surface list a ledger schema a cache decision and a component breakdown, and a differential test shows the owned tracker answering phase derivation ready set and gate status identically to the external one across the tracker whole history

## Scope

- `docs/work-tracker.md`

## Context

Removing the external binary from the engine is basicly-wpc8 and basicly-vkh0.29. This epic is the other half nobody had filed: every harness surface that still names the binary or its directory, and the deletion of that directory at the end.

The inventory was taken 2026-08-17 with a probe that excludes the mermaid line-break noise a naive word search picks up, `(^|[^a-z<-])br [a-z][a-z-]+`, over tracked files only. Counts of real invocations: the catalog sources 127 in 13 files, the projected skills 96 in 5 files, the documents 32 in 8 files, the config 7 in 1, the scripts 6 in 2, the workflows 1 in 1.

## The one that must move first

The commit gate does **not** spawn the binary. `.basicly/core/hooks/beads-commit-msg.py` validates the trailing id against `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is a file read. So the gate depends on the export file rather than the binary, and if the directory is deleted before the gate is repointed, every commit in this repository fails. That is child 1, and the deletion child blocks on it.

## What is deliberately not here

- The config, `basicly.toml`. It is inside basicly-vkh0.29's declared scope, and two beads declaring one file is a contention the plan gate should never be handed.
- `src/basicly/worktree.py` and the `.beads/redirect` filename. Architecture section 37.2 records that the filename is the binary's and changes at the flip, and that module is inside basicly-wpc8's scope.
- `br.PINNED_VERSION`. It leaves with `br.py` itself.
- The nine records with no body in the owned ledger. That is basicly-vkh0.41, and it is a precondition of the deletion rather than a surface.

## Sizing, measured

Four children are lane-sized and three are below the working-set band floor of 8000, which by basicly-esxp's rule makes them session work rather than a lane: the commit gate at 4152, the workflows at 5523, the deletion at 5019. Sized with `read_cost.scope_read_cost` times the task factor of 3.

## Order

Children 1 to 6 are independent of each other. The deletion is last and blocks on all of them, on basicly-vkh0.41 and on basicly-vkh0.29.

## Success Criteria

- The purge this epic was named for is discharged. Checked 2026-08-19: `.beads/` is absent from the tree, `src/basicly/owned_store.py` has `TRACKER_MODES = (MODE_OWNED,)`, and eleven of fifteen children are closed including the deletion child (`basicly-vkh0.42.7`) and every surface child. The four open children are the requirements-folder work, which is a new gate and two deletions rather than a purge.
- No surface a user reads names a command from the retired binary. Not yet true: `src/basicly/cli.py` prints `cover each: br dep add <root> <id> -t blocks` from `basicly loop preflight`, and six `--help` descriptions in the same module still say "a br gate", "child br issues", "br work type" and "pure read over br" (checked 2026-08-19). The criterion is zero occurrences in printed strings and in `--help` text, under a probe that separates those populations from docstring prose - 122 residue hits across `src/` and `.basicly/core/` under `(^|[^a-z<-])br [a-z][a-z-]+` are overwhelmingly prose, so a raw count is not the instrument.
- The requirements folder has one identifiable form with a gate that refuses a document outside it (`basicly-vkh0.42.12`), and `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` and `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` are absorbed into `docs/architecture/architecture.md` and deleted (`basicly-1hp91f`, `basicly-vkh0.42.6`, `basicly-vkh0.42.13`).
- Every citation of a deleted requirements document resolves after the absorption, and the two gates that read those documents - repointed by `basicly-vkh0.42.8`, closed - stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a clean checkout of `main` when a probe for real invocations of the retired binary runs over tracked files, with a positive control that reports a planted occurrence, then no occurrence sits in a string the engine prints or in a `--help` description, and every survivor is docstring prose or a historical tracker record.
- Given `docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` and `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` when they are absorbed and deleted then every surviving citation of them resolves, the requirements-folder gate passes on a deliberately malformed document, and `uv run basicly verify --mode full` is green.
- Given a commit in this repository when the commit-msg gate validates the trailing record id then it reads the owned ledger and no external export file, so deleting the export cannot fail a commit (`basicly-vkh0.42.1`, closed).

## The defect

`basicly loop preflight` prints a remediation line instructing the operator to run a command that cannot run. `src/basicly/cli.py` line 2931:

```
print(f"           cover each: br dep add {state.root_issue} <id> -t blocks")
```

The binary is gone from every checkout, so this is a consumer facing instruction that fails whoever follows it. Five more surfaces carry the same name in text a consumer reads, all in the same module: the verify help at 4402 and 4415, the decompose help at 4462, the scaffold help at 4535, the classify help at 4651.

`basicly-e2mz.44` is closed and covered a different thing, the seam **argument grammar** that a human types. This is the engine printing the retired name back at the operator.

## The population, and why a raw count is the wrong instrument

A search for the binary name across the engine and the catalog returns 122 hits and **the overwhelming majority are docstring prose**, which is history and correctly left alone. Only text a consumer reads is a defect: a printed line, a help string, an error message. Split the population before editing, name the expected count per population, and reconcile after. A sweep that treated 122 as a defect count is how a previous removal left four false user facing messages in the tree.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `basicly loop preflight` on a root whose blockers are not all covered, so the remediation branch is reached.
2. Read the printed line. Observe it instructs a `dep add` through the retired binary.
3. Run that instruction. Observe the binary is not on PATH.
4. Run `basicly loop preflight --help`, `basicly verify --help`, `basicly decompose --help`, `basicly policy scaffold --help` and `basicly loop run --help`. Observe five help strings naming the binary.
5. Positive control for the population split: the same search finds the name in docstrings, and those are history rather than defects, so a raw count over the tree does not answer this.

Observed: the engine prints an instruction naming a tool no checkout has, and five help strings do the same.
Expected: text a consumer reads names a command the consumer can run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the preflight remediation branch when it prints then the instruction names a command that exists on the current checkout.
- Given every help string in the command line surface when it is read then none names the retired binary.
- Given a docstring naming the binary as history when the sweep runs then it is left alone, and the record states how many were left and why.
- Given the counts when the work completes then the expected and actual count per population agree, and the record states both.
- Given a gate for this when it runs then it binds on printed and help text rather than on a raw tree search, because a raw search cannot tell prose from a message.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli.py`

## The defect

`basicly tracker show` reports the same parent-child edge more than once. Measured on `basicly-vkh0`: **65 parent-child rows for 60 unique record ids**, with five ids appearing twice: `basicly-vkh0.25`, `.26`, `.27`, `.28`, `.29`.

So any count read off that surface is inflated, and the inflation is silent. A child count is exactly the kind of number a reader takes at face value: it decides whether an epic looks nearly done, and it feeds a human judgment about whether to close one.

The five duplicated ids are consecutive, which suggests one batch of edge writes was recorded twice rather than five independent accidents. The fold applies each edge event it reads; nothing deduplicates an edge by its endpoints and type.

## Why the append only log is not the problem

The log correctly holds every event it was given. The defect is in the **derived view**: an edge is a relation, so folding two identical edge events must yield one edge. `events.append` already skips a draft whose content derived id is present, so an exact replay is idempotent; what is not deduplicated is two edge events that state the same relation while differing in some other field, for example a provenance label or a timestamp.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `basicly tracker show basicly-vkh0`.
2. Collect the dependents whose type is parent-child and count the rows, then count the distinct ids.
3. Observe 65 rows against 60 distinct ids.
4. Observe the five repeated ids are consecutive.
5. Read the edge events for one repeated id in the ledger and compare their payloads, to establish which field differs.
6. Positive control: do the same on a record with no repeats and observe rows equal distinct ids, so the probe discriminates.

Observed: the derived edge set contains a duplicate relation, and a count taken from it overstates the child set by five.
Expected: two events stating the same relation fold to one edge, and a count off the view equals the count of distinct relations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given two edge events stating the same source and target and type when the fold runs then the derived view holds one edge.
- Given two such events differing in provenance when they fold then the surviving edge carries the stronger provenance label and the weaker one is not a second row.
- Given the committed ledger when the fold runs then the parent-child row count for every record equals its distinct target count.
- Given the fold before and after the fix when it runs over the committed log then no record loses an edge it previously had.
- Given a record with no duplicate when the fix lands then its view is byte identical to before.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/provenance.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py`

## Context

`loop preflight` forecasts a pass at `per_lane x min(concurrency, open_children)`.
Provisioning does not use `concurrency`; `loop._ensure_child_worktrees` computes
`room = wt_config.concurrency - len(existing)` and seeds at most that many. So the
forecast over-states by exactly the number of worktrees already live.

Measured 2026-08-16 on `basicly-e2mz`, with 2 live worktrees and `concurrency = 5`:

```
worktrees: 2 live
forecast:  ~110949235 tokens if all 5 lanes start (per-lane x min(cap 5, 39 open))
```

The pass can seed 3 lanes, not 5. The honest forecast is ~66,569,541.

## Why the size of the error matters rather than the error

The figure exists to size a grant. An operator reading 110,949,235 against a
100,000,000 grant concludes the pass cannot run and either mints a larger grant than
the work needs or does not run it. Both were nearly done here. `admit_pass_spend`
totals the pass and refuses the whole thing on one violation, so the number a human
compares against the grant is the number that decides whether anything is dispatched
at all.

The preflight's own docstring states the intent — "the interesting number is what a
*full* fan-out would need, because that is what a budget has to be minted for" — and a
full fan-out is bounded by room, not by the cap.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the cap and count the worktrees already live:

       rg -n '^concurrency' basicly.toml
       git worktree list

2. Read the two expressions that have to agree, and observe that they do not.
   `cli._print_preflight_spend` prices `priced = min(cap, open_count)` on the line it
   prints as `forecast:`; provisioning computes `room = wt_config.concurrency -
   len(existing)` in `loop._ensure_child_worktrees`. Nothing subtracts `len(existing)`
   on the forecast path.
3. Run the forecast on a root with open children but no dispatchable lane - that is the
   only branch which prints it, because `_print_preflight_spend` returns early as soon as
   `supervise.ready_lanes` is non-empty:

       uv run basicly loop preflight <root>

4. Read the `forecast:` line, then multiply its `per-lane:` figure by the room from step 1
   by hand and compare.

Observed - this record's own measurement, 2026-08-16 on `basicly-e2mz` with 2 live
worktrees and `concurrency = 5`:

    worktrees: 2 live
    forecast:  ~110949235 tokens if all 5 lanes start (per-lane x min(cap 5, 39 open))

The pass could seed 3 lanes; the honest figure was ~66,569,541. Re-checked in this checkout
2026-08-19: `git worktree list` shows **4** lane worktrees against `concurrency = 5`, so
room is 1 while the forecast would still price 5 - the inputs have made the error larger,
not smaller.

Expected: the forecast prices the room provisioning would use, and its parenthetical names
room rather than the raw cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given live worktrees exist when the preflight forecasts a pass then the lane count
  is the room provisioning would use rather than the raw cap - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`
- Given no live worktrees then the forecast is unchanged - check:
  `uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_cli_loop.py -k forecast_room -q`

```text
contention.py:61   path not in scopes.get(lane, ())     literal string membership
merge.py:942       merge._scope_covers                  decompose.globs_overlap
```

So a lane that declares `docs/**` or `*.md` covers a configured append-only `CHANGELOG.md` at the landing, and the preflight counts it as a lane that contends without declaring.

## Why it matters despite being advisory

Nothing refuses on this surface. The cost is a false `contend:` line. This repository records that an advisory `contend:` line is a finding an operator acts on: one such line named the exact collision under a green verdict and four hand-resolved rebases followed. A false one spends the same attention.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the two scope tests side by side:

       rg -n 'path not in scopes.get' src/basicly/contention.py
       rg -n -A8 'def _scope_covers' src/basicly/merge.py

   `contention.append_only_report` asks `path not in scopes.get(lane, ())` - literal string
   membership against the lane's declared entries. `merge._scope_covers` asks
   `decompose.globs_overlap(path, glob)`. A lane declaring `docs/**` or `*.md` satisfies the
   second and fails the first.
2. Note the report is inert on this repo as configured, so the case has to supply a path:

       rg -n '^append_only_paths' basicly.toml

   Observed 2026-08-19: `append_only_paths = []`, and `append_only_report` returns its
   "no append-only path declared" line for an empty list before it reaches the membership
   test. So the reproduction belongs in `tests/test_contention.py` against a fixture repo
   that configures `append_only_paths = ["CHANGELOG.md"]`, not against this checkout.
3. In that fixture, give two lanes a `## Scope`: one declaring the glob `*.md` on its own
   backticked line, one declaring nothing that covers `CHANGELOG.md`. Call
   `contention.append_only_report` with both lanes.

Observed: both lanes appear in the `... lane(s) will each append to `CHANGELOG.md` and none
declares it` line, so the report names a lane that did declare it and the operator reads a
`contend:` line that is false.

"A lane that *declares* the path in its own `## Scope` is left out of the count" - so this is
the docstring's rule failing on a glob, not a behaviour change.

- When a lane declares a scope glob that covers a configured append-only path, then the preflight report does not count that lane as contending.
- When no lane declares coverage, then the report is unchanged.

## Context

`docs/requirements/factory-loop.md` records, as a measured finding dated 2026-08-09,
that agent definitions hot-reload and are not read once at process start, with two
named exceptions. That claim does not hold for the path the engine and an operator
actually use.

Measured 2026-08-16. `.basicly/core/agents/architect/agent.yaml` gained `Write` and
`Edit`; `basicly agents-build` wrote `.claude/agents/architect.md` and
`.github/agents/architect.agent.md`, and the projected frontmatter carries
`tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit`. A dispatch immediately afterwards
reported its live tool list as `Read, Bash` and refused the task it had been given.

## Why this matters beyond one dispatch

The catalog is the source and the projection is the delivery, so a projection that a
running host ignores makes every roster change invisible until a restart nobody
schedules. It is also the second instance of the shape this repo keeps paying for: a
capability asserted in a document, believed, and never probed.

## What is not established

Whether the stale registry is the host's or this harness's, and whether the
2026-08-09 measurement was wrong then or is stale now - it pinned no version, which
is the same defect `basicly-wbsz.3` was filed for.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a session that is already running, change a projected agent's capability at the
   catalog source - for example add `Write` and `Edit` to the `tools` of
   `.basicly/core/agents/architect/agent.yaml`.
2. Project it and confirm the projection landed:

       uv run basicly agents-build
       rg -n '^tools:' .claude/agents/architect.md .github/agents/architect.agent.md

3. Without restarting the host process, dispatch that role and ask it to report its own
   tool list and to perform an edit.
4. Compare the live tool list against the frontmatter from step 2.
5. Probe the harness for any code that notices the difference:

       rg -n 'stale_registry' tests/test_roles.py
       rg -n 'def ' src/basicly/roles.py

Observed - this record's measurement 2026-08-16: step 2's frontmatter read
`tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit`, and the dispatch in step 3 reported its live
tool list as `Read, Bash` and refused the task it had been given. Step 5's first command
returns nothing; **its positive control is the second command**, which lists six functions
in `roles.py` (`role_for_phase`, `lens_dispatches`, `role_is_available`, `resolve_role`,
`resolve_named_role`) - so `roles.py` is readable and the module simply carries no
registry-freshness check. Re-checked 2026-08-19: `rg -c 'def test_' tests/test_roles.py`
returns 17 tests and none of them matches `stale_registry`, so the gap is an absence rather
than a bad probe, and the projected frontmatter still reads
`tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit`.

Expected: either the dispatch carries the definition that is on disk at dispatch time, or
the harness reports that it cannot and names the process boundary as the reason - a roster
change must not be silently invisible.

- Given a projected agent definition changed after a session started when a dispatch

## Context

`pre-commit` snapshots the working tree before each hook and compares it after. A file
that changed during a hook is reported as **modified by that hook**. A concurrent
writer is indistinguishable from a hook write, so the blame lands on whichever hook was
running when the write arrived.

Measured 2026-08-16. Three commits in a row failed with
`catalog-lint: files were modified by this hook`, while `catalog lint: OK` printed in
the same output. A whole-tree probe cleared the command:

```
git ls-files -z | xargs -0 md5sum | sort > before
uv run basicly catalog lint
git ls-files -z | xargs -0 md5sum | sort > after
diff before after   ->  no output
```

The real writer was a background agent editing `docs/architecture/architecture.md`.
Its diff went from 416 to 528 insertions between the second and third attempts, so it
wrote inside the commit window. An hour went into the wrong hook.

## Why the framework cannot answer this and we can

`pre-commit` has no way to tell a hook's write from anybody else's, and it is not ours
to change. `basicly commit` already wraps `git commit`, so it is the one place that can
snapshot the tracked tree before the gate and compare after a failure. A file that
changed but is touched by no hook is a concurrent modification, and saying so turns an
hour of hunting into one line.

Post-hoc diagnosis on failure only. Not a refusal, and not a pre-flight heuristic on
file age - a human editing in another window is a false positive, and a gate that cries
wolf gets waived.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Stage a commit in this repo and start it through the wrapper:

       uv run basicly commit ...

2. While the gate is running, have a second process write to any tracked file the commit
   does not touch - for example append a line to `docs/architecture/architecture.md`.
3. Read the failure. `pre-commit` snapshots the tree before each hook and compares it
   after, so it reports `<hook-id>: files were modified by this hook` naming whichever hook
   happened to be running when the write arrived.
4. Clear the named hook by hand, which is the step that costs the time:

       git ls-files -z | xargs -0 md5sum | sort > before
       uv run basicly catalog lint
       git ls-files -z | xargs -0 md5sum | sort > after
       diff before after

5. Probe `basicly commit` for anything that would have said so:

       rg -n 'concurrent' src/basicly/commit.py tests/test_commit.py
       rg -c 'hook' src/basicly/commit.py

Observed - this record's measurement 2026-08-16: three commits in a row failed with
`catalog-lint: files were modified by this hook` while `catalog lint: OK` printed in the same
output, step 4's `diff` produced no output, and the real writer was a background agent whose
diff on `architecture.md` grew from 416 to 528 insertions between the second and third
attempts. An hour went into the wrong hook. Step 5, re-run 2026-08-19: the first command
returns nothing. **Its positive control is the second command**, which returns 15 `hook`
matches in a 586-line `commit.py`, and `grep -c 'def test_' tests/test_commit.py` returns 35
- both files exist and are searched, so the zero is an absence.

Expected: when a tracked file changed during a failing gate and no hook is configured to
touch it, `basicly commit` names that file as concurrently modified, post-hoc and on failure
only. When nothing changed, it says nothing about concurrency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a tracked file changes while the commit gate runs when the commit fails then
  the output names that file as concurrently modified rather than leaving the hook
  blamed - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_commit.py -k concurrent -q`
- Given no file changes during a failing gate then the output says nothing about
  concurrency - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_commit.py -k concurrent -q`

## Scope

- `src/basicly/commit.py`
- `tests/test_commit.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/commit.py`
- `tests/test_commit.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_commit.py -k concurrent -q`

## Context

`loop run` refuses to advance when the base checkout has **any** uncommitted change, including changes in files the incoming merge cannot touch. So one piece of unrelated work in progress blocks every lane landing, and the operator's only remedies are to commit work that is not ready or to discard it.

Observed 2026-08-17. basicly-wpc8.1 was green in its worktree — 4295 passed — and committed at 89a5436. The build-to-verify advance, which is the only step that merges, refused:

    base checkout has uncommitted changes; commit or stash first:
    M .basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py
    M src/basicly/cost_rollup.py
    ... 13 more, none of them in the lane's commit

Not one of the dirty paths appears in the lane's commit, so `git merge` itself would not have refused. The precondition is broader than the operation it protects.

## Why the broad form was chosen, and why it is still worth narrowing

The broad check is safe and cheap, and it prevents a class of confusion where a landing silently mixes an operator's work into a lane's merge. That reason is real. What it does not distinguish is dirt that **could** conflict from dirt that provably cannot.

The narrowing is checkable rather than judged: the merge's own file set is known before it runs, and so is the dirty set. Refuse on the intersection, on the engine tracker paths the advance itself commits, and on anything the rebase would regenerate. Admit the rest, and say in the advance detail which dirt was admitted, so nothing is silent.

## The operating cost this has today

Parallel work in the base checkout serialises against lane landings. An operator running several agents in one checkout - which is the obvious way to keep a backlog moving while a lane runs - discovers only at the landing that none of it may land until all of it is committed. The repo's own answer is a sibling worktree per unit of work, and that answer is right; the point here is that the precondition makes the failure appear at the worst moment rather than at the start.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take a lane green in its own worktree and committed on its harness branch.
2. Dirty one tracked file in the base checkout that the lane's commit does not touch - any
   file at all, since the check does not look at which:

       git -C <base> status --short

3. Run the advance that merges:

       uv run basicly loop advance <lane-id>

4. Read the refusal, then check the claim it rests on by intersecting the two sets by hand:

       git -C <base> diff --name-only
       git -C <base> log --format= --name-only <base-branch>..harness/<lane-id> | sort -u

5. Read the precondition itself:

       rg -n 'uncommitted changes; commit or stash first' src/basicly/merge.py

Observed - this record's measurement 2026-08-17 on `basicly-wpc8.1`, green at 4295 passed
and committed at 89a5436:

    base checkout has uncommitted changes; commit or stash first:
    M .basicly/core/kit/tracker/differential.py
    M src/basicly/cost_rollup.py
    ... 13 more, none of them in the lane's commit

Step 4's two lists had an empty intersection, so `git merge` itself would not have refused.
Step 5 confirms the refusal is unconditional on the dirty set: `merge.py` raises
`SystemExit` on any non-empty `dirty` with no reference to the incoming file set.

Expected: the advance refuses on the intersection of the dirty set with the merge's own file
set, plus the engine tracker paths the advance itself commits and anything the rebase
regenerates; it admits the rest and names in the advance detail which dirt it admitted, so
nothing is silent.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Context

The citation ratchet reports a stale `file:line` only when the cited line happens to be **blank or past end of file**. A citation that has drifted onto a different line of real code passes, and stays passing.

Measured 2026-08-17 on one block, `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` around line 124, which tabulates three call sites:

| Cited | Actually at | Off by | Gate said |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loop.py:869` `_run_agent` | 858 | 11 | passed |
| `loop.py:1119` `_run_proposer` | 1108 | 14 | **stale**, but only after an unrelated edit shifted it onto a blank line |
| `supervise.py:2651` `_dispatch_lane` | 2651 | 0 | passed, correctly |

Two of the three were wrong. The block was written 2026-08-15 in f8f6d34, so both survived two days and an unknown number of gate runs. The one the gate caught, it caught by luck: a three-line comment added elsewhere in `loop.py` pushed line 1119 onto a blank line.

## Why this is the worse failure mode

A citation pointing at nothing is an obvious defect. A citation pointing at the **wrong but existing** line reads as verified and is not — the same class the architecture rewrite hit, where three section references pointed at a real but wrong section. A reader who follows one lands on unrelated code and has no signal that the pointer, rather than their understanding, is what is wrong.

## What would fix it

The convention already exists and this repository states it: name the symbol, not the line. A symbol citation is checkable by search and survives every edit above it. The three entries above already name their symbol in the next column, which is why dropping the numbers cost nothing — that is the repair applied to the two stale ones in 1f3162b.

So the gate's own rule can be stronger: a `file:line` citation in a document is refusable on sight when the same entry names a symbol, and checkable against the symbol's definition line when it does not. What it must not do is treat a line's non-blankness as evidence.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the gate over the tree and read its summary line:

       uv run python .scripts/check_docs_citations.py

2. Take a `file:line` citation the gate just passed and resolve the symbol it names:

       rg -n '^def _dispatch_validation|^def _repair_in_place|^def _run_subtask' src/basicly/loop.py
       rg -n '^def _dispatch_lane' src/basicly/supervise.py

3. Read what actually sits at each cited line:

       sed -n '507p;1655p;1813p' src/basicly/loop.py
       sed -n '2651p' src/basicly/supervise.py

4. Read the staleness rule the gate applies:

       rg -n 'past end-of-file or a blank line' -B2 .scripts/check_docs_citations.py

Observed, measured 2026-08-19 against the block at `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` around
line 124. Step 1 printed:

    [docs-citations] 33 citation(s) in 17 document(s), 10 checkable against a named symbol,
    0 stale; no document is above its [tool.docs_citations.frozen] baseline

**That `0 stale` is the positive control as well as the defect** - the gate parsed 33
citations, so it is reading the documents; it simply reports none of these as stale:

| Cited | Symbol is at | Off by | The cited line actually holds | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loop.py:507` `_dispatch_validation` | 507 | 0 | the `def` | passed, correctly |
| `loop.py:1655` `_repair_in_place` | 1641 | 14 | `left where that dispatch reads it instead.` | **passed** |
| `loop.py:1813` `_run_subtask` | 1799 | 14 | `cwd = Path(session.worktree_path)` | **passed** |
| `supervise.py:2651` `_dispatch_lane` | 2626 | 25 | an f-string inside a different function | **passed** |

Three of the four are wrong and all three pass, because step 4 shows the only test is
`if at > len(lines) or not lines[at - 1].strip()` - non-blank and in range is treated as
evidence. A reader following `supervise.py:2651` lands 25 lines inside another function with
no signal that the pointer rather than their understanding is what is wrong.

Expected: a `file:line` citation whose entry also names a symbol is refused on sight, and one
that names no symbol is checked against the symbol's definition line. A line's
non-blankness is never accepted as evidence that the citation is live.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_docs_citations.py`
- `tests/test_check_docs_citations.py`

## Context

Found by the `basicly-e2mz.8` lane 2026-08-14 and confirmed by hand at main after the merge.

`cli.py:1808` hardcodes one reason for every path `agents.sync_agents` returns:

```text
cli.py:1808   print(f"Removed {...} (excluded by technology selection)")
cli.py:1693   the identical string on the skills path
```

`e2mz.8` gave `sync_agents` a second reason to remove a file - a projection whose catalog source was
deleted. The path printed is correct; the parenthetical is not. A consumer watching an upgrade is
told a technology selection removed the file when the source was deleted instead.

## Why this is not cosmetic

The two causes have different consequences for a reader. *Excluded by technology selection* means the
file will come back when the selection changes, so nothing is lost. *Orphaned* means the source is
gone and the artifact is retired. A consumer who reads the first and means the second will wait for a
return that never comes.

It is also the same defect class this session has now paid for three times: one string standing for
two facts. `basicly-9rv0` was two predicates that disagreed, `basicly-7jb5` was one gate name spelled
three times, and this is one message covering two causes.

## The skills path already had it

`cli.py:1693` prints the same string for resources `_prune_orphans` removed **because they left the
source**, so this is a pre-existing shape rather than one `e2mz.8` introduced. That matters for the
fix: correcting only the agents site would leave the skills site lying, which is how a defect class
survives its own bead.

`check_synced_agents` already returns `(path, reason)` pairs and words them correctly - the check half
is right and only the build half is wrong. The reason vocabulary therefore already exists; nothing
needs inventing.

## Steps to Reproduce

       rg -n 'excluded by technology selection' src/basicly/cli.py
       rg -n -A2 'def sync_agents' src/basicly/agents.py
       rg -n -A3 'def check_synced_agents' src/basicly/agents.py

2. In a scratch copy of a repo carrying projected agents, force the *technology* removal:
   record a selection that excludes one agent's technology and rebuild.

       uv run basicly install --technologies python
       uv run basicly agents-build

3. In a second scratch copy, force the *orphan* removal instead: leave the selection alone,
   delete the catalog source behind a projected agent, and rebuild.

       rm -r .basicly/core/agents/<name>
       uv run basicly agents-build

4. Read the `Removed ...` line each rebuild printed and compare the two parentheticals.
5. Repeat steps 2 and 3 against a skill and `uv run basicly skills-build`, which is the
   second site.
6. Run the check half over the same trees and compare its wording with the build half's:

       uv run basicly agents-check

`-> tuple[SyncResult, list[Path]]` - paths only, no reason - while `check_synced_agents` is
typed `-> list[tuple[Path, str]]` and words its reasons correctly already. Both build sites
hardcode the same string, `cmd_agents_build` at `src/basicly/cli.py:1858` (cited in this
record as `cli.py:1808`, since drifted) and `cmd_skills_build` at `src/basicly/cli.py:1743`
(cited as `cli.py:1693`). So step 4 prints `(excluded by technology selection)` in **both**
scratch copies, and it is true in only one of them.

file returns when the selection changes; *orphaned* means the source is gone and the artifact
is retired, and a consumer who reads the first while the second is true waits for a return
that never comes. The vocabulary already exists on `check_synced_agents`, so nothing needs
inventing - and `cli.py:1743` must be corrected in the same change, because fixing only the
agents site leaves the skills site lying.

- When `sync_skills` removes a resource, then the same holds on that path.

- `src/basicly/agents.py`
- `src/basicly/skills.py`
- `tests/test_agents.py`
- `tests/test_cli_catalog.py`

Install into two fresh scratch repos, deselect a technology in one and delete a source in the other,
upgrade both, and read the two lines. They must differ and each must be true. Read the output; do not

## The defect

Two halves, and the second is the one that is wrong rather than untidy.

**The cycle.** The board design has the producer read the supervisor lock file directly, and unit F has the supervisor write the snapshot on its tick. The supervisor is a band 2 driver, so the snapshot module must sit below it for unit F to import it, and above it to call the lock reader. That is a cycle, and the import contract declares itself **exhaustive**, with only two function level exemptions.

**The duplication.** The supervisor own lock reader carries a non-obvious invariant in its docstring: a corrupt payload still reports the heartbeat age, because **staleness is mtime only by design**, with the identity fields absent. A second reader written from the file format will very likely take the heartbeat from the payload timestamp instead of the file mtime. The two then disagree about whether a supervisor is alive, silently, and only when a supervisor crashes.

## The two shapes, and neither is obviously right

Either the lock info type and its reader move to a leaf module both bands may import, which is a real extraction along a nameable responsibility and touches a frozen module with 1503 tokens of headroom. Or the supervisor **injects** the holder into the snapshot producer, which is the pattern the kit already uses for redaction. The second makes the producer unable to answer the lock question on its own, so the on-demand mode must render not supervised rather than reading the lock, which is arguably more honest and matches the design own transcript.

The design must pick one and give the reason. This record does not pick for it.

## Steps to Reproduce

This is a defect in the design document, so it reproduces by reading three files against
each other rather than by running the product.

1. Read the design's lock requirement - the producer reading the supervisor lock directly:

       git show harness/basicly-rn0o:01-solution-design.md | rg -n 'supervisor lock'

   (the design lives on the epic's own harness branch per D33, not under `docs/`).
2. Read where the two modules would have to sit in the declared import stack:

       rg -n -A45 'contract:engine-layering' .importlinter

3. Read the reader the second one would duplicate, and the invariant in its docstring:

       rg -n -A6 'def read_holder' src/basicly/supervise.py

Observed, verified 2026-08-19 in this checkout:

- `.importlinter` puts `supervise` on the second tier from the top and `board_schema` far
  below it. The contract declares `exhaustive = True`, and `ignore_imports` carries exactly
  **two** function-level exemptions - `basicly.loop -> basicly.supervise` and
  `basicly.policy -> basicly.decisions`. So unit F's requirement (the supervisor writes the
  snapshot on its tick, which needs `supervise` to import the snapshot module) and the
  design's requirement (the snapshot module reads the supervisor lock, which needs the
  import back) cannot both hold, and there is no third exemption to hide in.
- `supervise.read_holder` documents the non-obvious half: "a corrupt payload still reports
  the heartbeat age (staleness is mtime-only by design), with the identity fields None."
  A second reader written from the file format takes the heartbeat from the payload's own
  timestamp instead of `path.stat().st_mtime`, and the two then disagree about whether a
  supervisor is alive - silently, and only once a supervisor has crashed.
- `src/basicly/board_schema.py` exists; no snapshot **producer** module does yet. So the
  cycle is still on paper and the fix is still a design edit rather than a refactor. The
  positive control for that absence is the same `ls src/basicly/ | rg -i board`, which does
  return `board_schema.py`.

Expected: the design names exactly one module that parses the supervisor lock, states the
import direction between the producer and the supervisor so `lint-imports` can prove it
acyclic, and says why the shape it did not choose was refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the revised design then exactly one module parses the supervisor lock and the design names it.
Given the snapshot producer and the supervisor then the declared import direction between them is acyclic and the import linter proves it.
Given a corrupt lock payload then the producer reports the mtime derived age with identity fields absent, matching the reader recorded invariant, asserted by a test rather than by inspection.
Given the chosen shape then the design states why the other was refused.
Demonstrated by: uv run lint-imports green, plus a test that the snapshot heartbeat age and the supervisor own reader agree on one fixture lock

## Scope

- `01-solution-design.md`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `.importlinter`

## Context

Second defect recorded on `basicly-jn1x`, **not fixed there** because its precondition is not met.

`runner.py` applies both flags on one argv: `_apply_role(spec, _apply_model(spec, ...), role)`.
Measured on the probe that filed `jn1x`: `--agent probeagent(model: haiku) --model sonnet` ran the
turn on **sonnet**, so `--model` overrides the model an agent definition declares.

The run record then reports `tier_honoured: true` for that shape, because the field means
something narrower than a reader assumes - `run_record.py` documents it as False "only when a tier
was asked for and the family could not pin one at all". A role whose declared tier was overridden
is not that case, so the record is not wrong by its own contract and is misleading against the
question a reader asks it.

## Why it is not actionable yet

Decision D30: a provider model id never appears in an agent file, generated or not. So **no
projected agent carries a `model:` today** and there is nothing for `--model` to override. The
injection that would put one there is `basicly-a3yi`, still open.

Filing a fixture for the override now would be inventing the shape rather than observing it, which
is the failure this repository has already paid for twice.

## What changed under it

`basicly-jn1x` landed the recorded argv, so the co-occurrence is now **visible in the ledger**: a
record whose command carries both `--agent` and `--model` is exactly the shape at risk. Before
that, 0 of 357 records named either flag and the question could not be asked of the data at all.

## When to take this

After `basicly-a3yi`. Then decide whether the fix is to drop `--model` when a role declares one,
or to widen `tier_honoured` to mean "the tier that was asked for is the tier that ran" - the
second is the honest reading of the name and changes an existing contract, so it is a decision
rather than a patch.

the control that says which.

## Context

Two committed and pushed files carry a person's username and a personal e-mail address. Architecture §32.7 claimed absolutely that no committed artifact carries a username, and the claim is false.

Measured 2026-08-17, twice by paths sharing no step — a field-wise count over the parsed records and a raw-line regex over the bytes — and both agree on the substance:

    .beads/issues.jsonl, 924 records
      created_by: <redacted:machine-username> 846, <redacted:machine-username> 78
      assignee:   niksavis@live.com 56, <redacted:machine-username> 26
      lines holding an e-mail address: 58

    .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl, 5616 lines
      lines holding an e-mail address: 59
      lines holding the redaction placeholder: 4944   <- positive control, the rule does fire

Both files are tracked, committed and pushed to a public remote, so this is published rather than merely present.

## Why every gate is green over it

`tracker-path-scan` builds its identity rule from `getpass.getuser()`, which on this machine is `<redacted:machine-username>`. The identity in the stores is a **different** one. So the gate is not broken and its green result is correct — it is answering "does this artifact carry *your* identity" when the requirement is "does it carry *anyone's*".

That is the general defect, and it is worth stating separately from the data: an identity gate keyed on the running user cannot see another user's identity, and a repository that several machines write to will accumulate identities no single machine's gate can find.

## What is bounded and what is not

Every identity-bearing event in the owned ledger carries the import's own source marker; no live write path produces one. So the population is inherited from the pre-cutover import and is not growing. That bounds the remedy to a backfill plus a format rule — it does not make the published values unpublished.

## The three remedies, and which needs an owner

Removing the values from the current files is a corrective append or a rewrite, and the rewrite of a committed append-only log is the exception architecture §4.2 reserves for an explicit owner decision. Removing them from **history** is a force-push, which is an owner decision of a different order and is not this bead's to take. Preventing the next one is the format rule and the deny-list configuration, which is ordinary work.

Note the deny-list the hook already names, `[[privacy.denied]]`, belongs in the gitignored `basicly.local.toml` — 787 bytes, all comments, parsing to an empty table. The mechanism exists and was never configured.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Count the identity-bearing lines in the committed store, with the redaction placeholder
   as the control that proves the rule fires at all:

       git grep -c -E '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}' HEAD -- .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl
       git grep -c '<redacted:machine-username>' HEAD -- .
       grep -c 'redacted:' .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl

2. Run the gate that is supposed to catch this and read its result:

       uv run pre-commit run tracker-path-scan --all-files

3. Read why that result is green, which is the general defect:

       rg -n 'getpass|getuser' .basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py

4. Check whether the deny-list the hooks already name was ever configured:

       rg -n 'privacy.denied' basicly.local.toml
       wc -c basicly.local.toml
       rg -n 'privacy.*denied' .basicly/core/hooks/internal-info-scan.py

   Observed 2026-08-19: the first command returns nothing, `basicly.local.toml` is **787
   bytes and every line of it is a comment**, and the third command is the **positive
   control** - `internal-info-scan.py` reads `data.get("privacy", {}).get("denied", [])`
   out of exactly that file, and `tracker-path-scan.py` names the same list. So the
   mechanism exists, reads this file, and was never configured; the empty result is a
   missing configuration rather than a missing feature.

Observed, re-measured 2026-08-19 in this checkout: the ledger holds 6027 lines, **61** of
them carrying an e-mail address and **213** carrying the username `<redacted:machine-username>`, and `git grep`
finds `<redacted:machine-username>` in that one file and nowhere else in the tree - so the values are committed
at HEAD, not merely present in a working copy. **The positive control is the third command**,
which returns **4955** lines carrying the redaction placeholder: the rule does fire, over the
same bytes, on the great majority of records. So the 61 and the 213 are a population the rule
missed rather than a probe that failed.

Step 3 shows why: `tracker-path-scan` builds its identity rule from `getpass.getuser()`, so
it asks "does this artifact carry *your* identity" where the requirement is "does it carry
*anyone's*". The gate is not broken and its green result is correct - the rule is the wrong
question. An identity gate keyed on the running user cannot see another user's identity, and
a repository several machines write to accumulates identities no single machine's gate can
find.

**One of the two stores this record was filed over is gone.** `.beads/issues.jsonl` and its
924 records are no longer in the tree or in git's index - `git ls-files .beads` returns
nothing - so the 846/78 `created_by` and 56/26 `assignee` counts in the Context above are
history rather than a current reading, and `docs/architecture` §32.7.1 ("two stores carry
another") is itself now one store out of date. The owned ledger half above stands and is the
live population.

Expected: the format rule refuses an identity-bearing field on the write path whoever the
running user is; the inherited values are removed from the current file by the corrective
route architecture §4.2 reserves for an append-only log; and the architecture claim is
restated to match what is measurable.

- `src/basicly/redact.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py`

## The defect

`docs/architecture/architecture.md` §30 *Roles at dispatch* carries this as the first of two
caveats:

> The curator and the retrospector are both inert on the supervised landing pass, which has
> no watchdog and no stream meter of its own. Under the supervisor they run only after the
> ship approval, on the interactive driver.

The first sentence holds. **The second does not.** Under the supervisor, both roles run on the
supervisor's own process after it approves the ship itself, and the driver the supervisor uses
to get there cannot switch them off even in principle - `loop.run_until_blocked` takes no
`repair_dispatch` parameter, so the ship advance runs with `advance`'s default of `True`.

So the text sends a reader looking for an interactive driver that is not in the picture, on
the one path where an unmetered dispatch actually happens.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the claim:

       rg -n -A3 'inert on the supervised landing pass' docs/architecture/architecture.md

2. Read the two dispatches the claim is about, and the flag that gates each:

       rg -n -A3 'def _dispatch_curation' src/basicly/loop.py
       rg -n 'if root is None or not ctx.repair_dispatch' src/basicly/loop.py

3. Read what the supervisor passes on each of its two advances:

       rg -n 'loop.advance\(|loop.run_until_blocked\(' src/basicly/supervise.py

4. Read whether the second of those can pass the flag at all:

       rg -n -A9 'def run_until_blocked' src/basicly/loop.py

5. Confirm which process approved the ship on a real supervised pass: read the pass log for
   the `ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates it` preflight line and then check the
   parent process of the curator's dispatch.

Observed, verified in code 2026-08-19 at main 9534ca05:

- `supervise._land_green` passes `repair_dispatch=False` to the build->verify
  `loop.advance` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:3971`), with a comment giving exactly the reason
  the architecture text gives. That is sentence one, and it is correct.
- Once `policy.approve_checkpoint_guarded(..., interactive=False, grant_root=session.root_issue)`
  approves - which an L3 grant does, with no human in it - the same function ships through
  `loop.run_until_blocked(repo_root, outcome.issue_id, grant_root=session.root_issue)`
  (`supervise.py:3998`). `supervise.advance_parked` reaches the same driver.
- `loop.run_until_blocked` has **no** `repair_dispatch` parameter and calls
  `advance(repo_root, issue_id, config=..., inputs=..., grant_root=...)`, so
  `repair_dispatch` takes its default `True`. `loop._dispatch_curation` and
  `loop._retrospective` are gated only on that flag, so both fire - in the supervisor
  process.
- The behavioural half was already observed 2026-08-16 on a supervised pass over
  `basicly-e2mz`: after `basicly-e2mz.13` landed, the curator was dispatched with the
  supervisor process itself as its parent, and preflight had reported
  `ship pending - the live L3 grant delegates it`.

Expected: §30 states that the supervisor dispatches the curator and the retrospector itself
once a grant delegates the ship approval, names the driver that does it, and does not claim an
interactive driver is required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given `docs/architecture/architecture.md` §30 is read at the *Roles at dispatch* caveats
  when it describes where the curator and the retrospector run under a supervised pass, then
  it states that the supervisor dispatches them itself once a grant delegates the ship
  approval, and it does not claim an interactive driver is required.
- Given the corrected text then it distinguishes the build->verify landing, which passes
  `repair_dispatch=False`, from the ship advance, which cannot pass it - so a reader learns
  which of the supervisor's two advances is metered and which is not.
- Given the corrected text then every claim in it names the module and function a reader can
  check it against, rather than describing a driver.
- Demonstrated by: reading the edited section against
  `rg -n 'loop.advance\(|loop.run_until_blocked\(' src/basicly/supervise.py` and
  `rg -n -A9 'def run_until_blocked' src/basicly/loop.py`, with no sentence left that the
  two outputs contradict.

## Scope

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
