payload.value:
## Context

Found 2026-08-20 while closing `basicly-z9xvwa` through the documented write surface. The
close landed and the reason did not.

`mirror._close_drafts` emits one `KIND_STATUS` draft and nothing else, so a `--reason` the
argv carries reaches the owned ledger as no event at all. Its docstring justifies the drop:
the reason is not mirrored **as a comment**, because br records it as a field of the close
and inventing a comment row would be a difference the mirror made rather than found. That
argument is correct and it is about the wrong shape. The kit already models the field —
`commands.CLOSE_REASON_FIELD`, written as a `KIND_FIELD` draft by `commands.close` — so
mirroring it as a field is exactly what makes the two sides identical.

`closed_at` is lost by the same route.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `basicly tracker write -- close <id> --reason "<text>"` on an open record.
2. Observe the surface print `recorded: close <id> --reason <text>`.
3. Run `basicly tracker show <id>` and observe `status` is `closed`, and that `close_reason` and `closed_at` are both absent.
4. Observe `max_seq` advanced by exactly **1**, so only the status event was appended - had the reason been carried it would be 2, because `commands.close` drafts the field before the status.
5. Positive control on the field itself: 663 of the 772 closed records in `.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl` carry `close_reason`, so the field is the norm rather than an unused one, and the 0 above belongs to the write path and not to the fold.

## The population, split rather than counted

109 of the 772 closed records carry neither `close_reason` nor `closed_at`, and the record
closed above now matches that signature exactly. That is one signature, not a proven
attribution: a record closed before either field existed is indistinguishable from one closed
through this path. **Split the 109 against the first commit that introduced the field before
reporting any of them as this defect** - the count is a question, and only the part of it that
postdates the field is an answer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a close carrying a reason through the write seam when the record is read back then the reason is on the record as a field - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_mirror.py -k close_reason -q`
- Given a close carrying no reason then exactly the events it carries today are appended, so no existing record's history changes meaning
- Given the 109 closed records with neither field then the record states how many postdate the field's introduction, measured rather than assumed

## Scope

- `src/basicly/mirror.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/mirror.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/commands.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`

## Context

Found 2026-08-20 by typing `basicly tracker write -- create --help` to read the verb's help.
It did not print help. **It minted a record** - `basicly-5m2xfd` - carrying one field,
`provenance: engine`, with no title, no type and no description.

`mirror._create_drafts` holds the detection point already:

```text
fields = {"title": positional[1]} if len(positional) > 1 else {}
```

The `else {}` branch is the seam knowing the title is absent and minting anyway. Its sibling
`_close_drafts`, twelve lines below, raises `TrackerDivergenceError` when the argv names no
record, so the refusal pattern is in the same function group and is not being reused.

The upstream half is `br`, which accepted `--help` as a create and replied with a minted id;
the mirror was faithful. That does not make this someone else's defect: the harness seam is
where a consumer types the command, and it is the side this repository can refuse from.

## Why the body gate does not catch it

`ledger-bodies` passed on the empty record - `all 1019 record(s) carry a body` - and that is
the gate keeping its word rather than failing open. Its definition of a body is **a `created`
event exists** (`.scripts/ledger_bodies.py:62`), and the empty record has one. A `created`
event whose payload names nothing is a different claim, and no gate here makes it. Do not
"fix" `ledger_bodies.py` for this; the refusal belongs at the write seam, before the event.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `basicly tracker write -- create --help`.
2. Observe it prints `created: <id>` rather than any help text.
3. Run `basicly tracker show <id>` and observe `fields` holds only `provenance`, with no title.
4. Run `uv run python .scripts/ledger_bodies.py` and observe it passes, because a `created` event exists.
5. Positive control that the seam can refuse: run `basicly tracker write -- close --help` and observe `Error: br close names no issue`, from `mirror._close_drafts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a create whose argv names no title when it reaches the seam then it is refused before any event is appended, naming the argv - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_mirror.py -k create_without_a_title -q`
- Given a create that names a title then exactly the events it appends today are appended, so no existing record changes meaning
- Given the refusal then it is raised on the same error class `_close_drafts` already uses, rather than a second one

## Scope

- `src/basicly/mirror.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/mirror.py`
- `tests/test_mirror.py`
- `.scripts/ledger_bodies.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`

## Context

Measured twice in one pass on 2026-08-20, by an identical mechanism, on two unrelated modules.
Filed because a second occurrence is a pattern rather than an incident, and because the
instrument that would have priced it does not exist.

**Splitting a module raises the prose share of both halves by construction.** The code divides
and the contract docstring does not: each half still owes a module docstring, and each moved
function keeps the one it had. So the size ratchet and the comment-density ratchet pull in
opposite directions on the same edit, and no arrangement satisfies both once a module is large
enough to need cutting.

Two measurements, both from splits the size ratchet demanded:

- `board_snapshot.py` lost 630 tokens of code and 505 of prose in one edit. It went from 3980 tokens to 2845 and from 47 percent prose to 51.5 - **smaller and denser at the same time**. `board_sections.py`, the half that left, landed at 51.5 too.
- `differential.py` split three ways. `views.py` is five frozen records whose docstrings are the payload: 73.4 percent. `derivation.py` is 52.7.

Four density waivers were taken across the two, after every cheaper reduction was measured
first: prose moved to the module whose code it describes, four stale cross-references the
splits themselves created were repointed, and four restatements of what a test asserts were
dropped. That moved 55.7 and 55.1 to 51.5 both, and it was not enough.

## The instrument that is missing

`check_module_size.py` reports only that a module is **over** its limit. It never reports that a
module is *within N tokens* of one. So a module at 99 percent of its cap is a blocker for the
next lane and reads as green in every gate output, and the cost of a split is invisible until
the lane that needs one pays it.

Measured on this tree the same day: 22 modules sit at exactly 0 tokens of headroom and 41 are
within 25. None appears in any gate output. `mirror.py` at 23 tokens cost `basicly-holhk4` its
declared placement, and `tests/test_handoff.py` at 0 has been rebaselined three times.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Take any module at or near the 4000-token cap whose prose share is under 50 percent.
2. Split it along a real seam, moving code and the docstrings that belong to that code.
3. Measure both halves with `check_comment_density.measure`.
4. Observe both shares are higher than the original's, because each half now carries a module docstring the original carried once.
5. Positive control: measure the original before the split and confirm it was under the cap, so the split is what moved it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a module within a stated margin of its size limit when the size gate runs then it says so, rather than reporting only modules already over - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_check_module_size.py -k margin -q`
- Given a split that trades one ratchet for the other then the pair is reported together, so the trade is visible before the second gate refuses it
- Given the existing 22 zero-headroom modules then the report names them without failing, because they are the debt this measures and not a regression

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `tests/test_check_module_size.py`

## Working Set

- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `tests/test_check_module_size.py`
- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest -q`
payload.title: the two size ratchets pull opposite ways on every split and no gate prices the trade

payload.text:
REFUTED, with the measurement, and this record's stated mechanism is wrong.

Three things were measured, each with a positive control:

1. The append path makes NO fsync. Spying os.fsync and os.fdatasync through a whole events.append of 5 drafts counted zero; the same spy counted 1 on a deliberate fsync. A tokenized scan of events.py excluding comments and strings - so the docstring's own sentence 'No fsync' cannot satisfy the probe - finds no fsync, fdatasync, O_SYNC, O_DSYNC or flush. Mutation: adding a flush plus fsync to _append_lines failed both new tests.

2. A partial batch is real and is a clean whole-line PREFIX, never a hole and never a tear. Emulating process death inside the write loop: a 9-draft batch left 0 bytes; a 2016-draft batch left 1890 events parsed, 0 quarantined, ending in a newline. Every kernel handoff fell on a line boundary. io.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE here is 131072, not the 8192 events.py asserts.

3. THEREFORE THE HOLE CANNOT BE THIS PATH. I verified the key evidence independently: basicly-vkh0.30's seq 8 and seq 10 are ONE FILE LINE apart and 525 microseconds apart, while one append over this ledger measures 54-61 ms. So they were minted in one batch and written by one _append_lines call, and a partial batch truncates a suffix - an interior line whose successor survives cannot be lost that way. The loss happened AFTER the bytes were in the file. Adding an fsync would not have prevented it.

The class therefore moves from 'an unflushed write' to 'a post-write mutation of the file', and the cause remains unidentified - as this record already said. What changed is that one whole branch is now closed by evidence rather than open by assumption.

AND THE NEXT ONE IS ALREADY DETECTED, which is this record's stated goal. The event above a hole carries totals a fold of the survivors cannot reach, and the next append restates from the fold, so exactly one event disagrees. Measured live: 1 mismatched_totals across 6263 events, 1 sequence hole, 0 quarantined. That is now a regression test.

Adjacent hazard found, NOT claimed as the cause: tracker.scrub_ledger is the only in-tree writer that rewrites this ledger whole - read_text, temp, rename - and it takes no LedgerLock, so anything appended between its read and its rename is destroyed. It re-emits every line it read, so it cannot produce a single interior deletion. Not filed as the cause; worth filing as its own hazard.

Also unfixed, and stated rather than hidden: events.py lines 215-220 claim the buffered writer flushes in ~8 KiB chunks and infers interleaved syscalls from it. Measured, the buffer is 131072 and every handoff fell between lines, so the figure is a floor and the inference did not reproduce. events.py is at 14978/14978 tokens and 57.1 percent density, both frozen at zero headroom, so correcting the prose there costs a rebaseline. The surviving true reading is now pinned instead: BUFFER_CHUNK_BYTES <= io.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE is asserted, and that constant had exactly one occurrence in the tree before - its own definition.

Unmeasured: ENOSPC mid-flush and syscall-level counting, neither available on this box; and machine-level power loss, which is the residual the push-is-the-durability-boundary choice accepts by design.

The acceptance check named in this record selects nothing - pytest tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py -k durable exits 5, because that module has 0 tokens of headroom and the tests had to go in tests/test_kit_tracker_events_durability.py. payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-20 while refuting `basicly-mbkqxi`, and deliberately **not** claimed as that
record's cause.

`tracker.scrub_ledger` is the only writer in the tree that rewrites the owned ledger **whole**
- `read_text`, write a temp file, rename - and it takes **no `LedgerLock`**. Every other writer
goes through `events.append`, which holds the lock for the duration of one append. So anything
appended between this function's read and its rename is destroyed, and destroyed silently: the
rename succeeds, the log parses, and the fold is internally consistent because the lost lines
were never in the text that was re-emitted.

**Why this is filed as a hazard and not as `basicly-mbkqxi`'s cause.** It re-emits every line
it read, so it cannot produce a *single interior* deletion, which is the shape `basicly-vkh0.30`
shows. It can only truncate a suffix of concurrent appends. The cause of that hole remains
unidentified.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read `src/basicly/tracker.py:800` and observe the read-modify-rename sequence.
2. Search that function for `LedgerLock` and observe none, against a positive control that finds the lock in `events.append`.
3. Observe `events.append` takes the lock for the duration of one append, so the two writers do not exclude each other.
4. Observe that a line appended after the `read_text` and before the rename is absent from the temp file and therefore absent after it.
5. Observe the result parses cleanly and folds consistently, so no gate reports it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a whole-file ledger rewrite when it runs then it holds the same lock an append holds, so the two cannot interleave - check: `uv run pytest tests/test_tracker_scrub_ledger.py -k lock -q`
- Given an append that arrives during a rewrite then it is either serialised behind it or refused, never dropped
- Given the lock is held then the hold is bounded, because a rewrite reads the whole log and an append that waited forever would be worse than one that failed

## Scope

- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_scrub_ledger.py`

## Working Set

- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_scrub_ledger.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_tracker_scrub_ledger.py -q`

## Context

Found 2026-08-21. `basicly-rn0o.4` blocked `basicly-rn0o.3` while `basicly-rn0o.4`'s own `## Plan` section declared it depends on `basicly-rn0o.3`. The renderer was therefore the one board lane no supervised pass could dispatch, and nothing reported the disagreement.

Two sources hold one fact. `plan_record.parse_plan_section` reads the declaration off the body; the `edge` events hold the graph. The decomposer writes both from one plan, so they agree at creation and can drift on any later hand edit or `dep add`.

Measured over the whole tracker with a positive control: 231 open records, 22 carry a `- depends on:` line, 313 live `blocks` edges, and the declared set is a subset of the edges on 19 of the 22. Two of the three misses declare by title rather than by id, which the title-keyed plan graph accepts at decompose time. One was the inverted edge.

## Why this is a gate and not a note

An inverted edge reads as correct from either side. The record says one thing, the ready set says another, and an operator reading the record believes the lane is dispatchable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a records `- depends on:` line names an id that is not one of its live `blocks` edge targets, THE CHECK SHALL exit non-zero and name the record, the declared id and the edges it does have.
- WHEN a declaration names a title rather than an id, THE CHECK SHALL resolve it against the titles in the tracker before reporting a miss.
- WHEN every open record agrees, THE CHECK SHALL exit zero and print the reconciled count and the population it covered.
- WHEN no open record carries a depends-on line at all, THE CHECK SHALL exit non-zero, because an empty population is the probe failing rather than the tree passing.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_declared_dependencies.py`
- `tests/test_check_declared_dependencies.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_declared_dependencies.py` printing the reconciled count, and exit 1 after a deliberate `dep remove` of one declared edge.
payload.title: reconcile a records declared depends on against the blocks edges it actually has

## Context

Backlog `docs/architecture/backlog.md` B3. The architecture document carries 16 mermaid blocks and the README one, and nothing checks that any of them renders. A block with a syntax error renders as a red error box on the hosting site and no gate here stops it landing.

The defect is not hypothetical. One revision named a `sequenceDiagram` participant `Loop`, which collides with mermaid's `loop` keyword. A parser caught it; review did not.

## Two corrections B3 carries, and both bind this work

A parse is the wrong instrument. Measured 2026-08-16 against mermaid 11 in a browser, `mermaid.parse()` accepts a `stateDiagram-v2` block whose transition label carries a second colon, and a renderer refuses the same block. The criterion is therefore *renders*, never *parses*.

And the reporting renderer could not be reproduced on mermaid 11, so which renderer the hosting surface uses is unestablished. The dependency is approved by the owner on 2026-08-21; establishing the hosting renderer and its version is part of this work, and the check records the renderer version it ran so a later mismatch is visible rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a tracked markdown file holds a mermaid block the renderer refuses, THE CHECK SHALL exit non-zero and name the file, the line, the renderer version and its message.
- WHEN every block renders, THE CHECK SHALL exit zero and print the block count and the renderer version.
- WHEN the renderer is not installed, THE CHECK SHALL fail rather than skip, because a skip reads as a pass.
- WHEN the tree holds no mermaid block at all, THE CHECK SHALL exit non-zero, because an empty population is the probe failing.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_mermaid.py`
- `package.json`
- `package-lock.json`
- `tests/test_check_mermaid.py`
- `basicly.d/*.toml`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_mermaid.py` reporting the tree block count and 0 failures, then exit 1 after a deliberate typo in one block.

## Context

Found 2026-08-21 while reconciling `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` against the tree. That document requires an opaque `actor` on every event, and sections 4.3 item 5 and item 6 both rest on it: reconstructing history and reconstructing a greenfield decision both need to know who wrote a row.

The field exists on the event record and the value never does. Census of the committed ledger: `actor` is empty on all 1,078 events written since the flip, against a positive control of 3,775 truthy actors across the whole log - the imported rows carry one and the live writer does not.

The consequence is quiet. Architecture section 32.2 lists `actor` as part of the event record, and a reader who greps the schema finds it declared. Nothing reports that it is never populated, so "every state change is attributable" reads as true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the engine appends an event, THE WRITER SHALL populate `actor` with the redacted identity the append is made under.
- WHEN a dispatched agent appends through the seam, THE WRITER SHALL record the agent rather than the operating-system user, so a landing names the runner that produced it.
- WHEN an actor cannot be resolved, THE WRITER SHALL record the reason rather than an empty string, because an empty field is ambiguous between unknown and unwritten.
- WHEN `fsck` runs, IT SHALL report the count of live events carrying no actor, so the population cannot grow in silence.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/commands.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py`

- budget: `140000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Append one event through the seam and read its `actor` back off the ledger non-empty and redacted, then run `uv run python .scripts/check_ledger_fsck.py` and read the no-actor count it prints.

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-21 over `.basicly/core/agents/*/agent.yaml` and `.basicly/core/skills/*/skill.yaml`. The catalog ships 41 skill sources, 20 of them model-invoked and 21 user-invoked `tool-*` entries. Six of the 20 model-invoked skills are declared on an agent. Five of the eleven agents declare no skill at all: auditor, curator, decider, reviewer, tester.

The engine inlines a declared skill into the dispatch prompt (`basicly-ey58`), so a skill an agent does not declare is guidance that role never receives. The pairing is machine-checked for the five loop skills that are declared (`agents.py` lint), so what is missing is the declaration, not the mechanism.

## The pairings the roster argues for

`interface-facts` is the researcher role stated in one sentence and the researcher declares it nowhere. `test-discipline` belongs to tester and implementer. `falsify-first` belongs to reviewer and auditor, whose whole posture is to attack a claim. `conventional-commits` belongs to implementer, which is the role that commits. `work-tracker` belongs to decider, which reads the corpus. `root-cause` belongs to reviewer and auditor beside retrospector.

## Why it is filed rather than done

Decision D-12: agent-authored guidance never reaches the catalog without a human. A pairing table is guidance, so the set lands only after an owner reads it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an agent source declares a role whose job a shipped skill states, IT SHALL declare that skill.
- WHEN lint runs over the agent sources, IT SHALL report every model-invoked skill that no agent declares, so the gap is visible rather than counted by hand.
- WHEN a user-invoked skill is unreferenced, LINT SHALL NOT report it, because a `tool-*` entry carries no description and is reached by a human typing its name.
- WHEN the wiring lands, `basicly agents-check` SHALL stay green over both roots.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/agents/auditor/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/curator/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/decider/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/reviewer/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/tester/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/researcher/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/implementer/agent.yaml`
- `src/basicly/agents.py`
- `tests/test_agent_lint.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly agents-check --all-default-roots` green, and `uv run basicly catalog lint` reporting zero unreferenced model-invoked skills.

criteria), `### What appears on the TV` (the eight regions and the five-second question each

2. `board_schema.verdict(repo_root, document)` already returns `absent`, `renderable` and

3. `board_snapshot.build_document` has no caller outside tests and `pyproject.toml` carries a
   vulture entry for it. Wiring it is what makes this subtree live; drop the entry.

body.post_ship_action: Two of the three findings must be settled BEFORE the tag moves, not after, and that ordering is the whole point: `basicly release` folds `changelog.d/` fragments at the tagged commit, so a fragment written after the tag never publishes. (1) Pre-tag blocker — author `changelog.d/basicly-rn0o.3.added.md` describing the command, the self-contained page, the `board-snapshot.json` sidecar and the per-panel age, and have it land in the commit that gets tagged; without it the release ships an unannounced CLI command and `.scripts/check_release_notes.py` turns red the moment the record closes (probed: owed=True). (2) Pre-tag decision, owner's call — either cut the sentence "In wall mode with a live supervisor it refreshes on the supervisor's 15-second tick." from `board_cli.FRESHNESS` (src/basicly/board_cli.py:37-38) until `basicly-rn0o.5` lands, or keep it and record in the release note that wall mode is not in this release. I recommend cutting it: the surrounding test asserts string presence, so removal is a one-line test edit, and a `--help` that advertises an invalid subcommand is the exact failure mode no gate here catches. (3) Post-ship, non-blocking — file a follow-up to add a shipped→documented direction to `.scripts/docs_claim_surfaces.py`, or to accept that surface coverage is a human decision, since the gate's docstring already says "a false claim in code is caught by a gate; on a README it is caught by a consumer" and this release is an instance of it. I moved no tag, pushed nothing, and changed no file. Coverage boundary: I ran tests/test_board_cli.py and tests/test_board_render.py (28 passed), lint-imports, docs_claims --check, check_release_notes.py, and the demonstration command. I did NOT re-run `basicly verify --mode full` or the full pytest suite — the operator's parked-stall comment claims full verify is PASS on the merged tree and I did not reproduce that. I did NOT open /tmp/b_audit.html in a browser, so the demonstration's "assert the file opens in a browser" is verified textually (12 panels, 12 age lines, 8 regions, no external origin) and not visually; layout, contrast and the reduced-motion behaviour on a real wall display are unexercised. I did not review the sibling lanes a2dfa30f, 0eabe86a or 645de536, and I did not audit the uncommitted modification to .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl currently in the working tree.

unsupported.claim: `basicly board --help`: "In wall mode with a live supervisor it refreshes on the supervisor's 15-second tick." (src/basicly/board_cli.py:37-38, rendered in the shipped `--help` description)
unsupported.why: Wall mode does not exist in this release, so a consumer who reads this cannot reach the behaviour it describes. `src/basicly/board_serve.py`: No such file or directory. `uv run basicly board serve` → exit 2, `argument board_command: invalid choice: 'serve' (choose from 'validate')`. `board_cli._HANDLERS` is `{None: cmd_emit, "validate": cmd_validate}` (src/basicly/board_cli.py:124). The owning record `basicly-rn0o.5` ("serve the board in wall mode read only") is listed as a dependent with status `open`. The one test that touches this string, tests/test_board_cli.py:31, asserts only that the sentence is *present* in `--help` — a string-presence assertion, not a capability assertion — so no test, command or gate binds the behaviour. Confidence: high that wall mode is absent and unreachable (three independent probes). Separately, the number is real — `supervise.py:106 HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S = 15.0` — so this is a premature claim, not a wrong one. It is also spec-mandated wording (docs/requirements/harness-board.md:552-553), so the lane followed its instructions; the defect is that the spec's end-state sentence was frozen into a surface shipping before unit D. This finding does NOT say the freshness claim as a whole is unsupported — the first two sentences are evidenced above — and it does NOT say the page misreports its own age.

unsupported.claim: Nothing at all. There is no release note for this unit: `changelog.d/` holds no `basicly-rn0o.3.*` fragment, and the `## [Unreleased]` section of CHANGELOG.md is empty.
unsupported.why: `ls changelog.d/ | grep rn0o` returns only basicly-rn0o.1.added.md, basicly-rn0o.2.added.md, basicly-rn0o.10.changed.md out of 81 fragments; CHANGELOG.md:7 `## [Unreleased]` is followed immediately by `## v0.9.0`. So this release ships a new CLI command and publishes no consumer-visible announcement of it. This is also a gate that is about to go red, not a stylistic gap: `uv run python .scripts/check_release_notes.py` currently passes (`352 closed record(s) judged, 145 owing a release note and each at its frozen entry`) only because the record is still `open`. Probing the gate's own judgement with the status flipped: `_standing('basicly-rn0o.3', dict(record, status='closed'), accounted)` → `Standing(owed=True, reason='')`, with shipped scope `['src/basicly/board_cli.py', 'src/basicly/board_render.py', '.basicly/core/templates/board/*.j2']`. Positive control on the same probe: `basicly-rn0o.2` → `reason='already has a release note'`. `basicly-rn0o.3` is absent from `[tool.release_notes.frozen]` (only `basicly-rn0o.11` appears, pyproject.toml:662). Confidence: high — the gate's own function was called on the real record, with a control that discriminates.

unsupported.claim: `basicly board` is named on no surface a consumer meets before running anything: 0 occurrences in README.md and 0 in site/index.html.
unsupported.why: grep -c -F over both files returns 0/0, against a positive control of `basicly install` (3/5) and `basicly tracker` (1/0), so the zero is real and not a bad probe. This is deliberately reported as unsupported-announcement rather than as a gate violation: `.scripts/docs_claim_surfaces.py` watches exactly `CONSUMER_SURFACES = ("README.md", "site/index.html")` but only in the direction its own docstring names — "the architecture document is gated on every shipped command being documented, not on every documented command shipping" — so nothing checks shipped→documented on those two surfaces. `basicly release` is likewise absent from both, so README is demonstrably not an exhaustive command list and this is not a convention breach. What it does mean: the architecture document row is the *only* place this command is described, and architecture.md is not inside a docs-claims block at that line (the two blocks are at :665 and :3291), so that row is unbound prose. Confidence: high on the counts, moderate on the severity.

payload.description:
## Context

Reproduced 2026-08-21 on three consecutive ship advances. Two of the three refused:

```text
the release record was refused: basicly-rn0o.7's release-record artifact does not
validate: $.unsupported[0]: Additional properties are not allowed
('suggested_wording' was unexpected)
```

`basicly-rn0o.14` failed identically. `basicly-rn0o.13` passed, reporting `5 claim(s) bound, 3 unsupported`, so the failure is non-deterministic rather than total - which is what makes the cause the missing declaration rather than a wrong schema.

## The cause, and it is a contract asymmetry

`release-record.schema.json` sets `additionalProperties: false` on `unsupported[]` items and requires exactly `claim` and `why`. The curator source's `output_contract` says only *"each unsupported claim named"*. It never names the two fields, so the model chooses a shape, and a helpful extra key is the natural choice.

A producer told to emit an artifact and not told its field set will invent one. The consumer then refuses, and SHIP has already merged, so the refusal costs the release record rather than blocking anything - which is why this has been silent.

## Why the schema is not the thing to widen

`suggested_wording` is a claim about what the notes *should* say. The curator's stated job is to bind a claim to evidence or drop it, never to soften or rewrite one. Admitting the field would admit the behaviour the role exists to refuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the curator is briefed, ITS OUTPUT CONTRACT SHALL name every field the release-record schema requires and state that the object admits no other key.
- WHEN a curator reply carries a key the schema forbids, THE ENGINE SHALL name the key and the artifact kind, as it already does.
- WHEN three consecutive ship advances run, EVERY release record SHALL validate.
- WHERE another agent source produces a schema-validated artifact, ITS CONTRACT SHALL name that schema's field set too, so this is fixed as a class rather than one instance.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/agents/curator/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/blocks/*.block.yaml`
- `tests/test_agent_lint.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_agent_lint.py -q`, then one ship advance whose release record validates rather than being refused.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-21 while filing this session's findings. This create:

```text
basicly tracker write -- create "<title>" bug 1 --description "<body>"
```

minted a record with `issue_type` unset and `priority` unset. The verb takes `--type` and `--priority` as flags; `bug` and `1` landed as extra positionals and the seam discarded them without a word. The record then reads as untyped, which the plan-entry ratchet and the definition of ready both judge.

`write_verbs._create_drafts` already refuses a create naming no title, because *"a titleless record is a `created` event that states nothing"* (`basicly-1qi0sz`). The same argument covers an argument the seam cannot place: an ignored value is a caller who believes they set a field.

## Why silence is the defect rather than the parsing

A caller who wrote `bug 1` believed they typed the record. Nothing said otherwise, and the next reader sees an untyped record with no clue that a type was offered and dropped. The failure is invisible at the moment it is cheap to fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a create or an update carries a positional the verb cannot place, THE SEAM SHALL refuse and name the argument and the flag that would have carried it.
- WHEN a create carries only the title and recognised flags, THE SEAM SHALL behave exactly as it does today.
- WHERE a verb legitimately takes several positionals, such as `close` and `dep add`, THE REFUSAL SHALL NOT fire on them.
- WHEN the refusal fires, ITS MESSAGE SHALL name the verb, so a caller does not have to read the source to learn the flag.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/write_verbs.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_argv.py`
- `tests/test_write_verbs.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: A create carrying a stray positional exits non-zero naming the argument and the flag, against a control create with the same flags spelled correctly that still succeeds.

## Context

Session 2026-08-14. The handover carried the trap in plain words - "measure headroom before writing
prose, not after a gate refuses you" - and it was still paid for **three times in one session**,
because there are two ratchets and measuring one feels like having measured.

Each time, `module-size` headroom was measured and `comment-density` was not:

```text
basicly-jn1x   runner.py 59.9% vs frozen 59.8, run_record.py 58.0% vs 56.9
               two rounds of prose-trimming after the gate refused
basicly-c357   differential.py had +3 tokens AND 0.0pt density; the placement
               had to be redesigned into a new kit module
basicly-ejdm.2 lane_split.py landed at 56.5% against a 50% cap on a new file
```

The module-size trap is the one this repo has written down most, which is probably why it is the
one that gets measured.

## The shape of the fix

One command that takes a path and reports **both** ratchets in one answer - tokens against the
frozen baseline or cap, and prose share against the frozen share or cap - so "measure headroom"
is a single call rather than two an agent will half-do. `check_module_size.tracked_modules` and
`check_comment_density.tracked_modules` already produce both halves; nothing composes them.

Neither script currently takes a path argument either, so today the measurement is a python
one-liner importing both from `.scripts/`, which is why it is skipped under time pressure.

## What this is not

Not a new gate. Both ratchets already bind at commit time. This is the read that lets a change be
sized before it is written, which is the only point at which the information is cheap.

## Scope
- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `.scripts/ratchet.py`
- `tests/test_check_module_size.py`
- `tests/test_check_comment_density.py`

## Plan
- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py` naming every module within N tokens of its cap in one command, against a control run on a tree where nothing is close.

payload.value:
## Context

Found while landing two lanes on 2026-08-14.

Each ratchet gate ratchets its own waiver count. Nothing counts them together, and nothing reviews one after it is granted.

```text
module-size waivers      1 -> 2   basicly-r343, bought on cost, expires under basicly-kr7t
comment-density waivers  1 -> 2   basicly-feje, bought on cohesion, no expiry needed
```

Two waivers in one session, from two lanes that were not about size. Both were argued honestly and both are defensible on their own. The pattern is the finding, not either grant.

## Why a per-gate count is not enough

A waiver is the one escape every size rule leaves open, so it is where pressure goes when a ratchet blocks unrelated work. The `basicly-r343` case is the shape to watch: the ratchet refused **any** change to a file, so the fix could not land without either a waiver or a refactor that had nothing to do with the bug.

The design already says waivers are ratcheted so the count may not grow silently. It grows visibly and nobody reads the number, because it is a parenthetical inside one gate's pass line.

## The distinction that must survive

Not every waiver is debt. Two kinds exist and they need different handling.

- **Bought on cohesion.** A genuinely small module whose prose is the contract it carries. Correct, permanent, and no follow-up is owed. `lens_review.py` is this.
- **Bought on cost.** The ratchet refused a change and the real fix was out of scope. Debt, and it must expire. `.scripts/wired_or_deleted.py` is this, and `basicly-kr7t` retires it.

Today the record cannot tell them apart. A reader sees a count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When any waiver is granted, then its record states which of the two kinds it is.
- When a waiver is bought on cost, then it names the bead that retires it, and a check fails once that bead closes and the waiver remains.
- When the gates report, then one line states the total waiver count across all gates and how many are debt.
- Given today's four waivers, when the check runs, then it reports two cohesion and two cost, and it does not fail.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly verify --mode fast` prints one waiver total with its split, and a fixture whose retiring bead is closed while its waiver stands fails the check.

## Scope
- `.scripts/ratchet.py`
- `.scripts/check_module_size.py`
- `.scripts/check_comment_density.py`
- `tests/test_ratchet.py`

## Plan
- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: A second rebaseline on an entry already at its frozen count exits non-zero naming the entry and its count, against a control first rebaseline that is admitted.

The 'three times in one session' half has no in-tree artifact. The three incidents are named only in the tracker description and in the .scripts/headroom.py docstring (lines 10-14); basicly.d/ holds 63 rebaseline records (positive control) and none for basicly-jn1x, basicly-c357 or basicly-ejdm. The claim holds only in the explicit-path mode; nothing in the sentence tells a consumer which mode prints what.

unsupported.claim: Measured on this tree at the time it landed: 163 of 433 modules
unsupported.why: The numbers are true of the tree about to be tagged, but not of the landing tree, and the repo's own record says so: basicly.d/basicly-co64.toml:34 states '164 of 426 tracked modules' as the measurement for commit 5fb905e7. So 'at the time it landed' attributes a release-tree measurement to a landing that measured something else. I could not re-derive the 164/426 figure without checking out the landing commit, which would mutate the tree.

body.post_ship_action: Before the tag moves I recommend the owner correct changelog.d/basicly-at5tph.fixed.md: drop the "Every ledger write is attributed" headline and the "so ... is a fact" clause down to the seam the fix actually covers, and replace 1,078 with a figure a reader can re-derive (the 2,642 that check_ledger_fsck.py prints). If the tag moves as written, then after it moves: (1) file a bug against basicly-jr0l for the two unwired append sites — src/basicly/tracker.py:528 and .basicly/core/kit/tracker/commands.py:108 — with the acceptance criterion that no live append site may omit an actor, bound by a test that enumerates the call sites rather than the two seam functions; (2) file a docs-correction record against the published note naming the overclaim, since a shipped changelog is not edited in place; (3) record today's `uv run python .scripts/check_ledger_fsck.py` line (2,642) as the baseline and re-read it after the next loop lane — if the unattributed count has risen past 2,642 the remaining paths are still writing, which is the falsifiable check the release note lacks.

unsupported.claim: **Every ledger write is attributed.**
unsupported.why: Falsified on the shipping tree by the ledger this release itself wrote. Two live append paths pass no actor and so land the UNATTRIBUTED_ACTOR sentinel rather than an identity: src/basicly/tracker.py:528 `events.append(ledger, [draft], redact=redact.redact_committed, held_lock=lock)` (reached from tracker.add_artifact via src/basicly/artifact_record.py:137), and .basicly/core/kit/tracker/commands.py:108 `return events.append(ledger, list(drafts), redact=redact, held_lock=lock)`, which every kit write verb funnels through (commands.py:172,205,230,261,314,349,383). commands.py is named in the bead's own Scope and was never touched by the merge cc0a3fec. The proof is on disk: `python3 -c "import json,glob;[print(json.loads(l)['ts'],json.loads(l)['kind'],json.loads(l)['record']) for f in sorted(glob.glob('.basicly/ledger/events-*.jsonl')) for l in open(f) if l.strip() and json.loads(l).get('actor')=='unattributed:no-actor-supplied']"` prints two `artifact` events at 2026-08-21T14:35:56Z (basicly-co64) and 14:40:35Z (basicly-twfj) — both written after the resolver landed. I looked for a test or gate binding attribution over all append sites and found none: the closest, tests/test_owned_write_actor.py::test_no_event_the_seam_writes_can_carry_an_empty_actor, is docstring-titled "the property, over every write path" but exercises only owned_write.create and owned_write.append, and .scripts/check_ledger_fsck.py counts the population without failing on it.

unsupported.claim: empty on all 1,078 events written since the flip
unsupported.why: No committed instrument re-derives 1,078, and the lane's own record contradicts it. The provenance cross-tab gives 762 empty `engine` rows and 460 empty `dual-write` rows (1,222 post-import), 1,418 empty `EXTRACTED` rows, 2,640 empty in total; `uv run python .scripts/check_ledger_fsck.py` prints 2,642 for the census population. basicly.d/basicly-at5tph.toml:3-6 measures "2,608 of this ledger's 6,383 events" and line 22 says outright "the bead measured 1,078 for the same population" — i.e. the lane knew the figure had decayed and the changelog fragment shipped the decayed one anyway. I found no script, test or gate that computes an actor census restricted to "since the flip".

unsupported.claim: so "every state change is attributable" is a fact rather than a declared field
unsupported.why: Same refutation as the headline, and the conclusion is stronger than the mechanism it is drawn from. Attribution now holds at the owned-write seam only; add_artifact and the kit command verbs are state changes that remain unattributed, and 2,642 of 6,437 committed events name no actor. Nothing binds the property: .scripts/check_ledger_fsck.py:76-78 documents the census as "Reported and never failed", and tests/test_kit_tracker_fsck.py:821 asserts `report.clean, "an unattributed event is a census, never a finding to fail on"` — so the population is free to grow. .scripts/check_release_notes.py binds that a fragment exists ("145 owing a release note and each at its frozen entry"), never that its prose is true, and `docs_claims.py --check` reports "6 generated blocks current, 6 assertions current" without reading changelog.d at all.

## Context

Three instances on 2026-08-21, in three different code paths, all one shape: a gate refused, and what reached the operator named no gate.

```text
the salvage commit was rejected: protect-generated-commit...........Passed
routed: basicly-s07cgc -> error - routing failed: command failed (1): git commit -m ...
routed: basicly-co64   -> error - routing failed: command failed (1): git commit -m ...
```

The first prints a **passing** hook line as the rejection reason. The other two print the argv and the exit code and nothing else. In every case the real cause was one named check inside the captured output: markdownlint refusing a lane`s own gitignored scratch note in the first, `release-notes` naming the exact missing `changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md` in the other two.

## Why this costs more than it looks

Each one cost a diagnosis that the output already contained. The salvage case is worse than silence: a reader who trusts the line goes and looks at `protect-generated-commit`, which passed.

The repo already knows this class. `basicly-e84` closed on *"verify from explicit pass/fail lines not truncated output"*, and `basicly-lkzq` records that a hand-picked subset of checks reads exactly like the gate. This is the same rule turned inward: the engine`s own error text is doing to an operator what a truncated tail does to an agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a git command the engine runs fails because a hook refused, THE ENGINE SHALL name the failing check and its reported reason rather than the argv and the exit code.
- WHEN the captured output holds an explicit failure line, THE MESSAGE SHALL carry that line and SHALL NOT carry a passing line.
- WHEN no failure line can be identified, THE MESSAGE SHALL say so and name where the full output was written, so the fallback is honest rather than misleading.
- WHERE a lane close trips `release-notes`, THE MESSAGE SHALL carry the fix the gate already prints.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Drive a close whose `release-notes` gate refuses and read the failure name the check itself printed, against a control close that succeeds and prints no such line.

## Context

Found 2026-08-21 while recovering two lanes the spend bound stopped mid-flight. Both had committed-quality work staged and neither could commit:

```text
markdownlint............................................Failed
.basicly/usage/scratch/rn0o-3-plan.md:22 MD022/blanks-around-headings
.basicly/usage/scratch/rn0o-3-plan.md:23 MD032/blanks-around-lists
```

`.basicly/usage/.gitignore` holds `*`, so nothing under it is tracked or committable. The markdownlint hook globs `**/*.md !.venv/** !node_modules/**`, which reaches it anyway. A lane that writes itself a plan note - which the guidance encourages, and four of the five worktrees in this pass did - blocks every commit in its own worktree on a file that can never be committed.

One lane said so in its own transcript: *"I violated the scratch-file rule and it just bit me."* The rule it names is a prose rule; the gate is what actually fires, and it fires on the wrong population.

## Why this is the gate and not the lane

A machine-local, gitignored working file is not repository content. Linting it is the instrument reading outside its own population - the same class as counting a census file as part of its own census. The remedy is the glob, not more prose telling agents where to write.

Note the interaction with `basicly-jr0l.71`, which records a nested `node_modules` poisoning the same gate. Both are the same defect: the glob does not follow the ignore rules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the markdownlint hook runs, IT SHALL NOT lint a path git ignores.
- WHEN a lane writes a markdown note under `.basicly/usage/`, ITS COMMIT SHALL NOT be refused by markdownlint.
- WHEN a tracked markdown file breaks a rule, THE HOOK SHALL still refuse, and a test SHALL prove it on the same run that proves the exclusion.
- WHEN the hook reports its file count, THAT COUNT SHALL exclude the ignored paths, so the change is visible in the output rather than only in behaviour.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/markdownlint.py`
- `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
- `tests/test_hooks_markdownlint.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Write a deliberately malformed markdown file under `.basicly/usage/scratch/` and commit successfully, against a control malformed file at the repository root that the hook still refuses.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner verdict 2026-08-21 on the shipped Mode A page: *"visibility is zero. I do not see what features are being implemented, the visualization of the loop and where the current implementation is, in which state, I do not see the backlog, and I have no idea how to read any of it."*

The layout is a separate defect. This one is the data behind it. Measured on a snapshot from this repository:

```text
units      233 entries, fields: id, priority, status, title, type
           phase  = null on 233 of 233
           ready  = 0   on 233 of 233
lanes      ABSENT
session    ABSENT
asks       1 entry, fields: issue, kind, requested_at, subject, wait_id
repo       name only
```

So the loop position of every open unit is unknowable, the ready set is unknowable, the grant and its budget are unknowable, and an ask carries no question and no waiting time. A renderer cannot draw what the producer never sent.

## Why the producer is right to omit them, and what that means

`board_sections.units` states it: *"`phase` has the same authority problem `LaneFacts` documents, and `ready` is the tracker own derivation over a status vocabulary and the whole edge population... both stay absent until a caller supplies them."* That is the layer rule of architecture 34.1 - the layer above supplies the fact the layer below cannot honestly derive - and it must not be broken by giving `board_sections` a second spelling of `loop_state.derive_phase`.

**So the fix is the caller, never the section.** `build_document` takes the derivations as arguments, exactly as it already takes the lane and lock facts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the caller supplies a phase per record, EACH units row SHALL carry it, and the value SHALL come from `loop_state.derive_phase` rather than from a second derivation.
- WHEN the caller supplies the ready set, EACH units row SHALL carry `ready`, and `backlog` SHALL carry `ready` and `blocked`.
- WHEN a grant is live, `session` SHALL carry `grant_level`, `token_budget` and `spent_tokens`.
- WHEN a wait is pending, ITS asks row SHALL carry `question` and `waiting_s`.
- WHEN the repository is read, `repo` SHALL carry `branch`, `head` and `dirty`.
- WHERE a fact cannot be derived, THE SECTION SHALL stay absent rather than carry a zero, and a test SHALL prove the absence renders as absent.
- WHEN `basicly board validate` runs over the emitted document, IT SHALL report ok with no new violation.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_snapshot.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_usage.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `150000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html` then read the emitted snapshot and assert the first units row carries a real phase name, `backlog.ready` is positive, and `session.token_budget` is present under a live grant.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner verdict 2026-08-21 on the shipped Mode A page: *"the containers are too small for the content and they have to be scrolled - visibility is zero."*

The renderer emits one bordered box per schema key, each at a fixed height its content overflows, and repeats the same freshness sentence on all ten. The requirements document specifies the opposite: `### What appears on the TV` gives eight layout regions, each answering one question in under five seconds from six metres, on fixed-height rows that never reflow when a number changes.

**A layout count is not a section count.** The schema has 12 optional sections; the wall has regions, and one region may read several sections or none.

## The layout the owner chose

```text
1920x1080, no scrollbar, fixed rows

WATCH BAND    one line, five spellings, the only red on screen
THE LOOP      intake classify decompose build verify validate ship,
              a count per phase and the current position marked
IN FLIGHT     one card per live lane, left        | NEXT UP  ranked
              fixed size, truncating, never       | ready set, P and
              fewer than three shown, +N more     | id and title
FOOTER        backlog total with a closed bar and a per-priority
              histogram, then gates, spend and health as one strip
```

Reflows to a single column below 1280px so a laptop shows the same board.

## Six defects in the current render, all visible in one screenshot

1. `session`, `units`, `asks`, `health` and `events` are cut mid-row by a fixed-height container.
2. The freshness sentence repeats verbatim on all ten panels.
3. Every panel carries two ok badges, one on the title line and one on the freshness line.
4. `health` renders the list index as a row label; `by_priority` renders unsorted.
5. `events.text` overflows its column.
6. There is no red anywhere, so nothing distinguishes a calm screen from one with a person waiting on it.

## What this must not lose

The current render is honest and that half is right. Keep it: every value renders its own age, an absent section renders `not emitted by this producer` rather than a zero, the section inventory is derived from `board_schema.verdict` and never written a second time, and the page carries no external origin - no CDN, no framework, inline style and inline vanilla script only.

**A bar needs both of its numbers.** While a numerator or a denominator is absent, render the raw number and draw no bar.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the page renders at 1920x1080, NO REGION SHALL scroll and no content SHALL be cut without a `+N more` marker naming what was dropped.
- WHEN a value is rendered, ITS AGE SHALL be rendered with it, and the freshness sentence SHALL appear once rather than once per panel.
- WHEN every open unit carries a phase, THE LOOP REGION SHALL show a count per phase and mark where work currently sits.
- WHEN the ready set is known, THE NEXT UP REGION SHALL list it ranked with priority, id and title.
- WHEN a person is waiting on a decision, THE WATCH BAND SHALL say so in red, and red SHALL appear nowhere else.
- WHEN the snapshot is older than its declared staleness bound, THE WATCH BAND SHALL say STALE and SHALL NOT hide the last known values.
- WHEN a section the producer did not emit is drawn, IT SHALL read as absent rather than as zero.
- WHEN the viewport is below 1280px, THE LAYOUT SHALL reflow to one column.
- WHEN a proportional bar has an absent numerator or denominator, THE RENDERER SHALL draw the number and no bar.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/*.j2`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `190000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html`, rendered headless at 1920x1080 and at 1200x900, and every acceptance criterion read off the two screenshots.

payload.description:
## Context

Three records hit this on 2026-08-21: `basicly-sromom`, `basicly-ve0b7d` and `basicly-rn0o.5`. Each had a sibling worktree provisioned by `basicly worktree create <id>`, an agent built it, the work landed and verified green on main - and every one had to be closed by hand, because:

```text
issue:       basicly-rn0o.5 (task, open)
phase:       intake
worktree:    (none)
[blocked] intake -> intake: classify needs an agent-proposed work type
```

`loop_state.derive_phase` reads `build` off a **worktree binding**. `basicly worktree create` provisions the tree, the branch, the dependencies and the hooks, and records no binding. So the loop sees a record at intake with no work in flight, and no advance can land a merge that has already happened.

## Why this is a defect and not a workflow choice

The two provisioning paths disagree about the same fact. `loop`s own seeding advance calls `_ensure_child_worktrees`, which writes the binding, which is what derives `build`. The `worktree` verb is the documented way to isolate work by hand - `worktree-isolation` is a shipped skill that recommends it - and taking it silently forfeits every later advance.

The cost is not the hand close. It is that the record misses its landing gate, its ship checkpoint, its cost rollup and its release record, so a lane driven this way produces none of the evidence the loop exists to produce. All three of the above have a hand-written close reason where a `release-record` artifact should be.

## Two honest options, and the record should say which

Either the `worktree` verb writes the binding it just earned, or it refuses to provision for a record the loop is expected to drive and names the seeding advance instead. The first is smaller; the second is truer to *the engine disposes*. A third - documenting it - is refused: this is exactly a prose gate standing in for a default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly worktree create` provisions a worktree for a tracked record, THE ENGINE SHALL record the binding, so `loop status` derives `build` rather than `intake`.
- WHEN a record already carries a binding, A SECOND `worktree create` SHALL NOT write a second one.
- WHEN the work lands and an advance runs, IT SHALL reach the landing gate and the ship checkpoint exactly as a loop-seeded lane does.
- WHERE the chosen remedy is a refusal rather than a write, THE REFUSAL SHALL name the seeding advance that provisions correctly.
- WHEN a worktree is provisioned for no tracked record, THE BEHAVIOUR SHALL NOT change.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_worktree.py`
- `tests/test_loop_state.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Provision a worktree for a record with `basicly worktree create`, then read `basicly loop status <id>` showing phase `build` and the binding, against a control record with no worktree that still derives `intake`.

payload.description:
## Context

The wall layout landed and its loop region is the one question it still cannot answer. Measured on this repository 2026-08-21:

```text
THE LOOP   intake 8 · classify 0 · decompose 0 · build 0 · verify 0 · validate 0 · ship 0
           phase covers 8 of 234 units
```

`board_facts.PHASE_LIMIT` is 8, and the number is a cost rather than a taste. `loop_state.read_node_state` is the only route to `derive_phase`, and it reads the whole event log **seven times per record** - 591 ms over 20 records, measured - so 234 units is about 138 s against a 4.7 s build. The cap is at the ready front because that is the column a wall board is read for, and outside it `phase` stays absent rather than guessed, which is right.

The consequence is that a board whose whole point is *where is the work* reports every phase but intake as zero, and a reader cannot tell that from a genuinely idle factory.

## The shape of the fix

One fold, then a derivation per record over the folded state. `derive_phase` is a pure function of five values already in the fold; what costs is re-reading the log for each of them. The seam does not exist: `read_node_state` is per record by construction.

This is the same measurement discipline the fold already has - `board_snapshot` folds once and a spy pins the count - so the acceptance is a spy, not a stopwatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a phase map is built for every active record, THE READER SHALL fold the event log once, and a spy SHALL pin the fold count at one.
- WHEN the map is built, EVERY PHASE SHALL come from `loop_state.derive_phase` rather than from a second derivation.
- WHEN the map covers the whole active population, THE BUILD SHALL stay under the declared cap, and the demonstration SHALL print the measured duration.
- WHERE a record cannot be derived, ITS PHASE SHALL be absent rather than guessed, and the caption SHALL name how many units carry one.
- WHEN the cap is no longer needed, `PHASE_LIMIT` SHALL be removed rather than raised, so no reader is left believing a bound still applies.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_loop_state.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `140000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html` printing a build time under the cap, and the emitted snapshot carrying a phase on every active unit rather than on eight.

## Context

The wall layout landed green on its fixtures and clipped on first contact with real data. Measured 2026-08-21 at 1920x1080 on this repository:

- `HEALTH` renders its header and its content is cut off the bottom of the footer.
- The caption under the loop strip is cut to a partial line.

The cause is stated in the lane`s own report: *"the template`s row heights are hand-tuned px against the tallest content each row can hold; a future region gaining a line needs the screenshot re-run, not just the tests."* The fixture carried 12 gate checks and this tree has **36**, so `GATES` grew four rows and pushed `HEALTH` out.

The existing test asserts six fixed rows and one `minmax(0, 1fr)`, which catches a row losing its height and cannot catch a row going one line short of its content.

## Why a taller row is not the fix

A pixel tuned against today`s check count is the same defect one number along. The row has to be bounded by what it holds, or the content has to be bounded by the row with a `+N more` marker naming what was dropped - which is the rule the rest of the page already follows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a region holds more content than its row admits, IT SHALL render a `+N more` marker naming what was dropped, and SHALL NOT cut a line.
- WHEN the gate check count changes, NO OTHER REGION SHALL lose height.
- WHEN the page renders at 1920x1080 with this repository`s own snapshot, NO REGION SHALL be clipped, and a test SHALL assert it against a fixture carrying at least as many checks as the tree.
- WHEN a caption names a count, IT SHALL be fully visible.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/*.j2`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_footer.py`

- budget: `110000`
- depends on: none

## Context

Session retro 2026-08-21, two findings with a named control each. Filed after the fact so the change has a record: both landed in one commit.

## Finding one - a rendered surface was reported delivered without being looked at

Three board pages shipped in one day with every gate passing and the page unreadable: a schema dump, five clipped regions - four already clipped on the fixture the layout passed against - and a panel drawing zero over ten real edges. `quality-gate` says run it and read the output; for a rendered surface the output is an image, and reading the HTML is what produced all three.

Control: a **path-scoped** fragment `rendered-surfaces`, because the always-on tier had 8 characters of copilot headroom and architecture 12.2 says a cap warning means scope, never shrink. It cost `AGENTS.md` 1370 characters and the other two families nothing. Plus `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py`, which reports every element whose scroll size exceeds its client size.

Deliberately not a verify check: CI has no browser and a check that skips reads as a pass.

## Finding two - a lane branched behind a fix wrote a declaration that expired

`release-notes` reads the record from the shared ledger and the fragment from the lane`s own tree, so a record closed on base after a lane branched refuses every commit on that branch. Three lanes hit it; one answered by declaring the record invisible with a measured positive control that was true at its branch point and **false on arrival**.

Control: the refusal now names the fragment the base branch already holds and says rebase, so the incentive to invent an exemption is gone.

## What the instrument found on its own first honest run

Three false-positive classes, each removed with a reason rather than a tolerance bump: a declared `text-overflow: ellipsis` is not a clip, a box whose overflow is scrollable or visible is not a clip, and a 1920x1080 **window** renders a 1904x985 **viewport** - the last had already cost one lane a false 44px finding, so the script compensates rather than documenting it.

- WHEN a change touches a rendered surface, THE GUIDANCE SHALL say the rendering must be looked at, and SHALL cost the two families that scope nothing.
- WHEN an element hides content it cannot show, THE INSTRUMENT SHALL report it; WHEN the box scrolls or declares an ellipsis, IT SHALL NOT.
- WHEN the caller asks for a viewport, THE INSTRUMENT SHALL measure that viewport rather than a window of that size.
- WHEN `release-notes` refuses a record whose fragment is on the base branch, IT SHALL name the file and say rebase.
- WHEN no browser is installed, THE INSTRUMENT SHALL fail rather than skip.

## Context

Found 2026-08-21 from an operator screenshot of the running server: every region read `not emitted by this producer` while the same repository`s `board --out` was complete.

Measured side by side on one tree:

```text
                 served    emitted
units             232       232
  with phase        0       232
  with ready        0       229
backlog keys        5         7    (served omits ready, blocked)
repo keys           1         4    (served omits branch, head, dirty)
```

`board_cli._document` gathers session, repo, phases, readiness and questions and hands them to `build_document`. `board_serve.Board.refresh` called `build_document` with the lock facts alone. **Two producers against one contract, and the one a human actually looks at was the poorer.**

## The cause is a layer inversion this change introduced

`board_facts` was extracted *above* `board_serve` in the tier order, so the server cannot import the gatherers. Reaching for them would be an upward import the contract refuses - correctly.

## The fix, and it is the rule this codebase already states three times

The layer above supplies the fact the layer below cannot derive. `Board` takes a `build` callable; `cmd_serve` passes one closing over `_document`. The freshness stays the server`s, because a builder written for Mode A cannot know the cadence it is served at.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the server folds, THE DOCUMENT SHALL carry every fact `board --out` carries for the same tree.
- WHEN no builder is supplied, THE SERVER SHALL still fold, so a caller below this tier is not broken.
- WHEN the document is served, ITS FRESHNESS SHALL name the server`s own cadence rather than the builder`s.
- WHEN both paths run on one tree, A TEST SHALL assert the key sets agree, so a third producer cannot diverge in silence.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `tests/test_board_serve.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Fetch `/snapshot.json` from a running server and read the same phase and ready counts the emitted snapshot carries, against a control before the change reading zero.

## Context

Reported by the operator watching the live wall 2026-08-21, and it is the third instance of one defect: N producers, one contract, only one complete.

**Observed.** With no supervisor the board carried 232 of 232 phases, a ranked ready set and backlog ready/blocked. A supervised pass started and every one of those reverted to `not emitted by this producer`. IN FLIGHT stayed empty throughout.

## The chain, measured

```text
supervisor lock goes live
  -> board_serve.refresh() returns False without folding      (board_serve.py:159)
  -> the server serves the supervisor's file instead
  -> the tick calls _board_facts()                            (supervise.py:310)

```

So the richest producer is displaced by the poorest exactly when a human is watching. The handover of production is right - the supervisor has facts the server cannot see - but what it hands over is less than what it replaced.

**IN FLIGHT has never had a producer on this path.** `_board_facts` sets `lanes=None` with the reason at the declaration. Meanwhile `supervise.observe` at line 794 already builds `_lane_view` per adopted lane for `loop session`. The facts exist and do not reach the board.

- WHEN a supervisor holds the lock, THE SERVED DOCUMENT SHALL carry every section it carried without one, and a test SHALL compare the two.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner review of the live wall 2026-08-21, after the layout redraw landed. The layout is honest and legible; what it is not is *designed for a wall*. Five findings, each a design fault rather than a defect:

1. **The altitude is wrong.** 36 gate checks named individually is a debugging view. From six metres the answer is one token. That block is roughly 15% of the screen carrying nothing actionable, and the name-overlap defect (`basicly-uvpu6b`) is a symptom of forcing it in.
2. **Every region has identical visual weight** - same border, same scale, same mint outline. A wall ranks by urgency; this ranks by nothing. The orange ask band works only because it is the sole exception.
3. **Dead space dominates.** IN FLIGHT is 40% of the viewport and empty most of the time, announcing nothing three times with dashed placeholders, while NEXT UP is squeezed into a narrow column truncating every title.
4. **There is no time axis.** Totals with no trend. A reader cannot tell whether the factory is improving, which is the question a wall exists to answer.
5. **`148h 26m` does not read at distance.** The number that matters is six days.

## The principle

**A green state costs one token; an exception expands.** Everything below follows from it.

## The layout

```text
status bar   one line: repo, gates as ONE token, spend, throughput, freshness
the alarm    ~64px. Age is the headline, the id and kind beneath it
the loop     seven counts AND a proportional bar, so 212 against 1 is visible
running now  one card per lane; collapses to ONE LINE when empty, giving its
             width to next up, which then stops truncating
backlog      one line: total, closed bar, per-priority
events       one line
```

## The five decisions

- **Gates collapse to a single token** - `GATES GREEN`, or `1 FAILING: pytest` with the failing names only. This deletes the overlap defect rather than patching it.
- **Age is the headline.** `6 DAYS` at wall scale, not `148h 26m`.
- **RUNNING NOW collapses when empty** to `no lane dispatched - last landed 4m ago`, and its space goes to NEXT UP.
- **The loop gets a proportional bar** beneath the counts.
- **One throughput figure** in the status bar - closed today, derived from `status` events, the only honest trend the ledger supplies cheaply.

## What must not be lost

Everything the current page gets right: the freshness sentence once, an absent section naming the producer that did not emit it, the section inventory from `board_schema.verdict` and never a second list, no external origin, a bar needing both its numbers, every state on two non-colour channels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every gate passes, THE GATES REGION SHALL occupy one token; WHEN one fails, IT SHALL name the failing checks and only those.
- WHEN an ask is pending, ITS AGE SHALL be the largest text in that region, rendered in the coarsest honest unit.
- WHEN no lane is dispatched, THE RUNNING REGION SHALL occupy one line and the ready list SHALL take the reclaimed width.
- WHEN a ready title is rendered in the reclaimed width, THE TOP THREE SHALL NOT be truncated.
- WHEN the loop is rendered, EACH PHASE SHALL carry a bar proportional to its share of the active population.
- WHEN the ledger can supply it, THE STATUS BAR SHALL carry units closed today; WHERE it cannot, THE FIGURE SHALL be absent rather than zero.
- WHEN the page is measured, NEITHER the overflow instrument NOR the overlap instrument SHALL report anything at 1920x1080 or 1200x900.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/templates/board/*.j2`
- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_wall.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_footer.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `220000`
- depends on: `basicly-uvpu6b`
- demonstration: The board rendered headless from this repository's own snapshot at 1920x1080 and 1200x900, with both instruments reporting nothing, and each acceptance criterion read off the screenshots rather than off the tests.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while labelling a record for a supervised pass. The write reported `recorded:` and the field did not change. Three commands in a row reported success and wrote nothing:

```text
tracker write -- update basicly-fi1i7z --add-label live-demo   -> recorded:   labels stayed ''
tracker write -- update basicly-fi1i7z --labels    live-demo   -> recorded:   labels stayed ''
tracker write -- update basicly-fi1i7z --labels    live-pass-2 -> recorded:   labels became 'live-pass-2'
```

The events on the record explain it:

```text
field {"name":"labels","value":"live-demo"}     the first add
field {"name":"labels","value":""}              the remove
                                                 the second add: no event at all
```

## The cause is documented and this is it biting

Architecture 32.2: *"The id is a digest over the kind, the payload and the generation. It deliberately excludes the timestamp. A replay of the same logical write is therefore idempotent. The trap that buys is documented, not hidden: a re-record of an identical fact is swallowed, so a genuine reopen needs a new generation."*

So **an add, then a remove, then the same add again is permanently stuck at removed.** The third write is byte-identical to the first, its digest already exists, and it is swallowed. The fold takes the last event in canonical order, which is the removal.

This is not specific to labels. Any field driven to value A, then to B, then back to A has the same shape, and so does a close then reopen then close.

## Why it costs more than a re-typed command

The seam prints `recorded:`. Nothing distinguishes *appended* from *already had this exact event*, so a caller reads success and moves on. It cost three commands and a wrong diagnosis here; on a status field it would leave a record in a state the operator believes they changed.

## The generation exists and nothing reaches it

`events.event_id_for` takes a generation precisely so a genuine re-record can be distinguished. No write verb exposes it, so a caller has no way to say "yes, again, on purpose".

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a write produces an event whose id the ledger already holds, THE SEAM SHALL say so rather than printing `recorded:`.
- WHEN a caller means the re-record genuinely, THERE SHALL be a way to say so, and the resulting event SHALL fold to the intended value.
- WHEN a field is driven A then B then A, THE FOLDED VALUE SHALL be A.
- WHERE the swallow is correct - a true duplicate replay - THE BEHAVIOUR SHALL NOT change, because idempotent replay is the property the digest exists for.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 looking at the live wall: "I do not see any factory loop work visualization". Four lanes were running at the time. The board showed none of them working.

## What the operator sees against what the supervisor prints

The supervisor's own terminal, same moment, same four lanes:

```text
running:  basicly-kn4rip 67s 678828 tok [This file already has a family of "refuse a write that recor...]
```

The served snapshot, same moment, per lane, in full:

```json
{"branch":"harness/basicly-6oa3mt","id":"basicly-6oa3mt","live":true,"phase":"build","status":"open"}
```

Elapsed, spend and what the lane is doing reach the terminal and do not reach the board.

## The cause, measured

`board_facts.lane_facts` builds each card from `supervise.lane_view` alone (`src/basicly/board_facts.py:230-246`). `LaneView` carries `last_agent`, `last_outcome`, `last_run_at` and `last_tokens` (`src/basicly/supervise.py`, the `LaneView` dataclass) - every one of them the **last finished run**. A lane on its first dispatch has finished nothing, so all four fold to empty and the card drops the keys.

The live facts exist and are not read. `supervise.inflight_spend()` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:2359`) returns tokens-so-far per running lane and `supervise.inflight_activity()` (`:2366`) returns what each is doing. Both read `_LIVE_LANES` under `_LIVE_LOCK`, which is **process-local** - and since `basicly-bd4epr` the producer is the supervisor's own tick, so it runs in the process that holds them. `_inflight_note` (`:2130`) already calls both for the terminal line.

## The contract has the slots

`.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json` declares sixteen keys on a lane: `id`, `phase`, `status`, `agent`, `model`, `live`, `started_at`, `elapsed_s`, `tokens`, `cost_usd`, `context_used`, `context_window`, `rework_attempt`, `rework_allowance`, `branch`, `note`. `board_sections.LaneFacts` declares eight and the producer fills five. So this is not a schema change and not a design question - it is a producer filling five of sixteen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is running and the tick emits, THE LANE CARD SHALL carry the elapsed time, the tokens spent so far and the activity line, taken from the live stream rather than the last finished run.
- WHEN a lane has reported nothing yet, THE CARD SHALL omit the figure rather than state a zero, on the rule `_inflight_note` already states.
- WHEN a lane has a recorded agent or model, THE CARD SHALL carry it, so a reader can tell which agent works on which unit.
- WHEN the producer is not the supervisor tick, THE LIVE FIELDS SHALL be omitted rather than invented, because `_LIVE_LANES` is process-local and a second process holds none.
- WHERE a field is omitted, THE OMISSION SHALL not be reported to a human in producer vocabulary.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `130000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Start a supervised pass with a lane running, fetch `/snapshot.json`, and read the elapsed time, the tokens and the activity line on the lane card against the same three figures on the supervisor's own `running:` line at the same moment.
payload.title: a lane card reports the last finished run so a running lane looks idle
