## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "we have the id, priority and description, but we do not have a feature or epic name that is descriptive for the human. I cannot distinguish what each of these work items is implementing as I do not know with which feature it is connected."

A wall row today is `P1 | basicly-a4q3.10 | Carry a ranked kill list and its discriminator on a change summary`. Nothing on it says which feature that serves.

## The fact is already on the wire

Measured against the live `/snapshot.json` on 2026-08-22:

```text
parent-child edges in graph.edges : 544
distinct parents they resolve to  : 19, of which 15 are epic and 4 are feature
ready units                       : 187
  resolve to a parent             : 145  (77%)
  orphans with no parent at all   : 42   (23%)
```

The edge direction is `from` = child, `to` = parent. `units[]` already carries `title` and `type` for each of those parents. So the epic a row belongs to needs **no new producer field** - it is a fold over two arrays the document already serves.

The fourteen roots that own the ready set, by how many ready descendants each has: `e2mz` 37, `jr0l` 26, `u2hl` 20, `vkh0` 17, `tcmy` 16, `a4q3` 9, `imnu` 4, `u6jq` 3, `ze8z` 3, `a3ab` 3, `m4zv` 2, `kjc5` 2, `rn0o` 2, `agzx` 1.

## Why grouping rather than a column

Fourteen groups over 187 rows. A per-row epic column repeats the same long title 37 times for one epic and costs horizontal width the title needs. A group heading states it once. The 42 orphans become their own group, which makes a second fact visible that a column would hide: a quarter of the ready set is attached to no feature at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the wall renders a ready set, IT SHALL group the rows under the epic or feature each resolves to, and each heading SHALL carry that parent's own title and its ready count.
- WHEN a unit resolves to no parent, IT SHALL appear under one heading that names it as unattached, with a count.
- WHEN a chain has more than one level, THE HEADING SHALL name the root ancestor, not the immediate parent.
- WHEN the graph holds a cycle, THE FOLD SHALL terminate and the affected unit SHALL be reported as unattached rather than looping.
- WHERE grouping is applied, THE URGENCY ORDER THE WALL ALREADY RANKS BY SHALL be preserved within each group and SHALL decide the order of the groups themselves.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `tests/test_board_wall.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render the live board and read the wall, checking that a row under a heading names an epic whose id is the root ancestor of that row's id in `graph.edges`, and that the unattached group's count matches the orphan count computed from the same document.
payload.title: a wall row does not name the feature it belongs to so a human cannot tell what it implements

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 looking at the live wall: "I also do not know what does '6 days' in orange mean."

The band reads `▲6 DAYS / 1 WAITING ON A PERSON / basicly-b2n2 · checkpoint · ship · 160h 16m`.

## Three faults, measured

**The colour carries no information.** `band()` (`src/basicly/board_regions.py:145-181`) resolves state in a fixed precedence - withheld, absent, waiting, calm - and `WAITING` binds to `--orange` at `src/basicly/board_wall.py:73`. The state is `WAITING` whenever the `asks` section is drawn and its list is non-empty. **There is no duration threshold.** A five-second-old ask paints exactly the same orange as a six-day-old one; only the headline text scales. Orange is this page's only alarm channel (`board_wall.py:22-24`), so the one channel that should mean "act now" fires on existence.

**One quantity is stated twice in two units.** The headline is `coarse(waited)` and the detail is `duration(_waited(ask, now))`, both computed from the same `_waited(asks[0], now)` (`board_regions.py:172-179`). Measured on a probe render: 577,020 s renders as `6 DAYS` and as `160h 17m`. The second adds no fact.

**Nothing on the page says what it is.** A full-text scan of `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2` finds no tooltip, no `title=` attribute and no legend entry for the band. `legend()` (`board_footer.py:263-274`) glosses section render-states only.

## What the reader needs instead

The band is the page's only alarm. A reader must learn from it, without a second source: that the factory is stopped, that a person is what stops it, how long that has been true, whether that is normal or bad, and what to do next. Today it supplies the third of those and half the first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an ask has waited, THE BAND STATE SHALL be chosen from the wait duration against declared thresholds, so a short wait and a long wait do not paint the same colour.
- WHEN the band names a duration, IT SHALL state that duration once, in one unit.
- WHEN the band renders, IT SHALL state in plain words what is waiting and what a reader would do about it, without abbreviation a reader must already know.
- WHERE the thresholds live, THEY SHALL be configuration this repository declares rather than constants inside the region, and the test SHALL drive a wait across each boundary.
- WHERE no ask is pending, THE BAND SHALL NOT claim an alarm state.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render the board with an ask injected at each side of every declared threshold and read the band's colour and words at each, against a control render with no ask pending.
payload.title: the alarm band fires on existence not on severity and states one number twice

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "I also hate the squares with a dot in them indicators (signals)."

The page's last row reads `SECTIONS ●generator ●repo ●session ●lanes ●asks ●gates ●spend ●health ●backlog ●units ●graph ●events  KEY ●renders ◇withheld, and says why ○not emitted by this producer`, and the same glyphs appear inline beside REPO, RUN, SPEND, CLOSED TODAY and DEP EDGES.

## What the row is

`inventory()` (`src/basicly/board_footer.py:253-260`) lists the twelve named sections of the `harness-board/v1` schema and paints each one's render verdict. Its own docstring states the intent: *a section no region reads still reports itself here*. So the row is a **producer self-report**: it tells a producer author which parts of their document this consumer accepted. It is developer diagnostics, and it occupies a full row of an operator's dashboard.

`legend()` (`board_footer.py:263-274`) then glosses three glyphs, one of them with the string `not emitted by this producer` - engine vocabulary naming a role the reader does not have.

## The glyph is provably redundant

`src/basicly/board_wall.py:14-15` states the design: each state carries a glyph, a border style and a colour, and the rules are generated one-to-one from `STATES` into `.state-<key>` (`board_page.html.j2:506-514`). The glyph is one of three channels for the same fact. Removing it removes no information.

Nine glyphs are painted across the page: `●` U+25CF renderable, `◇` U+25C7 withheld, `○` U+25CB absent, `▶` U+25B6 live, `◆` U+25C6 stale, `▲` U+25B2 waiting, `◎` U+25CE calm, `✕` U+2715 failed, and `·` U+00B7 as a separator. A reader is given a gloss for three of them.

## The boundary this must respect

The diagnostic is real and a producer author needs it. It has a home already: `/snapshot.json` carries the document, and the schema verdict is computable from it. The claim here is about **placement**, not about deleting the check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a human loads the board, THE PAGE SHALL NOT paint the section inventory or the render-state key as a standing row.
- WHEN a section is genuinely withheld or absent, THE AFFECTED REGION SHALL say so in words a reader without the schema can act on, and SHALL NOT use the words `producer`, `emitted`, `section` or `withheld`.
- WHEN a producer author needs the verdict, IT SHALL remain reachable, and the record SHALL name where.
- WHERE a state is still marked, THE MARK SHALL use at most one channel beside colour, not three.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `tests/test_board_footer.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: `basicly-v8jwf0`
- demonstration: Load the rendered page and check that no section inventory row and no render-state key is painted, that a deliberately withheld section still produces a readable sentence in its own region, and that the verdict is still reachable where the record says it is.

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 as part of "we need improvements all over the board". The wall shows fourteen of one hundred and eighty seven ready units and prints `NEXT UP — +173 MORE READY`.

## The cap is fixed to the smallest supported wall

`board_regions.py:83-97` declares `READY_SLOTS_WIDE = 14` and `READY_SLOTS = 8`, and its own comment states the arithmetic: *14 rows of 24.1px under an 18.2px heading is what fits ... against 26 at 1920x1080*, and *both figures are the shortest wall this layout claims, not the roomiest*.

So on a 1920x1080 screen the region draws 14 rows where 26 fit. Measured on a probe render at 1920x1080: exactly 14 `<tr>` elements. Roughly half the available height is left blank, by construction rather than by overflow.

Row geometry, measured from `board_page.html.j2:412-416`: font-size 17px, line-height 1.3, padding 1px 0, giving 24.1px per row under an 18.2px heading.

## Why a fixed cap was right and is not now

A fixed cap cannot overflow, and the overflow instrument (`.scripts/check_render_overflow.py`) exists because four board pages shipped clipped. Choosing the smallest wall was the safe answer before that instrument existed. It now exists, so a fit computed from the viewport can be **measured** at each width the layout claims rather than assumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the wall renders at a given viewport height, THE NUMBER OF ROWS DRAWN SHALL be derived from that height and the measured row geometry, not from a constant.
- WHEN the derived count exceeds what fits, THE RENDER SHALL NOT clip, and `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report neither overflow nor overlap at every width the layout claims.
- WHEN rows are omitted, THE HEADING SHALL still state how many, as it does now.
- WHERE the viewport is unknown to the producer, THE FIT SHALL be resolved where the viewport is known rather than guessed at build time.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: `basicly-v8jwf0`
- demonstration: Render at 1440x900, 1600x1200 and 1920x1080, count the rows drawn at each, and run `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` at each width reading both the overflow line and the overlap line.

[measurement correction 2026-08-22] The 544-edge figure in the description was read off the SERVED document's graph.edges, which board_snapshot.py:300 filters to edges touching the drawn set. The ledger holds 688 distinct parent-child edges (697 raw events, 9 re-assertions, no record has two parents, zero parent-child retractions ever). Re-measured against the ready set: 149 of 188 resolve to an epic or feature root, 43 are orphans, and 39 of those have no epic ancestor at any depth. No cycles exist today.

THE TRAP THIS RECORD MUST AVOID: build the child-to-parent map from the PRE-FILTER edges list at board_snapshot.py:291, never from document['graph'], or a chain passing through a closed intermediate ancestor breaks and the row silently reports the wrong epic or none.

COST: no extra ledger read is needed. board_snapshot._read_and_fold (board_snapshot.py:157-178) already extracts every live edge as (source, kind, target) triples via board_sections.edge_triples in the same single fold that produces units and titles, and the root titles come from the records already bound at board_snapshot.py:175. The root walk is dict-chasing over data already in memory, memoisable across shared ancestors. That is cheaper than loop_state.phase_map, which needs a second all_views fold this path does not otherwise make.

NO SHORT LABEL EXISTS. There is no component, epic, code or short-name field on any record. Only 31 percent of open records carry any label and the values in use are phase and wave tags. The resolved root's own title is the only answer, so the design must handle long titles rather than hope for a short one.

The row shape to widen is Item at board_wall.py:144-150, which carries priority, ident and title and nothing else; it is built at board_regions.py:315-319.

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "I do not see any factory loop work visualization."

The page's largest region is headed `THE LOOP` and paints seven counters with progress bars: INTAKE 214, CLASSIFY 1, DECOMPOSE 19, BUILD 0, VERIFY 1, VALIDATE 0, SHIP 0.

## It is the backlog, not the loop

Measured against the live `/snapshot.json` while four lanes were building:

```text
phase histogram over units[]  : intake 215, decompose 19, build 4, verify 1, classify 1
sum                           : 240
backlog.active                : 240
```

The two are the same number because they are the same population. The region bins **every active record in the backlog** by phase. 215 of 240 sit in `intake` for the single reason that they have never been classified - `intake` is where a record is born, so the largest bar on the page measures how much of the backlog has never been touched.

Meanwhile the four lanes actually running contribute 4 to `build`, and nothing on the region distinguishes them from any other record that happens to be at that phase.

## What a loop visualization has to answer

A reader watching a factory wants to know what **this pass** is doing: which units it selected, where each one is now, which moved since the last beat, and which is stuck. None of those are answerable from a backlog histogram. The session's own selection is already on the document - `session.root`, and the lane rows - and the region does not use it.

## The counters are also not comparable

A progress bar implies a denominator. `intake` at 215 and `ship` at 0 share an axis on which 215 is not progress and 0 is not failure; they are two unrelated inventories drawn as if they were stages of one flow. A record at `intake` may never enter the loop at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a supervised pass is running, THE LOOP REGION SHALL show the units that pass selected and where each is, and SHALL distinguish them from records that merely share a phase.
- WHEN no pass is running, THE REGION SHALL say so rather than showing a backlog histogram under a heading that claims a loop.
- WHEN a counter is drawn with a bar, THE BAR SHALL have a stated denominator, and counters that share no denominator SHALL NOT share an axis.
- WHEN a unit has moved phase since the previous beat, THAT MOVEMENT SHALL be visible, because a still picture of positions cannot distinguish working from wedged.
- WHERE the backlog histogram is still wanted, IT SHALL be labelled as the backlog and SHALL NOT occupy the region a reader reads for the running pass.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `130000`
- depends on: `basicly-0hxck3`
- demonstration: Start a supervised pass over a known label, render the board, and read the loop region against the supervisor's own reported lane set, then stop the pass and read the region again.
payload.title: the loop region shows the whole backlog binned by phase instead of the running pass

## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while reading the live wall with four lanes building. The header's RUN field showed `basicly-jr0l · open · L3 · 0%` for the whole of a nine minute pass.

## Measured

At a moment when the supervisor's own terminal reported the four lanes at 4,977,290 / 6,981,880 / 4,583,052 / 5,390,046 tokens - about 21.9M live - the served snapshot carried:

```json
"session": {"grant_level":"L3","token_budget":150000000,"spent_tokens":0,"supervised":true,...}
```

## The cause

`spent_tokens` folds **recorded** run tokens, and a run record is written when a lane **ends**. A lane that has run for nine minutes and spent seven million tokens has recorded nothing, so it contributes nothing. The figure is correct for what it measures and wrong for what a reader takes it to mean.

## Two consequences, and the second is the expensive one

**The bar reads 0% for the whole of a pass.** An operator watching a thirty minute lane sees no movement at all, then a step change at landing. The one number that says "how much of the grant is gone" is the one number that cannot move while it is being spent.

**A ceiling that cannot fire.** The grant's budget bounds `spent_tokens`. If the recorded figure only advances at landing, the ceiling cannot stop a pass mid-lane - it can only decline to start the next one. This is the same shape as `basicly-jr0l.22`, reached by a different route: a bound whose input does not change while the thing it bounds is happening.

## The live figures exist

`supervise.inflight_spend()` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:2359`) returns tokens-so-far for each running lane, and `supervise.retired_spend()` (`:2373`) returns a monotonic total from lanes that have ended but not yet recorded. Both read `_LIVE_LANES` under `_LIVE_LOCK`, process-local to the supervisor - and since `basicly-bd4epr` the producer is the supervisor's own tick, so both are reachable from the producer.

They are not the same denomination as the recorded figure and the repository already knows by how much: `src/basicly/supervise.py:2379-2384` records that the live per-turn sum over-reports the run record, with four measured lane ratios. So the live figure is an over-estimate of known direction, which is the safe direction for a ceiling and must be labelled rather than silently substituted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is running, THE SESSION SPEND THE BOARD SHOWS SHALL advance, and SHALL NOT stay at the value it held when the lane started.
- WHEN a live figure and a recorded figure are both available, THE DOCUMENT SHALL carry both and SHALL name which is which, because they are different denominations.
- WHEN the live figure is shown against a budget, IT SHALL be marked as an over-estimate, with the measured direction stated.
- WHERE the recorded figure is what a gate binds on, THAT GATE SHALL NOT change behaviour under this record; this changes what is reported, not what is enforced.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-0hxck3`
- demonstration: Start a supervised pass, read the session spend from `/snapshot.json` at three points during one lane's run, and check the figure advances between them and agrees in direction with the supervisor's own reported per-lane totals at the same moments.
payload.title: the session spend meter reads zero for the whole of a pass so the grant bar cannot move

I implemented the bead's implied fix in .basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py: treat a colliding event id as a replay only when the record already states the fact, else walk Draft.generation to a free id. It passes the bead's demonstration exactly - labels A->B->A folds to A, status closed->open->closed folds to closed, and a single identical write still appends once. It is still wrong. Two tests pin the opposite on purpose: test_replaying_the_same_drafts_appends_nothing re-appends 3 events under such a rule, and test_a_repeated_status_needs_a_generation_or_it_is_swallowed asserts the swallow 'in both directions' as a documented property. The reason is not a fixable detail: replaying the history 'A, B' and deliberately re-recording 'A' after 'B' leave the ledger byte-identical, so no fact in it separates them. AC3 and AC4 are jointly unsatisfiable for any implicit rule. The refuted patch and the written-up finding are in .basicly/usage/scratch/refuted-state-based-replay.patch and .basicly/usage/scratch/finding-ac3-is-unachievable-implicitly.md.

The second, independent blocker is measured headroom. payload.description:
## Context

Owner directive 2026-08-22, after reading the live wall while four lanes were building: *"We need improvements all over the board. I give you the autonomy to iterate and build an enterprise professional board that is informative to humans so that agents can work unattended and we always know what is going on and on what thing are agents working."*

Seven complaints were named. Each was traced to code and filed as its own record. This record exists because nine independent patches on the present layout would not add up to the board the directive asks for. It is the design those nine build toward, and it is approved.

## The question the board must answer

**What is happening right now, and does it need me?**

Everything on the page earns its space against that question. A reader arriving cold must learn, without a second source: whether the factory is running, what each agent is working on this second, whether anything is stuck, and what a stuck thing needs from them.

## The principles

**The reader is an operator, never a producer author.** No word on the page may name a role the reader does not hold. `producer`, `emitted`, `section`, `withheld` and `renderable` are engine vocabulary and do not appear. A diagnostic a producer author needs is reachable, and it is not a standing row.

**A state is worth one channel, not three.** The present design gives every state a glyph, a border style and a colour for the same fact, and says so at `board_wall.py:14-15`. Colour plus a word replaces all three.

**A quantity is stated once, in one unit.** The present band states one wait as `6 DAYS` and as `160h 16m`.

**Colour means severity, not existence.** The page's alarm channel fires today whenever an ask exists. A five second wait and a six day wait must not paint the same.

**Space is spent on what is uncertain.** A green state is a word. An exception expands. This continues the principle `basicly-7ogfbq` landed rather than replacing it.

**Every figure names its own denomination.** A live token estimate and a recorded token figure are different quantities. Where both exist, both are shown and each is named.

## The layout, top to bottom

**1. Status line.** Repo, branch, head, the gate verdict as `GATES n/n`, and how fresh the document is. One line, recessive.

**2. The alarm, only when there is one.** Its severity comes from the wait duration against declared thresholds. It states in plain words what has stopped, that a person is what stops it, how long, and the command that answers it. Absent when nothing waits.

**3. RUNNING NOW - the hero region.** One card per adopted lane, carrying: the unit id, the feature it serves, its phase, the agent and model running it, how long it has run, what it has spent, and **the last thing it said**. That last field is what tells a working lane from a wedged one, and no other field can.

**4. The grant.** One bar: live spend against the budget, with the live figure named as an estimate that reads high, and the recorded figure named as the one that lands at completion.

**5. NEXT UP, grouped by the feature each row serves.** A heading per epic with its ready count, rows beneath. Units attached to no feature form their own group with a count, because that count is itself a finding - 45 of 190 today. Depth is spent on the highest-priority features and the row budget is computed from the viewport, not fixed.

**6. Footer.** Backlog totals, agent health, lifetime spend. No producer diagnostics.

## What was built and measured

A working mockup was generated from the live `/snapshot.json` and the supervisor's own terminal line, and every figure in it is real. It renders clean at 1200, 1440 and 1920 - `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` reports neither overflow nor overlap at any of the three.

Two fields in it come from the supervisor's terminal rather than the document, and that is exactly what `basicly-0hxck3` fixes. The grant bar reads 20.7% where the live board reads 0%, and that is `basicly-wctp0g`.

## The children

- `basicly-0hxck3` the lane card, which is the hero region's producer
- `basicly-eaw1dy` the feature name on a row
- `basicly-v8jwf0` the alarm band's severity and wording
- `basicly-jbd80w` the producer diagnostics leaving the human surface
- `basicly-ffm2yp` the row budget computed from the viewport
- `basicly-a68ggd` the loop region showing the pass rather than the backlog
- `basicly-wctp0g` the spend meter that can move while a lane runs

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every child has landed, A READER ARRIVING COLD SHALL be able to say what each agent is working on and whether anything needs them, from the page alone.
- WHEN the page renders, IT SHALL contain none of the words `producer`, `emitted`, `withheld` or `renderable`.
- WHEN a figure is shown, ITS DENOMINATION SHALL be stated where two denominations exist.
- WHEN the page renders at every width the layout claims, `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report neither overflow nor overlap.
- WHERE a child would satisfy its own criteria while contradicting this design, THIS DESIGN SHALL win and the child SHALL be re-scoped rather than landed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `src/basicly/board_footer.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
payload.title: raise the board to an enterprise operator surface that says what every agent is doing

payload.text: [owner-decision 2026-08-22] Asked which of three row budgets to build; the answer is fill the viewport, deepest first. Compute how many rows fit at the actual height and spend them on the highest-priority features rather than dividing them equally across features. The two options declined were a fixed count per feature (breadth over depth, predictable height) and dropping the general wall to show only the running pass. This decides the AC that says the count is derived from the viewport.

## Context

Observed 2026-08-22 during a four-lane supervised pass. `git status --short` in the base checkout reported:

```text
?? .basicly/ledger/.events.lock
```

## The file is transient and unignored

`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py:176` declares `LOCK_NAME = ".events.lock"`. The file is created and removed around a ledger write, so it exists only for the width of one append. The reading above caught a lane mid-write against the shared ledger.

It is **not** matched by any rule in `.gitignore`, confirmed with `git check-ignore -v`.

## Why this is worth a line

`.gitignore` states the governing rule twice in its own comments, at line 47 - *an untracked one would block every landing (basicly-jr0l.7)* - and at line 81 - *a checkout carries dirt outside the tracker, so an untracked one blocks every landing*. Both were written about exactly this class of file. `.basicly/ledger/snapshot.jsonl`, `checkpoint-*.jsonl` and `redirect` are all ignored on that reasoning; the lock is the one member of the family that was missed.

The exposure is a race, not a standing failure: a base-cleanliness check that samples during an append sees a dirty tree and refuses. With one writer the window is negligible. With four lanes writing a shared ledger it is not, and the failure it produces is a landing refused for a file that has already ceased to exist - which is the hardest kind to diagnose, because reproducing it means catching the same window.

## Not yet fixed, and why

`.gitignore` is on this repository's explicit-confirmation list. The one-line rule is not applied here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the tracker holds its append lock, A CLEANLINESS CHECK OF THE BASE CHECKOUT SHALL NOT report the checkout dirty.
- WHEN the rule is added, IT SHALL name the lock exactly and SHALL NOT widen to a pattern that could hide a real ledger file.
- WHERE the rule is added, A COMMENT SHALL state why, consistent with the two neighbouring comments that state the same rule.

## Scope

- `.gitignore`

## Plan

- integrity: `L1`
- budget: `20000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Hold the tracker's append lock, run the base cleanliness check, and read a clean verdict, against a control run with a genuinely untracked file present that must still report dirty.

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 looking at the live wall: "I do not see any factory loop work visualization". Four lanes were running at the time. The board showed none of them working.

## What the operator sees against what the supervisor prints

The supervisor's own terminal, same moment, same four lanes:

```text
running:  basicly-kn4rip 67s 678828 tok [This file already has a family of "refuse a write that recor...]
```

The served snapshot, same moment, per lane, in full:

```json
{"branch":"harness/basicly-6oa3mt","id":"basicly-6oa3mt","live":true,"phase":"build","status":"open"}
```

Elapsed, spend and what the lane is doing reach the terminal and do not reach the board.

## The cause, measured

`board_facts.lane_facts` builds each card from `supervise.lane_view` alone (`src/basicly/board_facts.py:230-246`). `LaneView` carries `last_agent`, `last_outcome`, `last_run_at` and `last_tokens` (`src/basicly/supervise.py`, the `LaneView` dataclass) - every one of them the **last finished run**. A lane on its first dispatch has finished nothing, so all four fold to empty and the card drops the keys.

The live facts exist and are not read. `supervise.inflight_spend()` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:2359`) returns tokens-so-far per running lane and `supervise.inflight_activity()` (`:2366`) returns what each is doing. Both read `_LIVE_LANES` under `_LIVE_LOCK`, which is **process-local** - and since `basicly-bd4epr` the producer is the supervisor's own tick, so it runs in the process that holds them. `_inflight_note` (`:2130`) already calls both for the terminal line.

## The contract has the slots

`.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json` declares sixteen keys on a lane: `id`, `phase`, `status`, `agent`, `model`, `live`, `started_at`, `elapsed_s`, `tokens`, `cost_usd`, `context_used`, `context_window`, `rework_attempt`, `rework_allowance`, `branch`, `note`. `board_sections.LaneFacts` declares eight and the producer fills five. So this is not a schema change and not a design question - it is a producer filling five of sixteen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is running and the tick emits, THE LANE CARD SHALL carry the elapsed time, the tokens spent so far and the activity line, taken from the live stream rather than the last finished run.
- WHEN a lane has reported nothing yet, THE CARD SHALL omit the figure rather than state a zero, on the rule `_inflight_note` already states.
- WHEN a lane has a recorded agent or model, THE CARD SHALL carry it, so a reader can tell which agent works on which unit.
- WHEN the producer is not the supervisor tick, THE LIVE FIELDS SHALL be omitted rather than invented, because `_LIVE_LANES` is process-local and a second process holds none.
- WHERE a field is omitted, THE OMISSION SHALL not be reported to a human in producer vocabulary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a supervised pass so at least one lane is building:
   `uv run basicly loop supervise basicly-jr0l --label <label>`
2. Wait until the supervisor's own terminal prints a `running:` line carrying an
   elapsed time and a token figure for a lane.
3. In another shell, fetch the served document:
   `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/snapshot.json`
4. Read the entry in `lanes[]` for that same lane id.

**Observed 2026-08-22.** The terminal read
`basicly-kn4rip 67s 678828 tok [This file already has a family of ...]`
and the lane entry read, in full:
`{"branch":"harness/basicly-kn4rip","id":"basicly-kn4rip","live":true,"phase":"build","status":"open"}`

**Expected.** The lane card carries the elapsed time, the spend and the activity the
terminal has, because they are the facts a reader needs to tell a working lane from a
wedged one.

**Control.** The same fetch against a lane that has completed at least one run does
carry `agent`, `started_at` and `tokens`, because those come from the last finished
run - which is what separates this from the whole path being broken.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `130000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Start a supervised pass with a lane running, fetch `/snapshot.json`, and read the elapsed time, the tokens and the activity line on the lane card against the same three figures on the supervisor's own `running:` line at the same moment.

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "we have the id, priority and description, but we do not have a feature or epic name that is descriptive for the human. I cannot distinguish what each of these work items is implementing as I do not know with which feature it is connected."

A wall row today is `P1 | basicly-a4q3.10 | Carry a ranked kill list and its discriminator on a change summary`. Nothing on it says which feature that serves.

## The fact is already on the wire

Measured against the live `/snapshot.json` on 2026-08-22:

```text
parent-child edges in graph.edges : 544
distinct parents they resolve to  : 19, of which 15 are epic and 4 are feature
ready units                       : 187
  resolve to a parent             : 145  (77%)
  orphans with no parent at all   : 42   (23%)
```

The edge direction is `from` = child, `to` = parent. `units[]` already carries `title` and `type` for each of those parents. So the epic a row belongs to needs **no new producer field** - it is a fold over two arrays the document already serves.

The fourteen roots that own the ready set, by how many ready descendants each has: `e2mz` 37, `jr0l` 26, `u2hl` 20, `vkh0` 17, `tcmy` 16, `a4q3` 9, `imnu` 4, `u6jq` 3, `ze8z` 3, `a3ab` 3, `m4zv` 2, `kjc5` 2, `rn0o` 2, `agzx` 1.

## Why grouping rather than a column

Fourteen groups over 187 rows. A per-row epic column repeats the same long title 37 times for one epic and costs horizontal width the title needs. A group heading states it once. The 42 orphans become their own group, which makes a second fact visible that a column would hide: a quarter of the ready set is attached to no feature at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the wall renders a ready set, IT SHALL group the rows under the epic or feature each resolves to, and each heading SHALL carry that parent's own title and its ready count.
- WHEN a unit resolves to no parent, IT SHALL appear under one heading that names it as unattached, with a count.
- WHEN a chain has more than one level, THE HEADING SHALL name the root ancestor, not the immediate parent.
- WHEN the graph holds a cycle, THE FOLD SHALL terminate and the affected unit SHALL be reported as unattached rather than looping.
- WHERE grouping is applied, THE URGENCY ORDER THE WALL ALREADY RANKS BY SHALL be preserved within each group and SHALL decide the order of the groups themselves.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render the board: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html`
2. Read any row under the `NEXT UP` heading.

**Observed 2026-08-22.** `P1  basicly-a4q3.10  Carry a ranked kill list and its
discriminator on a change summary`. Three fields, none of which name a feature.

**Expected.** A reader can tell which feature that row implements. `basicly-a4q3.10`
roots to `basicly-a4q3`, *Adopt the verification practices the RH campaign volume
evidences*, and nothing on the page says so.

**Control that the fact is present, not missing.** Over the same served document:
`jq '[.graph.edges[]|select(.kind=="parent-child")]|length' snapshot.json` returns a
non-zero count, and `units[]` carries a `title` and a `type` for each parent. The
fold is available; it is not performed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `tests/test_board_wall.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render the live board and read the wall, checking that a row under a heading names an epic whose id is the root ancestor of that row's id in `graph.edges`, and that the unattached group's count matches the orphan count computed from the same document.

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 looking at the live wall: "I also do not know what does '6 days' in orange mean."

The band reads `▲6 DAYS / 1 WAITING ON A PERSON / basicly-b2n2 · checkpoint · ship · 160h 16m`.

## Three faults, measured

**The colour carries no information.** `band()` (`src/basicly/board_regions.py:145-181`) resolves state in a fixed precedence - withheld, absent, waiting, calm - and `WAITING` binds to `--orange` at `src/basicly/board_wall.py:73`. The state is `WAITING` whenever the `asks` section is drawn and its list is non-empty. **There is no duration threshold.** A five-second-old ask paints exactly the same orange as a six-day-old one; only the headline text scales. Orange is this page's only alarm channel (`board_wall.py:22-24`), so the one channel that should mean "act now" fires on existence.

**One quantity is stated twice in two units.** The headline is `coarse(waited)` and the detail is `duration(_waited(ask, now))`, both computed from the same `_waited(asks[0], now)` (`board_regions.py:172-179`). Measured on a probe render: 577,020 s renders as `6 DAYS` and as `160h 17m`. The second adds no fact.

**Nothing on the page says what it is.** A full-text scan of `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2` finds no tooltip, no `title=` attribute and no legend entry for the band. `legend()` (`board_footer.py:263-274`) glosses section render-states only.

## What the reader needs instead

The band is the page's only alarm. A reader must learn from it, without a second source: that the factory is stopped, that a person is what stops it, how long that has been true, whether that is normal or bad, and what to do next. Today it supplies the third of those and half the first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an ask has waited, THE BAND STATE SHALL be chosen from the wait duration against declared thresholds, so a short wait and a long wait do not paint the same colour.
- WHEN the band names a duration, IT SHALL state that duration once, in one unit.
- WHEN the band renders, IT SHALL state in plain words what is waiting and what a reader would do about it, without abbreviation a reader must already know.
- WHERE the thresholds live, THEY SHALL be configuration this repository declares rather than constants inside the region, and the test SHALL drive a wait across each boundary.
- WHERE no ask is pending, THE BAND SHALL NOT claim an alarm state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render the board with at least one ask pending:
   `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html`
2. Read the coloured band beneath the header.
3. Now compare two waits. Render again with an ask a few seconds old, and read the
   band's colour against the first render's colour.

**Observed 2026-08-22.** The band read `▲6 DAYS / 1 WAITING ON A PERSON /
basicly-b2n2 · checkpoint · ship · 160h 16m`. `6 DAYS` and `160h 16m` are the same
quantity - both are `_waited(asks[0], now)` - in two units.

**Observed on the colour.** The band paints `--orange` for any non-empty asks list.
A five-second wait and a six-day wait paint identically; only the headline words
differ.

**Expected.** The page's only alarm channel distinguishes a wait that is normal from
one that has stopped the factory, states the duration once, and says what to do.

**Control.** With no ask pending the band takes the calm state, so the region does
respond to the asks list - it just does not respond to how long.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render the board with an ask injected at each side of every declared threshold and read the band's colour and words at each, against a control render with no ask pending.

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "I also hate the squares with a dot in them indicators (signals)."

The page's last row reads `SECTIONS ●generator ●repo ●session ●lanes ●asks ●gates ●spend ●health ●backlog ●units ●graph ●events  KEY ●renders ◇withheld, and says why ○not emitted by this producer`, and the same glyphs appear inline beside REPO, RUN, SPEND, CLOSED TODAY and DEP EDGES.

## What the row is

`inventory()` (`src/basicly/board_footer.py:253-260`) lists the twelve named sections of the `harness-board/v1` schema and paints each one's render verdict. Its own docstring states the intent: *a section no region reads still reports itself here*. So the row is a **producer self-report**: it tells a producer author which parts of their document this consumer accepted. It is developer diagnostics, and it occupies a full row of an operator's dashboard.

`legend()` (`board_footer.py:263-274`) then glosses three glyphs, one of them with the string `not emitted by this producer` - engine vocabulary naming a role the reader does not have.

## The glyph is provably redundant

`src/basicly/board_wall.py:14-15` states the design: each state carries a glyph, a border style and a colour, and the rules are generated one-to-one from `STATES` into `.state-<key>` (`board_page.html.j2:506-514`). The glyph is one of three channels for the same fact. Removing it removes no information.

Nine glyphs are painted across the page: `●` U+25CF renderable, `◇` U+25C7 withheld, `○` U+25CB absent, `▶` U+25B6 live, `◆` U+25C6 stale, `▲` U+25B2 waiting, `◎` U+25CE calm, `✕` U+2715 failed, and `·` U+00B7 as a separator. A reader is given a gloss for three of them.

## The boundary this must respect

The diagnostic is real and a producer author needs it. It has a home already: `/snapshot.json` carries the document, and the schema verdict is computable from it. The claim here is about **placement**, not about deleting the check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a human loads the board, THE PAGE SHALL NOT paint the section inventory or the render-state key as a standing row.
- WHEN a section is genuinely withheld or absent, THE AFFECTED REGION SHALL say so in words a reader without the schema can act on, and SHALL NOT use the words `producer`, `emitted`, `section` or `withheld`.
- WHEN a producer author needs the verdict, IT SHALL remain reachable, and the record SHALL name where.
- WHERE a state is still marked, THE MARK SHALL use at most one channel beside colour, not three.

2. Read the last row of the page.
3. Search the rendered file for the string `producer`.

`SECTIONS ●generator ●repo ●session ●lanes ●asks ●gates ●spend ●health ●backlog
●units ●graph ●events  KEY ●renders ◇withheld, and says why ○not emitted by this
producer`, and the search matched.

**Expected.** A human dashboard names no role the reader does not hold. `producer`,
`emitted`, `section` and `withheld` are engine vocabulary.

**Control that the glyph carries nothing a colour does not.** Each state's CSS rule
is generated one-to-one from `STATES` and sets a border style and a colour alongside
the glyph, so a page rendered with the glyph removed still distinguishes every
state.

## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22: "I do not see any factory loop work visualization."

The page's largest region is headed `THE LOOP` and paints seven counters with progress bars: INTAKE 214, CLASSIFY 1, DECOMPOSE 19, BUILD 0, VERIFY 1, VALIDATE 0, SHIP 0.

## It is the backlog, not the loop

Measured against the live `/snapshot.json` while four lanes were building:

```text
phase histogram over units[]  : intake 215, decompose 19, build 4, verify 1, classify 1
sum                           : 240
backlog.active                : 240
```

The two are the same number because they are the same population. The region bins **every active record in the backlog** by phase. 215 of 240 sit in `intake` for the single reason that they have never been classified - `intake` is where a record is born, so the largest bar on the page measures how much of the backlog has never been touched.

Meanwhile the four lanes actually running contribute 4 to `build`, and nothing on the region distinguishes them from any other record that happens to be at that phase.

## What a loop visualization has to answer

A reader watching a factory wants to know what **this pass** is doing: which units it selected, where each one is now, which moved since the last beat, and which is stuck. None of those are answerable from a backlog histogram. The session's own selection is already on the document - `session.root`, and the lane rows - and the region does not use it.

## The counters are also not comparable

A progress bar implies a denominator. `intake` at 215 and `ship` at 0 share an axis on which 215 is not progress and 0 is not failure; they are two unrelated inventories drawn as if they were stages of one flow. A record at `intake` may never enter the loop at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a supervised pass is running, THE LOOP REGION SHALL show the units that pass selected and where each is, and SHALL distinguish them from records that merely share a phase.
- WHEN no pass is running, THE REGION SHALL say so rather than showing a backlog histogram under a heading that claims a loop.
- WHEN a counter is drawn with a bar, THE BAR SHALL have a stated denominator, and counters that share no denominator SHALL NOT share an axis.
- WHEN a unit has moved phase since the previous beat, THAT MOVEMENT SHALL be visible, because a still picture of positions cannot distinguish working from wedged.
- WHERE the backlog histogram is still wanted, IT SHALL be labelled as the backlog and SHALL NOT occupy the region a reader reads for the running pass.

3. Compare that sum against `jq '.backlog.active' s.json`.

possible for its total to equal the whole active backlog.

document and are not what the region counts.

## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while reading the live wall with four lanes building. The header's RUN field showed `basicly-jr0l · open · L3 · 0%` for the whole of a nine minute pass.

## Measured

At a moment when the supervisor's own terminal reported the four lanes at 4,977,290 / 6,981,880 / 4,583,052 / 5,390,046 tokens - about 21.9M live - the served snapshot carried:

```json
"session": {"grant_level":"L3","token_budget":150000000,"spent_tokens":0,"supervised":true,...}
```

## The cause

`spent_tokens` folds **recorded** run tokens, and a run record is written when a lane **ends**. A lane that has run for nine minutes and spent seven million tokens has recorded nothing, so it contributes nothing. The figure is correct for what it measures and wrong for what a reader takes it to mean.

## Two consequences, and the second is the expensive one

**The bar reads 0% for the whole of a pass.** An operator watching a thirty minute lane sees no movement at all, then a step change at landing. The one number that says "how much of the grant is gone" is the one number that cannot move while it is being spent.

**A ceiling that cannot fire.** The grant's budget bounds `spent_tokens`. If the recorded figure only advances at landing, the ceiling cannot stop a pass mid-lane - it can only decline to start the next one. This is the same shape as `basicly-jr0l.22`, reached by a different route: a bound whose input does not change while the thing it bounds is happening.

## The live figures exist

`supervise.inflight_spend()` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:2359`) returns tokens-so-far for each running lane, and `supervise.retired_spend()` (`:2373`) returns a monotonic total from lanes that have ended but not yet recorded. Both read `_LIVE_LANES` under `_LIVE_LOCK`, process-local to the supervisor - and since `basicly-bd4epr` the producer is the supervisor's own tick, so both are reachable from the producer.

They are not the same denomination as the recorded figure and the repository already knows by how much: `src/basicly/supervise.py:2379-2384` records that the live per-turn sum over-reports the run record, with four measured lane ratios. So the live figure is an over-estimate of known direction, which is the safe direction for a ceiling and must be labelled rather than silently substituted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is running, THE SESSION SPEND THE BOARD SHOWS SHALL advance, and SHALL NOT stay at the value it held when the lane started.
- WHEN a live figure and a recorded figure are both available, THE DOCUMENT SHALL carry both and SHALL name which is which, because they are different denominations.
- WHEN the live figure is shown against a budget, IT SHALL be marked as an over-estimate, with the measured direction stated.
- WHERE the recorded figure is what a gate binds on, THAT GATE SHALL NOT change behaviour under this record; this changes what is reported, not what is enforced.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a supervised pass and wait until lanes have been running for several minutes.
2. Read the live spend from the supervisor's own terminal `running:` line.
3. Fetch the served document and read the session:
   `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/snapshot.json | jq '.session'`

**Observed 2026-08-22.** The terminal reported four lanes at 4,977,290 / 6,981,880 /
4,583,052 / 5,390,046 tokens, about 21.9M live. The served session read
`"spent_tokens": 0`, so the header's grant bar read `0%`.

**Expected.** A figure that says how much of the grant is gone moves while the grant
is being spent.

**Control that the field is wired at all.** The same session object carries
`token_budget: 150000000` and a live `holder.heartbeat_age_s`, so the section is being
produced - the spend value is the part that cannot move.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-0hxck3`
- demonstration: Start a supervised pass, read the session spend from `/snapshot.json` at three points during one lane's run, and check the figure advances between them and agrees in direction with the supervisor's own reported per-lane totals at the same moments.

parent-child edges in graph.edges : 544

Fourteen groups over 187 rows. A per-row epic column repeats the same long title 37 times for one epic and costs horizontal width the title needs. A group heading states it once. The 42 orphans become their own group, which makes a second fact visible that a column would hide: a quarter of the ready set is attached to no feature at all.

- WHEN the wall renders a ready set, IT SHALL group the rows under the epic or feature each resolves to, and each heading SHALL carry that parent's own title and its ready count.

- WHEN a chain has more than one level, THE HEADING SHALL name the root ancestor, not the immediate parent.

evidences*, and nothing on the page says so.

`jq '[.graph.edges[]|select(.kind=="parent-child")]|length' snapshot.json` returns a
non-zero count, and `units[]` carries a `title` and a `type` for each parent. The
fold is available; it is not performed.

- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

- budget: `120000`

- demonstration: Render the live board and read the wall, checking that a row under a heading names an epic whose id is the root ancestor of that row's id in `graph.edges`, and that the unattached group's count matches the orphan count computed from the same document.

## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while diagnosing why three of four lanes in one pass reported the size ratchets as a systemic blocker and spent real budget on them rather than on their task.

`python-guidelines` is a **path-scoped skill on `**/*.py`**, so every lane touching Python loads it. Its waiver recipe is stale and the gate refuses the format it prescribes.

## Measured

`.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml:88` instructs:

> a column-0 `module-size-waiver: <reason>` comment in the file, in the same diff that raises `waiver_count` under `[tool.module_size]` in `pyproject.toml`

Two faults in one sentence, and one omission.

**The kind is missing.** `.scripts/waivers.py` parses a waiver into `COHESION`, `COST` or `UNCLASSIFIED`. The skill's literal format carries no kind, so it parses as `UNCLASSIFIED`, and the gate refuses it - *states no kind, so nothing says whether this is permanent or owed back*. The accepted spellings are `# module-size-waiver: cohesion: <reason>` and `# module-size-waiver: cost(<record-id>): <reason>`.

**The counter moved.** `waiver_count` in `pyproject.toml` is the shared anchor that bounced three of five lanes on 2026-08-08 and that `basicly-ef7t` replaced with a per-record `count_delta` in `basicly.d`.

**Rebaselining is never mentioned.** `[ratchet.<gate>.rebaselined]` in `basicly.d/<record-id>.toml` exists for exactly the case a frozen baseline has to rise. It requires a reason and a `base_commit` that is an ancestor of HEAD, it is counted and printed on the pass line, and it is already used **50 times** across 26 entries - `events.py` seven times, `test_loop.py` four. It is the permitted, precedented route, and the file every lane reads does not know it exists.

Verified with a positive control: the file mentions `waiver` five times, and `cohesion`, `cost(`, `basicly.d` and `rebaselin` zero times.

## The cost is a measured lane loss

`basicly-kr7t` was dispatched 2026-08-14 and blocked before a commit; nothing landed. It built the named extraction, measured it against both ratchets, and reverted. It enumerated **all 8.4 million subsets** of the file's 26 natural blocks using the gates' own measurement functions: **225,756 satisfy both ratchets and not one is a nameable responsibility.** The refusal margin was 28 prose tokens - 112 characters. The owner's disposition was *waiver now, decomposition later*, which is the route the skill does not describe.

A median lane is 6.76M tokens and about six dollars. 178 of 447 modules sit within one ordinary edit of a bound, so the exposure is structural rather than incidental.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n 'waiver_count|cohesion|cost\(|basicly\.d|rebaselin' .basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml`
2. Read the one hit at line 88.
3. Run the gate's own parser on that literal format:
   `uv run python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.scripts'); import waivers; print(waivers.read_waiver('m','# module-size-waiver: some reason','module-size-waiver'))"`

**Observed.** The one hit is the `waiver_count` instruction; the other four probes return nothing. The parser yields `UNCLASSIFIED` and the gate refuses it.

**Control.** `rg -c -i waiver <the same file>` returns 5, so the probe reaches the file and the four zeroes are real absences rather than a bad pattern. And the `cohesion:` spelling parses to a `COHESION` waiver, so the parser is not simply refusing everything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane reads the waiver guidance, THE FORMAT IT IS GIVEN SHALL be one the gate's own parser accepts, and a test SHALL feed the guidance's literal example to that parser.
- WHEN the guidance names where a waiver is counted, IT SHALL name the current location and SHALL NOT name `waiver_count` in `pyproject.toml`.
- WHEN a baseline genuinely has to rise, THE GUIDANCE SHALL describe rebaselining, its two required inputs, and that it is counted rather than silent.
- WHEN the guidance describes a split, IT SHALL state the condition that makes a split satisfy both gates at once, because two in three natural extractions do not.
- WHERE the guidance is projected, THE PROJECTED SURFACE SHALL be regenerated and checked, not only the source.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Feed the guidance's literal waiver example to `.scripts/waivers.py`'s parser and read an accepted classified waiver, against a control feeding the old kindless format and reading the refusal.

## Context

`basicly-kn4rip` landed the reporting half of the swallow: the seam now says `already recorded` instead of `recorded:`. It deliberately left the swallow itself, and named the reason - nothing in the ledger separates a deliberate re-record from a replay, so the intent has to come from the caller. `Draft.generation` is the mechanism and no write verb reaches it.

Scoped 2026-08-22 against a scratch ledger. The live tracker was not probed.

## The mechanism, and it already works

`Draft.generation` is declared at `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py:450` with default `1`, read at exactly one place - `events.py:1334`, the skip - and reaches the id through `ids.evidence_id` at `ids.py:379-382`. It is **not hashed**; it is a visible suffix:

```python
suffix = digest if generation == 1 else f"{digest}-{generation}"
```

So `gen=1` gives `rec#ev-04bc122532` and `gen=2` gives `rec#ev-04bc122532-2`. `generation < 1` raises. Nine `Draft(` constructions in `src/basicly/write_verbs.py` and none carries the kwarg.

## Proved on a scratch ledger

Driving `status` open then blocked then open through the kit CLI: the third write appended nothing, the folded status stayed `blocked`, and the CLI raised. The same third write with `generation=2` landed at seq 4 and the fold moved to `open`. The reported label sequence reproduces identically.

## The constraint that decides the design

`tracker.scrub_ledger` re-derives every event's generation as the **dense occurrence count** of an identical `(record, kind, payload)` in file order (`src/basicly/tracker.py:789-797`, used at `:834`), and raises `TrackerDivergenceError` and rewrites nothing if any stored id fails to re-mint (`:838-842`). That runs on the commit path. So a caller flag may not mint an arbitrary generation - it must resolve to `occurrence_count + 1`, as `migrate.py:523` already does. The derivation was verified to reproduce a hand-written `gen=2` event.

## Which verbs need it

`update --status`, `update` label flags, `update` other fields, `close`, `dep add` and `gate report` all have a reachable A then B then A. `dep remove` is guarded by `_refuse_a_retraction_of_an_absent_edge`. `create` cannot collide, because the id is minted per call. `comments add` should keep the swallow, because an identical body is a genuine duplicate.

**`gate report` is worse than the others: it is a plain A then A.** Its payload is `{provenance, gate, provider, passed}` and carries neither the note nor the actor (`write_verbs.py:227-235`), so a gate that really runs twice and passes twice is recorded once.

## Where an unknown flag is refused today, and where it is not

`update` refuses an unknown flag loudly (`write_verbs.py:123-129`). `close`, `dep add`, `dep remove` and `gate report` **silently drop it**. So a misspelled repeat flag on those four degrades straight back into the swallow, and now invisibly, because the operator believes they asked for a re-record. A shape-level guard at the seam covers all verbs at once; `_refuse_a_write_that_records_nothing` (`owned_write.py:145`) is the precedent.

## Where it threads

The strip belongs in `owned_write.append` around `owned_write.py:276`, beside `_resolve_labels` - that is the one place holding the ledger lock, which a dense-occurrence resolver requires, and it means no translator changes at all. It must run **after** `_stamped` (`:280`), because stamping rewrites the provenance key and therefore the digest. A valueless flag matches the argv grammar's existing shape and needs no `VALUE_FLAGS` entry.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a throwaway ledger under a scratch directory. The kit CLI takes its ledger directory as its first positional exactly so it can point away from the live one: `uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py create <dir> --prefix scratch --title probe --status open`
2. `... update <dir> <id> --status blocked`
3. `... update <dir> <id> --status open`
4. `... show <dir> <id>`

**Observed.** Step 3 appends nothing and raises `IndexError`. Step 4 reports `status = blocked` with 3 events.

**Control.** Appending the same draft with `generation=2` returns one event id ending `-2`, and the fold moves to `open` at 4 events - so the ledger is writable and the swallow is the digest, not a broken probe.

**Never probe the live ledger at `.basicly/ledger/`.** An append-only log has no undo and a throwaway record's tombstone is permanent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a caller means a re-record genuinely, THERE SHALL be a flag that says so, and the resulting event SHALL fold to the intended value.
- WHEN that flag is used, THE GENERATION SHALL resolve to the next dense occurrence of the identical event, so `tracker.scrub_ledger` re-mints every id and does not diverge.
- WHEN the flag is absent, THE BEHAVIOUR SHALL NOT change, and `test_replaying_the_same_drafts_appends_nothing` SHALL still pass unmodified.
- WHEN a verb that silently drops unknown flags is given a misspelled one, IT SHALL be refused rather than degrade into the swallow.
- WHERE the flag is not idempotent by construction, THAT SHALL be stated rather than hidden; running it twice appends twice, and making it idempotent would reintroduce the swallow.
- WHERE an engine path calls `tracker.write`, IT SHALL NOT pass the flag, because a state re-entered on every advance must still record one event.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_argv.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker_write.py`
- `tests/test_owned_write.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `130000`
- depends on: `basicly-kn4rip`
- demonstration: On a scratch ledger drive one field A then B then A with the flag and read back A, against two controls - the same sequence without the flag, which must still fold to B, and an identical replay run twice, which must append once.

## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while probing the swallow on a scratch ledger. Two sites report a tracker write as having happened when it did not, and they are the sites `basicly-kn4rip` left because its own change was additive.

## The kit CLI crashes rather than reports

`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py:322` reads `appended[0].record` with no guard. When every draft is swallowed - the ordinary outcome of re-recording a fact the ledger holds - `appended` is `[]` and the CLI raises an unhandled `IndexError` with a traceback. That is the kit-side twin of the engine-seam defect `79bbe0db` just fixed, and that commit does not cover it: the kit is a separate consumer with its own entry point, which is the whole reason it takes a ledger directory as an argument.

A traceback is a worse answer than the wrong one it replaces. An operator reads it as a broken tool rather than as a write that recorded nothing.

## Two engine sites still report a swallowed gate as recorded

`basicly-kn4rip` made `tracker.write` return whether every draft landed. Its own commit message says every other caller discards that return and that the change is therefore additive. That is true, and two of those callers are where it costs something:

- `src/basicly/verify.py:415`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py:536`

Both discard the boolean and unconditionally print `recorded gate <name>=<status>`.

**`gate report` is the verb with the worst swallow shape.** Its payload is `{provenance, gate, provider, passed}` (`src/basicly/write_verbs.py:227-235`) and carries neither the note nor the actor, so two genuine runs of the same gate with the same verdict are byte-identical and the second is skipped. This is a plain A then A - it needs no intervening B, unlike every other verb. `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/gates.py:222-224` documents the shape as wrong.

So a gate that really ran twice is recorded once, and both call sites say it was recorded.

## Steps to Reproduce

**The kit crash.** On a throwaway ledger under a scratch directory - never `.basicly/ledger/`:

1. `uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py create <dir> --prefix scratch --title probe --status open`
2. `... update <dir> <id> --status blocked`
3. `... update <dir> <id> --status open`

**Observed.** Step 3 exits with `IndexError: list index out of range` at `cli.py:322`.
**Expected.** It reports that the fact was already held and nothing was appended.
**Control.** Steps 1 and 2 both succeed and print a record and an event id, so the CLI works and step 3's failure is the swallow path specifically.

**The gate report.** Record the same gate, provider and verdict twice on a scratch record and read the record's events: one `gate` event, two reports of success.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every draft a kit CLI write hands the ledger is skipped, THE CLI SHALL report that and SHALL NOT raise.
- WHEN a gate report records nothing because the ledger already holds it, THE CALLER SHALL NOT print that it was recorded.
- WHEN two genuine runs of one gate produce the same verdict, THE LEDGER SHALL be able to hold both, or the caller SHALL say which one it kept.
- WHERE the engine reports a gate, THE REPORT SHALL rest on what the write returned rather than on no exception having been raised.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/rubrics.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_cli.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `90000`
- depends on: `basicly-kn4rip`
- demonstration: Drive the kit CLI through a swallowed write and read a report instead of a traceback, then report one gate twice and read the second report against the record's actual event count.

payload.value:
## Context

Found 2026-08-22 while diagnosing why three of four lanes in one pass reported the size ratchets as a systemic blocker and spent real budget on them rather than on their task.

`python-guidelines` is a **path-scoped skill on `**/*.py`**, so every lane touching Python loads it. Its waiver recipe is stale and the gate refuses the format it prescribes.

## Measured

`.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml:88` instructs:

> a column-0 `module-size-waiver: <reason>` comment in the file, in the same diff that raises `waiver_count` under `[tool.module_size]` in `pyproject.toml`

Two faults in one sentence, and one omission.

**The kind is missing.** `.scripts/waivers.py` parses a waiver into `COHESION`, `COST` or `UNCLASSIFIED`. The skill's literal format carries no kind, so it parses as `UNCLASSIFIED`, and the gate refuses it - *states no kind, so nothing says whether this is permanent or owed back*. The accepted spellings are `# module-size-waiver: cohesion: <reason>` and `# module-size-waiver: cost(<record-id>): <reason>`.

**The counter moved.** `waiver_count` in `pyproject.toml` is the shared anchor that bounced three of five lanes on 2026-08-08 and that `basicly-ef7t` replaced with a per-record `count_delta` in `basicly.d`.

**Rebaselining is never mentioned.** `[ratchet.<gate>.rebaselined]` in `basicly.d/<record-id>.toml` exists for exactly the case a frozen baseline has to rise. It requires a reason and a `base_commit` that is an ancestor of HEAD, it is counted and printed on the pass line, and it is already used **50 times** across 26 entries - `events.py` seven times, `test_loop.py` four. It is the permitted, precedented route, and the file every lane reads does not know it exists.

Verified with a positive control: the file mentions `waiver` five times, and `cohesion`, `cost(`, `basicly.d` and `rebaselin` zero times.

## The cost is a measured lane loss

`basicly-kr7t` was dispatched 2026-08-14 and blocked before a commit; nothing landed. It built the named extraction, measured it against both ratchets, and reverted. It enumerated **all 8.4 million subsets** of the file's 26 natural blocks using the gates' own measurement functions: **225,756 satisfy both ratchets and not one is a nameable responsibility.** The refusal margin was 28 prose tokens - 112 characters. The owner's disposition was *waiver now, decomposition later*, which is the route the skill does not describe.

A median lane is 6.76M tokens and about six dollars. 178 of 447 modules sit within one ordinary edit of a bound, so the exposure is structural rather than incidental.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `rg -n 'waiver_count|cohesion|cost\(|basicly\.d|rebaselin' .basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml`
2. Read the one hit at line 88.
3. Run the gate's own parser on that literal format:
   `uv run python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.scripts'); import waivers; print(waivers.read_waiver('m','# module-size-waiver: some reason','module-size-waiver'))"`

**Observed.** The one hit is the `waiver_count` instruction; the other four probes return nothing. The parser yields `UNCLASSIFIED` and the gate refuses it.

**Control.** `rg -c -i waiver <the same file>` returns 5, so the probe reaches the file and the four zeroes are real absences rather than a bad pattern. And the `cohesion:` spelling parses to a `COHESION` waiver, so the parser is not simply refusing everything.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane reads the waiver guidance, THE FORMAT IT IS GIVEN SHALL be one the gate's own parser accepts, and a test SHALL feed the guidance's literal example to that parser.
- WHEN the guidance names where a waiver is counted, IT SHALL name the current location and SHALL NOT name `waiver_count` in `pyproject.toml`.
- WHEN a baseline genuinely has to rise, THE GUIDANCE SHALL describe rebaselining, its two required inputs, and that it is counted rather than silent.
- WHEN the guidance describes a split, IT SHALL state the condition that makes a split satisfy both gates at once, because two in three natural extractions do not.
- WHERE the guidance is projected, THE PROJECTED SURFACE SHALL be regenerated and checked, not only the source.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/python-guidelines/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md`
- `.agents/skills/python-guidelines/SKILL.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `60000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Feed the guidance's literal waiver example to `.scripts/waivers.py`'s parser and read an accepted classified waiver, against a control feeding the old kindless format and reading the refusal.

payload.value:
Fixed 2026-08-22 in the base checkout. The guidance now states the split's own economics (only 34.4% of 3588 real top-level defs are prose-heavier than their parent and so satisfy both gates), describes rebaselining with its two required inputs as the usual route, gives the waiver in both accepted spellings with the kind mandatory, points the counter at basicly.d's count_delta rather than pyproject's waiver_count, and warns that a waiver on a frozen module replaces its ceiling outright.

Verified by feeding every waiver example in each surface to the gate's own parser: three examples, zero unclassified, on all three surfaces. Running the parser over the whole file rather than over my edit is what found a THIRD stale kindless example at line 153 that the finding had not named.

The declared scope was also short: skills project to .agents/skills as well as .claude/skills, and projection-skills failed until skills-build --all-default-roots ran. The scope now names it. uv run basicly verify --mode full is PASS.

## Context

`basicly-0hxck3` filled the lane card from the three tiers that hold its figures and pushed `board_facts.py` from 3578 to 4219 tokens, 219 over the 4000-token cap. It shipped under a `cost(basicly-<this>)` waiver rather than a split, and this record is the debt.

## Why it was not split at the time

The extraction is real and nameable: `_lane_fact` and its three coercions (`_text`, `_number`, `_whole`) are one responsibility - building one lane's card from the live stream, the last run record and the tracker binding. They would move cleanly.

They cannot move yet because **every one of the 116 modules under `src/basicly/` is named in `.importlinter`'s layer list**, verified by set difference: zero are absent. So a new module requires an `.importlinter` edit, and that file is declared scope of `basicly-rn0o.6`, which was committed and unlanded when this was written. Editing it from a second worktree would have raced a landing.

Prose was cut first and it was not enough: 113 tokens came out of two docstrings before the remaining reasoning was the kind the cap exists to protect. `board_facts.py` is already prose-waived at 58.5%, so density was never the binding constraint here - size was.

## Where it goes

A new `board_lane.py` between `board_facts` and `board_sections` in the layer list. `board_facts` (line 25) imports it; it imports `board_sections` (line 64). `tests/test_board_lane.py` moves with it, because the test-naming gate binds a test file to each source unit.

Expected result: `board_facts.py` returns to roughly its pre-change 3578 tokens and the waiver is removed in the same diff.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run python .scripts/headroom.py | grep board_facts`
2. `grep -n 'module-size-waiver' src/basicly/board_facts.py`
3. `grep -n 'count_delta' basicly.d/basicly-0hxck3.toml`

**Observed.** The module reports over the cap, carries a `cost(...)` waiver naming this record, and the drop-in records the count.

**Control.** `uv run python .scripts/check_waivers.py` passes while this record is open and must fail once it closes with the waiver still in the file - that expiry is the mechanism making this debt rather than an exemption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the extraction lands, `board_facts.py` SHALL be under the 4000-token cap without a size waiver, and the waiver comment SHALL be removed in the same diff.
- WHEN the new module is added, IT SHALL be named in `.importlinter`'s layer list and `lint-imports` SHALL keep all three contracts.
- WHEN the new module is added, IT SHALL carry a test file named after it, and the module SHALL be git-added before the suite runs.
- WHERE the cut is made, IT SHALL follow a nameable responsibility and SHALL NOT be a `_part1`/`_part2` split chosen to satisfy a number.
- WHERE `count_delta` was recorded for the waiver, IT SHALL be removed with it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_lane.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `basicly.d/basicly-0hxck3.toml`
- `tests/test_board_lane.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `80000`
- depends on: `basicly-rn0o.6`
- demonstration: Run `uv run python .scripts/headroom.py` and read `board_facts.py` under the cap with no waiver, then `uv run basicly verify --mode full` for the import contract and the test-naming gate.

payload.value:
## Context

Three instances on 2026-08-21, in three different code paths, all one shape: a gate refused, and what reached the operator named no gate.

```text
the salvage commit was rejected: protect-generated-commit...........Passed
routed: basicly-s07cgc -> error - routing failed: command failed (1): git commit -m ...
routed: basicly-co64   -> error - routing failed: command failed (1): git commit -m ...
```

The first prints a **passing** hook line as the rejection reason. The other two print the argv and the exit code and nothing else. In every case the real cause was one named check inside the captured output: markdownlint refusing a lane`s own gitignored scratch note in the first, `release-notes` naming the exact missing `changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md` in the other two.

## Why this costs more than it looks

Each one cost a diagnosis that the output already contained. The salvage case is worse than silence: a reader who trusts the line goes and looks at `protect-generated-commit`, which passed.

The repo already knows this class. `basicly-e84` closed on *"verify from explicit pass/fail lines not truncated output"*, and `basicly-lkzq` records that a hand-picked subset of checks reads exactly like the gate. This is the same rule turned inward: the engine`s own error text is doing to an operator what a truncated tail does to an agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a git command the engine runs fails because a hook refused, THE ENGINE SHALL name the failing check and its reported reason rather than the argv and the exit code.
- WHEN the captured output holds an explicit failure line, THE MESSAGE SHALL carry that line and SHALL NOT carry a passing line.
