## Context

Owner 2026-08-22: *"the info on the card is cut in a normal widht browser so i only see 'agent claude claude...' instead of the model used."*

A Fable 5 architect rendered the page at 1280, 1600 and 1920 and found the truncation and the huge empty area are **one CSS decision**, not two defects.

## Measured

`.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2:59` declares a grid whose right column is a fixed `470px`, and `:72` makes the running row `minmax(0, 1fr)`. The consequence at 1920x2400: roughly **70% of the page is black** while `claude · claude-opu…` clips **even at 1920**. A lane card is about 390px wide inside that layout, and `_lane_cells` puts the agent and the model in one cell - `Cell("agent", joined(lane, ("agent", "model")))` at `board_regions.py:259` - so the model id has no room at any width.

So the fixed column starves the content that needs width, and the stretch row wastes the height it took.

## Why this is first rather than fifth

Every other board item assumes its region has room. The card rewrite needs width for a title and an identity line; the next-up row needs width for a title-first order; the loop diagram needs a full-width band. Fixing them inside a 470px column means fixing them twice. The architect's ranked order puts this first for that reason, and it also means the CSS is touched once rather than in five diffs.

Measured room after the change: a full-width identity line at 1280 is about 590px of text in a 1248px box, so the model id is readable **with roughly two times headroom**, and at 1600 two cards per row still leave about 760px each.

## What retires with it

The fixed-height slot arithmetic. `READY_SLOTS` and `READY_SLOTS_WIDE` (`board_regions.py:83-101`) exist to promise a rendered height against a fixed viewport, and `BAND_ASKS = 1` (`:107`) is justified by the same height argument. A page that flows does not need either, which is what lets the alarm band show more than one waiting ask.

## The one thing that must not be lost

The wall-display case is real: `board_regions.py:1-14` says the layout answers *from across a room*. That is a different consumer from a browser at a desk, and the owner is the second. Keep the fixed-viewport form reachable rather than deleting it - a variant - so the room display does not regress while the desk case is fixed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/ -o /tmp/b.html`
2. Render at 1280 wide and read the lane card's agent cell.
3. Render at 1920 wide and read it again.

**Observed.** `claude · claude-opu…` at both widths, and a large black region below the cards at both.

**Control.** The same document rendered without the fixed right column shows the full model id, so the clip is the layout rather than the data or the clip bound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the page renders at 1280, THE MODEL ID ON A LANE CARD SHALL be readable in full.
- WHEN the page renders at any width the layout claims, IT SHALL NOT leave a majority of its height empty while a region above it clips.

unsupported.claim: The server acquires no lock and writes no file, so it blocks no gate and a board can never be the reason a landing failed.
unsupported.why: The only binding I found is tests/test_board_serve.py:317, which asserts the sentence is present in `board serve --help` — a presence check on a frozen string, not a check of the property. This release adds `lane-kill`, which spawns `basicly loop kill <issue>` with the repo as cwd (src/basicly/board_actions.py:_kill, _spawn), and `checkpoint-approve`, which writes through the tracker. I looked for a test, a command or a gate showing that a board-submitted action cannot cause a landing to fail and found none; grep for `NO_WRITES` and `never be the reason` across src/ and tests/ returns only the constant, its one presence assertion, and an unrelated tracker docstring.

unsupported.why: The record's demonstration. tests/test_board_actions.py::test_the_wire_refuses_an_empty_code_and_accepts_a_typed_one substitutes `surface._run` with `_Spy`, which returns a canned `(0, "checkpoint ship: APPROVED (x-1)")` and spawns nothing, so what is proven is that the typed code reaches argv and is redacted from the reply — not that `policy checkpoint --approve` accepted it against a live minted code. test_the_real_parser_accepts_every_argv_the_table_builds parses the argv but does not execute it. It does not hold for every way install can refuse the value: _record_install_technologies still calls record_technology_selection (src/basicly/config.py:1516-1524), which raises ValueError and makes cmd_install return 1 on an unsupported [catalog] layout — and that call sits after cmd_install has already synced ~175 catalog files, written .basicly/state/install.json, scaffolded the user overlay, and added basicly.local.toml to .gitignore. payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context

Owner question, 2026-08-22: *"I also understand that the only things that are shown on the board are the ones started by supervisor. what about other subagents or background agents - are they also shown on the board?"*

The answer is **no**, and it is structural rather than an omission in the producer.

## Measured

A board lane comes from one place: `board_facts.lane_facts` calls `supervise.derive_session(...)` and reads `state.adopted` (`src/basicly/board_facts.py:237-238`). An `AdoptedLane` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:466-474`) is *"one in-flight lane re-adopted from its br worktree binding"* and carries a required `loop_state.WorktreeBinding`.

So a thing appears on the board if and only if it has **a tracker record carrying a `worktree:` external_ref**. A subagent spawned through a host's own agent tool has neither. A background shell job has neither.

`rg -n 'subagent|sub-agent|background|spawn' src/basicly/board_*.py` returns two hits and both are prose in unrelated docstrings, saying the producer *spawns* nothing. Positive control: `rg -c 'lane' src/basicly/board_facts.py` returns 30, so the probe reaches the files and the absence is real.

## Why this matters more than it looks

The region is headed `RUNNING NOW`. A reader takes that as *what is happening in this repository*, and on 2026-08-22 the true answer included four read-only investigation subagents and two background shell jobs that the board could not see and did not mention. The heading over-claims: it means *what the supervisor dispatched*, and nothing says so.

That is the same class as `basicly-a68ggd`, where a region headed `THE LOOP` shows the whole backlog. A heading that names more than its producer can see is a defect whichever direction the gap runs.

## What is genuinely hard here

A subagent is **not** a lane and should not be drawn as one. It has no tracker record, no worktree, no branch, no acceptance criteria, and no landing. Giving it a lane card would invite a reader to expect a merge that will never come.

It also may not be observable at all. A lane is a subprocess this engine spawned and metered, so its stream is readable; a subagent of the *host* is inside the host's own process tree and the engine has no handle on it. Whether it can be counted at all is the first question this record has to answer rather than assume - and if the answer is that it cannot, then the honest fix is the heading and not a new section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN work is running that the board cannot see, THE PAGE SHALL NOT imply it is showing everything, and the region's heading SHALL name the population it actually draws.
- WHEN it is established whether a host subagent or a background job is observable by this engine at all, THAT FINDING SHALL be recorded with its evidence, because the design depends on it and it is currently unknown.
- WHERE such work is observable and shown, IT SHALL be visually distinct from a lane and SHALL NOT carry a lane's affordances, since it has no branch and no landing.
- WHERE it is not observable, THE HEADING FIX ALONE SHALL be the deliverable, and the record SHALL say so rather than leaving a section stubbed.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: `basicly-ibzr0f`
- demonstration: Run a supervised pass while separately running work the engine did not dispatch, then read the board and check that nothing on it claims to be showing that second population - and if the design admits it, that it is drawn as something other than a lane.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run any agent without the supervisor - a bare claude session in this checkout, or `basicly loop run` before its worktree binds - then open the board: the lanes region names only records carrying a worktree external_ref, and `running now` counts more work than any visible lane, with nothing on the page saying the difference exists.

body.post_ship_action: Before this fragment is folded into a published CHANGELOG section (or immediately as an errata commit if the tag has already moved), hand-correct changelog.d/basicly-95mp1k.fixed.md to say the comparison now reads as 'stalled', not 'diverging' — the current wording is contradicted by the shipped code and its own regression test. Separately, close the basicly-95mp1k tracker record, which `basicly tracker show` still reports as status=open despite the merge, and re-check dependent basicly-kas8q7 (currently open/blocked) now that this fix has landed.

unsupported.claim: a strict superset now compares as diverging
unsupported.why: Replayed the bug's own reproduction (a 26-member superset of a 20-member truncated set) directly against the shipped src/basicly/policy.py: `uv run python -c "from basicly import policy; prev,_=policy._finding_signature_and_truncation([f'check-{n:02d}' for n in range(20)]); m,t=policy._finding_signature_and_truncation([f'check-{n:02d}' for n in range(20)]+[f'aaa-new-{n}' for n in range(6)]); print(policy._compare_finding_sets([prev], m, truncated=t))"` returns `('stalled', ...)`, not diverging. The shipped regression test asserts the same thing (`verdict == policy.STALLED` in tests/test_policy.py::test_the_stored_finding_set_is_bounded_in_members_and_in_length). In src/basicly/policy.py's _compare_finding_sets, DIVERGING is returned only by the untouched `set(members) > set(previous)` branch, which requires an *untruncated* superset; the new `if truncated: return STALLED` branch is what the fix actually added. No test, code path, or command run produces DIVERGING for a truncated superset — the changelog fragment (changelog.d/basicly-95mp1k.fixed.md, which `basicly release` folds verbatim into the published CHANGELOG) names the wrong verdict for the exact scenario the bug and its acceptance criteria describe as 'stalled'.

{"detail": "The work is complete and staged; `basicly verify --mode fast` passes every check except `release-notes`, and `--mode full` passes everything else too (pytest 4866 passed after the tripwire update). The single failure is not this lane's: `release-notes: basicly-bom07a: closed with a `## Scope` naming a shipped path and no release note` followed by the gate's own diagnosis, `changelog.d/basicly-bom07a.changed.md is on the base branch and absent here: this tree is behind, not in debt. payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-23 on the wall board: 'kas8q7 - checkpoint - classify - 1h 54m' rendered in the action band as a NEEDS YOU ask while (1) basicly loop decisions basicly-kas8q7 returned an empty list, (2) the live L3 grant on basicly-xglise delegates classify and ship (preflight prints 'checkpts: classify pending - the live L3 grant delegates it'), and (3) the lane was dispatched and running at that moment under the same supervisor. The checkpoint record stays PENDING until the engine crosses the boundary, so the board derives a human ask from a checkpoint no human needs to answer, and its age clock dates from provisioning - the owner reads a 2 hour bottleneck that does not exist. The one signal the action band exists for trains the owner to ignore it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Grant L3 on an epic, provision a lane, let the supervisor run it; render the board while the lane is in build. The classify checkpoint shows as a pending ask with a growing age.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a pending checkpoint whose issue is covered by a live grant that delegates it then the action band does not render it as a NEEDS YOU ask.
Given a pending checkpoint not covered by a grant then the ask renders exactly as today.
Given a decision in the queue (loop decisions non-empty) then it renders as an ask regardless of grants.
Demonstrated by: render the board against a fixture with a granted pending checkpoint and one queued decision, and assert the band holds only the decision.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

The test therefore passes over an empty population and cannot fail for the reason its docstring names. It is a vacuous pass today, not evidence that declarations in this repo are correct. This is a test-strength finding, not a consumer-facing claim, and I did not cite it as evidence for anything above.

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-23: a git push from base ran the pre-push hook while a live supervisor held unstaged ledger dirt. The hook printed 'Unstaged files detected' and stashed .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl to a pre-commit cache patch; the push was killed at a 2-minute timeout mid-hook, and the stash was never restored. One engine event (the basicly-mdv1qu worktree binding, external_ref seq 7) vanished from the working tree while the lane it bound was running. Recovered by git-applying the cache patch by hand; loop status confirmed the binding after. The window is structural: the ledger is append-only shared state that a second process writes between stash and restore, so even an uninterrupted hook can restore the patch over newer appends.

## Steps to Reproduce

Start a supervise pass (it leaves ledger events unstaged in base), run git push from base, interrupt the pre-push hook after the stash line.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given the pre-push hook runs with unstaged changes confined to .basicly/ledger/ then it does not stash them and runs against the tree as it stands.
Given unstaged changes outside the ledger then the stash behaviour is unchanged.
Given a hook interruption after a stash then the ledger file is byte-identical to before the hook started.
Demonstrated by: a test that dirties only the ledger, runs the pre-push script, kills it mid-run, and asserts the ledger file is unchanged.

## Scope

- `.pre-commit-config.yaml`
- `.scripts/`
payload.title: the pre-push stash window can lose live ledger events

The band reads `▲6 DAYS / 1 WAITING ON A PERSON / basicly-b2n2 · checkpoint · ship · 160h 16m`.

## Three faults, measured

**The colour carries no information.** `band()` (`src/basicly/board_regions.py:145-181`) resolves state in a fixed precedence - withheld, absent, waiting, calm - and `WAITING` binds to `--orange` at `src/basicly/board_wall.py:73`. The state is `WAITING` whenever the `asks` section is drawn and its list is non-empty. **There is no duration threshold.** A five-second-old ask paints exactly the same orange as a six-day-old one; only the headline text scales. Orange is this page's only alarm channel (`board_wall.py:22-24`), so the one channel that should mean "act now" fires on existence.

**One quantity is stated twice in two units.** The headline is `coarse(waited)` and the detail is `duration(_waited(ask, now))`, both computed from the same `_waited(asks[0], now)` (`board_regions.py:172-179`). Measured on a probe render: 577,020 s renders as `6 DAYS` and as `160h 17m`. The second adds no fact.

**Nothing on the page says what it is.** A full-text scan of `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2` finds no tooltip, no `title=` attribute and no legend entry for the band. `legend()` (`board_footer.py:263-274`) glosses section render-states only.

## What the reader needs instead

The band is the page's only alarm. A reader must learn from it, without a second source: that the factory is stopped, that a person is what stops it, how long that has been true, whether that is normal or bad, and what to do next. Today it supplies the third of those and half the first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an ask has waited, THE BAND STATE SHALL be chosen from the wait duration against declared thresholds, so a short wait and a long wait do not paint the same colour.
- WHEN the band names a duration, IT SHALL state that duration once, in one unit.
- WHEN the band renders, IT SHALL state in plain words what is waiting and what a reader would do about it, without abbreviation a reader must already know.
- WHERE the thresholds live, THEY SHALL be configuration this repository declares rather than constants inside the region, and the test SHALL drive a wait across each boundary.
- WHERE no ask is pending, THE BAND SHALL NOT claim an alarm state.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render the board with at least one ask pending:
   `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html`
2. Read the coloured band beneath the header.
3. Now compare two waits. Render again with an ask a few seconds old, and read the
   band's colour against the first render's colour.

**Observed 2026-08-22.** The band read `▲6 DAYS / 1 WAITING ON A PERSON /
basicly-b2n2 · checkpoint · ship · 160h 16m`. `6 DAYS` and `160h 16m` are the same
quantity - both are `_waited(asks[0], now)` - in two units.

**Observed on the colour.** The band paints `--orange` for any non-empty asks list.
A five-second wait and a six-day wait paint identically; only the headline words
differ.

**Expected.** The page's only alarm channel distinguishes a wait that is normal from
one that has stopped the factory, states the duration once, and says what to do.

**Control.** With no ask pending the band takes the calm state, so the region does
respond to the asks list - it just does not respond to how long.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_wall.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_wall.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `120000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Render the board with an ask injected at each side of every declared threshold and read the band's colour and words at each, against a control render with no ask pending.

## Context

Observed 2026-08-23 on the basicly-k6tpep supervise session launched with --tier medium under an L3 110M grant. At the first ship checkpoint the engine declined the grant's delegation with: 'L3 grant cannot be metered: 1 dispatch(es) under it reported no measurable usage, so only a chars/4 floor over their captured output exists (514323 estimated, far below real spend) and 54598042/110000000 tokens is not what this grant has cost; the session is human-only until re-granted or the runner is configured with a usage format' (decision basicly-ze0po3#ec15dfaca8). The decline is correct behaviour - an unmeterable grant must not self-approve - but the cause is that a dispatch under a tier override emits usage the meter does not parse, so every checkpoint of an otherwise autonomous session returns to a human. The prior unmeterable case (the decider dispatch) was fixed 2026-08-03; this is the tier-override variant.

## Steps to Reproduce

Grant L3 with a token budget on an epic, run basicly loop supervise <epic> --tier medium, let one lane finish and reach ship. The grant declines with the cannot-be-metered message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane dispatches under a --tier override, THE RUN RECORD SHALL carry measured usage in the same format as a default-tier dispatch, or name the model whose stream lacked it.
- WHEN every dispatch under a grant carries measured usage, THE GRANT SHALL remain delegable for checkpoints.
- WHEN a dispatch reports no measurable usage, THE DECLINE MESSAGE SHALL name the dispatch and the model so the operator can fix the runner configuration rather than guess.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `tests/test_run_record.py`

payload.value:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-23 on the wall board: 'kas8q7 - checkpoint - classify - 1h 54m' rendered in the action band as a NEEDS YOU ask while (1) basicly loop decisions basicly-kas8q7 returned an empty list, (2) the live L3 grant on basicly-xglise delegates classify and ship (preflight prints 'checkpts: classify pending - the live L3 grant delegates it'), and (3) the lane was dispatched and running at that moment under the same supervisor. The checkpoint record stays PENDING until the engine crosses the boundary, so the board derives a human ask from a checkpoint no human needs to answer, and its age clock dates from provisioning - the owner reads a 2 hour bottleneck that does not exist. The one signal the action band exists for trains the owner to ignore it.

**Second observed case, 2026-08-23 evening, reported by the owner.** The band read
'2 waiting on a person / basicly-kas8q7 - checkpoint - classify - 3h 45m / +1 more waiting'
while basicly-kas8q7 had been CLOSED for hours. A checkpoint of a closed record is not
answerable by anyone: there was nothing a human could do, no information the board offered,
and no action that applied. The owner's words: 'this seems misleading.'

## Steps to Reproduce

Grant L3 on an epic, provision a lane, let the supervisor run it; render the board while the lane is in build. The classify checkpoint shows as a pending ask with a growing age.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a pending checkpoint whose issue is covered by a live grant that delegates it then the action band does not render it as a NEEDS YOU ask.
Given a pending checkpoint whose record is closed then the action band never renders it.
Given a pending checkpoint not covered by a grant then the ask renders exactly as today.
Given a decision in the queue (loop decisions non-empty) then it renders as an ask regardless of grants.
Demonstrated by: render the board against a fixture with a granted pending checkpoint and one queued decision, and assert the band holds only the decision.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`
- `tests/test_board_render.py`

## Context

Owner feedback 2026-08-23, watching the live wall while six lanes built: 'there are 6 items in build and all have status open as if nothing is happening. it is impossible to identify what these items on the cards are a part of. having only an ID on the card does not help a human. humans do not memorize IDs. ... There is still too few signals - correct signals - on the board for human to fully trust it and understand what is going on. and the cards probably need to be larger or need to be able to be expanded to see the full messages during work.'

Three gaps in one card:

1. The card's primary status is the tracker record status ('open'), which never changes during a build, so six working lanes read as six idle items. The live signal a human needs is the lane's phase and that it is running now - the epic's design of record already rules this: line one is the phase plus 'started N ago'.
2. The card names only the record id. The design of record already found the join that costs nothing: lanes[].id joins units[].title on every snapshot. The title must be the dominant line.
3. Nothing on the card shows what the lane is doing. The supervisor already holds a per-tick activity snippet per lane (the bracketed last-message excerpt it prints every 15s). Surface it: the card carries the current activity line, and a card can expand to the full recent activity without leaving the wall.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is dispatched and running, THE CARD SHALL show the lane phase and a started-ago duration as its primary state, never the tracker record status alone.
- WHEN a card renders, THE UNIT TITLE SHALL be its dominant line via the units[] join, with the id demoted to a dim address line.
- WHEN the producer holds an activity excerpt for a running lane, THE CARD SHALL render it, and expanding the card SHALL show the recent activity in full.
- WHERE no supervisor is writing snapshots, THE CARD SHALL say the lane is not confirmed live rather than implying activity.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a supervise pass with several lanes, open the board, and compare a card against basicly loop status for the same id: the card says 'open' and an id; the status says build, a worktree and a branch.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Three occurrences on 2026-08-23, one supervised session each time: a record closes on main, its changelog.d fragment lands there, and every live lane worktree seeded before that close fails release-notes at its next commit - the gate is always_run at pre-commit, so the lane cannot commit at all, and cannot rebase either because that needs a clean or committed tree. Two lanes deadlocked on basicly-bom07a's fragment and then on basicly-1hp91f's (resolved by hand-copying the fragments with git checkout main -- <path>); basicly-wctp0g then failed the same way on basicly-ze0po3's fragment minutes after that record closed. The gate already diagnoses the case exactly: 'changelog.d/<id> is on the base branch and absent here: this tree is behind, not in debt. Rebase.' A gate that names the remedy it prevents is a deadlock, not a control.

## Steps to Reproduce

Seed two lanes, let lane A land and close with a changelog fragment, then have lane B attempt any commit. release-notes fails naming A's record; B cannot commit or rebase.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the fragment a closed record owes exists on the base branch and the judged tree merely predates it, THE GATE SHALL report the case as a warning naming the rebase, and SHALL NOT fail.
- WHEN the fragment exists on neither the judged tree nor the base branch, THE GATE SHALL fail exactly as today.
- WHEN the gate runs on the base branch itself, ITS BEHAVIOUR SHALL be unchanged.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_release_notes.py`
- `tests/test_check_release_notes.py`

body.post_ship_action: Owner pushes and tags; I move neither. Immediately after the tag, file three follow-up records against basicly-jr0l: (1) absent-state tests for board_footer.gates and board_footer.events so the fragment's six-cell list is fully bound, since the sentence ships as written; (2) the page-level vocabulary criterion against board_regions.py:207 and :367, which must also retire or invert tests/test_board_render.py:265 - that test currently requires the phrase the criterion forbids, so the two cannot both stand; (3) correct the board-snapshot.json reachability claim, either by emitting the render verdict into the sidecar or by amending the record to say the verdict is recomputable rather than present. Until (2) lands, do not repeat the acceptance criterion as satisfied on any consumer surface - README, site, release notes or repository description.

unsupported.claim: The board's own footer cells (spend, gates, agents, dep edges, events, and the "not drawn" roster) no longer spell an absent section as `not emitted by this producer`
unsupported.why: Two of the six named cells have no test on the branch the claim is about. board_footer.gates and board_footer.events route through the shared `_say` helper (src/basicly/board_footer.py:86) only when `read.drawn` is false, and nothing exercises that. The single gates assertion is a control in the opposite direction - tests/test_board_footer.py:130 reads `assert board_footer.gates(reads)[0].value != absent, "the fixture emits gates"`, which proves the fixture draws gates, not that an undrawn gates cell avoids the phrase. The only events test, tests/test_board_footer.py:139, calls `board_footer.events(_reads("wall-v1.json"))` on a fixture that draws. I looked for an absent-state fixture reaching either cell across tests/ and found none. The claim is true by code reading and false by evidence for `gates` and `events`.

unsupported.claim: WHEN a section is genuinely withheld or absent, THE AFFECTED REGION SHALL say so in words a reader without the schema can act on, and SHALL NOT use the words `producer`, `emitted`, `section` or `withheld`.
unsupported.why: Unmet on the shipped page. `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/jbd_check.html` then grepping the output gives 3 hits for `not emitted by this producer`, 5 for `producer` and 3 for `withheld`, including the rendered string `current position: lanes not emitted by this producer`. The source is board_regions.py:207 and board_regions.py:367, which interpolate board_wall.ABSENT_TEXT (defined board_wall.py:42) and are outside this record's declared scope. A committed test pins the opposite of the criterion: tests/test_board_render.py:265 asserts `board_wall.ABSENT_TEXT in flight, "the collapsed row named no producer"`, so removing the phrase from that region would turn the suite red. The changelog fragment does not make this page-level claim - it scopes itself to the footer cells - so no consumer-facing sentence is false; the acceptance criterion itself is what is unmet.

unsupported.claim: board_wall.ABSENT_TEXT is unchanged and still backs board-snapshot.json, the sidecar a producer author reads for the schema's own vocabulary.
unsupported.why: Contradicted by the artifact. The same board run wrote /tmp/board-snapshot.json; parsing it gives 0 occurrences of `not emitted by this producer`, 0 of `withheld` and 0 of `renderable`. Its top-level keys are the producer document (asks, backlog, events, freshness, gates, generator, graph, health, repo, schema, spend) - the verdict is recomputable from it, as the record's own description says, but it is not carried in it. This backs acceptance criterion three ("WHEN a producer author needs the verdict, IT SHALL remain reachable, and the record SHALL name where"), and the named place does not hold the thing. The claim lives in commit 319a221a's message rather than the changelog fragment, so it reaches a developer reading git log, not a consumer reading release notes.

## Context

Owner feedback 2026-08-23, watching the live wall while six lanes built: 'there are 6 items in build and all have status open as if nothing is happening. it is impossible to identify what these items on the cards are a part of. having only an ID on the card does not help a human. humans do not memorize IDs. ... There is still too few signals - correct signals - on the board for human to fully trust it and understand what is going on. and the cards probably need to be larger or need to be able to be expanded to see the full messages during work.'

Three gaps in one card:

1. The card's primary status is the tracker record status ('open'), which never changes during a build, so six working lanes read as six idle items. The live signal a human needs is the lane's phase and that it is running now - the epic's design of record already rules this: line one is the phase plus 'started N ago'.
2. The card names only the record id. The design of record already found the join that costs nothing: lanes[].id joins units[].title on every snapshot. The title must be the dominant line.
3. Nothing on the card shows what the lane is doing. The supervisor already holds a per-tick activity snippet per lane (the bracketed last-message excerpt it prints every 15s). Surface it: the card carries the current activity line, and a card can expand to the full recent activity without leaving the wall.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane is dispatched and running, THE CARD SHALL show the lane phase and a started-ago duration as its primary state, never the tracker record status alone.
- WHEN a card renders, THE UNIT TITLE SHALL be its dominant line via the units[] join, with the id demoted to a dim address line.
- WHEN the producer holds an activity excerpt for a running lane, THE CARD SHALL render it, and expanding the card SHALL show the recent activity in full.
- WHEN a lane is dispatched and its first run has not finished, THE CARD SHALL show the agent and model the supervisor dispatched (it holds both at dispatch time), not blanks until a run record exists.
- WHERE no supervisor is writing snapshots, THE CARD SHALL say the lane is not confirmed live rather than implying activity.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a supervise pass with several lanes, open the board, and compare a card against basicly loop status for the same id: the card says 'open' and an id; the status says build, a worktree and a branch.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23: every lane commit runs all 34 checks plus the full 4900-test suite (~2 min), then the landing runs them all again on the rebased tree. Quality needs the full suite exactly once per landing, on the rebased tree. The lane's inner loop only needs the gates whose inputs its diff touches.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane commits, THE PRE-COMMIT SUITE SHALL run the gates whose declared inputs intersect the diff, plus the always-cheap ones, and skip the rest naming the skip.
- WHEN a landing verifies, IT SHALL run the full suite unchanged.
- WHEN a skipped gate would have failed, THE LANDING SHALL still catch it - no green landing may depend on a skipped gate.
- Demonstrated by: a doc-only commit timed against today's baseline, and a landing that still refuses a planted cross-scope defect.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/`
payload.title: gates run whole-suite on every commit where a scoped subset would hold quality

payload.description:
## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23: six landings today each took 3-8 minutes wall-clock. A landing rebases, runs the full 34-gate suite plus 4900 tests, regenerates artifacts, merges, and commits tracker state. Which slice dominates is unmeasured - fix the measurement first, then cut the dominant slice. Candidate cuts once measured: run the full suite once not per hook layer, skip re-verify when the rebase was a fast-forward of an already-verified tree, parallelise independent gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a landing runs, IT SHALL record a per-stage timing breakdown on the run record.
- WHEN the dominant stage is known, A FOLLOW-UP RECORD SHALL carry the cut with the measured before/after.
- Demonstrated by: one landing's recorded breakdown summing to its wall clock.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`

## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23: each lane worktree runs uv sync, npm install and hook install (~1-2 min) although every sibling provisions the identical environment from the same lockfiles. Claude's own background isolation creates worktrees with no per-tree install at all - the repo already sets worktree.bgIsolation=none and relies on the harness. uv hardlinks from a shared cache, so the cost is mostly resolver and npm overhead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a worktree is provisioned and the lockfiles match a previously provisioned sibling, PROVISIONING SHALL reuse the cached environment instead of resolving again.
- WHEN lockfiles differ, THE FULL SYNC SHALL run as today.
- Demonstrated by: second-worktree provisioning timed against today's baseline with identical lockfiles.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/worktree.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23: 'checkpoints that wait on people should be immediately visible and actionable - that is why we are building a board.' Today a real decision waited 2240 s and a metering halt made every ship wait, while the board either showed stale asks (fixed by basicly-0i86tl) or showed them only on the supervisor's next snapshot. The action route exists (checkpoint-approve, loop-answer with a typed code) but the ask row does not always carry the exact command, and a new ask appears only when a producer writes a snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a decision or human-owed checkpoint is queued, THE BOARD SHALL render it within one fold even with no supervisor running.
- WHEN an ask renders, IT SHALL carry the exact command to answer it and the working action form beside it.
- WHEN the ask is answered anywhere, THE ROW SHALL clear on the next fold.
- Demonstrated by: queue a decision with no supervisor, watch it appear and answer it from the board.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`

## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23: a fresh context is right for review, architecture and analysis - independence is the point - but an implementer working the same feature re-derives the repo from zero every dispatch, 1-3M tokens before the first edit, measured on every lane today. The mechanism is already measured: --resume --fork-session gives ~10x cheaper warm starts, one-time penalty per working directory (plan row ejdm). What is missing is the policy: per-role inheritance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a dispatch role is implementer or repair on a feature with a seeded session, THE DISPATCH SHALL fork the seeded session instead of starting cold.
- WHEN the role is a reviewer, validator, decider or retrospector, THE DISPATCH SHALL stay cold, and the policy names why.
- WHEN no seed exists, THE FIRST DISPATCH SHALL create it.
- Demonstrated by: two consecutive implementer dispatches on one feature, the second's cache-read share and cost against today's cold baseline.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/roles.py`
payload.title: context strategy is one-size-cold where the role decides what a dispatch should inherit

## Context

Observed 2026-08-23 twice: after the crash, kas8q7 and e2mz.48.3 sat committed and rebased on their branches, and the next pass dispatched full agent runs (~12M tokens combined) instead of landing them. A lane whose branch carries commits, whose tree is clean and whose gates pass needs the merge queue, not an implementer.

## Steps to Reproduce

Commit a lane's work on its harness branch by hand, leave the tree clean, run a supervise pass: the lane is re-dispatched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a lane's branch has commits ahead of base and a clean tree, THE PASS SHALL route it to the landing queue without an agent dispatch.
- WHEN the landing then fails a gate, THE NORMAL REWORK PATH SHALL apply.
- Demonstrated by: the reproduction above ending in a landing with zero dispatches.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`

payload.text: [owner-decision 2026-08-23] Placement ruled: worktrees STAY siblings, never nested inside the repo. Claude nests its own under .claude/worktrees/ and gains free node_modules reuse via Node's upward resolution plus a single permission root - but a nested tree makes every whole-tree census gate double-count unless each gate excludes it, and that was observed here (agent worktrees poisoned whole-tree gates; markdownlint already bit an ignored dir, basicly-g5ce75). A new gate that forgets the exclude corrupts a ratchet through a green run - fail-open. So this record buys the reuse explicitly instead: share the uv environment when lockfiles match, link node_modules from a provisioned sibling; Python gets no upward resolution so nesting would not even help it.

payload.value:
## Context

Reported by the operator 2026-08-22 as part of "we need improvements all over the board". The wall shows fourteen of one hundred and eighty seven ready units and prints `NEXT UP — +173 MORE READY`.

## The cap is fixed to the smallest supported wall

`board_regions.py:83-97` declares `READY_SLOTS_WIDE = 14` and `READY_SLOTS = 8`, and its own comment states the arithmetic: *14 rows of 24.1px under an 18.2px heading is what fits ... against 26 at 1920x1080*, and *both figures are the shortest wall this layout claims, not the roomiest*.

So on a 1920x1080 screen the region draws 14 rows where 26 fit. Measured on a probe render at 1920x1080: exactly 14 `<tr>` elements. Roughly half the available height is left blank, by construction rather than by overflow.

Row geometry, measured from `board_page.html.j2:412-416`: font-size 17px, line-height 1.3, padding 1px 0, giving 24.1px per row under an 18.2px heading.

## Why a fixed cap was right and is not now

A fixed cap cannot overflow, and the overflow instrument (`.scripts/check_render_overflow.py`) exists because four board pages shipped clipped. Choosing the smallest wall was the safe answer before that instrument existed. It now exists, so a fit computed from the viewport can be **measured** at each width the layout claims rather than assumed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the wall renders at a given viewport height, THE NUMBER OF ROWS DRAWN SHALL be derived from that height and the measured row geometry, not from a constant.
- WHEN the derived count exceeds what fits, THE RENDER SHALL NOT clip, and `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` SHALL report neither overflow nor overlap at every width the layout claims.
- WHEN rows are omitted, THE HEADING SHALL still state how many, as it does now.
- WHERE the viewport is unknown to the producer, THE FIT SHALL be resolved where the viewport is known rather than guessed at build time.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Render the board: `uv run basicly board --out /tmp/b.html`
2. Count the rows the ready region draws: `grep -c '<tr>' /tmp/b.html`
3. Compute what fits: the region's row height is 24.1px (17px at line-height 1.3,
   plus 1px padding top and bottom) under an 18.2px heading.

**Observed 2026-08-22.** Exactly 14 rows, at every viewport, while the region's own
comment at `board_regions.py:90-97` states that 26 fit at 1920x1080 and that 14 is
the figure for the shortest wall the layout claims.

**Expected.** The count is derived from the height actually available.

**Control that this is a cap and not an overflow.**
`uv run python .scripts/check_render_overflow.py /tmp/b.html --width 1920 --height 1080`
reports neither signal, so nothing is being clipped - the space is simply not used.
Run the instrument against `tests/fixtures/render/clipped-and-not.html` first to see
it fire, or a clean result proves nothing.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `tests/test_board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_render.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `110000`
- depends on: `basicly-v8jwf0`
- demonstration: Render at 1440x900, 1600x1200 and 1920x1080, count the rows drawn at each, and run `.scripts/check_render_overflow.py` at each width reading both the overflow line and the overlap line.

payload.description:
## Context

Owner retro 2026-08-23 and the 2026-08-26 session: the factory is slower per unit than a bare agent, half by design and half by measured waste. This epic groups the throughput and reliability defects so one supervised pass can fan out over them. It replaces no record; every child was filed on its own evidence.

## Success Criteria

- A supervised pass over this epic lands every child with no human intervention caused by a harness defect.
- A committed, clean lane is landed by the supervisor with zero agent dispatches (basicly-pjaudy).
- A behind worktree commits while a sibling record closes on main (basicly-h8dxhy).
- A `--tier` override dispatch carries measured usage and the grant stays delegable (basicly-6y0tg5).
- A landing records a per-stage timing breakdown (basicly-tjhjmk).

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN every child is closed, THE EPIC SHALL close with a retro comment naming what each child measured before and after.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `.scripts/check_release_notes.py`
payload.title: Factory throughput and reliability: the pass lands without a human step caused by the harness

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on basicly-ibzr0f. The lane judged its change test-only and wrote no `changelog.d` fragment, as its brief allows. The build->verify landing merged green: `release-notes` judges closed records, and the record was still open. `loop run` at ship then dispatched the curator, tore the worktree down, closed the record, and the closing commit `chore(beads): close the shipped track` was refused by `release-notes` (33/34). The record sat closed in the staged ledger with no worktree left to repair in; a human wrote the invisible declaration on main. basicly-mcf2uh hit the same shape on 2026-08-23.

## Steps to Reproduce

Land a lane whose record declares a shipped path under `## Scope` and whose branch carries no `changelog.d/<id>.*.md` and no `[tool.release_notes.invisible]` entry. `basicly loop advance <id>` merges green. `basicly loop run <id>` ships, closes the record, and the closing commit is refused by `release-notes`. Expected: the landing refuses before the merge, while the lane still has a worktree to repair in.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the landing verifies a lane whose record declares a shipped path under `## Scope`, and the rebased tree holds neither `changelog.d/<id>.<category>.md` nor an invisible declaration for that record, THE LANDING SHALL fail `release-notes` naming both remedies, before the merge.
- WHEN the fragment or the declaration is present, THE LANDING SHALL pass as today.
- WHEN `release-notes` runs outside a landing, ITS BEHAVIOUR SHALL be unchanged.
- WHEN a dispatch brief is assembled for a record that declares a shipped path, THE BRIEF SHALL say that `release-notes` demands a fragment or an invisible declaration at ship for this record, instead of leaving the judgment to the lane.

## Scope

- `.scripts/check_release_notes.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_check_release_notes.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`
payload.title: a landing admits a lane that owes a release note so the ship close is refused by release-notes

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on basicly-0xtzf1. A landing failed pytest and wrote a repair brief. The defect was fixed by hand in the worktree and committed on the branch. The next `loop advance` blocked with `the repair brief for gate 'merge' was written against <old head> and the branch is now at <new head>, so its defect may already be fixed; re-run the gate to raise a brief against what is there now (needs input: validation)`. `repair_brief.take_repair_brief` had already unlinked the brief on that read, so the following `loop advance` landed normally. The message names a step that does not exist, and the block costs one invocation and one human read per hand repair.

## Steps to Reproduce

Land a lane whose verify fails on the rebased tree, so `_repair_in_place` writes `.basicly/usage/repair-brief.json` in the worktree. Fix the defect by hand, commit on the branch, run `basicly loop advance <id>`. Observed: blocked, needs input `validation`. Expected: the stale brief is discarded with a note and the landing runs in the same invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a repair brief is stale against the branch head, THE ADVANCE SHALL discard it, record on the lane that it did and why, and continue to the landing in the same invocation.
- WHEN the brief is not stale, THE REPAIR DISPATCH SHALL run as today.
- WHEN the brief predates the `branch_head` field or the head does not resolve, THE REPAIR DISPATCH SHALL run as today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/repair_brief.py`
- `tests/test_loop_repair.py`
- `tests/test_repair_brief.py`
payload.title: the stale repair brief refusal names a gate re-run when the brief is already consumed

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on the basicly-k6tpep pass. Two of three sibling lanes, basicly-0xtzf1 and basicly-ffm2yp, edited `src/basicly/board_render.py`, a path the third sibling basicly-a68ggd declared. Each landing blocked with `needs input: scope`, and a human widened each record and advanced again. `basicly brief <id>` prints the lane's own `## Scope` nowhere and its siblings' scopes nowhere, so the lane learns of the collision only from the merge queue.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run `basicly brief <child>` for a child whose root has open siblings with a declared `## Scope`. Observed: the brief names no path the lane may not edit. Expected: the brief lists the sibling-owned paths and the route to take when the work needs one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a brief is assembled for a lane whose root has open siblings with a declared `## Scope`, THE BRIEF SHALL list the paths each open sibling declares and say that an edit there blocks the landing until a human rules on the scope.
- WHEN the lane's own `## Scope` is declared, THE BRIEF SHALL restate it as the paths the landing admits.
- WHEN the work needs a sibling's path, THE BRIEF SHALL name `needs-input.json` with fact `scope` as the route, and not an edit.
- WHEN the root has no open sibling, THE BRIEF SHALL be unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_dispatch_brief.py`
- `tests/test_cli_brief_outcomes.py`
payload.title: a lane brief names no sibling owned path so a scope collision surfaces only at landing

## Context

`docs/architecture/status.md` is generated from `status.yaml` and is the only file that grades a capability. Four rows under "The board" read `designed` on 2026-08-26 while the tree holds the behaviour: "A command that emits a snapshot" says nothing calls the producer, yet `basicly board --out` writes `board-snapshot.json`; "A rendered page a human can open" says no renderer and no template exist, yet `src/basicly/board_render.py` and `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2` render the page the owner reviews; "Live modes" says sequenced behind the page, yet `basicly board serve` refreshes on the supervisor's 15-second tick with a wall view. Only the conformance kit row may be true: `.basicly/core/kit/` holds `tier` and `tracker`, no `board`. A status view that under-reports is as wrong as one that over-reports: it says the next unit is a renderer that already exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN each board row is graded, ITS STATUS SHALL match the vocabulary in architecture §2 against evidence measured in the tree, and the note SHALL name the command or module that is the evidence.
- WHEN a row stays below `shipped`, ITS NOTE SHALL name what is missing, not what was missing when it was written.
- WHEN the regenerated `status.md` is committed, `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check` SHALL pass.

## Scope

- `docs/architecture/status.yaml`
- `docs/architecture/status.md`

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-08-26 during the live basicly-zq9i2m pass, 109 s after dispatch, from `curl http://127.0.0.1:8377/snapshot.json`. A running lane row carried exactly `branch, id, live, note, phase, provisioned, status, tokens`. The snapshot schema (`.basicly/core/schemas/board-snapshot.schema.json`) declares `agent, model, started_at, elapsed_s, cost_usd, context_used, context_window, rework_attempt, rework_allowance` on a lane as well. The supervisor holds the agent, the model (`claude-opus-5`, tier `high`) and the dispatch time when it spawns the process, so the omission is not an unknown value. basicly-0xtzf1 shipped the card that draws these fields; with this producer the card draws the title, the phase and the tokens only, and the acceptance clause "show the agent and model the supervisor dispatched" holds on the fixture and fails on the live wall.

## Steps to Reproduce

Start `basicly loop supervise <epic>` with one dispatchable child, then `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8377/snapshot.json | jq '.lanes[0] | keys'`. Observed: no `agent`, `model`, `started_at`, `elapsed_s`. Expected: all four present while the lane runs, omitted only when the producer does not hold them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the supervisor dispatches a lane, THE NEXT SNAPSHOT SHALL carry the lane's `agent`, `model` and `started_at` from the dispatch it issued.
- WHILE the lane runs, EACH SNAPSHOT SHALL carry `elapsed_s` derived from `started_at`, and `cost_usd` and `context_used` where the live stream reports them.
- WHEN a value is genuinely unknown, THE KEY SHALL be omitted, never estimated (the omit-never-estimate rule).
- WHEN the lane finishes, THE ROW SHALL NOT carry a live value from the previous dispatch.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_sections.py`
- `tests/test_supervise_board.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_sections.py`

## Context

A read-only survey on 2026-08-26 checked architecture.md §17, §22-§31, §36 and status.yaml against the code. Ten claims are refuted by the code (each CONFIRMED by reading the symbol named). The owner's doctrine applies: delete the prose, or rewrite it and bind it to a tripwire in `tests/test_docs_drift.py` so it cannot drift again. Sections not surveyed: §1, §4-§16, §18-§21, §26.3-4, §29.2-4, §31.2-6, §32, §34, §35, §36.3-6, §36.8, §37, §38, §39, §40.

1. §3 line ~202 and §36.7 line ~3700 say nothing runs code to document for `§N` citations. `.scripts/check_code_citations.py` exists and is wired as verify check `code-citations` in `basicly.d/basicly-e2mz.49.toml`; `backlog.md` records B2 as landed. Fix: delete the TARGET paragraph in §3 (keep the probe), delete the §36.7 sentence, name `code-citations` beside `docs-citations` in the §36.6 ratchet table, flip `status.yaml` line ~106 to `shipped`.
2. §36.2 lines ~3475-3479 count fast 22, full 26, total 27. `config.load_verify_config(Path('.'))` over basicly.toml plus basicly.d returns total 39, fast 34, full 38, staged 3. Fix: correct the table and bind the four numbers to `config.load_verify_config` in `tests/test_docs_drift.py`.
3. §22 line ~1359 says `board serve` answers GET alone and a POST is 405. `src/basicly/board_serve.py:309` `do_POST` runs `board_actions.handle_post`; 405 is the `--no-actions` path; `--bind` takes a literal IPv4. `.basicly/core/skills/harness-client/skill.yaml:50` repeats the stale GET-only claim. Fix: rewrite the row (GET reads, one POST route behind a one-time confirm code, `--no-actions` removes it, `--bind` for a wall) and the skill line; pin the row against `board_cli.add_parsers` flags.
4. §27.1 lines ~1742-1744 say the tracker redirect file went with the external binary. `src/basicly/tracker_paths.py:24` `REDIRECT_NAME = "redirect"` and `worktree.py:183` write it at provisioning; §36.3 relies on it. Fix: rewrite to "provisioning writes a git-ignored `redirect` naming the base checkout; `tracker_paths.tracker_root` is the single resolver"; bind on `tracker_paths.REDIRECT_NAME`.
5. §27.1 line ~1759 says the tracker's own three-way merge reconciles tracker state. No merge driver exists in `.gitattributes`; the ledger is append-only and every checkout redirects to base, so no divergent state exists. Fix: delete that sentence and the one after it.
6. §23.3 lines ~1518-1520 say per-type templates are compiled into the tracker binary and a test pins the installed binary. `config.py:435` `DEFAULT_TYPE_SECTIONS` and `config.load_type_sections` read `[policy.type_sections]`; the binary is removed. Fix: rewrite to the config table with the engine fallback, pinned by `tests/test_config.py`.
7. §28.2 diagram line ~1891 labels admission gate 3 "grant coverage / does the level delegate this". `supervise.py:1955-1959` calls `metered_without_a_budget` (`supervise.py:1386`): the gate refuses a metered runner with no budget-carrying grant; delegation coverage is checked at checkpoint approval only. Fix: relabel the node and cite the function.
8. §36.1 line ~3443 says layer 3 runs the same checks as layer 2. `.basicly/core/hooks/pre-commit.py` runs mode fast (34 checks), `pre-push.py` runs full (38). Fix: rewrite to "layer 3 runs the same full mode as layer 2's pre-push stage; pre-commit runs the narrower fast mode".
9. §30 line ~2192 says 11 agent sources plus 4 shared blocks. `.basicly/core/agents/blocks/` holds five `*.block.yaml`. Fix: write 5 and bind both counts in `tests/test_docs_drift.py`.
10. status.yaml lines ~235-248 grade three board rows `designed` (snapshot command, rendered page, live modes) while `board_cli.py` has `cmd_emit`, `cmd_serve`, `board_render.page` renders `board_page.html.j2`, and `cli.py:3513` emits a tick snapshot from the heartbeat. Covered by basicly-stqfoh, which this record depends on; do not edit those rows here.

Verified correct, no change: §9.1-2, §17, §23.3 checkpoints, §24 ladder, §25 funnel, §26.2, §28.1, §28.3, §29.1, §29.5, §30 role table, §33 kinds, §22 command count, §36.7 block counts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN each of findings 1-9 is applied, THE DOCUMENT SHALL state what the cited code does, and `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check`, `uv run pytest tests/test_docs_drift.py -q` and `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` SHALL pass.
- WHEN a finding carries a number (2, 8, 9), THE NUMBER SHALL be bound to the code that produces it by a tripwire in `tests/test_docs_drift.py`, so a later change fails a test rather than drifting.
- WHEN the survey's unreached sections are listed, THE RECORD'S CLOSING COMMENT SHALL name them so the next survey starts there.

## Scope

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `docs/architecture/status.yaml`
- `docs/architecture/status.md`
- `tests/test_docs_drift.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-client/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/harness-client/SKILL.md`

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-26 on the basicly-zq9i2m pass, log lines `wip: 0/5 unlanded downstream of build; 5 lane(s) admitted; REFUSED: basicly-oqspon` and `dispatch: basicly-oqspon via claude - not started: downstream work in progress is at the [policy] max_downstream_wip limit of 5 (0 unit(s) past build)`. Six lanes were ready, `[worktree] concurrency` is 10, nothing was past build, and one slot stayed idle for a whole pass.

Two sources describe one bound and disagree. `src/basicly/wip.py` (module docstring, "The pass's own admissions count toward the limit") admits `limit - downstream` lanes per pass and refuses the rest. `basicly.toml` `[policy] max_downstream_wip` says the opposite: "Ten lanes may run, and the sixth to finish waits for one of the first five to land ... make review, not slots or tokens, the thing that limits throughput." Requirement 3.1 reads "downstream WIP below limit", which the config comment follows and the code does not. The owner's 2026-08-23 retro named idle capacity as the factory's cost; this bound idles half of a ten-slot pass by design while the review queue is empty.

## Steps to Reproduce

Root with 6 ready children, `[worktree] concurrency = 10`, `[policy] max_downstream_wip = 5`, nothing past build. `basicly loop supervise <root>`: observed 5 admitted, 1 refused naming the limit with 0 units past build. Expected: 6 admitted; a refusal only once 5 units stand in verify, validate or ship.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN fewer than `max_downstream_wip` units stand downstream of build, THE PASS SHALL admit every ready lane up to `[worktree] concurrency`, and the count of lanes admitted in the same pass SHALL NOT reduce the headroom.
- WHEN `max_downstream_wip` or more units stand downstream of build, THE PASS SHALL refuse further dispatch naming the units to land, as today.
- WHEN the bound is described, `wip.py`'s docstring, `basicly.toml`'s comment and architecture §28.2 SHALL state the same rule.
- Demonstrated by: a test with 10 ready, limit 5, concurrency 10, 0 downstream that admits 10; and one with 5 downstream that admits 0.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/wip.py`
- `tests/test_wip.py`
- `basicly.toml`

## Context

Measured 2026-08-26 in the basicly-zq9i2m supervisor log: 25 lines `warning: VIRTUAL_ENV=<base>/.venv does not match the project environment path .venv and will be ignored` in one landing. The supervisor is launched with `uv run`, which exports `VIRTUAL_ENV` for the base checkout; `verify.run_check` (`src/basicly/verify.py:228`) and the lane dispatch (`src/basicly/runner.py:1513`) hand that environment to every subprocess whose cwd is a worktree, where `.venv` is a different directory. `uv` ignores the variable, so the tree runs correctly, and prints the warning on every gate. The noise buries the one gate line an operator reads a landing by, and a lane agent reads it too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the engine starts a subprocess whose cwd is not the checkout `VIRTUAL_ENV` points into, THE ENVIRONMENT SHALL NOT carry `VIRTUAL_ENV`.
- WHEN the cwd is that checkout, THE ENVIRONMENT SHALL be unchanged.
- WHEN a landing runs in a worktree, ITS LOG SHALL contain no `does not match the project environment path` line.
- Demonstrated by: a test that sets `VIRTUAL_ENV` to a base path, runs a check with a worktree cwd through `verify.run_check`, and asserts the variable is absent from the argv's environment.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Observed 2026-08-26, basicly-zq9i2m round 1, supervisor log: `routed: basicly-j7spdb -> error - routing failed: a gate refused git commit -m chore(beads): sync tracker state for the harness loop (basicly-j7spdb): pre-commit-script refused: [tester] WARNING nosec encountered (B607) ... Contracts: 3 kept, 0 broken.` Then `routed: basicly-pjaudy -> held - landing paused after an earlier failure this pass` and the same for basicly-1djm17. Round 2 re-dispatched basicly-j7spdb to an implementer although its branch held 2 commits on a clean tree. `uv run basicly verify --mode fast` in base 20 minutes later: 34/34 pass. Three defects in one chain:

1. `checkout._failure` (`src/basicly/checkout.py:117-131`) hands the joined hook output to `gate_refusal`, which returned the bandit `nosec` warnings and the import-linter summary instead of the `FAILED: <check>` line and the `checks failed: N/M` summary. The operator cannot tell which gate refused a ledger-only commit, so the cause stays unknown.
2. `supervise.route_outcomes` (`src/basicly/supervise.py:3055-3062`) turns any RuntimeError from `_route_one` into route `error`, and the next pass treats an `error` lane as work to dispatch. A landing that failed on the engine's own tracker-sync commit is not a lane defect; it needs the landing retried, not an agent (~8M tokens, the basicly-pjaudy shape).
3. `landing_blocked` then holds every later green lane for the rest of the pass. That is right for a lane defect that could poison the base, and wrong for an infra refusal the next attempt would clear.

## Steps to Reproduce

Make the tracker-sync pre-commit refuse once (for example a hook that fails on its first call and passes on the second), run a supervise pass with three green lanes. Observed: lane 1 routed `error` with no gate name, lanes 2 and 3 `held`, lane 1 re-dispatched next pass. Expected: the refusal names the check, the tracker-sync commit is retried once, and a committed lane is never re-dispatched over a landing-side refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN an engine-run `git commit` is refused by a hook, THE ERROR SHALL name the failing check from the `FAILED:` line and carry the `checks failed: N/M` summary, and SHALL NOT be built from warning lines alone.
- WHEN the tracker-sync commit is refused and the refusing check passes on an immediate re-run, THE LANDING SHALL continue in the same pass, and the pass narrative SHALL record the retry and the check.
- WHEN a landing fails on the engine's own commit rather than on the lane's diff, THE LANE SHALL keep route `ready to land` for the next pass and SHALL NOT be dispatched to an agent.
- WHEN a landing fails on the lane's diff, THE HELD RULE SHALL apply as today.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/checkout.py`
- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_checkout.py`
- `tests/test_merge_ledger.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

body.post_ship_action: Before the tag moves I have changed nothing and moved nothing; the owner pushes and tags. Immediately after the tag moves: (1) file a bead against the pyright hole with two candidate fixes — add "full" to basicly.toml's pyright `modes`, or add a check_runner-level assertion that every check declaring `inputs` is also declared for `full` — and prefer the second, because it is the gate that makes the changelog sentence true for the next check anyone adds; (2) amend the shipped fragment's third clause, or the release notes entry it becomes, to state the exception rather than the unconditional 'nothing green rests on a skip'. unsupported.claim: `--mode full` (the landing, the push) ignores `inputs` and runs all of them, so nothing green rests on a skip (`basicly-j7spdb`).
unsupported.why: The second clause is refuted by a live counterexample in this tree, and nothing enforces it. `full` runs every check declared for `full`, which is not the same set as every check that can be skipped. basicly.toml:182-184 declares `name = "pyright"` with `modes = ["fast", "staged"]` and an `inputs` list, so pyright is skippable at commit time and absent from `full` entirely. Enumerated: `load_inputs(root,'fast') - {n for n,_ in load_checks(root,'full')}` returns `['pyright']` (full mode = 38 checks, pyright not among them). A docs-only commit therefore skips pyright at commit time and no landing and no push runs it. I looked for a test or gate asserting `declared-inputs ⊆ full-mode` and found none: the two invariant tests added by this change (test_every_declared_input_set_matches_something_in_this_repo, test_every_declared_input_set_carries_the_lock) check glob liveness and uv.lock membership, not mode membership, and test_the_landing_mode_still_fails_on_a_gate_the_commit_skipped uses a synthetic fixture whose gate is declared `modes = ["fast", "full"]`, so it cannot see this case. ## Context

Observed 2026-08-26, basicly-zq9i2m pass 2 (log `supervise-zq9i2m-2.log`): the round adopted four merged lanes at verify, then seeded (`Created worktree` for 18iz59, 6ajmrc, uq3pki at lines 11-29), then routed the four to `shipped`. basicly-2kh170 (blocked by pjaudy and 6y0tg5) and basicly-08rnmd (blocked by j7spdb) were dispatchable the moment those shipped, but seeding had already run against the pre-ship tracker state, so both wait a full round (30-60 minutes) with 7 of 10 slots idle. The dependency edges are the ones the plan gate asks for, so this cost is paid on every epic with a declared order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a round starts with adopted lanes parked at verify, validate or ship, THE ROUND SHALL advance those parked units before it seeds new lanes.
- WHEN a parked unit closes in that step, A CHILD IT BLOCKED SHALL be eligible for seeding in the same round.
- WHEN no unit is parked, THE ROUND SHALL be unchanged.
- Demonstrated by: a root with child B blocked by child A, A merged and parked at verify under a covering grant; one round ships A and seeds B.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`
- `tests/test_supervise_parked.py`

## Context

Read-only survey on 2026-08-26 of the nine loop skills (`.basicly/core/skills/*/skill.yaml`) and the four always-on fragments that mention the loop, the tracker, worktrees or gates, 61 claims checked against the code. Eleven are refuted; ten CONFIRMED by reading the code or `--help`, one SUSPECTED. Two would make an agent act wrongly (2, 4). Edit the YAML sources only, then `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots`, `basicly build`, and the projection gates.

1. `harness-client/skill.yaml:54-56` says `board serve` binds the loopback only and answers GET alone, a POST is 405. `src/basicly/board_cli.py:136` (`actions=not args.no_actions`, default on), `board_serve.py:402,411`, `board_actions.py:349` (405 only with `--no-actions`), `--bind` on `board serve --help`. Replacement: "It takes no lock and writes no file, but by default it registers one POST route that runs the basicly command an operator submits - pass `--no-actions` for an unattended wall, and leave `--bind` unset so it stays on the loopback."
2. `fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml` body: phases "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → ship → teardown → retro)". `src/basicly/loop_state.py:31` PHASES = intake, classify, decompose, build, verify, validate, ship, done; the `harness-loop` skill description itself says teardown and retro are not phases. Replacement: "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → validate → ship → done)".
3. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:5` and the phase table `:186-194` omit `validate`. `loop.py:451` `_on_validate`, `:470` blocks with `needs_input="validation"`; `validate-as-consumer/skill.yaml:12` covers phase `validate`. Add a table row between verify and ship: "| **validate** | the merged unit owes the consumer check its integrity level requires; the engine dispatches a validator and blocks on `needs input: validation` until a verdict is recorded | `basicly policy gate <id>` to inspect; a failed validate repairs in the lane's worktree and re-lands (see `validate-as-consumer`, `repair-in-place`) |" and fix the description's arrow chain.
4. `catalog-authoring/skill.yaml:41` "Project + verify: `basicly skills-build` then `basicly skills-check`." `src/basicly/skills.py:181-183` writes `.claude/skills` only without a flag; `basicly.toml:415-416` `projection-skills` checks both roots. Replacement: "Project + verify: `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots` then `basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` - bare, both touch only `.claude/skills`, and the `projection-skills` gate checks both roots."
5. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:54-55` "one `chore(ledger)` commit". `merge.py:654` commits `chore(beads): ...`. Replacement: "one `chore(beads)` commit".
6. `decompose-plan/skill.yaml:24` "Acceptance criteria | absent, **or not in EARS**". `plan_gate.py:194` checks presence only; `grep -ri ears src/` is empty (positive control: `demonstration` has many hits). Replacement row: "| Acceptance criteria | absent | The gate checks presence only, so the EARS discipline is yours to keep |".
7. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:401-404` "Two `VERDICT` lines mean fix this first". `cli.py:2966-3269` joins at least eight blockers with `; ` on one line. Replacement: "A `VERDICT: not ready - ...` line joins every blocker it found with `; ` - a dirty base, an unrecognised config key, a metered runner with no token budget, a spent or unmeterable grant, an unapproved root checkpoint, or no open child in the band. Read the whole line."
8. `release-process/skill.yaml:19-21` enumerates four pin files. `release.py:81-86` has `PIN_FILES` plus `PIN_GLOBS = ("docs/how-to/*.md",)`, with the comment that the enumeration is what failed. Add "and every page under `docs/how-to/`".
9. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:194` ship row omits the demonstration guard. `loop.py:646-648` blocks ship with `needs_input="demonstration"` before the not-landed guard. Add: "Two guards run first and both block with no side effects: the recorded demonstration must still select something (`needs input: demonstration`), and the branch must already be merged."
10. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:408` "`supervise.py:_band_verdict`". `src/basicly/working_set.py:285`. Replacement: "`working_set.py:_band_verdict`".
11. SUSPECTED. `decompose-plan/skill.yaml:65` "skills project to **three**" against `:84` "writes two roots"; `skills.py:47-50` has two default roots. Replacement: "the YAML source plus both projected roots - `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`".

Verified correct, no change: `--runner` on run/advance/supervise, the 15-minute confirm TTL, rework n=2, `dep add` without `-t` refused, the label-write refusal, `needs-input.json`, the redirect file, the changelog categories, the four band verdicts, dot-to-hyphen worktree names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN each finding is applied to the YAML source, THE PROJECTED SKILLS AND INSTRUCTIONS SHALL be rebuilt, and `uv run basicly check`, `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots`, `uv run basicly agents-check`, `uv run basicly catalog lint` SHALL pass.
- WHEN the always-on fragment is corrected, THE PROJECTED `AGENTS.md` AND `.claude/CLAUDE.md` SHALL carry the eight-phase chain and no `teardown` or `retro` phase.
- WHEN finding 11 is checked, THE RECORD SHALL say which reading was right before the edit.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-client/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/catalog-authoring/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/decompose-plan/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/release-process/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/**`
- `.agents/skills/**`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- `.basicly/generated-manifest.json`

Fix: relabel the node and cite the function.

Covered by basicly-stqfoh, which this record depends on; do not edit those rows here.

Verified correct, no change: §9.1-2, §17, §23.3 checkpoints, §24 ladder, §25 funnel, §26.2, §28.1, §28.3, §29.1, §29.5, §30 role table, §33 kinds, §22 command count, §36.7 block counts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN each of findings 1-9 is applied, THE DOCUMENT SHALL state what the cited code does, and `uv run python .scripts/docs_claims.py --check`, `uv run pytest tests/test_docs_drift.py -q` and `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` SHALL pass.

## Context

`docs/plan/implementation-plan.md` §7 names the `v1.0.0` row of the release ladder as "stabilize and declare": `1.0` is a promise, so the last release proves it instead of adding capability. On 2026-08-27 no tracker record existed for any §7 item (search of 254 open records for semver, surface, acceptance test, breaking, forward-version, compatibility: zero hits on the §7 work). The row carries seven items; two are already recorded elsewhere (`basicly-tcmy.24` error-path polish, open; `basicly-u2hl.46` scope precedence, closed) and are referenced, not duplicated.

The exit criteria are the §7 exit criteria verbatim: the acceptance test passes on a machine that has never seen this repo; the compatibility policy is published; a surface-breaking commit without a `!` marker fails deterministically; `v1.0.0` is tagged by `basicly release` with both pushes owner-approved.

## Success Criteria

- The five consumer surfaces are enumerated in one machine-readable place and frozen: CLI commands and flags, `basicly.toml` plus the `.basicly-local/` overlay contract, the catalog source schemas, the generated-file contract, and the owned ledger event format.
- A commit that changes a frozen surface without a `!` marker is refused by a deterministic gate (hook and `basicly verify`), with a test that trips it.
- A published compatibility policy states what `1.x` promises for each surface and how a break is announced.
- A fresh consumer repository (git plus a uv-provisioned interpreter, nothing else) installs basicly, runs every gate green, and drives one unit of work to a landed commit; this runs as a test, not as prose.
- The next Python minor is exercised in CI so the `3.14+` floor claim is tested, not asserted (CI edits need explicit owner confirmation; the child names that).
- The two requirements documents are folded into the architecture and deleted, and §3 of the plan is refreshed once; the plan file itself is deleted when the ladder is spent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the frozen-surface manifest when `basicly verify --mode full` runs then a diff to any listed surface in the commit under test without a `!` in the subject fails the `surface-freeze` check naming the surface.
- Given a clean machine with git and uv when the acceptance test runs then it installs the packaged basicly into a new repository, every projection gate passes, and one task record advances intake to a landed commit.
- Given `docs/` when the release is cut then a compatibility policy document exists, is linked from the README, and names each of the five surfaces.
- Given `basicly release 1.0.0 --dry-run` when run on main then release-notes, release-fragments and docs-claims are green and the dry run prints the assembled notes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/**`
- `tests/**`
- `.basicly/core/**`
- `.scripts/**`
- `docs/**`
- `README.md`
- `basicly.d/**`
- `changelog.d/**`

## Context

Observed 2026-08-27 on `basicly-6ajmrc`: the landing failed `pyright-windows`, and the repair brief at `.basicly/usage/repair-brief.json` carried `"evidence": [{"check": "verify full", "command": "basicly verify --mode full", "output": ""}]`; `verify-run.json` recorded `"detail": ""` for the failing check. The next session had to re-run the check by hand to learn the two errors. The ledger shows the pattern repeats: 35 landings failed `verify full` (pytest 44, lint-imports 24, docs-claims 16 by check), and the finding-set warning "the gate reported the same 2 finding(s) as the previous attempt ... this round changed nothing it reports" appears on lint-imports rounds, which is what a repair briefed with no output looks like.

The output exists at the moment it is dropped. `merge.py` re-runs the failures with `verify.rerun_failures(report, worktree_path, verify_mode, capture=True)` for its unreliable-gate test, so `rerun.results[*].output` holds the transcript; `MergeResult` keeps a one-line `detail` and the transcript is discarded. `loop._landing_verify_evidence` documents the gap in its own docstring ("Only the command, not the output ... widening it is merge's contract to change").

## Steps to Reproduce

In a worktree bound to a lane, introduce a type error that only `pyright --pythonplatform Windows` reports, commit, run `basicly loop advance <id>` from base. Observed: the landing fails, the brief's `evidence[0].output` is `""`. Expected: `evidence` holds one entry per failing check with the check's captured stdout+stderr, clipped from the front to the configured brief length.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a landing whose re-run reproduces N failing checks when the repair brief is written then `evidence` holds N entries, each naming the check, its command, and the captured output of the re-run.
- Given a failing check when `verify-run.json` is written then its `detail` holds the check's captured output or a one-line reason, never an empty string for a `fail` status.
- Given a landing with an unreliable or foreign verdict when the brief is written then no evidence entry is fabricated for it (behaviour unchanged).
- Demonstrated by: `uv run pytest tests/test_loop.py tests/test_merge.py tests/test_repair_brief.py -q` with a test that lands a worktree carrying a failing check and reads the captured output back out of the brief.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/merge.py`
- `src/basicly/loop.py`
- `src/basicly/repair_brief.py`
- `src/basicly/verify.py`
- `tests/test_merge.py`
- `tests/test_loop.py`
- `tests/test_repair_brief.py`
- `tests/test_verify.py`
- `changelog.d/*.md`

The mechanism is already measured: --resume --fork-session gives ~10x cheaper warm starts, one-time penalty per working directory (plan row ejdm). ## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the role is a reviewer, validator, decider or retrospector, THE DISPATCH SHALL stay cold, and the policy names why.
- WHEN no seed exists, THE FIRST DISPATCH SHALL create it.
- Demonstrated by: two consecutive implementer dispatches on one feature, the second's cache-read share and cost against today's cold baseline.
