## Context

Four operating traps lived only in one agent's local memory on one machine, so a second machine or a second agent re-discovers each at the price of a round. Probed 2026-08-29 with `rg -c` over `.basicly/core/`, AGENTS.md and the ledger (control: `positive control` = 8 hits): `setsid` 0, `scratch clone` 0, `2x` wall-clock rule 0, `headroom` 0. Each has a code form that is a separate record; this record is the interim skill bullet so the knowledge is in the repo today.

1. A supervisor started through an agent tool's background job dies at that tool's ceiling (10 minutes for one host) mid-round; three lanes died with it on 2026-08-28. Detach it (`setsid nohup ... & disown`) and watch the log. Code form: `loop supervise --detach`.
2. `basicly release --dry-run` runs no commit gate (basicly-vwh3aq, open); the proof is a scratch clone that applies the release steps, stages, and runs the pre-commit framework and the whole suite.
3. A wall-clock cap in a test must clear the slowest CI runner by 2x or it is a flake generator (basicly-7aler3: 3.0 s cap measured 0.48 s locally, 3.1 s on windows-latest).
4. Measure the module-size and comment-density headroom of every file a change will touch before writing (`.scripts/headroom.py <files>`); the two ratchets pull opposite ways and paying them after the code is written is the slowest order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the `harness-loop` skill's supervise section is read, IT SHALL say how to start a supervisor so no agent tool ceiling can kill it, and what to watch in its log.
- WHEN the `release-process` skill is read, IT SHALL carry the scratch-clone proof as the step before handing the owner the release command, and name basicly-vwh3aq as the record that retires the step.
- WHEN the `test-discipline` skill's Determinism section is read, IT SHALL carry the 2x rule for a wall-clock cap.

## Context

A supervisor round runs 20 to 40 minutes. Started through an agent tool's background job, the process dies at that tool's ceiling (600 s for one host) mid-round: on 2026-08-28 three lanes died with it, their worktrees dirty, ten ledger events uncommitted, one round of spend (~25M tokens) lost. The remedy today is shell knowledge (`setsid nohup env -u FORCE_COLOR uv run basicly loop supervise ... > log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown`) that lives in a skill bullet (basicly-scmpfp) and differs per platform. The engine should own it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly loop supervise <root> --detach` runs, IT SHALL start the supervisor in its own session detached from the calling terminal on Linux, macOS and Windows, print the log path and the pid, and return within 5 s.
- WHEN the calling process exits or is killed, THE detached supervisor SHALL keep running and its round SHALL land.
- WHEN `--detach` is combined with `--max-passes`, `--label` or `--tier`, THE flags SHALL reach the detached process unchanged.
- WHEN the `harness-loop` skill is read, ITS detached-launch bullet SHALL name `--detach` and no shell incantation.

## Context

A grant's spend is read from `.basicly/usage/run-records.json`, which is gitignored; `board_facts.grant_spend` returns None without it and `basicly session start` prints `spend unknown` for every grant on a fresh clone (measured 2026-08-29: `basicly-hnnmk9` shows 149,252,215 spent on this machine and `totals.spend_micros` 0 in the ledger). The spend bound, the forecast and the tier priors all read the same file, so on a second machine the factory cannot refuse on budget and `usage tuning` has no sample. D-11 says the ledger is the travelling read; spend is the one grant fact that does not travel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a dispatch completes, ITS recorded spend SHALL be appended to the ledger as a typed event on the lane record, and `basicly session start` on a fresh clone SHALL print the same `spent` figure the originating machine prints.
- WHEN the run-record file is absent, `grant_spend` SHALL derive spend from the ledger and report None only when the ledger holds no dispatch for the root.
- WHEN the existing run-record file and the ledger disagree, THE command SHALL report both figures rather than choose one silently.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`

## Context

The owner asks that the board be visible before development starts, because it is the human's view of open, in-progress and planned work. The board is engine code (`src/basicly/board_*.py`), not a kit: `.basicly/core/kit/` holds `tier` and `tracker` only, so a kit-only repository has no board to start. `basicly board serve` acquires no lock and writes no file, so nothing can tell whether one is running; there is no `[board]` port in `basicly.toml` and no VS Code task starts it. An always-on instruction telling every agent to start a server is wrong for a headless lane (no viewer, one server per lane) and violates the session-finish rule that no background process outlives the session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly session start` runs and a board answers on the configured loopback port, IT SHALL print one line with the URL and the snapshot age; WHEN none answers, IT SHALL print the command that starts one; IT SHALL never start a server itself.
- WHEN `[board] port` is absent from `basicly.toml`, THE command SHALL use the documented default and say so.
- WHEN the repository has no owned tracker, THE line SHALL be absent.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/board_serve.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_cli_session.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

- depends on: none

payload.text: [owner-decision 2026-08-23, 2026-08-18] (1) The factory is the product: the execution plane (loop, supervisor, tracker engine) ships to consumers; the scope question is closed, do not re-ask. (2) There is no upper limit on agents or loop lanes; only a human may impose one. The driving session decides the width from the shape of the work. Cost is bounded by sizing the work (decompose --dry-run first), never by running fewer lanes. The binding constraint is isolation: two or fewer agents in the base checkout, every further lane in its own worktree. (3) Parallel engine lanes (worktrees + headless agent CLIs + serial merge queue) are the default for every plan; never ask whether to use the factory. Recorded here from an agent's local memory so the decisions travel with the ledger (basicly-hnnmk9).

[owner-decision 2026-08-23] Full release autonomy: the driving session chooses the version, cuts and pushes when verify is green. Revocable by the owner. Recorded here from an agent's local memory so the decision travels with the ledger (basicly-hnnmk9).

[owner-decision 2026-08-23] (1) Board wall: a non-loopback LAN bind, and destructive touch actions need a typed confirm code. (2) The board is a developer cockpit first and a TV wall second: a developer inside a consumer repo uses it to track many parallel agent sessions. [owner-question 2026-08-29] The owner asks that the board be visible before development starts. Facts: the board is engine code (src/basicly/board_*.py), not a kit; .basicly/core/kit/ holds tier and tracker only; a kit-only repository has no board; the server writes no file and takes no lock so nothing can detect it; no VS Code task starts it. basicly-2n5dfe makes session start report a serving board and never start one. Open for the owner: whether a standalone board kit (stdlib only, reads the ledger and the snapshot) is wanted.

[owner-decision 2026-08-22, 2026-08-01] Code is the only authority. Four rules: docs/architecture/architecture.md is the single permanent document, kept in sync; every other document survives only while it describes a future state and is deleted once the code exists; prose belongs in the ledger, never in a comment; convert before you delete - a checkable comment becomes a test, an assert or a gate first. Operational knowledge belongs in the repo: if an agent must search its own memory to run basicly correctly, that knowledge is an undocumented runtime dependency; externalize deterministic knowledge as a command or gate, semi-deterministic as a script plus a skill, the rest as instructions. Recorded here from an agent's local memory so the rules travel with the ledger.

## Context

The always-on layer now tells an agent to open a session with `basicly session start` (basicly-1ciu6w), but the command still runs only when the agent obeys the line or the user asks. The hook projector knows two agent-side stages, `pretooluse` and `posttooluse` (`.basicly/core/hooks/hooks.yaml`, `manager: claude` and `manager: copilot`); neither fires at session open. Claude Code and Copilot both expose a session-start hook event whose stdout is injected into the agent's context; Codex has no hook surface, so the always-on line stays the floor there. With a `sessionstart` stage, the orientation reaches the agent before its first turn with no prompt from the human.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a hook declares `stage: sessionstart` with `manager: claude`, `basicly hooks-build` SHALL project it into the matching event section of `.claude/settings.json`, and `hooks-check` SHALL report drift when the projection is stale.
- WHEN a hook declares `stage: sessionstart` with `manager: copilot`, `hooks-build` SHALL project it into the managed `.github/hooks/basicly-<id>.json` under the event name the vendor documents; the name SHALL be verified against the vendor's current documentation (the `interface-facts` skill) and recorded on this record, not recalled.
- WHEN a Claude or Copilot session opens in this repository, THE hook SHALL run `basicly session start` and its output SHALL reach the agent's context; WHEN the repository has no owned tracker, THE hook SHALL exit 0 and print nothing.
- WHEN the hook script runs, IT SHALL finish within 10 s or print a one-line reason and exit 0; a slow fold must not block the session.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/hooks/hooks.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/hooks/session-start.py`
- `src/basicly/hooks.py`
- `.claude/settings.json`
- `.github/hooks/**`
- `tests/test_hooks.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

- demonstration: open a new Claude Code session in the repo and read the `Handover (...)` line in the injected context before typing anything; `uv run basicly hooks-check` is green.

COPILOT: event name is sessionStart (camelCase). Source: docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference and docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-hooks, both fetched 2026-08-31 (HTTP 200). Schema: .github/hooks/NAME.json, version 1, hooks keyed by event name; a sessionStart entry takes type/bash/powershell/cwd/timeoutSec, default timeout 30 s. Output contract: stdout is parsed as ONE JSON object and only additionalContext is injected, as a prepended user message - plain text is unparseable and dropped without a word. PascalCase SessionStart is the VS Code-compatible alternative, whose payload carries hook_event_name and snake_case fields; camelCase selects the camelCase payload (sessionId, timestamp, cwd, source). Observed firing on 2026-08-31 in a 1.0.82 session debug log: [rust:hooks] [hook stdout] {"additionalContext": "ledger: 1187 records, ...} and the same text in the turn message payload. The model call was then refused for quota, so injection is proven from the log, not from a model answer.

CLAUDE CODE: event name is SessionStart. Source: docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks, fetched 2026-08-31. The matcher filters how the session started (startup, resume, clear, compact, fork) and "*" or omitted means all - so the write-tools default matcher would never fire, hence matcher "*" in hooks.yaml. Plain-text stdout is added to context on this event (one of four exceptions); command-hook default timeout is 600 s. Demonstrated: a fresh claude -p session quoted the Handover line back before any tool call.

claims.claim: `basicly board serve [--port N] [--bind ADDR] [--refresh S] [--no-actions]` | Serve the board for a wall display. GET reads; **one POST route** runs a `basicly` command an operator submitted, behind a one-time confirm code the operator types and this server never holds. `--no-actions` registers no action route and every POST is then 405 — the recommended flag for an unattended wall. `--bind` takes a literal IPv4 interface address, refusing a wildcard or a hostname, and defaults to the loopback.

**The per-type set is configuration.** `[policy.type_sections]` declares what each work type owes beyond the acceptance criteria every bead owes whatever its type, and `config.load_type_sections` reads it — falling back to the engine's `DEFAULT_TYPE_SECTIONS` and saying so. A type the table omits owes nothing extra, so an empty table is a real answer. `tests/test_config.py` pins both halves.

The mechanism is a git-ignored `redirect` file that provisioning writes into the new worktree's ledger directory, naming the base checkout. `tracker_paths.tracker_root` is the single resolver every reader and writer goes through, and it honours the file only when the directory it names exists — an absent or empty redirect resolves to the checkout itself rather than to nothing.

**Gate 3 asks for a budget, not for delegation coverage.** It refuses a pass whose configured runner meters spend while the session's grant carries no token budget. Whether the grant's *level* delegates a given decision is asked at checkpoint approval and at decider delegation, never here.
Layer 3 runs the same `full` mode as layer 2's **pre-push** stage. Layer 2's **pre-commit** stage runs the narrower `fast` mode, so a clean commit predicts less than a clean push does.

## Context

Split from basicly-rhzr6d, whose working set the sizing band refused (2,113,392 tokens against the 8,000..264,000 band, measured by `basicly loop preflight` on 2026-09-01). This child carries the write path only. A grant's spend lives only in the gitignored `.basicly/usage/run-records.json`, so the fact does not travel with the ledger (D-11: the ledger is the travelling read). The fold already carries `totals.spend_micros`; the missing part is the writer that feeds it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a dispatch completes, THE engine SHALL append one typed spend event on the lane record through the engine seam, carrying the tokens spent, and the event kind SHALL be a member of `events.KNOWN_KINDS` drawn from the architecture §32.3 vocabulary.
- WHEN the same dispatch completion is recorded twice, THE ledger SHALL hold one spend event, by the content-digest event id.
- WHEN `ledger-fsck` runs over a log holding the new kind, IT SHALL classify the kind as applied or delegated, never unknown.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `src/basicly/tracker.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py`
- `tests/test_run_record.py`
- `tests/test_tracker_seam.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.added.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: record a dispatch completion through the seam against a scratch ledger, then `uv run python .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py show <scratch-ledger> <lane-id>` returns the spend in `totals.spend_micros`.

Split from basicly-rhzr6d, whose working set the sizing band refused (2,113,392 tokens against the 8,000..264,000 band, measured by `basicly loop preflight` on 2026-09-01). This child carries the read path and depends on the write-path child. `board_facts.grant_spend` reads only the gitignored `.basicly/usage/run-records.json` and returns None without it, so `basicly session start` prints `spend unknown` for every grant on a fresh clone (measured 2026-08-29: basicly-hnnmk9 shows 149,252,215 spent on the origin machine and `totals.spend_micros` 0 in the ledger). The spend bound, the forecast and the tier priors all read the same file, so on a second machine the factory cannot refuse on budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the run-record file is absent, `grant_spend` SHALL derive spend from the ledger and report None only when the ledger holds no dispatch for the root.
- WHEN the run-record file and the ledger disagree, THE command SHALL report both figures rather than choose one silently.
- WHEN `basicly session start` runs on a fresh clone whose ledger holds spend events, IT SHALL print the same `spent` figure the originating machine prints.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`

## Context

A supervisor round runs 20 to 40 minutes. Started through an agent tool's background job, the process dies at that tool's ceiling (600 s for one host) mid-round: on 2026-08-28 three lanes died with it, their worktrees dirty, ten ledger events uncommitted, one round of spend (~25M tokens) lost. The remedy today is shell knowledge (`setsid nohup env -u FORCE_COLOR uv run basicly loop supervise ... > log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown`) that lives in a skill bullet (basicly-scmpfp) and differs per platform. The engine should own it.

Scope narrowed 2026-09-01: the two whole-tree skill globs (`.claude/skills/**`, `.agents/skills/**`) put the working set at 317,367 tokens, over the 264,000 band cap measured by `basicly loop preflight`. Only the harness-loop projection changes, so the globs now name that subtree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly loop supervise <root> --detach` runs, IT SHALL start the supervisor in its own session detached from the calling terminal on Linux, macOS and Windows, print the log path and the pid, and return within 5 s.
- WHEN the calling process exits or is killed, THE detached supervisor SHALL keep running and its round SHALL land.
- WHEN `--detach` is combined with `--max-passes`, `--label` or `--tier`, THE flags SHALL reach the detached process unchanged.
- WHEN the `harness-loop` skill is read, ITS detached-launch bullet SHALL name `--detach` and no shell incantation.

## Scope

## Context

Found 2026-09-01 while committing tracker state. tracker.scrub_ledger repairs what tracker-path-scan refuses (machine identity and paths, via redact.redact_committed), but internal-info-scan refuses a disjoint token set ([[privacy.denied]] in basicly.local.toml). scrub_ledger re-mints every rewritten line, internal-info-scan reads added lines only, so any whole-file scrub re-presents old payloads carrying a denied token as new lines and the commit is blocked with no engine repair. A one-off script re-using the scrub machinery cleared 9 events this time; the engine should own it, as it owns the path scrub.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN scrub_ledger runs in a repo whose local config declares [[privacy.denied]] tokens, IT SHALL replace each token in event payloads with <redacted:NAME> and re-mint the ids, the same way it treats machine identity.
- WHEN no local config exists, THE scrub SHALL behave as today.
- WHEN the printed repair command in tracker-path-scan is shown, IT SHALL name a module that exists (today it names basicly.br, deleted at the flip).

## Scope

- src/basicly/tracker.py
- src/basicly/redact.py
- .basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py
- tests/test_tracker_scrub_ledger.py
- changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- depends on: none
- demonstration: seed a scratch ledger with a payload carrying a locally denied token, run the scrub, and read the placeholder back with the kit CLI.

## Context

`_print_preflight_spend` (src/basicly/cli.py) has two branches. With lanes dispatchable it prints `admit_pass_spend(...).coverage`, the figure the gate will use. With none dispatchable it prints `forecast:  ~{per_lane * priced}` — the unsizeable-lane bound times the lane count — and never calls `admit_pass_spend` at all. Four lines later the same branch builds `candidates` working-set admissions for the band table, so the sized estimate is already in hand and is discarded.

Measured on basicly-atrqcd 2026-09-01, base 24a0d6f3, four open children:

- preflight printed `forecast:  ~93153836 tokens if all 4 lanes start`, which is exactly `23288459 x 4`.
- `supervise.admit_pass_spend` over the same four working sets returns `87214845 tokens forecast ... sized: basicly-jt0dgi, basicly-3iaw0x, basicly-mfavrh, basicly-rv7q88` with `assumed: ()`.

The gap is 5938991 tokens (6.8 percent) here and is unbounded in general: the printed number is independent of the scopes. The branch exists precisely so an operator can mint a budget before the pass starts — its own docstring says so — so the one number a budget is sized from is the one number that ignores the sizing. It also reads as evidence that the lanes are unsizeable when they are not, which is how a session concluded a scope rewrite had failed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN preflight runs with no dispatchable lane and the open children have readable scopes, IT SHALL print the sized pass forecast from `admit_pass_spend` over those children.
- WHEN an open child has no readable scope, ITS contribution SHALL still be the unsizeable-lane bound, and the printed coverage SHALL name it as assumed.
- WHEN preflight runs with no open children at all, IT SHALL keep the leaf behaviour of pricing the root as one lane.
- WHEN the printed forecast is compared with the figure `admit_pass_spend` returns for the same candidate set, THE TWO SHALL be equal.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `uv run basicly loop preflight basicly-atrqcd` prints 87214845 and names the four lanes as sized
payload.title: preflight prints the unsizeable bound as the forecast when no lane is dispatchable yet so a budget is minted from a number the gate never uses

## Context

`decisions.enqueue` is idempotent per `(issue, kind, question)`. When the item is already pending it returns the existing item at src/basicly/decisions.py:100-102 and never rewrites the detail. `PASS_SPEND_QUESTION` in src/basicly/supervise.py is deliberately constant so a repeatedly refusing pass finds the item it already queued, and the numbers live in the detail for exactly that reason. The consequence is that the detail is frozen at first-queue time and every later refusal leaves it untouched.

Measured on basicly-atrqcd 2026-09-01, base 24a0d6f3. `basicly loop decisions basicly-atrqcd` prints for `basicly-atrqcd#3018546b66`:

- `93153836 tokens forecast; 60000000 remaining under the grant; assumed at the unsizeable-lane bound (measured): basicly-jt0dgi, basicly-3iaw0x, basicly-mfavrh, basicly-rv7q88`

Every number and every classification in that line is now wrong. `supervise.admit_pass_spend` over the same four lanes returns `87214845 tokens forecast; 4345392 remaining under the grant; sized:` all four, with `assumed: ()`. Remaining is off by a factor of 13.8, and the line asserts the lanes are unsizeable when their scopes read.

The detail is the only thing a human sees when answering. `PassSpendAdmission.coverage` exists so an operator can see that a number is an assumption before it is the only thing standing between them and the bill; a frozen copy of that sentence defeats it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a pending decision item is re-enqueued with a different detail, THE ITEM SHALL keep its decision id and carry the current detail.
- WHEN a pending item is re-enqueued with an unchanged detail, NO further comment or notification SHALL be produced.
- WHEN `basicly loop decisions <id>` prints a pending item, THE DETAIL SHALL be the one from the most recent enqueue.
- WHEN a stale detail is superseded, THE ORIGINAL SHALL remain readable in the append-only log rather than being overwritten in place.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `basicly loop decisions basicly-atrqcd` prints the current forecast and remaining budget for basicly-atrqcd#3018546b66
payload.title: a pending decision item keeps the detail it was first queued with so a human answers a budget escalation from stale numbers

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-09-01 on a clone of this repo at commit 7e858322, folded in the clone own uv environment so the reading is not an artifact of a borrowed interpreter.

```text
working checkout:  board: sections  11 rendered, 0 withheld, 1 not emitted
fresh clone:       board: sections   7 rendered, 0 withheld, 5 not emitted
```

The five the clone loses are `gates`, `health`, `lanes`, `session` and `spend`. Four of them are absent for one reason: their producers read `.basicly/usage/`, which the repo git-ignores, and a clone has no such directory at all. `board_usage.gates` reads it; `run_record.load_run_records` reads `.basicly/usage/run-records.json` and feeds both `health` and `spend`; `session_facts` needs a supervisor lock that has never been taken. The `Act` panel disappears with them. `lanes` is a separate defect with its own record.

The ready set travels fine - the clone drew 211 ready rows - so this is not a ledger problem. It is that half the board is derived from a store that never leaves the machine that wrote it. An operator on a new clone reads a board that says a producer did not measure, and concludes the tool is broken.

basicly-0eexh5 and basicly-7hebuh made *grant* spend travel by writing a typed `dispatch` event into the committed ledger. The board `spend` panel does not read that path, so the same figure is on the board and off it depending on the checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the board is folded on a checkout that holds committed ledger dispatch events and no `.basicly/usage/` directory, THE `spend` SECTION SHALL be emitted from the committed ledger.
- WHEN no run history exists in either store, THE SECTION SHALL still be omitted rather than emitted as a zero.
- WHEN the board is folded on a checkout with no gate history, THE `gates` SECTION SHALL name that the history is local rather than reading as an unmeasured producer.
- WHEN `basicly board` runs on a fresh clone, ITS section line SHALL report fewer than five sections not emitted.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_usage.py`
- `src/basicly/board_snapshot.py`
- `tests/test_board_usage.py`
- `tests/test_board_snapshot.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `basicly board --out` on a fresh clone reports a smaller not-emitted count and draws a spend panel

payload.description:
## Context

`board_facts.document` takes `in_flight` defaulting to False and emits the `lanes` section only when it is True. Exactly one caller passes True: `board_facts.emit_tick` at src/basicly/board_facts.py:572, the supervisor 15-second beat. Both one-shot producers call the bare form - `board_cli.py:97` for `basicly board --out` and `board_cli.py:135` for the server `build` callback - so neither emits it.

Measured 2026-09-01 on this checkout:

```text
board_facts.document(Path(".")) -> lanes present: False
```

The consequence is that on any repo with no supervisor running, `running now` reads `not emitted by this producer` and the loop note reads `current position: lanes not emitted by this producer`. Two markers, and the section can never say anything else. A live supervisor replaces the whole document with its own tick file, which does emit lanes, so the section works only in the state where an operator least needs to be told what is running.

The omission is deliberate and the reason is recorded at the parameter: Mode A and Mode B fold whatever lock they find without knowing its selector, so a label pass drawn from there would name the root children instead of the lanes in flight. That constraint is real. It argues for a different reading, not for silence - the same document already distinguishes `no lane is dispatched` from an absent producer, and a checkout with no supervisor has a true answer to give.

This is the third instance of the shape basicly-bd4epr closed for the opposite direction. That record closed on a live-supervisor page; the unsupervised page was never the control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the board is folded with no supervisor lock held, THE `running now` SECTION SHALL read that no pass is running rather than that no producer emitted it.
- WHEN a supervisor lock is held, THE SECTION SHALL keep reading the tick producer lanes unchanged.
- WHERE the producer cannot know the pass selector, IT SHALL NOT name any bead as in flight.
- WHEN `basicly board --out` runs on this checkout with no supervisor, ITS output SHALL carry no `not emitted by this producer` marker for lanes.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `src/basicly/board_cli.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_board_cli.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `basicly board --out` with no supervisor running draws a running-now section that names the idle state
payload.title: the running now section can never say anything without a live supervisor because no one-shot producer emits lanes

payload.description:
## Context

CONTRIBUTING.md section Development setup tells a new contributor to run `uv run pre-commit install --install-hooks -t pre-commit -t commit-msg -t pre-push`, commented as activating the git gates for all three stages. It does not.

Measured 2026-09-01 on a fresh clone of this repo, run in the clone own uv environment:

```text
$ pre-commit install --install-hooks -t pre-commit -t commit-msg -t pre-push
pre-commit installed at .git/hooks/pre-push
$ basicly hooks-check
Note: git hooks are not installed for stages: pre-push. Run `basicly hooks-build` ...
$ grep -c ledger .git/hooks/pre-push
0
```

The positive control, in the same clone:

```text
$ basicly hooks-build
Activated git hooks for stages: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push.
$ basicly hooks-check          # no note
$ grep -c ledger .git/hooks/pre-push
5
```

So the documented command is the one `hooks-check` exists to warn about, and the warning names the fix the document does not. `hooks.py` already records the fact at `apply_pre_push_guard`: a bare `pre-commit install` rewrites the pre-push hook and drops the ledger guard.

`basicly hooks-check` prints its note on stderr and exits 0. That fail-open is deliberate - cli.py:1891 states that CI runs the scripts directly and does not install git hooks - so no gate refuses a clone that followed the document. A contributor gets a note they may not read and a pre-push stage that is missing its guard.

Reported by an operator whose colleague cloned this repo, started the board, and found the gates not installed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a contributor follows the Development setup block verbatim on a fresh clone, `basicly hooks-check` SHALL print no missing-stage note.
- WHEN the setup block names a command, THAT COMMAND SHALL be the one whose remedy `hooks-check` names.
- WHERE the pre-push ledger guard exists, THE DOCUMENT SHALL say that `pre-commit install` alone does not write it.

## Scope

- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L1
- demonstration: on a fresh clone, running the documented block then `basicly hooks-check` prints no note and `grep -c ledger .git/hooks/pre-push` is non-zero
payload.title: the contributor setup command leaves the pre-push ledger guard unwritten so a fresh clone commits and pushes past a gate

payload.description:
## Context

Measured 2026-09-01 during a live supervised pass on basicly-atrqcd. A commit staging the ledger was refused:

```text
spend-accuracy: basicly-rv7q88: basicly-rv7q88 spent 1,025,735 tokens against a
  recorded forecast of 11,610,753 (0.088x), outside the 10x band
```

At that moment `basicly-rv7q88` was in phase `build` with exactly 1,025,735 tokens on the live board. The gate compared a lane that had not finished against the forecast for the whole lane, and named the estimator as the fault.

`decompose.spend_accuracy` filters the dispatch population four ways and none of them is about completion. It drops an entry that is not a write phase, one whose tokens are unmetered or estimated, one whose outcome is `FAILED`, and one whose forecast was a stand-in. A dispatch entry for a bead whose lane is still open passes every one of those and is folded as though the work were done.

The remedy the gate prints is to freeze the record or fix the estimator. Both are wrong here: freezing banks a partial measurement as history, and the estimator is not what produced 0.088x.

The failure mode is that any commit taken while a pass runs can be refused by a lane that is merely early, and the operator is invited to bank a false number to get past it. The supervisor own tracker-state commit is exposed to the same refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a bead has a dispatch entry but its own work has not finished, THE GATE SHALL NOT score it.
- WHEN the bead finishes, ITS folded actual SHALL enter the population unchanged.
- WHEN the gate excludes a bead for being unfinished, ITS summary SHALL count it, so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.
- WHEN the population is empty of finished beads, THE GATE SHALL report that rather than passing quietly.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decompose.py`
- `.scripts/check_spend_accuracy.py`
- `tests/test_spend_calibration.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: a commit taken during a live pass is not refused by a lane still in build, and the gate summary counts the beads it held back
payload.title: the spend accuracy gate scores a lane that has not finished so a commit during a live pass is refused on a partial number

payload.value:
## Context

Architecture backlog entry B5 (backlog.md at commit 4618f614); architecture §14 marks it a target and status.yaml carries the row 'Both skill roots written by every skills command'. skills.resolve_skill_roots writes DEFAULT_SKILL_ROOTS[0] alone unless the caller passes --all-default-roots or an explicit --root. basicly install passes it and is correct; a bare basicly skills-check is not, and this repository's CLAUDE.md compensates with guidance - a prose gate standing in for a default. agents-build takes no root flag and always writes both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly skills-build` runs with no root flag, IT SHALL write every default root.
- WHEN `basicly skills-check` runs with no root flag, IT SHALL check every default root.
- WHEN `--root` names a root explicitly, ONLY that root SHALL be written or checked.
- WHEN `--all-default-roots` is passed, IT SHALL be accepted as a no-op with a deprecation note.

## Scope

Widened by the owner 2026-09-01 after two identical scope-collision refusals. The lane
edited 17 files outside the list below and the engine said the plan was wrong, not the
merge. Three groups were missing, and each really belongs here.

Projected output this change regenerates. Editing a skill source rewrites every agent
surface, so a skills lane cannot avoid them:

- `.claude/skills/**`
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `.agents/skills/**`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- `.basicly/generated-manifest.json`
- `docs/architecture/status.md`

Catalog sources naming the flag this change deprecates:

- `.basicly/core/skills/**`
- `.basicly-local/fragments/user/commands/commands.fragment.yaml`
- `basicly.toml`

Consumer surfaces documenting the flag. `docs/reference/cli.md` was basicly-mfavrh's
deliverable and `docs/how-to/upgrade-and-check-drift.md` was basicly-rv7q88's; both have
landed, so this ground is free:

- `docs/reference/cli.md`
- `docs/how-to/upgrade-and-check-drift.md`

The original list:

- `src/basicly/skills.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `src/basicly/scaffolds.py`
- `tests/test_skills.py`
- `tests/test_docs_claim_status.py`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/**`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `docs/architecture/status.yaml`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`
## Plan

- integrity: L3 (the CLI flag set is a frozen surface)
- demonstration: `uv run basicly skills-check` exits zero naming both roots

I did not run it myself; it is an install and mutates the machine's tool environment. pyproject.toml:82 shows a console script exists, which is a precondition for the recipe, not a demonstration that the recipe works.

## Context

Architecture backlog entry B5 (backlog.md at commit 4618f614); architecture §14 marks it a target and status.yaml carries the row 'Both skill roots written by every skills command'. skills.resolve_skill_roots writes DEFAULT_SKILL_ROOTS[0] alone unless the caller passes --all-default-roots or an explicit --root. basicly install passes it and is correct; a bare basicly skills-check is not, and this repository's CLAUDE.md compensates with guidance - a prose gate standing in for a default. agents-build takes no root flag and always writes both.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN `basicly skills-build` runs with no root flag, IT SHALL write every default root.
- WHEN `basicly skills-check` runs with no root flag, IT SHALL check every default root.
- WHEN `--root` names a root explicitly, ONLY that root SHALL be written or checked.
- WHEN `--all-default-roots` is passed, IT SHALL be accepted as a no-op with a deprecation note.

## Scope

Widened by the owner 2026-09-01 after two identical scope-collision refusals. The lane
edited 17 files outside the list below and the engine said the plan was wrong, not the
merge. Three groups were missing, and each really belongs here. The whole-tree globs `.claude/skills/**`, `.agents/skills/**`
and `.basicly/core/skills/**` were tried first and priced the lane at 562,854 working-set
tokens against a 264,000 ceiling; they are named per file instead, as basicly-uhrji9 was.

Projected output this change regenerates. Editing a skill source rewrites every agent
surface, so a skills lane cannot avoid them:
